review: I love some kebabs and I was excited the website said they were planning lamb roasts every Sunday.  The chicken and falafel sandwiches are alright but the lamb pastrami is the best thing I've had here.  I could tell that they really take some time to use some quality ingredients in a lot of what they prepare but they still have a lot of kinks to work out.  One of their unique offerings is the young coconut they pop open for you to drink.    Areas that could use some improvement:  They didn't have any self-serve ice next to the drinks so that was a bit of a challenge.  They also got my tables order confused with a to go order so that caused a bit of mix up so they need to develop a better order system.  Something got burned and caused a really bad burned odor and fumes; so accidents happen but maybe a better venting system over the oven could help it from being so overwhelming a sensation when they do.    The website is a bit confusing with the hours listing being Friday-Monday  3PM-12AM and 3PM-12PM in different locations on the site so that needs to be cleaned up to fix the AM/PM confusion.  The environment was also a bit confused inside with half art gallery and half restaurant and I  don't think the art gallery did much for me other than limit my seating options.  The crowd consisted of a lot of really dirty unwashed gutter punks and other Bywater hipster types that gave off quite a bit of unpleasant body odor so just be prepared for the possibility that if enough of them are there you might want to just get a to-go order to avoid their retched stench.  I think the Bywater restaurants might want to start posting signs that say, "No shower no service!"    50 cent surcharge for using credit cards!  I completely understand how credit cards abuse business owners with their fees but you should at least post a sign stating that policy instead of telling folks after the fact or NOT telling them at all!  The specials board is very badly placed way over to the left where nobody will see it unless they know to look way over to the left above the drinks.  You need the specials right underneath the register where folks can see them as they are approaching to order so they know they are there and really you should hang a board above the register.  Overall there are just a whole lot of other Middle Eastern and Greek restaurants that have better food to me at this point in the city but I certainly see this joint has some potential if they get their act together as they are the only restaurant of this genre in the Bywater.  So I'm just going to wait and see what develops but I'm still going to go back to try the roast lamb and get another coconut.

review: The third child of New Leaf Cuisine (Manayunk & Broomall being the elder siblings), Purple has replaced the ill fated Golden China at the Floral Vale location in Lower Makefield. While "Asian Fusion" is often just confusion, this house seems to actually know what it's doing when it comes to Sushi and Chinese food.   Their menu is a complex of decent sushi, "Street Food," noodles and Chinese dishes, all well done with a touch of creativity and lots of flavor. Prices reflect the talent in the kitchen, so even the dim sum small plates add up fast. As a first timer, and suspecting that Mandarin was the primary language, we opted for that part of the menu to sample.   Smart move.  Our four dishes were; Beef Chow Fun (traditional Cantonese broad noodles), Chicken with Dry Pepper (medium heat w jicama for cool crunch) from Chinese Kitchen - Entrees, Spicy Crispy Chicken (crunchy fried chicken Szechuan style) and Wok-fried Lemongrass Beef (hottest dish w Thai spice sensibilities). They were all very good, with tender sliced beef, white meat chicken and no skimping on the spices nor portions. Three of us supped to our hearts' content with leftovers for another day. Each made its own statement without redundancy. The kitchen was well trained in the mystic art of Asian sauces.   If the sushi and other Japanese pieces are on par with the mainland portion of the menu, Purple Leaf could well be worthy of that fifth star. review: It is so simple. Check-in, name called, blood drawn and you're on your way.   I had no idea this location was so close to home. I have always used the Quest closer to my doctors office, stopping by on my way home. This time I had to have blood drawn a week before seeing a specialist, so I Googled Quest and found this location which is conveniently located in my hood. It is hidden on the backside of the building so it is unnoticeable as you drive by the medical building. Out of site, out of mind.   I did not go on-line and make an appointment ahead of time. I just showed up, signed my name on the registry and took a seat. I barely had time to check in on Yelp and my name was being called. I presented the technician with my paperwork, insurance card and ID. She quickly got busy, preparing the vacutainer tubes as I tried to relax listening to the music playing from a small boom box she had sitting on the floor. I HATE having my blood drawn and have veins that most technicians hate. My veins are small, roll and hide when it is time to be poked and drained. My tech was not chatty, but she was professional. I give her four stars because, she jabbed me without hurting me and got in a vein on the first poke. I was In and Out in nothing flat, it was express service at its' best.   Now that I know a Quest is near my home, I may make this location my choice for blood draws. Instead of using the one near my doctors office, I'll come here. When I'm  finished here, I can get myself a treat at Starbucks or Ted Drew's which both are conveniently located across the street. You get a treat when you donate blood, why not get one after having a blood draw.

review: My second visit to Bristol in one week after a few years absence. Mill Street is coming back to life, and the area close to the Delaware River seems to be spearheading the revival. It is great to see a renaissance in this old river city.  It has suffered hard times through some neglectful governments and perhaps not so fatherly town elders. Yet, it is hard to keep a good old ville down when it has natural beauty and a real purpose over the centuries.  So it is with the King George II Inn. Originally built to be close to the ferry to Burlington, New Jersey, the only way across this water course for more that 250 years AFTER the ferry was started, the KGII evolved into a restaurant and subsequently an inn. Sitting in the oldest part of the building, the tavern, it is easy to imagine what it was like to be living and traveling in colonial America.  The various farmers, businessmen, hucksters, cons, grifters, and cutthroats gathered here to do their business, and wait for the ferry to take them to the colony of West Jersey.   Even today, that historic atmosphere permeates the Inn. Certainly there are ghosts stories aplenty.  I stopped into the Tavern for late lunch, sitting at a small table at the window overlooking the bottom of Mill Street, and the river just beyond.  The server (who was as gracious as an owner) greeted me warmly, took my order, and left me to my mental wandering.  The Pierogies appeared on a long thin white dish, covered in sautéed onions and fresh chives. A dollop of sour cream occupied one corner.  They were lightly fried, potato and cheese. They were pretty good at 6 for $9. I knew I was paying for the privilege of location.  No complaints.  The Tavern itself was excellently preserved and rehabbed to feel very original. All dark woods, heavy oak tables, and mirrored bar.  A perfect place to reenact debates between Patriots and Tories over lagers and locally distilled whiskey.    It is certainly worth a visit and a meal if you are into American history.  It is not quite Williamsburg, Va., where the entire community is a historic park and everyone is in costume.  Still, with a little imagination it is capable of taking you on quite a trip.

review: The last time the locksmith came to my house? I hugged him. That's how much I love their service.   My house is old; they are doing beaucoup construction work in my neighborhood causing my house to shift on it's foundations. Locks don't like shifting foundations, so sometimes they spaz out. Or you discover that there's a button lock on the front door that gets accidentally pushed and how do you get OUT?! So I just call up the office and someone comes out usually with 24 hours (weekdays).   I have had a variety of locksmiths come out but my favorite is the older man because he reminds me of my grandfather. (He's also the one I hugged last time. Yes I think he thought I was crazy.) Everyone has been very professional and really helpful, giving me hints on how to prevent future problems.  I know they have gift items in their store and really should get over there and shop.

review: When this new IHOP opened, it wasn't open 24 Hours any day of the week. I am now happy to say, it has expanded it's hours for Thursday - Saturday to 24 Hours.  This location use to be a Denny's Diner that closed several years ago and sat vacant. IHOP came in did a full remodel and has brought new life and a new breakfast place to the Alton area.   Part of my work schedule requires me to work in Alton on weekends and except for the local McDonald's the choices for an early breakfast were bleak. Now that this IHOP has expanded its hours, my options have expanded. I can easily stop in grab a quick coffee and a Simple Breakfast and still be at work by 6 AM.   Their Simple Breakfast is a good value. It's simple, two eggs, choice of two bacon strips or two sausage patties, Hash Browns and Toast. I have them hold the toast, the Hash Browns are enough starch for this dieting man.   The staff from what I have experienced is small town friendly and attentive to their diners. I may find myself getting up a little earlier just so I can have a hearty breakfast. After all, it is the most important meal of the day.

review: Excellent burgers on South 5th Street, just where Passyunk intersects with the 5. Design your own using the three computer stations, or go to the counter to talk with the people working there. Either way you get a standard double patty complemented any way you choose. If you don't want to think that much about it, the menu offers several great combinations that are bound to make you happy.   Just the right amount of grease, potato or pretzel roll, natural sugar carbonated beverages, Bassett ice cream based shakes, and fresh fruit smoothies, all surround the ultimate comfort food for your indulgence.   Prices that won't break the bank just off the hippest street in town.   If there is something to improve upon, it is that it appears that every burger is finished to well done regardless of how you request it. Still, they are so juicy I almost didn't notice.

review: I go to Le Bon Temps often and they have some good music.  They also have FREE oysters on Fridays but they go quick so you need to get there early!  The kitchen serves food til pretty late and I don't even know when they close it down so that is an option to keep in mind.  The bar is divided into 2 main areas with the front being full of pool tables and the back where the bands play.  This is usually a really fun bar to watch music until the point that it gets too crowded, which is way too often, but you always have the front area of the bar to escape to.    The back area, where the bands play, can just get miserably crowded especially on Thursday nights when Soul Rebels play (it also is a bad "tradition" that the Soul Rebels NEVER start on time so it is like 12:30 or 1am before they start usually so if you have to work the next day that really is a challenge).  There are also some people that take their pool games WAY too seriously in here and I've seen a few fights break out over a stupid game so don't get in those folks way.  Parking can sometimes be a bit of a challenge but if you get far enough away you can always find a spot.      They usually have pretty quick bar service and I usually prefer the front bar when there is music as it is quicker to get served than fighting the often formidable crowd in the back.  There is always an interesting crowd here and there is a special plaque on the bar involving a historical person that I will let you discover yourself.  There always seems to be something going on here when it seems nothing else is anywhere else in the area.  FYI:  This is yet another of the bars that claims the notoriety of having had Lee Harvey Oswald as a frequent customer.

review: I really liked the wild berry smoothie and the Kurt V sandwich I had here.  Both were ready in a matter of a few minutes and were full of flavor.  The smoothie was super cold and almost gave me brain freeze upon three different occasions!  It was so good which was so tempting.    The sandwich was grilled with portobello, provolone, roasted red peppers, fresh spinach, and garlic aioli.  Very tasty and with a bit of a chew getting through the different textures in the sandwich.  Very colorful sandwich, as well.  I definitely recommend this!  Since I am in the neighborhood about once a month, I would probably stop in again, but even at lunch time, there was little to no conversation.  Nobody smiling.  Maybe that's just the way restaurants / coffee shops are now.  Everyone is on their phone or laptop and many have earphones in.  Sad that conversation seems to be non-existent in these types of places.  I remember "in the olden days" when these types of places were great for discussion on world problems, without getting into name calling.  Different times. review: Sweet, Mother of God! Tripel is amazing.   I can not tell you the last time I had something this good in my mouth. I could, but one of us (me) might blush. From the first bite of Terrine, to the last bite of Creme Brûlée my taste buds were screaming, "OMG, don't stop, faster, give it to me faster, I want more."   Proving that every dish was a foodgasm.   We started off with a Terrine, which was made with chicken liver and bone marrow. I am not a fan of liver, especially chicken and this Terrine won me over. It was served in a small mason jar with crostini's on the side. I had no idea, a chicken liver could taste so good.   I love escargot and this is the best I've had in my entire life. I bet even Lucy Ricardo would have skipped using ketchup and enjoyed these exquisite snails. They were served with bone marrow and with the two of them combined on a baguette, totally set off fireworks in my mouth. If you are a fan of both of these culinary delights, you'll understand how delicious it would be when they're combined into one.   Next we enjoyed two pots of mussels. A la Marimiere, was a traditional white wine shallot broth and Provencales, a tomato, garlic and fresh basil broth. They were served in small black pots on plates with slices of baguette on the side. When the top was removed, it was the perfect place to discard the shells. It made it so easy to shuck all the mussels at once. I was then able to enjoy my mussels with a soup spoon as if I were eating a hearty soup. When I was done, I wanted to pick up the pot by its' handles and do my best Oliver Twist imitation, "More, please".   We were both stuffed like the Thanksgiving turkey, but it did not stop us from exploring the dessert menu. If you're going to over stuff yourself, why only share one dessert? You might as well, go hog wild and experience two. We ordered the Belgium Waffles with Baked Apples and Cheesecake with Cherries and Candied Bacon. The bartender claimed the Cheesecake was his favorite, so I ordered it instead of my original intention Creme Brûlée.  The house made cheesecake with the candied cherries and bacon was unbelievable. Forget about breaking me off a piece of that Kit Kat Bar, break me off another piece of that candied bacon, it is so addicting. The Belgium Waffles with baked apples was like eating an ready to assembled pie. It was a great way to end our meal.   As a bonus, the bartender treated us to a Creme Brûlée. He wanted to make sure, he didn't steer me wrong on ordering his favorite. He was right his was the best of the three, but the Creme Brûlée was still outstanding. I'd be torn on which one to reorder on my next visit.   The ambiance is a mixture of blast from the past  (classic cocktail lounge) and as Megan stated, "industrial chic". It is both relaxing and romantic.  This is an ideal place for a date night, business meeting or hanging with friends. The staff is extremely friendly and very knowledgeable about the menu offerings. I was so impressed, I plan on being a regular at Tripel.

review: Don't get it. Seriously, I do not understand all these 5 Star reviews for these donuts. I was not impressed. I stopped by when my favorite radio station was broadcasting live, expecting to be blown away. It didn't happen.   I always judge a donut shop by their  Chocolate Long Johns and the one I had here was dry and rather flavorless. It was chewy and a bottle of milk didn't even help. I think my second one was a Buttermilk type donut. This one, I took only a single bite and threw it back in the bag. Yeah, it was that good.   It had to be an off day, they were slammed with a popular radio station in their parking lot. Next time I'm headed south to shop at Costco, I'll detour and give them a second chance. As of now, I think the donuts at TDS are just average. A Long John at QT is fresher and better.   The staff was friendly and I liked that the young lady asked if I wanted my Long John plain or creme filled. Customer Service was good and they kept up with the busy crowd.   I'll be back? - Everyone deserves a second chance.   When: August 9, 2019 Why: 1st Experience - Radio Broadcast

The other night with the fabulous Shercole, I tried a Rosy Disposition, at first I though the Pernod might be too much for me, but that was just the first sip. Refreshing and delicious. Second I had the Wrong Way Home, so tasty and citrusy.   I also tried the pimento cheese on a saltine which is stupidly delicious and the carrot puree which pops with ginger.  Service was great. And the atmosphere is well designed and fun. The outdoor courtyard is great... when it's not 80bajillion degrees.

review: Five stars for Hawthorne Painting! I was driving near my neighborhood when I spotted a sign for this company, and I pulled it up on Yelp as soon as I got home. I sent a request a quote message and ended up chatting with John, the owner, the same day. He stopped by to see my project, sent me a quote, and within days he and his crew were at my house!   We needed our front railing, front door, and roof deck railings to be sanded down and re-painted. Our house is only four years old but, as we've discovered, new construction doesn't always equal the best quality. John and his crew showed up bright and early around 8:30am, and worked tirelessly in the sun until the project was finished around 4pm.   John explained the differences in the types of paint he needed to use for the railings and door. Everyone in the crew was friendly and careful about their work space - by the time they left, you wouldn't have known they were even here, aside from their gorgeous handiwork! My husband and I think the railings and door look even better now than they did when we bought our house.   My only regret? Not taking before and after photos! These guys made a world of difference and I'm so happy every time I look at my front door. I highly recommend Hawthorne Painting and wouldn't hesitate to hire them again for another project.

review: This is really a small little spot that you might easily walk past and miss if you aren't paying attention but they certainly deserve your attention.  They have some good versions of items that not many other places in the area offer and then they offer some much better versions of items than many other Chinese places seem to push out of their kitchens these days which often seem like recently defrosted factory made food.  This place is similar to the quality and care in their food that Hong Minh and Little Chinatown put out except they are more expensive while also offering items those other establishments don't.    The dumpling selection here definitely has more of a house made and not factory made (then frozen and reheated) texture to it like many of the other Chinese restaurants offer so Dian Xin really seems to be putting out among the best available dumplings in the area now. Their Szechuan chicken was well spiced and was a large serving of mostly meat for the price but I would appreciate more vegetables in the dish.  Their hot tea selection includes items I haven't seen in a long time and it was quite nice to have some golden buckwheat tea again after many years without seeing it as an option around these parts.  The hot and sour soup was well flavored but I noticed there was no wood ear fungus in it which I consider to be pretty essential to a proper and HEALTHY part of any hot and sour soup.    The service was very attentive and kept the drinks refilled along with dealing well with my grumpy dining companion that was just all surly over several of the menu options being sold out already (do come earlier than later as they seem to often sell out of items these days).  The only big area of improvement I would argue for is that they could offer more dishes without pork as quite a large portion of the menu contains pork mixed in without even saying it is in there in true Chinese style but in the USA some more pork free options would be nice and accurately labeling the dishes with pork in them on the menu would be appreciated.    Overall I certainly look forward to more visits here to sample more of the menu.

review: This is a review of my Covid-19 testing experience; I never set foot inside the hospital as all testing is taking place outside, in the driveway off of Sansom Street, just past 10th.   I recently returned from a trip to Mexico. Despite taking proper precautions during my travels, I wanted to get tested for my own peace of mind and to ensure that I would not unknowingly expose anyone if I was an asymptomatic virus carrier. Jefferson's testing site is by appointment only. I had a brief televisit with my primary care doctor, who wrote me a script and recommended that I book my appointment for three days after my return home. I called Jefferson and had no problems booking my desired day and time.   I arrived for my appointment about fifteen minutes early. I was admittedly pretty nervous after watching far too many videos on the Internet! After a few paperwork formalities, a medical professional came over to my car, explained the test and asked if I was ready. I nodded, closed my eyes, and braced myself for torture. Much to my surprise, there was no torture! While I definitely felt the swab inside my nasal canal, it wasn't painful at all, just a little strange. The medic counted down - 5, 4, 3, 2, 1 - and it was over! I couldn't believe how simple it was and would have no hesitation taking the test again in the future, if needed.   Thanks to the medical staff at Jefferson, who were friendly and professional and made this experience as easy as possible!

review: This is a review of a wedding reception that I attended here.  I had never eaten at Muriel's before so when I found out that I would be attending a wedding reception here, I was pretty intrigued and I had no idea what to expect.  When we arrived, the entire group was lead upstairs to the reception area. There were two rooms: one for music and dancing and one for socializing and food. Upon our arrival we immediately dug in. The first thing that I tried was a delicious brisket that was thinly sliced and served with a delicious cream sauce. It was out of this world and I probably would have been happy just eating that.  The next thing I tried were the sweet potatoes with pecans mixed into them and the pecan encrusted drum. Both were AMAZING! They also had salad available, which I didn't get a chance to try, but I did try the cheese and fruit plate! There was an assortment of amazing cheeses accented with strawberries and grapes.   Out of all of this amazing food, my favorite definitely had to be the raw oysters. OH YEAH! This isn't your mama's wedding reception. There were fat ice cold oysters and they were incredible. I had about 6 of them and I honestly could have eaten 12 or more. I like that they had already been cut of their shell, and they were just sitting nicely in there. It made them really easy to eat. And they went really quickly and the staff was quick about getting fresh ones out immediately.  As for the venue itself, the place is just beautiful and very classic New Orleans. We were able to walk out onto the balcony and chat and look out over Jackson Square on this nice evening. The staff was EXTREMELY attentive- as soon as we were finished with a plate, it was taken from away. If I needed something, the staff was immediately on it. I was really impressed.  All in all, my experience here was amazing. I will definitely return to Muriel's for a proper dinner. I would love to spend a birthday or another celebratory occasion here.

review: Plat 99 is the house bar and coffee lounge for the Alexander Hotel. It sits on the second floor overlooking the activity of CityWay.  From early morning until 3, it is a coffee and pastry shop.  Only after three does it begin offering cocktails and the menu items listed on their webpage for customers to get a side dish or something from the kitchen.  Plat 99 has a gorgeous interior which was designed by artist Jorge Pardo who also created all the beautifully shaped and colored lights that hang inside and out into the lobby/stairway that leads up to the lounge.  (Note that elevators are available on the other side of the lobby.)  Inside the lounge, the bar area forms a central rectangle with a number of small tables all around for guests to nestle into.  Note that there are no bar stools and no waitress service (at least during the coffee shop hours.)  The woman behind the counter was very pleasant and was able to converse while getting my Tinker Coffee (ready to drink!) and offered to heat my cranberry muffin for me.  Both were excellent!  The atmosphere was very open with windows all around the lounge.  Quite different than a lot of closed off coffee houses I've been to.    I will definitely have to come back during the evening hours to check out the bar for their house cocktails.  I've had some at their annual Miracle on South Street pop-up and enjoyed those.  Note that there is affordable metered street parking available or a somewhat more expensive parking garage on the north side of the hotel.  Review #3334

review: I like Metairie Cemetery so much that I did my 6th grade social studies project on it. There was a time where I could tell you about the specific types of tombs throughout the cemetery and some of the more notable people buried therein. Alas, that was a long time ago, so now I can only wax poetic about the beauty in the design of these gorgeous resting places.  I've been a regular visitor to Metairie Cemetery throughout my life. We have family buried here and my parents knew and worked with quite a few people who ended up here. The graves are gorgeous and beautifully designed and it seems that each one holds a different story. I think a few of my favorites are the one that is shaped like a pyramid complete with sphinx, the Angel of Grief which is in a locked enclosure, but can be viewed through a window and the grave with the statue of the woman knocking on the door with flowers in her hand. Some of the more notable folks buried here include local legends Mel Ott and Louis Prima.  If I'm being honest, there is something slightly creepy, if not beautiful, about this cemetery. If you are here around sunset you definitely get some chills, especially if you are near the graves with the statues with faces somewhat worn off due to time or other where the heads have been knocked off. It's always pretty quiet here and if you visit, remember that it is a cemetery so be respectful. The style of Metairie Cemetery is something that makes New Orleans unique. I'm glad that it is looked after and taken care of.

review: After attempting to come here 3 other times (the crowds are crazy - especially on weekend mornings because this is a NEW place in an underserved area) our party of 4 got in for brunch on Sunday 3/17 (St. Paddy's Day).  In addition to the full diner menu they had corned beef & cabbage and corned beef omelettes on the menu.  Angela, our over-worked server, was friendly and terrific.  She got all of our orders right and got us in and out in short order.  (The longest part was the wait for a table.)  Aston needs more restaurants, and I surely hope the Aston Diner succeeds. The booths however (as Jamal P. states) are meant for huge fat people.  I weas sitting miles away from the table and you can't move the booths nor the table.  Next time I want to be seated NOT at a booth.  I ordered the $7.95 Aston Special - a breakfast platter with one (big) pancake, 1 slice of french toast (great), 2 sausages and 2 strips of crisp bacon (a little hard).  Very fresh tasting food.  I am pleased and will return. But I'm coming on a Tuesday and not sitting in a booth.

review: If you love simple and delicious Polish food, Pierogi Factory is singing your song.    This tiny four table restaurant is in the Shops at Red Lion on Bustleton Avenue, Northeast Philly.  The menu focuses on the staples: Pierogies, Stuffed Cabbage, Potato Pancakes, Kielbasa and a few other goodies.  Service is casual and sincere.    We ordered their Combo Dinners in order to sample as many of their dishes as possible.  Combo # 1 had two potato pancakes, 3 pierogis of choice (traditional potato and farmer's cheese), and 1 Golabki (stuffed cabbage), with a little container of sour cream ($9.95).  Every element was excellently prepared with taste as good as my grandmother used to make.  The other combo swapped out the potato pancakes for a nice length of smoked (grilled) kielbasa ($10.95).  Also, fantastic.    I was full, but not stuffed, when we finished eating.  We shared a piece of apple cake ($3.00).  It was not as good as granny's, as it lacked the moisture, density and large apple slices she used to fatten up her grandchildren.    Still, a very pleasant surprise on Bustleton. Will definitely visit here again.

review: I love my new shoes. I now have, "Happy Feet".    One of my New Year, New Me Resolutions was to actually use my gym membership. I've been going regularly and doing a minimum of 4-5 miles on the treadmill as my warm up.  Shelby, one of my Shelties has gained weight  and I've also been giving her daily walks around the neighborhood. With these increased activities, I've noticed my feet hurting after each of these activities. I finally realized my inexpensive tennis shoes from the warehouse club were not the right shoes for my fat feet.   As we entered True Runner, we were cheerfully greeted by a sales associate. I quickly told her I needed new shoes for serious walking. She measured my foot and asked me some key questions, before recommending a couple of shoes. The first one she showed me fit fine, but I was not wild about the color scheme. She then showed me a second pair and that color scheme was more to my liking. When I tried that pair on  and walked around I knew they were a winner. The gel in the sole had me walking on air.   When Laura asked me how I liked them I responded, "Much better, then the other." She said, "Really." I asked her why she was surprised. She responded that she wasn't,  she was just amazed how definitive I was in my answer. She said, most people aren't that exact in their answers. My feet felt so good and were so happy, I could not walk out without these shoes.   A great selling point here was the treadmill. They had an actual high end treadmill that they allowed you to use while trying on the shoes. It was like buying a car, you actually got to take them out for a spin ride before buying. This store could be dangerous for me, they had lots of orange items and if you know me well, you know I am a sucker for anything orange.   When I'm ready to kick my program up a notch and become a "True Runner"  they'll be able to help me. They offer a Newbie Running Clinic where I'll be able to get all my questions answered. If you're a runner, I recommend this store.   Big bonus, they have parking to the side of the building so you do not have to worry about that crazy parking lot, that we all dread when going to  Whole Foods or Nordstrom Rack.

review: This is a tough spot to survive for a pizza shop due to its awkward location at the intersection of Buck and Holland Roads. Too many odd angles to negotiate unless your heading south on Holland. Still, it is worth your patience and driving skills to go to Giovanni's if you want a hot lunch or dinner to bring home.   I picked up a Sweet Italian Sausage Sandwich with sauteed onions and green peppers (sauce on the side) today. I called ahead and when I arrived 15 minutes later it was being kept hot on top of the pizza oven, wrapped and ready. It was a jumbo sammy, jammed with enough for at least two people, it's contents cut into bite size pieces of sausage and smaller virginized pepper & onion. The roll was a little soft due to being housed in one sided aluminum paper which trapped all the moisture inside, but even so it was an enjoyable lunch experience.   I managed to consume half before my warning lights alerted me to reaching overfull capacity. Repackaged the rest for home delivery.   Overall, a very good submarine @ just under $10 for a zoftig belly buster.

review: Great Shanghai Chinese Restaurant in the Morrisville Plaza Shopping Center is another primarily take out shop that has been around for many years providing Chinese/American dishes to the neighborhood at affordable prices.  Although there are two tables in the house, the lack of heat in winter makes it obvious they don't expect (want) people to consume their products there.  So, when I ordered sesame chicken and hot/sour soup and indicated I would eat while the food was at its peak heat, they asked me twice if they understood me correctly.  They did, and pulled out a plastic orange tray to deliver the take away containers to me, along with cheap utensils.  They were kind enough to remove the staples used to close the styro lid, so that I could gain prompt access.    My lunch was pretty much okay.    The hot & sour soup was made without MSG, and had a good taste with ample tofu and veggies, and the right amount of vinegar.  The sesame chicken was not over breaded, and the meat could be tasted, and was not lost in the goop.  The quantity was plenty for a midday meal.  The fried rice had been made earlier, had the tint of the bouillon it had been cooked in, and had a fairly fresh texture of being prepared earlier in the day, not yesterday.    Overall, it was what was expected from this type of kitchen, and perhaps, slightly above average based on the soup and rice.    The price/quality ratio was just about right, but having to wear a coat while eating is inhospitable, and knocks it down from average to just below.

review: It would have been helpful to know that white tuna (aka, butterfish) is known for causing digestion issues... especially since I ordered the white tiger roll, loaded with white tuna, about an hour before I had to pedal my company's wares for three hours at an exhibit hall cocktail party nearby.    That information would have been useful.  Never again!  Last week's dinner/gastrointestinal lesson was my second time trying Raw.  My first visit was at least two years ago, during the dreaded Restaurant Week.  On that occasion, my friend and I had to send cocktails back twice and put up with a know-it-all server who insisted that eel could not be removed from (the top of) a specialty roll because "it would compromise the flavors of the roll." Although we did enjoy most of the dishes we ended up ordering that night, the experience as a whole fell flat and I did not return...  Until last week.  I was in the area and had time to kill, so I pulled out my iPhone and utilized my yelp app to find a nearby sushi restaurant.  Raw was very close, and since it had been so long since my last visit, I decided to give it another try.  My server was great, and repeated the specials several times at my request because I couldn't decide.  I usually stick with regular tuna or even yellowtail, but something on this evening told me to go balls to the wall and try something different.  Enter the aforementioned white tiger roll.  In fairness, I enjoyed the roll, although I still preferred the taste of regular tuna to the fattier consistency of white tuna.    The roll, a bowl of miso soup and a cosmo ended up costing a quick forty bucks, including tip.  I wish I could point my finger and blame it on the ambiance, or the location or something... but I can not.  I'm just not all that impressed and I think there is better sushi to be had, in swankier digs, around the city at the same price.

review: I really enjoyed my first meal at V Street. I'm not big on faux meats, so I was excited to see a lot of options that were veggie-based. I ordered the XO broccoli to start. The dish was sort of a salad (served cool, not hot) and had some nice flavors, though at the end of the day it was still broccoli. It did accomplish my goal of starting the meal with something light.  My friend started with the Peruvian fries. I had a bite and they were absolutely delicious. I'd definitely go out of my way for this snack again. My main course was dan dan noodles, which came loaded with tasty mushrooms. The spice level was high but tolerable, and I found this dish every bit as satisfying as other dan dan, even without the pork. V Street nailed the thick, peanut-y sauce.  As a non-vegan, I enjoyed V Street a lot more than Vedge, and found the menu to be more approachable. I definitely see myself going back to try more from the menu (and also revisiting those Peruvian fries and dan dan noodles).

review: I really wanted to LOVE Tir Na Nog and be "pleasantly surprised" by the tricked-out pseudo-Irish-stylized pub grub - but here's what really happened...  I went to Tir Na Nog last night as part of a private dinner party - there were about 14 of us.  We had a semi-open bar for 45 minutes - and beer on tap and house red or white wine.  I had the Pinot Grigio which I did not enjoy.  However, the barkeep (a lovely young lady) and hostess were attentive and very, very hospitable keeping everyone's glasses full.  I shoulda had a pint of Harp or Bass.  Oh well.  Next time.  Then we were ushered into a private dining area.  A choice of soup or Salad (this was - in my opinion) the best part of the meal.  The house salad was EXCELLENT - 4 stars easily - perfectly dressed fresh greens, lots of cukes & carrots and 2 perfect cherry tomatoes.  Accomanied by a basket of fresh warm bread.  I succumbed to the Irish Soda Bread with creamy butter.  Sooooo good!  A friend had the potato parmesan soup which looked awesome (and fattening as hell) and she just LOOOVED it.  But the entree failed me.  We had 4 choices - a burger (looked great), grilled salmon (looked OK - not earth shattering), a big greasy plate of delicious fish and chips (I tasted a friend's fish - which was begging for malt vinegar - a bottle quickly appeared.) - and my entree - the roast chicken.  Or should I say the dessicated chicken?    This chicken was so dry and over cooked it was just not enjoyable.  UGH.  OK - Star off for that.  Dessert redeemed TNN - with a luscious banana split - with warm caramelized banana halves.  We had a lovely time and I will return (and maybe even give 'em 4 stars next time) but no WAY would I order the roast chicken EVER again.  Oh - you should also know that prior to our dinner - a colleague and I sat on the outdoor patio (we had arrive early) and were given water in FILTHY dirty glasses.  The server hastily replaced them - but it skeeved me out quite a bit.  Glassware in general is not well washed here.

review: The Mann Center for the Performing Arts (full moniker) opened in 1976 in West Fairmount Park.  It is one of the finest outdoor music venues in the USA, with room for about 14,000 people, both inside under the roof, and outside on the grass knoll.  There is no question that it brings life to this part of the city, especially at night, when the sound from a loud band or orchestra can be heard well into the surrounding streets of West Philly.   I was there the other night with my teenage son, who was attending his first concert. A right of passage from one generation to the next, I was transporting him to see/listen to Kid Cudi (Scott Ramon Seguro Mescudi), a rap, reggae, original actor and hipster, where I had previously gone to see Stevie Ray Vaughan, Roger Daltry and Robert Cray.  I was happy to be passing the baton. The venue hasn't changed much in the past 40 years.  It is still an awesome place to listen to music, and mix with like-minded heads.  The place was sold out and had the expected carnival atmosphere before, during and after the show.  There was enough haze generated to give everyone within a half mile a contact high.  Everyone inhaled.    The show was great.  Kid Cudi is a first rate musician and showman.  He played for about 90 minutes, despite coming on stage about an hour late.  His band was tight, and all the singers, lights and stagecraft contributed to a first rate experience. Wasn't sure I would like his style, but he was way better in person than listening to him on recordings or watching his videos. He had everyone moving and shouting for more.   Most of the main boulevards in the nearby park were closed to traffic, and it took a while to find our way to the parking area and the main entrance. There was a heavy police presence in the park just in case, but they did not interfere in any way with the happening.   At the end of the evening, my son and his friend were exhausted from all their singing and dancing, not to mention the inebriants in the air. They had a great time, and scored Kid Cudi T-shirts as memorabilia.   Just hope The Mann is around when my grandchildren are ready to boogie!

review: It's become a tradition among some NOLA Yelpers to make every 100th review a "milestone" review. It was tough trying to decide what my 2,000th review should be, but after much consideration, I settled on reviewing this local favorite for this very special review.   I have lived in New Orleans my entire life and I had never set foot in the original Willie Mae's. Oh sure, I had tried their chicken at their short-lived St. Charles Avenue location, but I had a feeling that I hadn't tasted Willie Mae's until I had it here. When I found myself in the neighborhood for work, we saw the line was short so we decided to pop in.  As I said, there was a line at about 11:00 am, but it was short and moved fast and we were inside and seated within about 10 minutes. Once we sat down, out waiter was on top of it- he came right over and handed us menus and took our drink orders. I already knew what I was getting: white meat fried chicken meal with mac and cheese and a side of fried okra. Once we ordered, the food came out fairly quickly. Not shocking, since it seems that they have perfected the fine art of getting people in and out as quickly as possible.  The food looked amazing: big pieces of crispy chicken with creamy mac and cheese and peas on the side. I started with a wing it was really good- nice and juicy with just enough "crunch". I then tore into the breast, which was equally juicy, but sadly, the wet batter was so thick that it wasn't quite cooked all the way through. The chicken was cooked perfectly, but the batter was cakey in some spots. They probably should have left this one in a little longer. The mac and cheese was excellent and the fried okra was plentiful and delicious.  The place itself is small, so that's why there's a line. Also, when we were here, I'm pretty sure that we were the only locals. This place has been Bourdain'd and Zimmern'd to death, which is great for them, but tends to keep some of the locals away and draw in the tourists. And yes Anthony, everyone knows what to order, but there IS a menu. Calm down.  All in all the food was good. Was it the best chicken I've ever had in my life? Am I going to be standing in that super long line at Fried Chicken Fest just to get my fix? Not quite, but there's a charm about this place and it's a definite New Orleans institution that everyone should visit at least once, if for no other reason than to say you tried it. It's a part of New Orleans culture and one of those places that makes our city so special.

review: I wasn't really familiar with this cute little Lakefront spot, but when my dad told me that he wanted to try a new seafood place for his birthday, the good reviews guided me to Sala.  It was around noon when we were here for lunch, and the place was empty except for one other table. The first thing I noticed is how big the restaurant is- it seems like a nice place to celebrate a special occasion and there's a nice "living room" area in the middle where you can just sit and enjoy happy hour drinks.  I decided to start with an order of the calamari. The serving here is huge and it's plenty enough for two people, and it comes atop a mixed salad concoction with a yummy sauce. The batter is light and not overwhelming at all, so you still get the flavor of the dish.  For the entree, my dad and I both got the drum almondine, which is lightly fried and topped with a lemon butter sauce and toasted almonds and is served with a side of brabant potatoes. This dish was outstanding! The fish was full of flavor and perfectly fried and the lemon butter sauce was out-of-this-world decadent. In fact, my dad RAVED about how good it was (he's a pretty hard sell) and said that it's one of the best dishes that he's had in years. I have to agree- you get two big pieces of fish, with a generous serving of potatoes for $23 and it's all cooked to perfection. This dish is a MUST, if you visit.  Our waitress was so sweet and I wish I had gotten her name. She was attentive and knowledgeable of the menu and made sure that we had everything that we needed. Sala is a hidden gem and I'll be back.

review: I first heard about this business through a Yelp event, but because there was so much demand (Yelpers got to actually make their own ice cream!), the line was long and I made a decision to come back on my own to give them a try.  So, after lunch, I decided to try the place for myself.  There are basically eleven "starter" flavor mixes to choose from.  Once you make a selection and pay, one of the staff begins making your ice cream on a frozen metal disc.  I missed the start where the basic ingredients are mixed because I was checking out which of the many toppings I was going to add. (You can select three types of toppings which is included in the price.)  I stepped over to watch the process unfold, then refold.  Basically, the ingredients are continuously mixed and spread thin to freeze them over and over.  Then additional flavors are added based upon your selection.  Once all those have been added, the ice cream is shaped like a large square which is then slowly scraped into a roll shape.  There were five rolls about 3 inches across and they were stacked on their ends inside a paper cup.  Then, your toppings are carefully added (the ends of the rolls are taller than the cup, so they don't want the toppings falling off.)    There are self serve napkins and sturdy spoons which are needed.  The ice cream is very cold and until it warms a bit, can require a bit of pressure from the spoon to get through the rolled ice cream.  Fortunately, the spoon was equal to the challenge and I was able to enjoy my treat.  Be aware that these are full cup servings.  I didn't see any options on the menu board for different sizes.  So, either come with an appetite, or bring a friend who likes the same choices you do!  Good flavor, fun to watch, and lots of options to make the ice cream fit your taste.  Review #1186

review: After seeing a banner posted over the patio facing SR 267 (Quaker Blvd), I was curious if this new restaurant was any good.  So, I decided to catch lunch there last Tuesday.  It's a good thing they have a banner/sign on the back.  Otherwise, I might never have been aware of them.  Located between Hadley and Reeves Rd, I turned east on Hartford Avenue and then north on Cambridge Way to pull into the shopping plaza on the left.  There was plenty of parking out front so I made my way into the restaurant.  There are two main sections:  The dining room with table seating in the middle and booth seating on the sides; The bar which is on the north (right as you enter) that is only about half as big as the dining area (the kitchen fills the other part of the space).  A sign at the entrance listed all the lunch specials of the day. Seems like many of the common items were about $8.  I was greeted promptly and seated at one of the booths.    The interior is clean and bright with a bit of a pattern to the table tops, but otherwise, the place could pass for any standard diner.  No wild colors and images plastered on the walls or chairs.  Just tastefully done.  I was greeted by my waitress and she brought complementary salsa (decanter) and chips with my water.  I found the salsa to be quite good with just a hint of heat, but not enough to alienate most diners.  The chips were fresh and the small decanter allowed me to fill the dipping bowl a few times.  Before I finished my chips, my lunch was served.  I had ordered the Burritos Tipicos with beef tips, in two flour tortillas and topped with burrito salsa.  There was also shredded lettuce, chopped tomatoes, and guacamole salad.  The flavor was really good!  The beef was very tender and moist.  The dish also comes with a chicken option as well.  The portion size was huge, so I made the smart choice (for my waistline) and got a to go box for the second burrito.  (My wife grabbed the box out of the frig and said it was still delicious as she was heading out the door, so it makes for good leftovers!)  Friendly service, short wait times, and good food made for a pleasant dining experience.  Not a lot of atmosphere, but I didn't sit in the bar or on the patio either.  Maybe my next visit will allow me to explore.  Review #3109

review: I have such fond memories of eating at Drago's. My HS banquets were held here.  In fact I had dinner in that same room on Saturday night...definitely not for private parties any more.    The pros:  The chargrilled oysters were tasty and fresh. I sampled the fish special that one of dining companions got and it was delicious. Lots of variety to the seafood dishes. They have a Chandon sparkling split for a glass or so of bubbly.  The cons: They do not take reservations, even for large parties. So my group arrived at 5 pm. We were seated immediately. By the time we left, the hordes has descended. It was craziness. The crabmeat au gratin dip tasted like velveeta.  The weird: Drago's is no longer an inexpensive restaurant and the server was very much...the jokester nephew of the owner style. I found an oyster shell under my chair....remember we were seated at 5; had it been there since lunch?  The verdict: My entree (an fine but not remarkable shrimp & pasta dish) fed me for 2 additional meals since Saturday. I would rather pay less and have an entree that doesn't feed 3.  I wish the meal had been better and that our waiter hadn't disappeared so we could pay the bill and escape the gathering hordes of people.

review: I would said the best Italian restaurant for my list.  Please read on why they did not get 5 stars. Do I come back. Hack yes. Hopefully I can give them a 5 stars next time.   Before you come to this restaurant, you need to know a few thing. 1. Do not just show up. Make a reservation. Even though they said is highly recommended, I said is a must. Almost every day for people just walk in they have to wait for 2.5 hours at dinner time. If you don't have reservation,come at the time they open. 2. Go for the menu items. They are match the value of the food. 3. Be patient. They really don't have much help on the kitchen since it always back up on the order.   Today we show up with reservation and we still have to wait for our table to be ready. Not a long wait. While waiting there is a special of the day on the board for your choices. We have appetizer and pre-meal item that come with the entree. The first course is about 30 minutes. But the entree is about an hour wait. I did ask the waiter why. They have accommodated with addition wine and dessert no charge for our situation.   We begin our appetizer with Vongole Marechiara. It is the baby pasta clams sautéed with garlic, basil, and white wine sauce. The sauce is great. Please ask a loaf of bread to go with it. It is excellent dipping the bread in this sauce. The baby clam is about 25 to 30 count. But they are small portion in the big bowl. They taste very good.   My entree is the special on the board. Pan seared blacken Scottish Salmon on top of roasted slice potato with house cure pork belly. The salmon cook just right and the fish is fresh. The cure pork belly is awesome. It is a bit pricy for this dish. The entree come with the soup or salad of your choice.   The restaurant only have the wine and beer for alcohol. We were accommodated with great dessert for the time lost while waiting. Seem like they have a smaller kitchen. This may be the only area they need to improve. Increase the speed of food preparation or bigger kitchen. Don't let the customer wait.   The dessert is magnificent. They brought out the Tiramisu, Cannoli, Lemon Cake, and pyramid chocolate. It look awesome when they are in one big plate. I applause they accommodated the customer long wait time.

review: And they're off and you're off to a fun afternoon or evening of fun. FPRT is one of the places that I need and want a half star, so I can make this 3.5 Stars.   The best way to describe FPRT is a dive bar with horse races. The facility is old, rundown and in serious need of a renovation. However, that gives it character and adds charm to the gambling experience. There is enough down time between races, to enjoy drinks, visit with other characters and select your next horse to win, place or show.   I would have never thought of going to FPRT if it were not for my friend Norma wanting a day at the racetrack for her birthday. When you get to our ages, we usually have everything we want, so a fun social outing like this makes the best type of gift.   You can sit in the grandstand, or get down and dirty outside right next to the racetrack. We started out in the grandstand, but moved down to trackside and that is when it really got to be a fun time. The regulars, are true characters. I'd love to see a reality showed filmed here, it would be hysterical.   The beer, nachos and other stadium type foods are cheaper then a ballgame. I cannot rate the food, I only enjoyed the Blue Moon beer on draft. My beer was only $4.50 and it was a large glass. The staff behind the betting cages are very helpful to the newbies. I stayed with the same lady and she was amazing. She remembered my bets and would joke with me. I had the luck of a newbie, I won and I lost and when the day was over, I was Even Steven.   I had a fun afternoon, I'll be back with more friends for another fulfilled outing.

review: 4 star food - Excellent and not too greasy. However the icy service I received knocked them down to 3 stars.  I walked in on a Thursday night at around 8:25 PM.  It turns out they close at 9 Anyhow the place was dead-empty - nobody dining in but me and the only other person who came in was a local cop for take out (good sign).  The lady folding napkins when I arrived seemed genuinely miffed that I dained to eat dinner.  Anyhow - I was able to elicit a smile by the end of the night. I ordered Chicken with Broccoli ($9.0) and brown rice (no extra charge - nice!).  I asked for it "light on the sauce, dry" and thus - it was perfect.  Fresh crunchy broccoli that nearly tasted sweet when I bit into it and lots of slices (not slivers) of tender whit meat chicken.  I will return - maybe next time she'll WANT to see me.  Oh and the teapots and silverware were very clean.  As Dan H. mentioned there is a $5 per person lunch, $8.00 per person dinner minimum.

review: Came here for a business Lunch. The Husband's business Lunch, i was just tagging along for the free food. It's been a while since I've visited Casa Tina, and It looks like they are in the midst of a renovation.   The salsa and chips is always Delicious. The food is always fresh and the service is most often with a smile.    I ordered the Enchilada Roja, or Enchilada's with red sauce, it was very tasty, but not at all spicy as the menu said it was - which is good because i was kind of afraid. The husband ordered the Burrito, which was HUGE, but tasty. Our friend, the one doing the business ordered civiche and black bean soup, he said it was delicious.   We even opted for dessert, I got flan and the others split an order of fried plantains ala mode. I wasn't thrilled with the flan, it lacked the caramel sauce it usually comes with, but the fried platains were plentiful and apparently VERY good.  Occasionally (I'm not sure of the timing) They do aerial shows! Catch these if you can, they're REALLY good.

review: Went looking for a place I've never visited, and the Beau and I stumbled upon this spot.    The biggest challenge was finding parking that wouldn't tow us, but we found it at the back, it was crowded and a bit difficult, but we were able to fit into a spot.   Once inside, we noticed how packed they were. We waited just a moment before we were seated, and our waiter came over and took our order.  I placed an order for the French Dip and the Beau got the reuben, both came with fries, and a soup or salad. We chose soups.   We didn't wait very long for the starter, Greek Wedding Soup to come to the table, it was very good, but it was SUCH a big bowl that I knew better than to finish it. review: There is a simple reason almost all the reviews for The Dutch on S. 4th Street are 5 Star. They deserve every star they get!   I am not a regular part of the weekend breakfast/brunch scene in Philly, but given a reason to be in the Pennsport neighborhood early on a Saturday morning, I willing partake of this lovely cottage industry.  The small corner shop is bright and airy, even on an overcast day.  Pale and deeper blues offset the whitewashed walls, giving the feel of happiness and cleanliness.  There are two levels.  Dining room in the front of the house with around 10 small wood top tables, and a step up in the rear with a traditional counter and semi-open kitchen.  The owners are very hands on, supervising, serving, cashiering and hosting.  The "Double Wilkum" hex suits the personality of this place.   We walked in around 8:30 to a half full room.  We were shown to one of the small deuces toward the back of the dining area, and had a fresh large cup of java steaming my glasses in less than a minute.  The menu is short and sweet.  But, don't be misled by its list of offerings that look like any other hash house.  Hidden within the deceptively simply names are the creative energies of these "Dutchmen."    My Huevos Rancheros was not very South of the Border, but certainly tipped their sombrero in homage to the venerable dish.  Rather than tortillas, upon a base of Corn Meal Waffle were placed a shiny Sunny Side Up Egg, melted Cheese,  Fresh Tomato Salsa, Guacamole, Black Beans and well grilled and pressed thick cut Bacon; covered in mild Hollandaise.  Pretty as a picture on the plate, the assemblage had a great taste, if not overwhelmingly Mexi heat.  I never thought of corn and waffles in the same breath, but it worked like a charm.  It held all the component parts together, and sent the meal in an unexpected direction.    My companion's Ham & Eggs with 3 Over Easys, interestingly delicious Hash Browns, and thick sliced Marble Rye, was devoured with little offered to me to taste.  I did manage a couple of sly bites when she went to the WC, and understood why she was not in a particularly sharing mood.    This neighborhood is gentrifying, but still maintains its authentic South Philly personality.  On a less muggy day, sitting at the sidewalk tables would be a nice way to watch this part of the world go by.

We did find my friend's grandparents and I could send him a photo. So he could see the condition of the wall tomb. So that was an achievement. review: Approaching Rozmaryn (Rosemary) Restaurant on a rainy January night takes a bit of courage.  The store front is a rowhouse with a neon "Open" sign in the window and an old unlit sign beneath it.  The front door is open and all you see is a long hallway with dim yellow lighting.  Sketchy characters on the sidewalk make you involuntarily prepare your fight/flight responses.  Be ready for anything...  But, first walk across Olden Avenue to the liquor store to pick up authentic Polish beer to make the experience complete.  In the back of the store is the Polish section.  More sketchy guys standing around - these 'packin' employees watch your every move.  But, the Xywiec Beer is back there in bottles or cans. I pulled out a six pack of glass and brought it to the counter. $10. minimum for credit cards, so I had to pull out my wallet (I really didn't want to do it).  Done. Walked back across the street and up the front steps of 925.  On the first door to the left was the restaurant sign bidding we enter.  What was behind the door?   I went in first.  I was greeted by an apartment converted into a small eatery.  Yellow walls, stained wood trim. Wall sconces, but little other adornment.  No one else in the main dining area.  We stood a moment and waited to see if someone would come out to seat us.  A few long seconds later a woman appeared from the rear with a warm smile and firm voice welcoming us to her shop.  She was the owner, hostess, and chef.  Very big persona.  Lovely, and I immediately relaxed.  At 6:30 we expected other patrons, but we were the first and only folks there all night.  She sat us at a central table for 4, allowing us to spread out.  NFL Playoffs had depleted her clientele, but we were quite happy to have all her attention.    After getting the lay of the land from the gracious Madame, we ordered off the rather small menu, which is in both English and Polish.  The Polish Plate to share as our appetizer.  It consisted of Meat Pierogies, Potato Pancakes, Kielbasa in Yellow Mustard, and Apple Sauce.  The Pierogies were the least enjoyable part of the dish. While the dough was lightly fried and was a good consistency, the meat was too dense and organ-tasting for me. The Potato Pancakes were large and thin, not very oily, and a good mix of potato and flour (to hold them together).  They were crispy on the edges and tasty with a dollop of Apple Sauce to mix a little sweetness with the mild saltiness of the latke. The Kielbasa was excellent.  Scored before grilling to help the heat penetrate and to avoid splitting, the outer skin was just firm enough to hold the link together, but when bitten, it gave way nicely to allow the very tender innards to meet the tongue, disclosing its softness and interesting spice.  It was the surprise star of the plate.  The mustard kicked up the flavor, but did not overwhelm the essence of the sausage.    We had the Stuffed Cabbage and Breaded Chicken Cutlet as our entries.  The Cabbage dish came with Mashed Potato and Cucumber Salad.  The Cabbage was tender and the mix of beef and something else was good, but perhaps a little bland.  It needed something to sweeten it, or at least that was how my Polish-Jewish grandmother prepared them. The potatoes were not hot enough, and seemed to have been plated before visiting the oven. Mild disappointment.  The Cucumber Salad was a cream base and decent.    My Chicken dish was excellent.  The breast was large, with a pleasantly hand dipped breading coating it.  I opted for Mushrooms rather than Tomato Sauce, and was very pleased with the freshness and amount piled on the chicken.  Very tasty and definitely something I would order again.  The mashed were again cool and I left most of them alone.  The Red Beet Salad finished the plate.  Served appropriately cold, it was a nice fit, bringing mild sweetness to the mix of flavors in the breading, chicken, and shrooms.  I was happy.  To complete the repast, we ordered the Blintzes stuffed with Farmer's Cheese, and dusted with Powdered Sugar.  These babies were wonderful.  Perfect crepe wrap, and a whipped sweet cheesy filling.  Light, and a perfect end to the meal with freshly brewed coffee.    This is a one of a kind richly local ethnic urban place that is easy to love.  The entire experience from the sidewalk scene, to the liquor store, to the special charm of the owner/chef, make Rozmaryn worth a visit or two.  When a meal becomes the food for a short story you have found something remarkable.   This was definitely that, and more.

review: FYI:  My rating is based upon the bakery side of the business.  I had already dined at another place before stopping in on Tuesday afternoon, so I didn't have enough room in my stomach to sit down for a full meal.  But one look in the pastry counters (yes, more than one), and I knew I would be kicking myself if I didn't ask for several items to go!  Sure, I spent a while wandering around the seemingly endless nooks and crannies of this place before coming back to place my order.  It seemed everywhere I looked were collections of anything and everything related to German culture.  I also found numerous little niches where tables were occupied by diners....seemed like a full house when I was there.  Anyway, I selected four items and anxiously made my way home and called my wife over to see what I had selected.  Of course, we had to sample each one before putting them away for tomorrow...you know, just to make sure we got to taste them at their freshest!  :)  Our favorite was the Peach Streusel.  The serving was large and had a great balance of bite sized pieces of peach layered over a dough crust with light, but plentiful streusel topping.  Totally delicious....I could see ordering this for a brunch and wowing all my friends!  Another tasty choice was the Cherry Cream Puff.  (It didn't survive until evening!)  My wife doesn't even like cherries, but she ended up snapping up about 2/3's of it! The puff portion was light and flaky and perfectly balanced the whipped cream and cherries inside.  I also liked the Apple with Toasted Almonds.  This roll up had excellent balance in flavors as well.  My only negative on this was that the almonds seemed a bit raw (not enough toasting) and weren't as good when eaten by themselves.  But with the rest of the flavors, they seemed okay.  Finally, our fourth selection was the Raspberry and Blueberry with Hazelnut Buttercream.  This multi-layered cake and fruit paste dessert was topped with colorful buttercream.  Although the presentation looked beautiful, the cake portion seemed a little bit dry.  Of course, when comparing to the wonderful selections mentioned above, any little thing stands out.   I can't wait until tomorrow when I can sample what remains again with a hot cup of coffee!  Review #98

review: I attended a wedding at Jack's Firehouse on Saturday night and I honestly can't think of one thing that would have made it better. The staff at Jack's was on point - everyone I encountered was friendly, professional and helpful.   The ceremony was held on the first floor behind the bar. It was a bit of a tight squeeze and a lot of folks were left standing but having everyone so close together made for an intimate vibe. After the ceremony, cocktails and hors d'oeuvres were served in the bar area and the outdoor space in front and to the side of the restaurant. I saw plenty of interesting looking cocktails making the rounds but a full bar was available as well. Having so many drinks prepared in advance was a great idea - everyone had a drink in hand within minutes after the ceremony and there really wasn't a wait at the bar for the rest of the night.   The passed apps during the cocktail hour were plentiful (and also really tasty) and ran the gamut from bruschetta to steak tips with blue cheese fondue. Meanwhile, chairs from the ceremony were cleared and the area behind the bar became the dance floor.   Upstairs, a buffet-style dinner was served, featuring everything from salads and pastas to fish and carved meats. There was a lot of seating upstairs which fortunately freed up the even better seating downstairs in the outdoor area.   The party was still going strong at 11:30 when I hit the wall and had to turn in for the night, but what a blast. If you're looking to host a wedding at an alternative venue, I'd strongly suggest checking out Jack's.

review: Well, my husband & I finally tried this place - we've driven by a bunch of times but never went.  And we would consider returning (although Shiroi Hana is more convenient for us - and lately I've been really into Vic's.)  The place was nearly empty at 5:30 on a Friday.  The hostess asked if we had a reservation and we told her that we did not.  She made a negative face so I asked her if that was a problem (The place was empty except for one male couple lingering - and they were there before we got there AND after we left.).  She said no and seated us.  I stopped by the sushi bar to bow to the chef and take a peek at the fish.  Looked good.  Chef recommended the Red Snapper and O-Toro.    We started with an order ($3.00) of Pork Wasabi Shumai.  - 2 large shumai.  Tasty and very wasabi-ish.  My husband ordered a bowl of udon (very tasty dashi broth) a spicy tuna roll which he loved, and a negi-hamachi roll which was just OK.  I got a special roll (Jay roll?) with rice "pops" on it - good but I did not care for the spicye-level of the tuna filling.  It was too hot for me.  (And I had asked for it mild.)  I bet if you are a spicy lover you'd like the rolls here.  Tuna was fresh - but not the yellowtail.  Also my $6.00 piece of O-Toro was gristley and GROSS.  What a shame.  Toro should be a mouth-gasm and this was not.  The best sushi I got was the Inari stuffed with chopped tuna (spicy tuna - this time WAS made mild) and garnished with chunks of avocado and a few pine nuts.  The pine nuts really made it so special.  I would DEFINITELY get that again.  For dessert we had the green-tea icecrem filled mochi which was very good.  Oh - and they do NOT make their own tamago - it's frozen - so we did not order any.

review: Sedition is conduct that encourages acts of rebellion against the state. If a failure it is a serious crime; if successful, an act of revolutionary heroism. In times like these that try the souls of patriots, when it is difficult to differentiate between the criminals and the righteous, it is understandable that a subterranean public house would choose "Sedition" as its identity. No doubt the dark bricked, grottoed, underground tavern evokes an epoch when such weighty matters were discussed in hushed tones by serious people.   Chose a side or stand aside, but at least here you can do so with quality drinks and kitchen. We stopped in after visiting Penn Med a few blocks away. The basement felt cool in the dim light of reimagined industrial fixtures. We walked through coved rooms until taking a booth rather far from the bar. Yet, the friendly bartender found us with menus in hand. There were good beer choices, but having to return to see the medical staff after lunch, our libations were strictly water. We ordered the Philbano and Beer Braised Brisket sandwiches, and settled in.   Both were very good, as were the accompanying fries. The "Philly Cubano" was made up of smoked Berkshire pork butt, provolone, peach BBQ sauce and pickled long hots, all stuffed into a fresh Parker House roll. Simply put, it was a great pulled pork sammy. The combination of ingredients played well together and it was fun to identify the flavors as they announced themselves to the tongue.  First rate. The brisket was not quite as entertaining, but was tender and slathered in horseradish and coleslaw between the semi spheres of a brioche bun. Satisfying. Both were substantial enough to bring half home.   Whether you intend on sedition or will wait the next act out from the sidelines, be sure to enjoy life and stop in to Sedition for drinks and grub before deciding.

review: Yum!  Since we didn't have reservations, we were seated in the bar area and our table was...intimate for three, but fun.  The bar is elevated and so you get to look down on all the other patrons and spy on their food.  PLUS we were right across from the meat & cheese curing cabinets...which was a little disturbing for our strict vegetarian.  Northern Italian is not a cuisine you see often in New Orleans as most of the Italian immigrants here were Sicilian.    The food did not disappoint.  We had 8 course amongst the three of us.  The octopus carpaccio (which my friend said was amazing), the bruscetta and a salad.  The mozzarella on the bruschetta was delish and the salad was excellent (arugula, pistachios, blue cheese).  For our entrees we all stuck with pastas; I had the pumpkin stuffed pasta in a browned butter & sage sauce.  I couldn't stop myself from eating and I probably should have. While the large plate did not look huge, it did dash my plans at dessert.  E had the spinach gnocchi which he found very good.  And our friend had the stracci (maybe) which was big broad noodles with chicken livers.  She pronounced it amazing.  E had the rum cake for dessert and our friend had the chocolate/hazelnut pudding. Both were excellent.

review: My experience here was SO disappointing.  I had been waiting for months to go to Kyoto.  I had never been and I had always heard how fabulous it was.  I was pretty excited when I was finally able to make it here for dinner after the St. Patrick's Day parade.  First of all, when we walked in, the first table at which we were seated was located under some stairs.  It was so dark I could barely see my menu and I was with my friend who is 6'5" and he could barely fit.  I would have totally understood if there were no other tables available, but there were, so to be seated under the stairs was not only ridiculous, it was insulting.  In fact, never seat  anyone under there.  EVER.  Remove that table completely.  It's insulting, when you have two dining areas, to ask a paying customer to sit in the "connection" between the two rooms.  When we were reseated in the actual dining room, we ordered some soup, the salmon sashimi, the stella roll and the funky margarita roll, which we had heard were the best special rolls that they had.  The soup was pretty good and it's hard to mess up raw salmon.  The two special rolls, unfortunately, were nothing special.  Sure, they were good, but they didn't seem much bigger than the regular rolls that you would get at any other restaurant.  My friend noted that the rolls were expensive for what you got and the tables were really close together.  The latter I can understand, because the place is small, but when I order a special roll and I pay "special roll" prices, I expect it to be a good size and something, well...special.  I might go back to Kyoto and give it another try, but I think I will stick to my favorite sushi place, Hana, where the special rolls are huge and good and definitely worth the money.

review: Authentic Ethnic Cuisine #49. Southeast Asia Cuisine. Malaysia and Burmese.   I miss my home street vendor food. I found it here at one of the Indianapolis restaurants. A great Hokien Mee is not easy to find. This may be the only one I can find outside of Malaysia. Mee is in Malay. It mean noodle.   I got the dry wonton mee. Most wonton noodle are wet with a lot of soup. Only southeast Asian prepare it dry. The Mee is egg thin noodle cook and mixed with dark sweet soy sauce and sesame oil. They add BBQ pork and wonton. It is sell in Malaysia street food by Chinese descendent. It is very good here. We also got the wet Pan Mee hand made noodle with Burmese touch. They add some dry fried pork fat on top. Very good.   Lastly is the Malay rice goreng. This is fried rice with Malay shrimp paste. Spicy. Very delicious. I have not seen this dish sold elsewhere in the United state. Our visit here is definitely the best. Love it.

review: Far away from the majesty that is some of the "nicer" places of rest in New Orleans, lies Holt Cemetery.  A bit of history: Holt is where the poor of the city were (and in some cases still are) buried.  There aren't many (if any) above ground tombs and Holt remains one of the exclusively "in ground" burial sites in the city.    Walking through the grounds, you are immediately overwhelmed with sadness, mainly because the graves themselves are mostly handmade, falling apart and old.  You get a  personal and intimate feeling when you are looking at them.  Dates are handwritten and headstones are made out of various household materials such as plywood and even plastic.  It's a real testament to all the types of people that live within our city.  The fact that you can walk a few blocks and see some of the most gorgeous places of rest you will ever see and then come here and see the opposite, really speaks to you.

review: If your sweet tooth is acting up while you're in Alton, you need to head over to LuciAnna's Pastries. If you cannot find something in her pastry case to satisfy your sweet craving, that is on you. I was amazed at her variety of sweetness and thrilled that she had one of my favorite pies.   After a fabulous lunch up the street at, Brown Bag Bistro, my cousin and her friend wanted dessert so we headed up Broadway to LuciAnna's. LP just recently moved to this new location and the ladies wanted to check it out. I just wanted something sweet, my sweet tooth was aching big time. From what I was told, this new location is more spacious and inviting to the patron that wants to linger and enjoy their treat with a cup of coffee.   I have two favorite pies. One is, Traditional Pecan Pie and the other is, Chocolate Pecan Pie. The day I visited, LP had  decadent offering of the later. The precision positioning of the pecans on top of the chocolate, blew my mind. It truly was picture perfect and so was the rich chocolate flavor.   My cousin is a fan of Tiramisu and could not resist enjoying one of the thick slices on display. She said it was moist, extremely flavorful and a perfect accompaniment to her cup of black coffee. Her friend ordered the Chocolate Mousse Cheesecake. She made it to the table before the rest of us and started eating, so there is no picture of her delightful and delicious dessert. My cousin, informed her when dining with a seasoned Yelper like me, she has to wait for pictures to be taken before eating. Lesson learned. Next time she joins us, I may still give her a kind little reminder - LOL.   Again, if in Alton and you're craving pastries from a French trained chef, check out LuciAnna's. You'll be glad that you did. It's also a great intimate tea room to meet up with friends for a gab-fest.   I'll be back? - When in Alton do as the locals do - yes.   When: April 17, 2018 Why: Dessert
