They also have a sandwich of the day and a smattering of appetizers including a cheese tray.  The array of beverages is impressive. There are beers, wine, & cocktails.  There were Kalita and Carafe coffees, Kaija teas. I wasn't familiar with all the varieties, so I opted for the Cinnamon Plum tea.  After paying, I took my croissant to one of the window tables and waited for my tea to brew.    There was light conversation in the place, otherwise it was generally quiet with the exception of the service taking place behind the counter.  I devoured my croissant too quickly so that it was gone before my clear pot of tea arrived.  It had a bright plum color and had a pleasant fragrance.  The plum was probably a bit more dominant than the cinnamon flavor, but it was quite enjoyable.  I wasn't sure about bussing, so I took my mini tray with the finished pot and cup to the counter when finished.  I think they are still catching up with being a newly opened business.  The menu doesn't appear on their website (I've included photos of what it was during my visit.)  I would also like to see them develop a couple staple sandwich options so that visitors could plan on having lunch there instead of arriving and deciding they may not like the single daily option.  The staff were friendly and did a good job of clearing used dishes and would have cleared my dishes when I left, but I don't like leaving my used dishes on the table..with limited seating, I want to make sure the next customer can find a spot.  They also brought out the tea as soon as it had finished brewing.  I like that they delivered it without calling out my name or a number.  (That's a perk of being small!)  Seems like a nice place to stop by for a beverage and something light to go with it.  Review #2296

review: Pura Vida (Good Life) is a new Costa Rican casa y taberna on Cummings Avenue in old Chambersburg, Trenton, NJ.  A lot of effort has been put into refinishing the outside in stone, while retaining the mid-Twentieth Century dark wood tones of the long bar and dining areas.  The place feels cool and comforting, with HDTVs in every corner playing Latin music videos that most of the customers can sing along with.    My server, Arlene, was smoothly bilingual as she welcomed me and brought me a menu. A picture of grace and beauty.  The food offerings were diverse, but focused primarily on the native cuisine of this Central American nation.  I ordered the "Sandwich Pura Vida" with Chicken, and a fresh Bastida Mora (Raspberry shake).  When it arrived, it was in the form of a Panini, with scorch marks top and bottom, and compressed down with lettuce and tomato showing from the edges.    After squirting on a little mayo from the table rockets, I clamped down for a big bite.  The juicy contents were hot and flavorful, although the chicken was slightly overcooked and dry.  Still, the overall impression was of a zesty, filling torta, well worth the $7 tag.  The accompanying French Fries were crispy and nicely spiced.  The Raspberry frappe was cool, tart, delicious, and made from real berries (not a mix).    I enjoyed my visit to Pura Vida, and it was obvious that the other clientele felt the same, as most were there engaged in conversation long after their meals were done.  This resto joins a growing community of casas Latinas taking root in the capital city; each distinct, yet providing a broad palette of color and exotic rhythms to the streets of Trenton.

review: Hummm I've been going to this place a long time now.  I used to really enjoy the place in a prior incarnation when it was basically just a plate lunch type place with really great fresh veggies (but it was a bit on the dirty side).  When the place changed owners a little bit before Katrina they went for a much more upscale dining experience and it took them awhile, and going through some other owners, to find exactly what they needed to do but they have finally hit a good stride (I'm still not sure about that giant frying pan they installed outside).  This place has a great brunch, lunch and dinner but it does get crowded and the small space generally requires making reservations.  The ambiance is often ruined when they turn up the music way too loud.  They have also brought in the silly small and large plate trend (I look forward to seeing that trend end) and I would generally avoid the small plates and stick with the large plates.  It can sometimes be a nice change of pace from some of the other better known restaurants.

Cons are that their pantry and household items are limited to a couple different brands. Some products I do like, but I often have to do a Target run for things where I have a brand preference. In terms of the basics, Sprouts covers us pretty well and I am so happy to have them nearby.

review: Outstanding!  Service, food and ambiance are all 5 Stars in my opinion. I was totally blown away on my recent visit. I cannot wait to go back. If I still lived in the STL metro area, I would be a regular here.   I was in the big city to run errands and have lunch with a friend. The original restaurant I wanted to dine at, was packed and we couldn't get a table. My friend recommended, Perennial on Lockwood and I am so glad that she did. Both of us were impressed and luck her, she has already returned for a repeat visit.   Instead of a table, we opted for the bar and Carson the bartender was a delight. He was friendly, a skilled mixologist and spoke professionally about the menu items we asked about. He described them so fluently, we could not resist ordering them.   Starting out we ordered some liquid refreshment. I enjoyed the, Fall Old Fashioned and my friend enjoyed one of their many craft beers. The FOF was made with; rye, spiced apple cider, big o walnut and angostura bitters. It was the perfect welcoming to the autumn season.   To accompany our first adult beverages we enjoyed an order of their house made, Onion Rings. They were the perfect size. Not super large and not to small, as Goldielocks would say, "They were, just right." The light crisp battering is what made them, the perfect starter to our lunch.   When our glasses got empty and it was time to fill them up again, my friend ordered a couple of their 5 oz beers (sorry, forgot to capture a photo) which was smart. It was a great way to sample multiple brews. I on the other hand, switched to the, House G+T. Once Carson explained and told me how he enjoyed the dry-hopped brokers gin, I was sold. It was so refreshing, I could enjoy this cocktail year round.   For our entree, we decided to split, Claire's Grilled Cheese. I have no idea who Claire is, but she makes on hell of a grilled cheese. It was delicious, but next time I will add bacon and take it to the next level. The fries that came with the sammie, were some of the best I have had in a while. They reminded me of the Shoestring fries you use to get at Steak-n-Shake (when they were good). The fries were super crisp and seasoned perfectly with both salt and pepper. To our surprise, Carson and the kitchen split our order on to two plates without us requesting. That is outstanding customer service.   Other things that always make me happy when dining at a bar, is outlets under the bar for charging electrical devices. I was surprised they didn't have hooks for purses and jackets, but I'll take outlets by themselves. I also, am a big fan of linen napkins over paper. Linen just makes dining better.   If you have not been to, Perennial on Lockwood, I insist you go immediately.   When: October 28, 2021 Why: Lunch with a friend

review: I really liked my first lunch at Mission Taqueria, and am excited to go back for dinner and margaritas. We started with the guacamole, which was a healthy portion and served up a nice kick with chunks of jalapeño. The tortilla chips were thin and crispy. We asked for a side of salsa and were later charged $6 unexpectedly - this was removed from our check but I have noticed in the meantime that there is a salsa section on the menu that I somehow missed. To me, guac without salsa is peanut butter without jelly so this combo will sadly set me back mucho dolares in the future.   My salad choice was the romaine and bean, to which I made a couple modifications (no cheese, vinaigrette instead of creamy dressing). I also added shrimp. This salad was filling and delicious and the shrimp were really nicely seasoned. Would order again. My dining companion's kale salad looked solid.   We were treated to a couple fresh juices on the house and I loved the light and refreshing red pepper drink I received. It was just a touch sweet which was perfect for me. Our server, Zareen, was a doll.   Can't wait for the visit numero dos!

review: It had been almost 10 years since I went to Bayona.  I just don't get to the FQ fancy restaurants that often...typical local, I know.    I had a lovely lavender cocktail while we waited for our reserved cocktail - it was made with violet, elderflower liquer and bubbly.  So yummy I had another.  My 1st course was a special of crawfish pie; while it was fine, it was nothing super special and honestly, I've had better at festivals.  My main course was amazing though; I had the pepper encrusted tuna and it was cooked perfectly and the green peppercorns elevated it above the usual.  My dinner companions had the lamb, hangar steak, and fish.  Everyone agreed that the food was great.  We also sampled three desserts: a basic, but good creme brule, the strawberry pistachio bombe which was light and airy and not at all what I expected, and one of the daily sorbets but I can't remember the flavor.

review: It's great to have a high end Napolitan pizza house in Newtown!  It's even better that the enterprise is owned by Pasquale and Anna, the proprietors of Osteria Vecchia, the excellent casa Italiana right down the street. This shop is for the daughter and son-in-law.  Thus, begin empires.   The building is on the site of the former Minuteman Press.  That old structure was taken down to the foundation, and a new Euro-Country Casual establishment arose.  Attention to detail is obvious, as the space is beautiful, with quality stone, wood, glass and a "just off the boat" wood burning hive oven covered in red glazed tile and contrasting white ceramic lettering that shouts, "Pasquale & Anna/Acqua e Farina!"    We were greeted by Sal, the maestro de la casa, who sat my son and I at the corner table where we could see the whole operation.  We ordered a Siciliana pie, and as we waited, other servers brought thin slices of red sauced bread, and a small plate of Brussel sprouts that were soft and delicious from their time swimming in olive oil and spices.  I was even offered a glass of red wine on the house. Very cool touch!  The pie arrived with steam shimmering above it, on a large white platter.  It was cut in quarters, and covered in mozza, afterburn peccorino and chunks of eggplant.  Truly, a work of art with the bubbled crust and scorched undercarriage.  The special deal with these ovens is that they hold extremely high heat, such that the raw pie is placed in the oven for less than three minutes, while baking everything quickly and capturing all the flavor of the ingredients before they burn off and escape. The result is a wonderfully textured and tasty crust that is flavored by the ingredients you choose.  It is all about the dough (thus, the name, Water & Flour), and secondarily about the toppings.  Quite different than the better known pizza experience provided by most joints.   So it was here. A beauty to behold, and a pleasure to consume.  Of course, there is a downside to this approach to baking.  While the crust is excellent, the more ingredients you put on top, the wetter the center of the pie will be on the plate, because it is not possible to fully cook the veggies and meats in such a short time, and as a result of the lack of evaporation in the oven, the finished product will be softer that normal, and the drip from the collected moisture under the hood will be noticeable, and require care to avoid making a mess.   The secret is to order a simple pie with minimal topside accessories, so that the crust, cheese and sauce have the maximum opportunity to vent off the moisture.  This provides a drier bottom and optimal crustiness.   Dining at Acqua & Farina is very different than eating at pizza parlors.  It is designed as a feast for the senses.  There are more moving parts, and the resulting cost enhancement is noticeable. There is a time when "two slices and a soda," is what you want, but there are also times when although you yearn for pizza, you want a more rousing experience.    At those moments, Acqua e Farina will be calling your name.

review: Literally right down the street from my house, it was formally known as the Tarpon bar and grill.   They start the service off with little pastries - which are quite tasty. The service can be hit or miss. When they first opened they had nice, fresh flowers. Now they have cheap looking silk flowers on the tables.   I've seen service be spot on, and I've had the service go t*ts up.  Usually it's just fine.  The place is ALWAYS busy. Take today, we stopped in, but just as we arrived, the kitchen told the waitstaff that the people ordering then would be waiting AT LEAST a half hour due to how many folks had recently arrived.   My favorite is their fried chicken salad. The chicken breast is light and crispy, the greens are always fresh and tasty. my husband likes the Meatloaf, for me it has a slightly sweet taste and I don't like sweet meat.

review: This is a decent TexMex place with one of the larger menus in the area.  The interior is nicer than you might expect from the outside and its often quite crowded.  You get two dips brought out with your complimentary chips and its good to have the selection.  They have some combo platters that let you sample a good range of their offerings.  Nothing is really great here and all the sauces seem to end up tasting very similar with most things being covered in gooey melted cheese.  The service is usually adequate to a bit slower to get drink refills with larger groups.  You get what you pay for here and the combo plates will definitely leave you full. review: On an early summer evening with a nice breeze, we brought our friends with us for their first visit to Mama's.  We opted for seating in the beautiful shaded garden on the south side of the restaurant.  The garden is filled with reddish orange table umbrellas, statues, and a gazebo.  Frank Sinatra music was playing in the background but never interfered with conversation.    After a round of cocktails/wine and a bread course, we decided to try sharing a couple of the appetizers.  The Sicilian Asparagus patties were roughly shaped like hamburgers, but were filled with a wonderful blend of flavors:  grilled diced aspargus, egg, parmesan, and bread crumbs.  These were topped with a lemon aioli and marinated diced tomatoes.    We also ordered the Fried Fresh Mozzarella which is a ball of cheese stuffed prosciutto and crusted with breadcrumbs before frying.  It comes served atop a balsamic glaze and marinated tomatoes.  Not as complex a flavor as the patties, but still very tasty!  Not to be outdone, our entrees were delicious too!  I selected the tilapia with angel hair pasta.  The fish is breaded with chopped walnuts and herbs and drizzled with blackberry basil sauce (asparagus spears on the side.)  The savory combo of nuts and berries are fantastic with the whitefish.  Highly recommended.  My wife opted for the Chicken Picatta with angel hair pasta.  This comes with the standard lemon and olive oil sauce with capers.  She needed a to go box.  Our guests ordered the Clams with mushrooms over linguine sauteed in butter with herbs, parmesan and a splash of Crown Royal.  Veal Marsala with angel hair pasta was sauteed with prosciutto, fontina cheese, and mushrooms and drew great compliments about how generous the cut of veal was as well as the flavor.  For desserts, the guys ordered the Tiramasu (moist and tasty without the harsh alcohol taste) and the ladies went with the creme brulee.  Nice sugar crust with large berries on top also drew favorable comments.  If you plan to go to Mama's, know that there is limited parking in a lot on the south side of the building.  Early is better than later in the evening if you want to reduce your wait times and weekdays are better than weekends.    There is indoor seating as well, but for us, the indoor dining seems a bit darkly lit.  So, we always time our visits to the summer, watching for days when it won't be too hot and with little chance of rain.  If you are flexible in your schedule, you can have an amazing evening of food and conversation.  Review #337

review: First visit was made ahead of time through the nurses at my Mom's rehab center. It was made more than a week a head of time.  When we arrived on the appointed day, there is a notice that our appointed doctor was not available, and that we'd be seeing one of his PA's. If this was an issue you could re-schedule.  Where's the courtesy in letting your clients know ahead of time? Their time is valuable too.  (This kind of thing is repeated frequently, sadly)  When we were finally called back into our room - it was more than a half hour later. This is after we were a half hour early. So by now we're here an hour.  Once in the room, the PA took the info from my mom, and made sure she'd get an Xray to see how the knee was healing. To his credit and the Xray tech's as well, they were both efficient and did their job without hesitation.   After at least 45 minutes, without anything to read in the office, and the ONLY THING in the very cramped lobby being male oriented magazines such as Golf, NBA or industry magazines, we were finally seen by one of the Residents. She was awesome and personable and the whole reason that this office gets a 2nd star.   We got our orders, got the approval to drive and to come back in 2 weeks, and while I won't be able to go back with my mom for the 2nd visit, I do hope they actually read these reviews and take into consideration how they're perceived. While I didn't have trouble with their staff, it's clear there's an issue.   My issue is that they lack the courtesy of notifying their patients about delays or even if the doctor that the patients are supposed to see isn't even going to be there and leave it on the patient-who's already made the trek to the office to either deal with it or re-schedule out at another time which is not at all good for anyone. That they are slow and don't really seem to give any care to the cost in time and comfort once the patient is in their office. It shows an over all lack of concern for anything but the all mighty dollar.

review: It really saddens me to write an update like this. I went in this evening because I've been having trouble with my phone ever since there was an Android update 2 days ago. Since it went into effect, my phone fights powering on. If it DOES power on, it doesn't stay on for long. Essentially it's become absolutely useless.   I looked up on line how to do a hard re-boot, but the phone wouldn't get to the code screen. It was being obstinate and simply refused. It would come up to the actual usage screen, but then in a short matter of time.. go away once more.  It was frustrating to say the least.  In the past, I've been able to go to the stores and one of the people working there either knew of a fix or knew someone who could help me. NOT TONIGHT.  I walked in at 8pm, an hour before closing, and got Shae, a bespectacled, pinup banged young lady with a very blasè attitude. "How may I help you" she asked as we looked around.  So I came over to where she was.  As I settled into what was wrong, I explained the situation, that I -COULD NOT- get to the hard re-boot screen, and I needed help because of the issue with the recent update. She was NOT actively listening.   She took the phone, turned it over in her hand, looked at it as if it were a piece of offal and then set it on the counter, she asked my name, asked for my phone number and ID to make sure that it cleared and then she scanned my account. "Well You don't have insurance on the phone." Ok.. what?  I've had insurance on the phones - all of them since I've been with T-mobile. I also had just been here recently to check on something and KNEW that I had insurance, so when I was told this, I took exception. "I pay for it." So she looked deeper. "You have it on XXXX, But not this number." Uh huh.. My husband came over to find out what she was saying. He got a touch heated, "So what your saying is that We don't have insurance on the phone, even though I know we pay for it?" She looked at him and said, "That's not what I said." (Actually it is just what you said.) And so she looked a little deeper and Guess what? We have insurance on ALL THREE LINES!    "Well, your choice is you can Pay off the phone or you can invoke the insurance but your deductible is $175."  Wait, wait wait.. You're expecting me to pay off a phone that's busted due to NO FAULT Of my own, due to a softwear push?  "Well, there's nothing that I can do, I'm not allowed to take back phones that aren't in working order."  I didn't ask once to have the phone taken back. I had asked for HELP. To see if they could get the phone back to the hard reset screen.  This is when she told me what she "thought" she heard. Clearly the girl didn't care, didn't want to know how she could truly help.   She simply wanted us out of there. She had the flat, monotone tone of boredom. We weren't buying anything and all we were doing was taking up her time now, and clearly, she'd screwed up, and she wasn't going to take any responsibility for it. There was no apology for the misinformation. No, "I'm sorry, I read that wrong." Only an "I'm just reading what I see on your profile." Really? I suggest a remedial reading course.     So now, I have a conundrum: I have a phone, with a $400.00 balance. I can pay it off. I can invoke my insurance (Though I'm not sure why, since NOTHING I DID effected the phone) and get a new one. OR I can call the customer service in the morning  and talk with them to see what will happen. Since frankly, I'm a little underwhelmed by the level of non "Customer service" I've received.  Do I want to continue this 10 year+ relationship? In the past they've done right, but this one employee has put a dark coloration over my eyes. I know that this branch won't see much of me from now on. I don't trust the competency of their employees.

review: Victory wasn't too bad, but after waiting a while to check this place out, I was left unimpressed.  Victory is really small and is really a bit of a dive in nice clothing.  I can picture coming here on a nice night out, but on the night I was here, it just felt like your average run of the mill bar.  When we received our drinks, the order was messed up not once but twice.  I understand that it was our waitresses first time ever waiting tables (that's what she told us), but on a busy Friday night, the wait staff should really know what they are doing and management should maybe not put the new girl on the floor.  Would I go back?  Yeah, if I was in the area, but I wouldn't really go out of my way.

review: The Indiana Medical History Museum is a worthwhile field trip for anyone interested in history, medicine, psychiatry, and, to some extent, the macabre.  On the site of what used to be an 160 acre campus that housed 2000 patients with a variety of "mental illness", very few of the buildings escaped the wrecking ball.  Now, the tour concentrates on the Pathology Building which was the center for instruction as well as supporting the testing and autopsy of the patients on campus.      Tours start hourly.  Because there is limited volunteer staff available, the doors are locked between tours. So plan on arriving a few minutes before the start of each hour or you will have to wait outside.  I am not sure if they can take credit cards, so plan on having $10 per adult on your tour.  Know that this isn't something for juveniles since most items are not to be handled.  Cameras are welcome, but the tour guide will tell you about places where cameras are not allowed due to privacy of the former patients' records.    After a brief wait, our group proceeded into the Amphitheater.  This large room served as both a lecture hall and taught through the autopsies performed in the spot where the lecturer would stand.  Students from the Indiana Medical College and from the Central College of Physicians and Surgeons received instruction.  In 1907, these two schools merged with the Ft Wayne College of Medicine and the IU School of Medicine.  By 1910, the autopsies were no longer conducted in the large room since the spread of tuberculosis affected nearly all of the physicians doing the autopsies and contaminated those who sat close to the dissection table.      Of interest in the Amphitheater is the original ice fed water fountain so that the lecturers would be able to get a drink.  Note that students were not allowed to have a drink from the fountain.  A large block of ice was loaded into a cabinet on the back side of the wall and as it melted, made fresh water available in the lecture room.    The next stop on the tour led to the smaller autopsy room.  A smaller room at the entrance held a "body cooler" while the surgeon prepared for the autopsy.  The larger room was sparse for easier cleanup and contained a metal table, a floor drain, weight scales, and a speaking tube where the surgeon performing the autopsy could speak into and have another surgeon on the floor above transcribe the notes.  Each autopsy had four pages of documentation per corpse.    The autopsy room has become a bit of a storage room now.  In there now, you will find donated equipment like an iron lung for youths, an old wooden phyician's chair, assorted wheel chairs of many years, and an odd collection of items that children/people had swallowed and had to have surgery to remove.  In the drawer we viewed, there were mostly an array of buttons and safety pins.  Other drawers had a collection of just about anything small enough to be swallowed.     The next room was the Anatomical Museum where a number of glass jars housed sections of brain traumas and abmormalities.  We were given time to wander through the exhibits and ask questions.  Of note was a "Brain-Slicing Machine".  Wow!  Another point of interest were a student's project of removing an actual nerve system from the spinal cord down to the fingers.  At first, it looked like a sideways tree, but upon closer examination, I could see it was real and had small labels identifying where the nerve sensations would originate.      The tour advanced more quickly through the remaining rooms.  On the rest of the first floor, there was a Chemical Storage Room, a Bacteriology Laboratory, and a reception area. The story of how syphilis was treated before the discovery of penicillin was discussed.  Syphilis' third stage could lead to insanity, so there were many patients on campus who were there due to this disease. Tests were developed there to help physicians identify the disease.  Early treatments included giving Mercury to patients.  That was replaced by Arsenic!  One of the last treatments before  the availability of penicillin was to infect the patients with malaria where the extreme fever would kill off the STD in about 30% of the patients.      The upstairs (sorry, no elevators available) houses the library, Histology Laboratory (microscopic tissue study), Clinical Chemistry lab, Photography lab, and patient records (where the autopsies were recorded from dictation below.)  In these rooms you will hear stories about advances in patient care and perception.  Mental patients were often shackled or kept drunk in the early days of treatment in order to manage their behavior.  Eventually, knowledge and acceptance that these illnesses could be treated and that patients should not lose their dignity and rights as humans prevailed.    The tour lasted about an hour.  In the spring, the tour expands to include the former morgue (repurposed as a 1950's doctor's office) and an herbal garden.  Review #212

review: Although Ginger Wok in the shopping center anchored by McCaffrey's Supermarket in Lower Makefield, PA, is oddly named given its decor and menu, it is an attractive modern Asian house with a dual identity. Operated by Chinese folk, it offers Japanese sushi and Chinese American standards in a room that feels much more oriented toward raw fish. A lot of money was spent on dark slate floors, white wavy walls, nautical wallpaper, and subtle lighting. No denying the place is beautiful. I was pleasantly surprised by how good it looked.   I was there to try their Chinese lunch menu, and was not disappointed. For $6.50, all the usual suspects were available with soup or eggroll and fried/white rice. While most deliver such deals in takeout packaging or cheapo plates, my meal arrived on a strong white sculpted platter and metal flatware. The black tea (+$1.50) came in a ceramic mug and with strong flavor.   The General's Chicken was well prepared (although a lighter coating would make it better), with a legit semi-hot amber sauce complete with small Szechuan chilies. The fried rice was copious, but could have been warmer. The wonton soup had a good light broth, with average wontons. Service was friendly and timely.   I walked out $10 lighter, but quite satisfied with my Friday afternoon meal.   PRO TIP - Walk to the back of the house to see the sushi bar and fish tanks, the second of which has a few Gar in the crystal tank. Exquisite fish.

review: It pains me to remember the recently completed dinner at Taco Suave.  Such high expectations after reading the other reviews.  Such auspicious beginnings. Such a sudden and disappointing finale.  We walked in to this tiny strip mall corner restaurant. About a dozen tables with white table clothes.  I was thinking that in my experience, the hole in the wall Mexican joints were always the best.  At least, that had been true in Arizona, New Mexico, Colorado and even SoCal.    We sat and ordered the Agua de Pina (Pineapple Water), which was a first and a pleasant drink of diluted pineapple juice whipped to a froth.  Really good! I was getting more excited as I imagined we had just discovered the Fountain of Youth drink right here in Warrington.  Then the homemade Chips and Fresh Salsa came out. Heavy crunchy mild oily sensation with a mild Mexi flavor, and a Tomato, Cilantro Salsa with a sweetness equal to the chili's heat.  Loved it.   Encouraged and feeling adventurous by the fun of the apps and drink, I went for the Pollo Dorado (Golden Fried Chicken), the most expensive item on the menu.  Visions of plump chicken breast with a wonderful fruity sauce danced in my head. My friends had a Burrito de Carne Asada, and a Taco con Queso.    What was placed before me was instead three over cooked deep fried drumsticks with an oil soaked brown coating that tasted primarily of salt.  My physical reaction to eating this was matched by the instantly deflated sense of gluttony so rudely assaulted and kicked to the curb.  I kept eating hoping for a secondary burst of flavor to save this.  It did not come. I passed around the chicken and the reaction was universal. Bad.   The Burrito de Carne Asada was large and full of bits of beef and cheese, but way too mild, and a bit too fatty.  It was left one third eaten.  The Taco con Queso presented well, but was practically tasteless.  We liberally added hot salsa to throw them life preservers, but we could not save them.  The dinner was a victim of drowning.   We will not be back.  I wish I had a different review to write about Taco Suave, but true to the Yelpers Creed, I cannot hide from the bitter taste of a disappointing meal.    Our server, Mirna, was great!

review: It's been almost 8 years since I posted my first review for this USPS and my opinion hasn't changed. I'll admit, I may be a little biased since it is at the beginning of my street.   When you live this close to a PO, it does make life easier. It is so easy to buy unique stamps, ship packages and mail those thank-you notes your mother taught you to write. If I walk out my front door and see a full parking lot, I go back inside my house and wait until the lot is emptier. Yes, that is one of the perks of living close. I watch the lot and I never have to wait.   The staff here on average is fairly friendly. Like most postal workers and DVM workers, they don't move real fast, but they do complete their task efficiently.

review: 4 for our service (Hailey) and 3 for the food. Cooperage is a soul-ish/southern American Whiskey Bar - with a decent selection of wines as well.  A good friend and I dined here on Friday night.  We made a reservation and sat inside, although the weather was perfect for outdoor as well.  The house Lynchberg Lemonade looked tempting, but my companion opted for a mojito - which he enjoyed.  I had a bunch of Arnold Palmers. (Being a HARD CORE drinker - not!!!)  We both had salads.  My friend's duck pastrami salad was good but a little light on the duck.  My Southern Chopped salad was excellent - and to my surprised I even liked the fried okra.  Once again proof that if you fry something, people will eat it.  I ordered shrimp on top of it- and for some reason I did not catch that they were to be"blackened" shrimp.  It was a shame, too - as they were GORGEOUS big shrimp (4 of them) but so spicy I could not eat them.  Hailey took them off our bill.  So anyhow - we had an enjoyable time at Cooperage. Food was solid 3 stars. Not mind blowing - but really tasty for bar food.

review: What brought us all the way to Kenner, was the promise of cheap crawfish. I had been doing my due diligence in researching what places had the cheapest crawfish in town and at $2.99/lb, this place was the big winner. I had also had it on my list because I wanted to try one of their Crabby Mary's.  We were here on a Saturday night and there was a good size crowd at 7. We decided to start with some fried pickles, just because we both like them and we wanted something to munch on. We then got the boiled crawfish with sausage and potatoes and I got my Crabby Mary.  The crawfish was pretty close to perfect: they were a good size (bigger than I had had at a previous spot) and while they could have been a tad spicier, they had a good flavor. The sausage also could have been spicier, but I enjoyed it as well. My Crabby Mary was pretty good. What it is is a bloody Mary topped with a fried soft shell crab, two fried shrimp and two hush puppies, all for $20. Honestly, as good as it was, I probably wouldn't rush to get it again. My suggestion would be- order this for lunch with a side and call it a day. I'm not sure if it was worth the $20.  Our waitress was extremely nice and went above and beyond, especially when we thought we had a "sausage emergency" (we thought they had forgotten the sausage, so our waitress brought us more). I would love to go back and see what else they have to offer and I will probably be back for some more crawfish before the end of the season.

review: With the challenge of construction, one way streets, and interstates making this location a difficult space to get to for those who aren't familiar with 11th and College, take solace knowing that the food and service is worth the effort!  Located in the former site of R2Go, there is free street parking along 11th though it does get a little crowded quickly.  Just be sure to look it up on your GPS before you go and you should be okay!  Although there is a door on the southwest corner, they are directing everyone to go through the large double doors on the west side of the building.  Inside, the order counter is straight back (menus mounted on the wall behind the cashier). On the right is the pastry and baked goods counter but you don't order from the staff stationed there.  Just remember what you want and place the order at the cashier along with any beverage you wish and with any sandwiches/other food items you want.  Understand that this isn't some cheap donut shop or fast food place.  If you want sandwiches for lunch, I think the ones we ordered were $10 and $12 apiece.  They serve them sliced and because we ordered some pastries as well as the grain side salad with our sandwiches, neither of us finished our sandwiches at lunch.    We chose to sit outside by the entrance to the building.  I found it a little unusual that they didn't give us a table number, but the staff successfully delivered out pastries and sandwiches to our table.  We carried our beverages with us.  They also bus the tables, though it would be nice if they had a trash can near the outdoor patio so that we could get rid of our trash or could set our used silverware in a tub to make it easier for the staff.  Everything we tasted was uniquely tasty!  I ordered the Roast Beef Chimichurri and the bread was toasted and the sandwich sliced for easier eating.  Lots of yummy ingredients that I would never think of or go to the trouble of preparing at home.  My wife ordered the LVTHNTBA (a turkey, bacon, and avocado sandwich on marbled rye) that she also liked I got a bite and liked it too!  From the pastry side, my wife ordered some almond croissants and a crispy pastry called the Kouign-Amann which she raved about.  I ordered a slice of the Blueberry-Lime coffee cake that has a crumbled top.  Excellent.  When we added drinks, tax and tip, some would complain it was an expensive lunch.  But considering some was taken home for dinner and the pastries (what didn't get devoured immediately) would be nice for breakfast tomorrow!  It's multiple meals unless you are just a beast that stuffs yourself each meal.  Everything we tried was unique (other than the almond croissants), so in a time when I've become bored with my own cooking, it was fun to get out and try some new flavor combinations.  Very pleasant staff and plenty of seating inside as well.  If you want to try something different, make a plan for a day trip to downtown.  Just take College north to 11th and be patient going passed the Bottleworks construction.  Review #3784

I love their house tomato sauce and who wouldn't prefer mozzarella cheese over provel. My service at the bar placing my carry-out order and enjoying my beer was typical of all the Hamilton Group restaurants. It was friendly, attentive and professional.   I'll be back? - Yes. Pizza, Wings, Salads and Beer - it's all good.   When: September 20, 2018  Why: National Pepperoni Pizza Day

They have a good BBQ restaurant, good patio bar, little swimming pool and hot tub.  The swimming pool and hot tub are free to use.  They also offer camper trailers, "tropical villas" and permanently moored houseboats for rent so you can visit for a short time or just live out here.  There are a wide range of interesting people here both tourists and locals that you probably won't meet anywhere else.  This is still a relatively unknown place and not many locals seem to know about it so if you want an interesting new experience this place can be a fun diversion from your usual list of activities.

review: I absolutely love this store. It is one of my go to stores for Christmas gifts and also unique gifts for that person who is always hard to buy for.   First off let me tell you the name can be a little misleading. Yes, they do have gardening items, but they are also a home decor store. Today I found a couple of decorative Easter themed items for my mantel in the living room. I change the mantel for every holiday or season, to for me these were great finds.   In addition to the gardening and home decor, you'll find cookbooks,  a small variety of gourmet food items and entertaining accessories. Those who know me, know I have a love for jalapeños so I almost went crazy when I found a jar of, Jalapeño Pickles. The brand is, Natural Pickled Pink. So, I guess you could say, I was tickled pink.   I am also known for my cocktail napkins. I take them to parties, gatherings with friends at restaurants and I usually add a package to coordinate with gifts. So, if you too are in to unique and funny cocktail napkins, come shop the rack here. I can guarantee you will walk out with more then one package.   Whoever is working, the service is friendly and attentive. It the type of service you expect and deserve when shopping a higher end store.

DH had a smooth, delicious Malbec.  My cocktail (and later iced tea) had blood orange (aka Moro) juice in it.  Best bite of the night?  Watermelon salad with pine nuts and flash-fried basil.  Super delicious.  We enjoyed the risotto side (a steal at $5) and duck breast entree.  The ony disappointment?  The "classic" bolognaise sauce (atop perfectly home-made strotaprezzi - yum) had a sour vinegary note to it and I did not love it.  We were too full for dessert but nearly ordered the spring special - a strawberry rhubarb crostata.  (We passed - we were just too stuffeed.)  A memorable, beautiful, gourmet evening. Can't wait to return!  Does Wilmington know what a gem this place is???

review: Was on my way to St. Mary's to visit the roommate who just had a appendicitis and I needed breakfast. I selected The Market for convenience, being located down the street from the hospital. I've been to The Restaurant and Basso, but not The Market so  I was looking forward to this breakfast.   When I entered, I was immediately greeted by a cheerful man, so I followed his voice and veered to the right. It appeared to be the right direction, there was the counter to order, a coffee bar and tables. I ordered the Smoked Salmon Breakfast Sandwich and a black coffee.  I was given a HUGE cup and saucer and told they'd bring my sandwich out when it was ready.   I filled my cup with a rich dark roast coffee, selected a high top table and started working on my iPad. Shortly, the perky young man brought me my sandwich. It was a simple, but tasty sandwich. It was smoked salmon and a fried egg on toasted wheat bread that had been smeared with chive cream cheese.  Now, this is the way to start a morning.   Once I finished, I bussed my table and walked over to see what I thought was the "retail part" of The Market. To my surprise, it was no only retail, but more seating space and a huge stone fireplace. OMG! If I sat down in one of those big comfy chairs next to that roaring fire, I may still be sitting there today. That fireplace was so inviting. I could be comfortable sitting there, sipping coffee and working on my computer or iPad all day. They'd be asking me to leave.....LOL  Great place, I gotta come back to try lunch.

review: I love Zavino so much I am upgrading to five stars. Between delivery orders (which always arrive as-ordered and just as delicious as when you dine-in), to experiences at the restaurant, I think this place is such an unsung hero on the Philly dining scene.   The cheese and charcuterie plate is huge and filling. My friend and I decided to scrap pasta/pizza and order just a couple small plates to round out our meal after devouring this medley of deliciousness last weekend at the bar. The spaghetti squash is so delicious I don't even miss real pasta. Paired with the meatballs, you have an incredible meal that doesn't weigh you down the way regular pasta would.   Our service at the bar was great and I especially appreciated the bartender's willingness to hunt down some after-dinner wine. The port was delish!

review: Warehouse space that has been updated into a restaurant space is the best way to describe this restaurant.  The front of house seems pretty disorganized as there was no hostess when I arrived so I sat at an empty bar seat but then was told that it might already be taken by somebody on the wait list but then I got to keep my seat as it seemed there was no list. review: I've picked up food from JC Teriyaki two days in a row to try a few of their main dishes to see what was happening there.  I've eaten their Fried Chicken and Hibachi Chicken, along with sides of Lima Beans, Potato Salad, Corn Bread and the Cabbage/Carrots combo that comes with the Hibachi offerings.    JCT sits on Parkside Avenue just north of Olden Avenue Extension in a somewhat rundown retail strip center which also has a Chinese takeout joint and an Italian pizzeria. Nice to have options.   While I enjoyed the entertainment of watching these three guys preparing the food, the actual finished products were only average.  The Fried Chicken combo of breast and wing was nicely meaty and never frozen, however the coating did not have very much flavor compared to the standards we all know.  It lacked sufficient spices to really stand out.  The white meat was plump and juicy and would have really shined with the right flour mix.  The accompanying Potato Salad was nicely sweet, but the Lima Beans were supersized and mushy.  The Corn Bread was pretty good.   The Hibachi Chicken order was large and with the Veggies really weighed down the container.  It was cut into small strips and doused well with Hibachi Sauce throughout grilling.  It was interesting to see the American short order grill used for a Japanese dish.  I had not thought of that before, but it was cool to put those two cultural icons together. The chicken was tender and had a nice flavor.  The veggies of Steamed Cabbage and Carrots were a little boring; lacking much taste.    JC Teriyaki is a mixed bag.  I like the concept demonstrating the cross-cultural bonds between Southern American cooking and Japanese grilling, but had higher expectations for the actual results.  Perhaps, the pricing of the meals (quite low) interferes with the ability to really pull out the stops and make the meals memorable.   3.5 Stars is probably the right place to be here, but I want to encourage an upgrade in performance quality which won't happen without a little mild criticism.

review: This corner bake/cake shop is easy to miss in a strip mall on the northeast corner of Madison and Stop 11.  The shop is small and when I entered, I didn't see anyone working, but I grabbed a serving tray and tongs to the right of the entrance and began shopping.  They have a large number of breads, pastries, and cookies available, but none were labeled, so it required a bit of guessing on my part.  At some point during my shopping, a woman quietly appeared at the cash register.    My wife is a big fan of the large, crispy pastry that looks like the dough is rolled out then the lengths get folded a couple times to spread out across the bake sheet.  Some places add a bit of sugar to make a glazed/sweet layer.  This place had just a light coating.  However, she still enjoyed the crisp crunch of the treat.  I also picked up a horn stuffed with a vanilla filling, a long roll with a berry jelly filling, a large cookie (like a sugar cookie, but not much flavor), and a triangle filled with pineapple filling (I thought it was lemon when I bought it.)  My favorite was the large triangle.  The horn was more like bread than like pastry.    The prices are low and I got all six items for less than a $6 ($0.89 to $1.25 each).  It's nice to know I don't have to drive all the way to 38th Street on the west side to pickup Mexican pastry.  I have a feeling my wife is going to want to visit here again.  Note:  This spot is adjacent to a Mexican grocery/restaurant so you can take care of getting all your Mexican food shopping/dining without moving your car.  Review #2699

review: Stopped in for lunch on Christmas Eve.  A note on the door said they closed at 1:30 and the time that I arrived was 1:09. There was no rolling of the eyes, no gnashing of teeth that I was there 20 minutes before closing.   The place was clean, the service was amazing.  I ordered something new for me, the Spartan Skillet: Gyro meat, onions, tomatoes & feta cheese with hash browns topped with 2 eggs any style and a side of carbs ( i chose their 'Famous' pancakes.  When the food came out, it was both fast and tasty. I was quite pleased with what they offered. Only that there was no butter for the pancakes. The runner brought me 3 little packs of whipped butter, and when I asked for 2 more, she kind of tossed them on the table.   The pancakes were light and fluffy, as were the eggs. The flavours of the Spartan mingled nicely. Usually I don't like onions in my food, which is why I omit them from EVERYTHING. But when they're cooked, they're ok. Today they added just the right taste.   I would come back.

review: "Music gives Soul to the Universe, Wings to the Mind, Flight to the Imagination..."                                             Plato  So believes Joel Zazyczny, the founder idealist who created Cafe Soul in Doylestown, PA. Scientist, innovator, philanthropist, Joel operates this simple, yet attractive eatery, as a non-profit to work with the younger people of the community in support of music and STEM education programming and scholarships. For this alone he has my admiration and support; for actually pulling off a well functioning breakfast/lunch haven with good food, he has my loyalty.   Now fully vaccinated against Covid, I visited Cafe Soul for my first professionally made Brioche French Toast in over a year. Walking in, the space was open, clean and prepared for social separation. I sat at a booth in back where I could see the entire room. Soon, I was approached by the young man running the front end. He was friendly and deferential. I did the short stack FT, and a mug of their Ellis Coffee brew. The joe was fresh and strong as expected from Philadelphia's oldest caffeine roaster (since 1854).   The frenchie was well panned, with plenty of caramelized edges for melted butter and syrup to accumulate. The egg mix tasted of vanilla and cinnamon, just as I like it. But for the Stuckey containers of corn syrup sweetener, it was a strong reintroduction to a favorite and missed morning meal. review: I've landed at this Continental quite a few times recently. It's a super convenient location for a pre-River Rink meal and I've taken advantage of that twice in the past month. Service is always friendly and fast - you place that order and food starts arriving at your table within five minutes, it seems.   Our go-to starters are usually the French onion soup dumplings, the Szechuan shoestring fries, BBQ chicken quesadilla or the Korean tacos.   I generally follow up with something much healthier. The Continental salad is my go-to on four out of five visits. Last night I ordered it with shrimp, which came with something around a seven dollar up-charge. But I really wanted shrimp! The salad was delish, as usual. There is a lot of flavor but it's still pretty light overall (even though they give you a mountain of salad). Although I haven't had it in ages, the seared tuna with mushroom risotto has always been a fav.   The desserts are small but perfect for sharing if you only want a few bites of something sweet. Our go-to has been The Grasshopper, which is a very fudgy brownie, scoop of mint chocolate chip ice cream, chocolate sauce, whipped cream, and chocolate candy topping.   Continental's prices aren't too bad for each individual dish, but when you start adding up plate after plate it can get expensive.

review: Seriously, I cannot believe I have not updated my review until now. I've bee eating here on the regular for four years. It goes to show how we get so comfortable going to our faves, that we forget to give them a shout out. So here it is, "Hey, Vinnie. I'm giving you that well deserved 5 Stars."  My go to when I do not want to cook, or just want a simple salad for dinner is a Large Greek Salad with Gyro Meat. It is huge and fills me up. They're not stingy with the Gyro Meat that is place on top of the salad. I could go for a little less dressing, but I always forget to tell them to go light. That's on me, but it is one of the better Greek dressing in the neighborhood.   Another of my favorites is the Reuben Sandwich. If I remember correctly it use to be an occasional daily special that has made its way on to the regular menu. Mentioning daily specials, that is one chalkboard you need to take note of when ordering. Tonight I finally made it here to experience their famous, Cheeseburger Cheeseburger.   The Cheeseburger Cheeseburger is flat grilled, diner style. It is two patties, both topped with American Cheese and then topped with thinly sliced white onion and dill pickle chips. I ate half of mine with not ketchup or mustard. The simple seasoning of salt & pepper was enough. For the last few bites, I did add ketchup. Simply because I am a ketchup freak for my burgers. The bun was also lightly toasted on the grill.   If you are super hungry, order the famous Vinnie's Fried Potatoes. They are Baked then fried and tossed in parmesan cheese and Vinnie's seasoned salt. The serving is so massive, be sure to have a friend to share them with.   Service is neighborly. The staff is always ready to chat while they prepare your order. I'm so glad this #smallbusiness is succeeding in my hood.   Will I return? - I support my hood.   When: January 2, 2018 Why: Burger Time

review: This is the second location for Hard Rock Cafe in New Orleans.  I had a lot of fun times at the original location along with a LOT of nostalgia for the space so I was a bit sad to see them relocate to their current location on Bourbon Street.  This location is better placed to draw more tourists and they have brought over a lot of the old memorabilia from the original location.  Hard Rock Cafe always has some good food and their burgers are always very nicely done.  This is a great spot to check out for some good food along with some rock & roll history.  They have the usual great gift shop with lots of items for the Hard Rock Cafe collectors.  Overall this is a great spot for fun times with American food in the New Orleans French Quarter if you are not in the mood for any of the local Creole cuisine.  Hard Rock Cafe also offers military veterans a discount all the time along with a free burger on Veterans Day which is a really great show of support for our veterans!  My video review of Hard Rock Cafe New Orleans is here:  https://youtu.be/uHt5J5EEkKQ

The bartenders of course are very knowledgeable on the beers on tap. If you're not sure what you'll like, tell them what your preferences are and they'll guide you. Today I didn't take advantage of their flights, but they do offer them. So many of our local breweries don't offer flights, so I'm happy to see Bluewood is on board with offering them. It's a great way to experience multiple brews, to find out which one is your new favorite.   A BIG plus for BB is having Mac's Local Eats sharing their space. The combination of the two makes for a fun filled experience. Beer and Burgers, what more could you want.   I'll be back? - Hell, YES! review: Once you start shopping at The Green Goose you will realize how fun it is to shop at consignment stores and how many $'s you can save. For me it has become a very repetitive behavior, I bounce back and forth between selling and buying at TGG. I love the Love Seat I bought at TGG, it is so comfy for watching TV.   If you have a tight budget this holiday season, I highly recommend TGG for your gift shopping. I was there today and the selection was amazing. They had all types of framed art work, mirrors, decorative home accessories and so much more. You can even find Christmas decorations to make your own home festive for the holidays.   Another great thing about a consignment shop is that they can help you sell your "stuff". Selling through a consignment shop gives you more customer traffic then you'd get having your own yard sale. It also, allows you to actually get what the item is truly worth. When you take your items into TGG they'll work with you on pricing your merchandise. Keep in mind  they get a percentage when your item sells, but it is well worth it. After all, they did the merchandising and their sales associates provided the customer service.   If you've taken then the Yelp Pledge to Shop Local, The Green Goose would be a great place to start.

review: Color me surprised and use the color orange. It has been eons  since I used a taxi in the city of Saint Louis. I normally only use cabs when I am in Chicago or some other major city.  So I needed a ride earlier this week and called Laclede and they impressed me with an A-Game.   It was a simple ride from the Lindenwood neighborhood to The Gateway Station downtown. The dispatcher who answered the phone was pleasant and cheerful. She assured me the wait time would not be long and it was under 15 minuets. When the cab arrived at my home, it looked as if it had been freshly detailed. Not only was the car clean on the outside, but the inside was pristine.   My driver was  articulate, making small talk on the short trip pleasant. We shared a chuckle when I got in and stated "Gateway Station" as my location. He responded, "bus station?" and I in turn said, "train station, it is all the same." Nobody calls it by the correct name, typical Saint Louis. However, being a good driver, he knew where I wanted to go.   So many times when in a Chicago cab, it is like riding an amusement park ride and you exit with white knuckles.  Not on this trip, my driver would get the safe driver discount from All State. Also, he was as clean as his cab. His white shirt was pressed and starched for  going to church.   In my hometown I normally do not have a need for a cab, but when I do my new assisant Siri will be calling Laclede.

review: After going through a few different dermatologists over the years and not being very impressed with any of them, I was finally steered in the right direction to Alta.  Dr. Finkelstein's knowledge of dermatology combined with his excellent bedside manner makes him one of the best physicians I have encountered.  Because skin cancer runs in my family, I have had several biopsies over the years just to be on the safe side.  Dr. Finkelstein has performed these procedures with minimal pain/discomfort and hardly any scarring, which is amazing considering my scars from the years before I was referred to Alta.    Wear your SPF and self-check your skin regularly.  If you see anything out of the ordinary, do not hesitate to visit a dermatologist.  Skin cancer is one of the most preventable forms when caught early.    This concludes my public service announcement of the day!

My husband and I arrived feeling pretty hungry so we started off with two apps: veggie fried spring rolls and shrimp papaya salad. We also ordered the coconut drink and the Vietnamese limeade. review: Most of the food here is pretty decent.  The fried food is usually the focus of a trip here and they also do some good chargrilled oysters.  They also feature a seafood pizza and some various other items along with the expected po boys.  I enjoy the little boiled potatoes they bring as a snack while you wait for your food.  I've generally had pretty good service here and sometimes there is a wait but usually not too bad except on the weekends and during lent.  The boiled shrimp have ALWAYS been WAY overcooked here EVERY time I've ordered it (or tried other peoples).  The BBQ shrimp is usually WAY better here than the boiled shrimp.   I usually only end up here if the wait at R & O's is ridiculous or on days when they are closed.  After so many chances over so many years I would have to say avoid the boiled shrimp but enjoy most everything else.  It isn't my favorite seafood place but it does some things well.

review: It's Pizza Hut, we had a coupon. I have no excuses.  They had a special offer, a large 3 Topping Pizza and an 8 piece order of chicken wings for $16.99. We thought this would be a nice treat while we watched the SAG Awards. Of course, those actors were dining on much better food as they handed out their trophies.  When we called to order we were informed all they only had thin crust and pan pizza available. What? Are you shocked as much as I am? How can any pizza place be out of hand tossed crust? We were disappointed, but still placed our order for a thin crust with Italian Sausage, Green Pepper and Onion.    Ordering our chicken wings was a big deal. Not having ordered from Wing Street before, I had no idea there were so many different types of wings. We had to decide if we wanted boneless, bone-in or traditional. I was so confused, I had to ask for clarification on bone-in and traditional. Wouldn't a bone-in be traditional? Oh no, a bone-in is breaded and traditional is not. We went with traditional in buffalo sauce.   Since we live in a neighborhood that has so many pizza joints within driving distance, I always opt for carryout. I may have to get out of the house and drive, but I get my food faster. When we arrived here, outside the employee door some of the employees were experiencing some, "sister drama". Their loud voices, spurting out profanities is not the first thing a new customer wants to see and hear.   Once inside the counter staff was friendly and very helpful. At this time we noticed different levels of hotness for the buffalo wings. We quickly asked which level we ordered and they said the hottest. Again, quickly we asked if ours had not been sauced if we could drop it a notch. Ours had been tossed, but they had an order after ours that had not. They quickly tossed them in the next level down and gave the next order ours. Talk about perfect timing.   I liked that when they brought our pizza out, that they lifted the lid to show us our order. For me that is taking customer service to the next level.   Once home, the wings were a sad excuse of chicken wings. They were tiny, tiny. If I didn't know better, I swear they were from baby chicks because they were that small.  The sauce was bland, perhaps we should have stuck with the Extreme. The pizza was just okay. I did like the way they chopped the green pepper and onion. They were larger pieces and not diced like so many other pizza joints.  I'm still miffed that they didn't have hand tossed crust.

review: OMG! I have held off going here, because so many friends gave it the thumbs down. They moaned and groaned about the wait and size of servings. What is wrong with, them. I was pleasantly surprised with the quality of product, the size of serving and value.  I admit, I was here right as they opened on a Tuesday, but I shocked how fast they young lady made my ice cream. I placed my order and as I checked in to Yelp on my smart phone and read the adult ice cream menu - she was done. I wanted to start watching her and she was scooping it out of the mixer and adding my toppings. So much for a scientific show. I'll have to pay closer attention when I come back for a boozy ice cream. Mrs. Marshall's Old Fashioned is calling to me.   I went with Ian Froeb's "must order" recommendation from his STL 100 list, the Salted Dulce de Leche Custard. Again, I must repeat, OMG! It was so rich, creamy and decadent. The regular size is big enough, how anyone can eat a large by themselves is beyond my comprehension.   Ices Plain & Fancy is being added to my Sweet Tooth list and will now be in my ice cream parlor rotation. It's off the beaten path, but is an easy find with plenty of street parking.   IPF is dog friendly. They can make a special ice cream for your fur-baby to enjoy on the patio, or in a to-go container to enjoy in the comforts of his dog house.   To those who complain about the wait time - get over it. Once you enjoy this decadent treat, you'll understand it was well worth the wait. A quality product, takes time and that is what IPF is serving.   Will I be back? Yes. My waistline may not like it, but I sacrifice and make cuts in others calories, so I can enjoy this sweet treat.   When: November 15, 2016 Why: The time had come to experience decadence.

review: Yelping 1900. Authentic Cultural Food No. 47. Center East Chinese Cuisine  This restaurant use to call Tao Asian Fusion. Recently has changed their name. The menu is also changed. I had the caprese panini and my friends has a burger and a philly cheesesteak. They both really enjoyed their sandwiches and mine was fine but a little skimpy on the fillings. The crisps and fries were aces though. DELICOUS. They have coffee and tea and then a cooler of drinks. So there's a good selection for your beverage needs and a water area near the front.  Of course then we got ice cream and we all enjoyed our scoops. I had the hummingbird flavor (no actual birds, more the southern cake) and I can't remember what my friends had. Again delicious.  Staff was great and the space is really fun but with limited seating. I think most folks take their sammiches to go.

review: Great to spend the morning in Fishtown having breakfast at the Milkcrate Cafe at the corner of E. Columbia and Girard. Interesting enviro with a huge record collection spanning music of the late 20th/early 21st Centuries. I didn't make it down to the vinyl shop in the basement (just read about it in their Yelp page), but as a holder of old wax, I wish I had. Next time.   Still, the cafe is part of the gentrification of this part of Philly and is in the perfect location to take advantage of it. It is a bit dusty around the edges, but with La Colombe coffee holding court and a good kitchen, it offers a mellow sitdown and strong java flow, with comfort food designed for the pioneering spirit of the surrounding neighborhood. Easy to spend hours there sipping joe and doing light sledding on your screen.   Loved the caffeine and found the well stuffed "Flying Breakfast Burrito Brother" a large tasty bite and chew. It was hot and moist and almost more than I could eat; but I managed to slay that dragon, and spend a few extra minutes watching the street life on Girard Avenue on a cold sunny morn.   It would be great to have a home on one of the narrow streets of this old revivalist corner of P.delph, but until that day arrives, Milkcrate will just have to be that place I can feel at home.

review: Some things just make sense.  You want good steak?  Go to a steak house.  You want a good burger?  Go to a burger place.  (I hate reviews that order some obscure menu item and then complain that it wasn't the best they had ever had.  Really???)  So it seems to make sense that if you are a meat eater, but want to try something Vegan, then go to a place that specializes in Vegan foods and has a lot of options for you to try.  That was the case for my visit to Three Carrots' new sit down restaurant on Virginia Avenue, on the Fountain Square side of the interstate overpass.  My visit came during the first week and the sign wasn't even up on the outside and the roof was being worked on.  It may not look open if you drive by, but trust me, it is and ready to serve!  So, after finding free street parking, I entered into the newly refurbished building.  The interior was a mixture of artistic ceiling lanterns and art work with bare concrete floors and unadorned tables.  There were a number of two-top and some longer tables, and in the back on the left side, some bar stool seating.  I was greeted promptly and sat at one of the two-tops.  The waitress brought me a menu of lunch items as well as beverages (including alcoholic types) to choose from.    Being curious and having had little exposure to Vegan cuisine, I thought it best to order something that had meat and dairy counterparts out in the restaurant world.  I started with the "Mac and Cheese Croquettes" and then ordered the "Seitanderloin" as my sandwich.  The croquettes are made from what looks like mac and cheese, then rolled in breading, and deep fried.  I got five croquettes, somewhere between the sizes of golf balls and tennis balls, and my choice of BBQ or Buffalo sauce.  Too big for even my big mouth, I cut each croquette and dipped them into the sauce.  Wow!  Very nice texture and flavor.  The BBQ sauce had a little bit of heat (mostly in the aftertaste) and really complemented the M&C.  I still don't know what binding agent they use instead of cheese, but whatever it was, it did a fair job of looking like cheese and mostly held the croquette together.  Note that once you break the outer breading, there is enough moisture inside that the noodles may not stay in place.  At least they weren't dry and pasty, so chasing a stray noodle wasn't too much to accept.  Moving on to the sandwich, it also did a fair job of taking on the look of a breaded tenderloin, even extending beyond the bun as all good tenderloins do!  The sandwich comes impaled with a steak knife for those who like to slice their sandwich in half.  Here I encountered one of the negatives.  The "meat" part of the sandwich was a bit overcooked and made slicing through the sandwich neatly a bit difficult.  The sandwich also comes stacked with tomatoes, lettuce, red onion, mustard, and garlic aioli, and maybe some pickle (I don't recall seeing them, but they are listed on the menu.)  I ended up toppling my sandwich halves during the carving, but quickly reassembled the halves and took my first bite.... and I liked it!  The bit of overcooking made for a delightful crunch which my teeth had no trouble cutting through.  The flavor was very similar to a seasoned breaded tenderloin and provided a satisfying chew.  (I've had an under cooked bean burger elsewhere before and it fell apart, so I recommend erring on the side of crispy, not soggy.)    The sandwich also came with blue chips and salsa on the side.  The chips were crisp and the salsa a bit tangy, but served in a very small round dish.  Since the salsa was not thick, it tended to fall off the pointed end of the chips.  I ended up breaking my chips into smaller pieces to better scoop out more salsa.  Hopefully, the mgmt will figure out a better way to make salsa dipping easier.  Service was friendly, welcoming, and prompt.  Water was iced in pitchers and was topped off during my meal.  Noise level was moderate with a mixture of music styles playing over the speakers.  Overall, even if you aren't a Vegan, they have very approachable options that are available if you want to expand your palate exposure.  I did, and I liked it!  Review #461

review: Scarlett, I'm going to be honest with you, it took several visits for me to become a fan. However, I saw the potential  that you had and kept coming back to give you a second, third and finally a fourth chance. On that magical fourth visit we finally clicked and now I can sing your praises.  I'm confident those earlier visits were growing pains and you got all the kinks worked out and you're now a favored spot in the CWE.   What won me over on the fourth visit was the Pan Seared Norwegian Salmon. Once I saw that on the menu, I knew I had to go beyond the booze. It was a healthy portion of salmon, served with potato gnocchi, prosciutto, asparagus and tomatoes in a light garlic cream sauce. I love salmon and this entrée inspired me to create a List on Yelp to give shout outs to those who do it well. You will be my first addition to this list.   Normally I am not a dessert person, but Bread Pudding is one dessert that can always win me over. I especially was excited to see Pumpkin Brioche Bread Pudding with Cinnamon Ice Cream and Maple Syrup on your menu. However, my heart sank when I was informed that it had been replaced by, Triple Berry Bread Pudding. I would have preferred the pumpkin, but the Triple Berry satisfied my Sweet Tooth (another list for you to be one).   Prior to my fourth visit, the customer service lacked. That is why; I'd have only one, maybe two drinks and move on to other locations for dinner. This time, even with the same staff, it was a different game. I guess the machine was out of cash, which is odd because we were here on a weeknight and not a busy weekend. The experience immediately soured us on the place and we left. review: Imli (Tamarind) Indian Kitchen sits on Passyunk Avenue just a few blocks north of Washington.  It is in one of the few strips along this diagonal thoroughfare that is not very commercially developed.  The upside is there is usually street parking to be found nearby.  The down, is that Imli does not benefit from being around other choices for potential customers.  It stands on its own, an excellent South Indian house that is very worth finding. If you live in the neighborhood you have the best of both worlds; the relative quietude of living in a gentrifying residential area, and a great place to walk to for a superior South Asian repast.  Lucky you!  Early Sunday evening there was only one couple dining when we entered.  First impressions were very favorable, with odd angles due to its placement on a narrow point of the star caused by transecting streets; dark wooden and slate hues on walls and floors offering a cool vibe to chill the heat coming from the curry kitchen, and large storefront windows on the urban world, made shade from mature street trees. Two young women approached with smiles and menus in hand, and invited us to sit anywhere. We selected the front corner table with a view of the streetscape without, and the whole room within.  These ladies were definitely sisters, and they admitted to kinship with the owners.    As firsttimers, we ordered a cross section of the offerings: Chicken 65 for an app; Began Bhurta (veggie curry dish), and Chicken Korma (mildly sweet and loudly hot at the same time). The house put down a plate with Papadum and two dipping sauces, which was a nice gesture. Garlic Naan, Mango Lassi and Chai completed the symphony. The "65" dish came out deep red and slightly crispy.  It was a delicious opening gambit. It was expertly grilled so the tops and edges were near-black, making it visually stunning.  The eggplant (Began Bhurta) came in a deep silver dish and thick curry sauce.  It mixed well with the Basmati Rice and was great for sopping with the Naan.  The Korma arrived in a yogurt/creamy/nutty champagne-colored curry with a nice amount of fresh cut chicken.  Everything was ordered, "hot," and was true to its word.  The lassi and chai helped to reduce the heat as needed, and allowed us to continue through to the end of the meal with calling the fire department.  The Garlic Naan was served flat on a wooden board rather than in a basket (nice touch), and the bowls of rice were more the enough to cover our main dishes.    I have not been to every other Indian kitchen in Philly, but of the many I have tried in the region, Imli is right up there with the best of them.  It offers a pleasing combination of cool atmosphere, warm, efficient service, and excellent cuisine. It may not be strictly South Indian (who cares), but it certainly knows how to create an unforgettable meal.    Try to get there soon.

review: This spot just opened, so I was jazzed to find myself in the area around lunch.  Those of you might remember when O'Henry's was in this location, so it's nice that another good lunch spot has moved in here. We sat upstairs and the place wasn't packed at all around noon.They have a little bit of everything here including sandwiches (which you can also get as a wrap) and a nice selection of entrees.  We started with the calamari and I got the grilled chicken sandwich with no ranch. All sandwiches come with fries. The calamari was great! It was lightly battered and nice and crispy. When my sandwich came out, I was disappointed that my chicken was fried instead of grilled. They've only been open a week, so I wasn't going to make an issue over it and the sandwich looked good, so I rolled with it. It turned out to be a happy mistake because the fried chicken was great! It was super flavorful and juicy in the middle. After tasting it, I didn't even mind that they messed up my order a little.  I'm not sure of our waiter's name, but he was really nice and attentive and made sure that we had everything we needed and kept our drinks refilled. I loved eating on the balcony and I hope that they plan on adding some fans once we are in the dog days of summer. It's nice to have a spot like this back on Carrollton and I'd return for lunch.

Next time, a weekday evening will be explored to see if the overall experience will feel less risky.

review: I wasn't sure what to expect, but the parking lot was full so that's got to be a good sign, right?  When we stepped in, we found out you put your order in first, before you sit down. Given that they were so busy, and it was an hour before closing, their ordering board said they were out of a few things. That's ok. We could work around that.   We placed our orders, I got a pulled pork combo, and my husband ordered a ribs combo, both of us would get our meat plus 2 sides for $11 or $13 with cornbread.  Not a bad price really, just a bit over average.  Once our order was placed, we walked into the small seating area and waited.  .. And waited.. And waited. As I mentioned it was packed in the parking lot, and so it was packed inside.  When we sat, they were calling #96, our ticket was #107 so we knew we'd be waiting for a while.   Time passed slowly, the husband and I chatting quietly, taking a look at the people around us plates, when I noticed one lady had just gotten her hush puppies, she must have had about 10 on her plate. I told her how good they looked and she offered me one. I politely declined, but I really thought that was nice.     As we were waiting, the woman who took our order came around to several of the waiting orders and told them that they were out of ribs.  She finally came to us and told the husband that they were out of ribs and would he rather a different meat. He chose brisket, he was fine with that.   When it was time to pick up our plate we were doubly surprised! The serving size of the sides were huge (Unless you got the onion rings, you only get 4) and he got Ribs. Apparently they found the last order of them.  This kind of made the lady who was sitting near us upset as she too, had ordered ribs and ended up getting prime rib. She was not a happy camper.   The food itself was good. There were 3 different sauces offered. One was very sweet, with a hint of Maple. The next one was kind of sweet but much more smoky and the last was smoky with a lot of heat. I liked the smoky one and the Hubby prefers the hot one.  The pulled pork was well smoked and very flavourful, the potato salad had a *special ingredient* that added some zip to it and made it unforgettable. While the fried okra that the husband had was very tasty as was the coleslaw.    What I was really surprised to see was that you couldn't get either Coke Or Pepsi there, but rather Kodiak soda, I've never heard of this brand but people seemed to like it. They also had unsweetened flavoured teas to try.   We will certainly try this place again when there isn't a groupon out, and have a better chance of trying everything we really want to.  I guess you can't fault a place for being popular, and having to turn customers away by telling them "I'm sorry, we've run out of food!"
