review: This is a nice Mid-City neighborhood bar that is located on the bottom floor of a house adjacent to a baseball field so you can drink and then play games.  The name of this bar is a play on the fact that the water level in the neighborhood during Hurricane Katrina was very high (aka it was flooded) and the bar is built out of refurbished flood damaged wood.  They have pretty comfortable inside and outside seating.  The bartenders are attentive and efficient and the beer is cold.  They have crawfish boils on Fridays when the bugs are in season but the last time I ate them there I ordered at 5pm and didn't get them til 8pm and they were WAY overcooked and MUSHY!!!  This bar attracts an interesting and eclectic mix of people of all ages and ranges from sparse to crowded depending what is going on and the day of the week.  When this place gets crowded it can get really smokey inside and it often gets crowded during Saints games when they usually have some free food.  This location is certainly worthy of a stop on a Mid-City bar crawl.

review: It's one thing to be almost out of donuts late on a Saturday night, quite another to leave the shop like it was hit by a cyclone.   There were very few choice by the time we arrived around 8:00 p.m., but enough for our limited sweet tooth and caffeine needs. I grabbed the last toasted coconut, and my sidekick the double chocolate. It was difficult to see what was in the bins because the paper liners were pulled out far enough to block the view, but not removed all together. The same was true around the trash receptacle, where many of the used napkins were scattered around, and the thin waxy sheets used to pick up and bag the donuts were crumpled and tossed haphazardly on the floor and counter.   Dude in the sloppy outfit and bedraggled white apron seemed to be working alone. Tidiness had gotten away from him, but he did have time to talk on his mobile, and with a bud who was hanging out at a corner hightop. review: I love a good pastrami sandwich. When I moved away from STL, the one thing I knew I was going to miss, was the good ole Jewish deli's. Once I was settled into my new surroundings, I had an epiphany. I suddenly remembered this little sandwich shop from when I worked in Alton years ago. To my surprise it was still open and going strong.   Their pastrami sandwich is as good as the finest Jewish deli's in STL. It's made simple. It a big pile of pastrami, topped with Swiss cheese and served on marbled rye with a smear of spicy mustard. You can have either cold or grilled. I highly recommend grilled, but if you choose cold, I promise not to judge you. However, I may talk about your choice behind your back. LOL  Fries would make a great side, but it's a sandwich shop so they have a large variety of chips for you to enjoy as your side. I'm not a soda drinker, so I did not notice if they have fountain drinks or not. I just grabbed myself a bottle of Straight Up Iced Tea.   The customer service was just average. The three workers were more into talking to each other about some drama with a common friend. I didn't mind because as I watched them make my sammie, I knew it was going to be great.   Lucky for me, the drive home is fairly short. The aroma of that pastrami was making me more hungry as I drove and if I didn't live close, I would had to pull over and take a bite.   Will I return? - Jewish or not, this is going to be my new deli.   When: October 1, 2020 Why: Craving Pastrami

review: Two Slices and a Drink review only.   I came in around 3 on Sunday afternoon and asked for their 2 slices and a drink special, which is listed on the board for $4.99.  I requested the plain pizza I saw sitting in the display be served, "well done," so that it was heated enough to remelt the cheese and bring them back to life.    The pizza arrived hot enough, but also clearly past its prime.  Although the underside was firm and held its load well, it was approaching staleness. There should be a time limit for how long a pie can sit around before it is disposed of and replaced for the next customer.  Too, I am not fond of having my fingers burned from the hot oil dripping out the back of the slice when I fold it over in order to gain a stronger grasp.    Finally, I was charged $6 and change for the snack, clearly above the listed price.  Perhaps, I was there too late, or it was not available on weekends.  The sign should have so stated if that was so.    Clean shop. But, I have experienced better pizza by the slice.

review: This is the main parking lot for the French Market area.  I like this lot for two reasons: #1- if you get here after 4 or so, parking is painless- there are always a lot of spots. #2- This is one of the few remaining lots that has a real life actual person taking the parking lot payment. I am no fan of the machines, because when I go down to the Quarter I don't know how long I'm going to be down there. Paying for my time ahead of time is a pain. I want to go down there and wander around and not worry about, "okay, I have to be back to my car by 3 because that's as long as I paid for." I don't know why they changed all of the other lots to machines.  In this lot you have a nice view of the river and it's the perfect place to park if you are going for a ride on the Steamboat Natchez or if you want to just sit on the river and enjoy a nice afternoon. It's also perfect proximity to the French Market, Jackson Square and Cafe du Monde. Long story short: this is my "go to" lot when I'm in the area.

review: This particular Saladworks was recently reopened by the franchisee from the Collingswood location that I used to frequent. The staff at Delran Saladworks are equally friendly and fast - a big plus since that line can get pretty long during prime lunch hours.   The cafe was bright and clean, though I took my salad to go. All of the ingredients were really fresh. My only gripe is the salad dressing part of the line. Two huge scoops of dressing is way too much for the size of the salads (which seem to get smaller as the years go by - remember the big seafoam green bowls from Saladworks of yore?). The person in charge of dressing should probably ask "one scoop or two?" Sounds silly, but she was so fast I didn't have time to ask her to stop, as I watched her dump the second onto my salad, which was swimming in italian vinaigrette when I got home.   Dressing aside, this Saladworks is better than most and I'll likely return next time I have a craving and I'm in the area.

review: Having been to the original shake shack and a satellite NYC location before, I knew what I was getting when I walked in (and out) of the Philly Shake Shack a few weeks back.  12:30 is NOT the time to go.  So today I was wiser and went at 11:40 AM. Perfect.  No line.  2 minute wait for a single burger with lettuce and tomato (no Shack-mayo for me) and a Half 'n Half made with STRAWBERRY lemonade.  I also got a taste of the Red Velvet Custard.  It was uber-rich and loaded with cake pieces and cream cheese icing.  The taste was enough - I did not need to get a cup of that caloric-disaster.  Meanwhile, my burger was great (I also enjoy the burgers at 500 degrees and when I've got cash to burn, Village Whiskey).  And they don't call me the "Empress of the Arnold Palmer" for nothin'.  That half 'n half was just what I needed.  Counter lady (I can't remember her name) was lovely and the guy cleaning the tables on the floor was a doll.  Execllent service (prior to the thundering herd that arrives at noon).  Do not come here during peak times. It's night and day.  Oh - and they were selling a $9 (NINE Dollar!!!) artisinal Brooklyn chocolate bar at the front counter.  Come ON!  It can't be THAT good????

review: The long-awaited Rival Bros. coffee bar is as cool as the names of their signature roasts. The neighborhood seems to be on board big time - there have been people in and out every time I've swung by for a cup. review: Tropical Family Restaurant at the western end of Lalor Street, Trenton, is one of the many converted corner bars that in their heyday were packed with the people who toiled the heavy industries of Trenton's steelworks and watered their weary souls here.  Those folks are mostly gone now; replaced by the next wave of immigrants who prefer their corners to provide spicy sustenance along with the cervesa. Tropical Family fills that need for the Puerto Rican pallet.   I stopped here for lunch last week.  I was pleasantly surprised by several things. First, they have a nice size parking lot surrounding the premises. So much easier than searching for street space.  Second, the house is very well renovated with brilliant color and murals and new buffet table, making it one of the nicer Latin places in the city.  Third, the service was first rate and came with sincere smiles from the bilingual staff.  Finally, the lunch menu while small, offers enough comida authentica to still the savage beast.    My Pernil Sandwich was loaded with Pork, Lettuce, Red Onion, and Mayo on a fresh roll.  The meat was tender and everything together was a fun munch.  I did find it a little lacking in the heat department, but the table Tabasco took care of that.  I also ordered a Refresco Mango - a blended ripe Mango with water and ice.  It was very good, but next time I would go without the ice to avoid the brain chill the came along with it.    Tropical Family seems like a solid choice for dinner, too.  And, as the name implies, it is a family joint where spouse and chachos would be comfortable and have plenty of great options for a meal.

review: Behind the town hall in Avon, there is a beautiful park with lots of open space for hiking and disc golf.  To the east of the town hall is a playground, a remote control car course (bring your own), a pair of outdoor ping pong tables, and a twin set of shelters.  Behind the town hall is a large pond that allows fishing and makes for a pleasant view while hiking around it.  The pond also has a couple art pieces along the trail.  "200 Years" was commissioned for the Bicentennial while "Angel of Hope" is a secluded monument area for parents who have lost children.  Behind the pond is a huge disc golf area that has quite a bit of elevation to it.  There is plenty of space on the east and west wings of the park that are great for hiking too.  Overall, it is a well maintained park with plenty of parking at the front and easy access from US 36.  Review #724

review: I just checked the Village Bagel website to confirm what I had read before; "...You will not be disappointed...Stop by..."  Well, when I arrived at their shop after a 30 minute drive from home to sample their product, I followed the directions posted on their windows to call in an order. No problem. Happy to comply.   Unfortunately, the friendly sounding woman on the line advised me that they were not conducting any retail business for the day, but only filling orders for Christmas. I could not walk in, nor order a breakfast bagel (onion w garden veggie & coffee), but would have to leave empty handed. Not even explaining my long drive, nor the absence of any notice on their website, let alone, Yelp, nor sign on their front door, could persuade her to extend a humanitarian exception and slice/smear a bagel for me.   Nope. I would have to drive away without satisfaction.   Ho hum...  Merry Christmas to you, too!   There wasn't any room at the inn, either. At least I am in good company.

review: This is a cool little bar that is part of a house right in the middle of a residential neighborhood.  I recently discovered this joint during my adventures along the Metairie Road St. Patrick's parade.  It is a long rectangular building with a long bar that covers most of the length of the structure.  We had a cute bartendress, that is also a nurse, and she took good care of us during our visit.  We learned that they frequently have free food here and that this is a popular spot in the area to watch Saints games.  During my visit they had some sausage pasta and mac n' cheese.  There were some serious smokers in here so I really didn't enjoy that aspect of this establishment.  I met some interesting characters in here and I even got invited to go on a  fishing trip to Grand Isle.  This seems like a nice secret spot to go and grab a few drinks and there are certainly some friendly and interesting people in here.

review: The space is beautiful and the staff seemed friendly, but we were just picking up takeout for a quick weekday lunch.  But oh dear. I really wanted to like this place...and maybe I might try their breakfast/brunch.  With the quality of food we received for lunch, I don't think I'll be trying their higher priced dinner options.  *the bad* If you say "lump crabmeat" on your menu, any good New Orleanian is going to expect blue crab. I'm not sure what was on my panini (which wasn't pressed so I'm not sure  what that was about) and I'm going to say maybe it was a different variety of crab (and not krab) that wasn't as tasty as the blues in the gulf.  If I had been dining in for lunch, I would have sent the sandwich back.   *the good* My coworker who got the curry chicken sandwich really liked her dish and she said the steak fries were yummy. Only error here, was that the menu says served on a croissant, but she got toast.  Also the side of corn was tasty.  The one person who got a juice (the ginger ale) from the bar really liked it.  *the meh* Other coworker's turkey club was dry and had no condiments at all included and that her potato salad side was a bit mayonnaise-y.  Also, my side salad was undressed so left me scrounging in the work fridge for dressing.

review: Solid! My fiancé suggested tacking a five dollar burger date on to our annual tradition of Christmas tree shopping in South Philly, so I happily agreed. Last night was my first visit to Fountain Porter. It's a cozy neighborhood bar with lots of stools in the bar area and some seat-yourself tables in the back.   The menu is small and direct: five dollar cheeseburger, three dollar fries, assorted pickled vegetables and some cheese and charcuterie. We both went for the burger, fries and a side of dill pickles. A pint of Kenzinger was a very reasonable three bucks, and the rest of the beer list was very well rounded with something for everyone.  The burger tasted great and was nicely sized - not too huge but large enough to satisfy. The fries were perfectly crisp, and the pickles were tangy and spiced just right. Also, the bartenders were really on top of things and they were both nice guys. I see a return trip in my future.

review: When: March 6 Why: Traditional Sunday Dinner  We decided we wanted to have a traditional Sunday dinner, so we choose fried chicken. It is amazing how a television commercial promoting 10 pieces for $10 pushes you over the edge. (Next Sunday, I'm cooking a pot roast myself.)  I remember when all KFC had was the original flavor. Now you get to choose between, original, crispy and grilled.  We mixed our bucket with original and crispy. For an extra $6, I got to add two sides and four biscuits. I love the Cole Slaw. In fact I have been know to buy large containers, place in a "cover dish" and take it to a pot luck picnic. We selected Mash Potatoes as our other side, fried chicken and MP's just seem to go together. I'd prefer a nice white milk gravy, but their brown is seasoned well.   What made this KFC stand out was the customer service. The young ladies behind the counter were cheerful and actually seemed to be enjoying their job. Brad loves thighs so I asked the young lady if she could  make sure we got two thighs in each flavor. She giggled at the way I asked her and said she'd do her best. I didn't care what the other six were as long as he had his thighs. She made it happen.  For those of you who are doing math and figuring 10 pieces is a lot for two people, don't worry. Four pieces were left over for lunch the next day.

review: When the most positive thing I can say about a new restaurant is the ambiance, "Houston, we have a problem." They've created a very beautiful space to relax and enjoy your meal. However, the most important points of a restaurant, food and service fall short.  I heard some great things about CSS, so when I was in Creve Coeur at lunch time, I stopped by. Being a lone diner, as my usual, I choose to sit at the bar. Looking over the Signature Cocktail list, they had one of my favorites, Smokey Old Fashion. How could I resist? I should have. It was weak and bland with no smokey taste or garnish. However, I did like the water being served in a Cobalt Blue glass.   After reading the entrees, I choose their Mixed Grill, but was told it was sold out. They wouldn't have it until dinner, after they received their delivery.  Bartender explained it was very popular and they sell out of it regularly. I then choose their Crispy Catfish Sandwich with Fries.   Since I was doing a sandwich and not a full entree, I decided to add an appetizer to my lunch. I was torn between the Crab Cakes and the Tempura Green Beans. I asked the bartender and she informed me the crab cakes were really good and were another of their most popular items. I went with the Green Beans, because I wanted a green veggie.  They were crisp and very lightly coated for a tempura item. The sweet and spicy sesame syrup served as a dipping sauce was delightful.   My crispy catfish was an extremely thin piece that was dominated by the bread. I did like the hot peppers as a topping to the catfish. When I choose the sea salt chips as my side the bartender informed me they no longer did them and it was fries. When I asked what type of fries, she replied, steak fries. review: Thank God my Sea Scallops were top notch and as always the Sangria went down smooth. Otherwise, this was a very disappointing visit to one of my normally 5 Star restaurants.   The service on my recent visit was on the level of a greasy diner.  The hostess, was not only snotty, she was snooty, too.  I found her looks of disdain at our party of 10, to be unprofessional. It was obvious she was not pleased that we were all not arriving at the exact same time. We all did arrive within 15 minutes, but she still seemed miffed.   Upon my arrival one of our party was already at the bar, so I joined him. I was cheerfully greeted by the bartender and I in return cheerfully said I'd like to enjoy a Sangria and showed her my Yelp check-in.  It were as if a switch was flipped, she quickly snipped, "We've had some major changes here and we no longer honor that." I responded, "Okay, I'd still like a Sangria, please." I am fine that they no longer honor a check-in special, but cut the tone and snippiness. I don't need to know about your "major changes", just say "I'm sorry that offer has expired and we no longer honor it." The words I'm sorry, go a long way in damage control.   Once we were seated, I was thrilled beyond words to see that Sea Scallops was one of the specials for the night. It made my decision process on what to order so much easier.  Pan Roasted Sea Scallops served over Butternut Squash Risotto with Passion fruit Gastrique. I was a happy diner. I have not idea how a guy raised on a beef farm, loves sea scallops so much, but I do.   When ordering, I requested, Jalea (a small plate) to be brought out first. I wanted to enjoy the crispy fried fish bites, shrimp and calamari before my scallops. When our server brought out other diners, salads, soups and other small plates, mine and another diners Jalea were missing. We thought the server went back to get them, but he never returned. In fact, we never saw him again until he brought out our entrees.  I just thought he didn't hear that part of my order and didn't worry.   When he brought my friends entree and my scallops, he also had our Jalea. My friend was a gentleman and kept his, I declined mine. I had scallops and nothing interferes my taste buds when I'm enjoying sea scallops. Our server understood and did apologize profusely. I was even offered to take them home after it was removed from my bill, but I declined.   The House Sangria here is always a winner, so I treated our table to a pitcher. If two or more are drinking the Sangria, I highly recommend ordering a pitcher. If you need or want dessert, I highly recommend the Torta de Chocolate. I took a slice home to the other half and with a cold glass of milk it was gone in a flash.   The food here is still excellent, but the customer service has taken a serious nose dive. If there has been a change in management, I hope they get this turned around quickly. Bad service can out shine excellent food. I will be back and like Sarah, I hope for better service and a more positive attitude.   When: 13 Jan 2014 Why: Dinner - Group of 10

review: I made my way downtown to this new crepe franchise located on the first block east of Meridian on the north side of Washington Street.  It shares the space with two other places:  Citybytes Cafe which is upstairs and Wei Ramen which occupies the back half of the first floor.  T-Swirl is located at the front of the building with the order counter to the left of the aisle leading back.  The order counter has flyers for seeing all the options which I found easier to look at than the overhead screens.  Once you decide what you wish to order, you pay at the counter and wait for the crepe to be made for you.  They can only make two crepes at a time, so wait times will be dependent upon how many folks are ahead of you in line.  Fortunately, my wait time was minimal since only one order was ahead of mine.  There were 14 types of Sweet Crepes available to select from plus a Brulee option and Chocolate option where you get to select the fruit you wish to add.  There are also 12 Savory Crepes to choose from if you want something more meal than dessert.  They also have salads, teas, and slushes available.  I ordered a Caramel Fuji Apple Crepe (#4) that comes with caramelized apple slices, raisins, custard cream, whipped yogurt, caramel, and granola.  Wow!  It was so good!  You can dine in or choose to get it to go.  They offer tear away sleeves for  the crepes which are rolled into a conical shape.  They also have fitted plastic bags with handy handles for carrying them without spilling the contents.    Parking is always a challenge and requires some fee.  I chose to park in the Circle Centre Mall ($3 for a few hours) and walk over to the location.  Hopefully, folks already downtown will choose to try this (these) shop(s) and enjoy some delicious Japanese crepes for a change to their routine.  Review #3650

review: Can you believe it? I went to a wood fired pizza restaurant and ordered a salad and it was a sensational salad. Their house vinaigrette, was incredible. If they bottled it, I would buy it.   What impressed me most about this salad, is that it had no iceberg lettuce in it at all. It totally was a mixture of mixed greens, in bite size pieces. In addition to the mixed greens, it had artichoke hearts, kalamata olives, roasted bell pepper, house-made croutons, parmesan cheese and then was tossed  with that amazing signature vinaigrette. It was huge, two people could share it if they were also ordering a pizza. For me, it was the entire meal.   My friend Christy thought it was wrong that I was at a pizza joint and not having one, so she shared hers with me. She was enjoying a Sara with some slight modifications. Being a fan of goat cheese, I think hew switching the parmesan cheese for goat, really made this pizza the real deal. I enjoyed the cracker thin crust and of course the wood fired char.   The service was friendly and attentive for our group of 9 and the server did not flinch when we asked for separate checks. They did however add 20% gratuity on to each of our bills. Which was okay, because our service was worthy of the full 20%.   I'll definitely be back, perhaps for a lunch special so I can try a pizza all to myself.   When: August 6, 2016 Why: Unofficial Yelp Event

review: Capital Health's new medical center in Hopewell, NJ, follows the trend in modern healthcare to merge the concepts of hospitals and hotels into a one stop shop for all medical needs, with a level of comfort and service that blurs the line between the two industries. Thinking of it as a hotel providing for health needs is probably accurate.   This is both good and bad. No one complains when a facility is clean, well staffed and meets the needs of everyone walking through the front door. The menu of services is extensive, with well trained professionals all around. Yet, the cost associated with these offerings can be excessive, and even with some insurance, beyond the financial means of most people. Those insurers have become more severe in their rejection of most invoices, realizing they are being asked to pay for a level of comfort for patients and visitors previously unavailable. What do you do when the hospital provides only private rooms and your carrier contracted with you to pay only a percentage of the semi-private rate? You hope you aren't admitted.   The level of specialization in each sub-discipline means a higher trained doctor is at your call, but while that is critical for some conditions, it is not for others. Still, the expense of over treatment is spread among all the patients without notice, nor consultation.   Part of this built in excess is due to how medical centers are developed, and the amazing tax advantages a health facility developer has over regular commercial work. The developer makes its money as the construction is done, while the management arm of the business can only expect pay as you go. Medicare, Medicaid and private insurers continually cut their portion of the bills to be paid, while the price tag on the service constantly goes higher. No wonder even the wealthy fear unanticipated medical expenses.   So, you have to hope the best medicine is available when needed, but also understand the cost of readiness and proximity may break your budget.

They are usually very good about stamping you and letting you go in and out as you please. As with many things in the area it can be challenging to find parking at times so plan accordingly.

review: I woke this morning with a mission to brunch, only I really wanted to try something new. There's certainly something to be said for the restaurants on Twitter; they grab my attention when I'm hungry and I'm more likely to check out their menus. Alla Spina's brunch menu offered several interesting-sounding bites, and I didn't have to ask my better half twice to make a trip to what is quickly becoming one of his favorite spots.   We pulled up to one of the prettiest corners of real estate I've seen in Philly. Route 6 and Alla Spina: nice work! The free parking in front of the church across the street wasn't bad, either.   The restaurant was even larger than I expected, and boasted a super fun atmosphere. I love the outdoor seating, the family-style table above the bar, and the lounge area. And the huge garage doors, which are clearly meant for opening on a beautiful breezy day. I loved it all.   Our brunch was awesome, too. I went a little crazy and ordered the egg panino, which comes with a sunny side up egg, provolone, house made pickles and bacon and pork terrine on a homemade English muffin. I typically stay away from any meat product I don't know the origins of but I decided to try something new and I'm glad I did. The sandwich was oozy and delicious and just the right size - not overly huge where I felt extreme guilt but just right. It also came with a crispy triangle of hash browns.   Also on our table was the crespelle, which expertly combined salty, savory and sweet. The kitchen graciously sent out a ham and eggs plate, which was another successful sweet and savory combo that I'd likely order next time.   The bloody mary I had at the start of the meal was nice, but the spritz was just perfect. I wanted another, but a third ten dollar brunch cocktail seemed excessive (the BM clocked in at $8). Especially in light of the fact that we had each sprung for the shakerato - espresso shaken with sugar and ice. Worth every penny.  I'm anxiously awaiting the first opportunity I have to check out happy hour. I'm crushing on this place hard.

review: When it comes to cool streets with lots going on, this one is at the top of the list.  One of the main selling points of Frenchmen is that it's a good hangout for tourists and locals alike, and it's not Bourbon St.  The places on the street feel a little more "authentic" New Orleans, because you can go here and actually see live local acts.  Jazz, blues, swing and more can all be found over the course of just a few blocks.  I know that Frenchmen isn't in the safest area, so whenever I go, I'm always sure to go with a big group, and I always end up having a lot of fun.  Also, every year on Halloween, Frenchmen hosts a huge block party, which ends up being the "place to be seen" for grown ups who want to have as much fun as the kids.  It seems that anything you want can be found here.  Check out jazz at Snug Harbor, a local blues act at DBA, do some salsa dancing at Blue Nile, hit the club at Maison, or get something to eat at 13.    Frenchmen is a definite "must" for anyone who is looking for the heart of New Orleans.

By larger, I mean in circumference and in size of the component parts.  Yet, while the fish seemed fresh, they did not offer a pronounced flavor beyond the sauce that was drizzled on top and the Soy/Wasabi/Ginger accompaniments.    Too, the Wasabi was the mass produced green variety that most offer, and the Ginger was the artificially colored orange, rather than the actual white of natural Ginger.    It was adequate and fresh, but certainly far from best of breed that is available only a short distance away.    The family is very pleasant, and the hostess friendly and helpful. Her husband does the artistry, while the kids and grandmother sit nearby, making it feel somewhat like I was eating in their dining room.    Not bad, but not exceptional.  When convenience is the primary factor, it serves its purpose well.

review: Fred M., my newest Yelp friend turned me on to a very well kept secret here in St. Louis. The BBQ Ribs at Biggie's are FABULOUS and only available on Saturday night.   I've been determined to go ever since Fred made the announcement in his review and last night I finally made it. I arrived just before seven and a good thing I did. They were almost sold out already. The waitress informed me that the Ribs are so popular that they sell out early in the evening. 7 is early? I guess those rib lovers come "real" early to get these hearty ribs.   My waitress was a true jewel, she was very accommodating. I ordered a full slab of ribs with the intention of eating half myself and taking the other home for Brad when he got off work. I mentioned this to her while ordering and to make things easier, she held half a slab back in the kitchen until I was ready to go. That is good service. It was provided without me even requesting it.   The Ribs are huge, meaty, tender, moist, fall off the bone good. I have not seen bones come cleaner at any other rib joint. I guess you'd say they are done KC Style, because the ribs are basted and served with the BBQ sauce already on them. In this case that is fine by me, because the flavor was astounding.   I enjoyed a Dinner Salad with Sweet & Sour Dressing which I liked more then the White French I had on my first visit and a Baked Potato. What is it about Baked Potatoes, they always seem to taste better out then the ones you make yourself at home. I guess food always taste better when someone else is doing the cooking.   Can't wait for this week to get over. I'm getting another full slab as carryout next Saturday.

review: Cute and simple cafe. Not only do they offer hand brewed coffee, but you can get a shrub cocktail or a mimosa to start your day.   I was impressed with the pour over, Chemex preparation of my coffee. They use Perc Coffee which is out of Savannah, GA. It's a decent coffee, but with all the great coffee roaster here in STL, I wish they supported another local business.   As of now, the pastry offering are minimal. However, I must say they are very good. I was surprised to find out they are done in house. I devoured a Spinach & Feta Croissant and thought it was from a popular French bakery out in West County. It was that good.   The only negative I will comment on, is the service. The staff was not friendly or engaging.  In fact as I watched them during my visit, they hardly smiled. They almost were robot like.  Smile, engage and encourage me to return. It's a great place, if they kick up the customer service.   Will I return? - Yes, I'll give them another try. review: If you count the value, traditional, authentic, good dining at dinner, I would said 5 stars for this restaurant. I have been to this restaurant 5 year ago and it does not give me an impression of good Vietnamese cuisine.   I have read many of my friend review about the pho, it is not the best. Why we revisit. I saw Joel review on the vegan food and decide to try it again. After I have read their menu, we discover the dishes that not normally serve in Pinellas Park Vietnamese hub. You need to navigate to their house special. Tonight we have a dish that we have try in Hanoi and did not see anyone doing it. The chargrilled fish. It is the grill fish "Thang Long" style. The fish is marinated with turmeric and baby dill. This dish we found at the street of old town Hanoi. Now we know they have it.   We also order the autumn roll with fresh roll on grill ground pork. Interesting. We order the the authentic happy pancake with large rice crepe with pork, shrimp and bean sprout. It is very unique. The other dish include traditional Central Vietnam Rice Noodle. This is special noodle of the central Vietnam. That how it got the name.   Overall they are good. I would suggest if you are here, don't try the pho for once. But try their house special menu.

review: I had a $20 Rum Bucks coupon from an event I went to last year that I finally put to use last Saturday. The rum list was huge, but I flipped to the cocktail section of the menu to make my decision. Right away I noticed a skinny mojito, made with Splenda syrup instead of simple syrup. Unfortunately, there was no Splenda syrup made. Did I mention it was a Saturday, just after opening? I sucked it up and went with a regular mojito instead. The drink was tasty, I even had two, but I don't see myself dropping $12/drink there regularly.   The decor feels dated but it's still a nice looking place. But the tacky pirate in the lounge area up front has got to go.   If you aren't in the mood for a fancy drink, the happy hour specials are pretty recession-friendly and are offered seven days a week. Also, the bartender was nice, which certainly isn't a given these days. I don't know that I'd go out of my way for Rum Bar, but if I were in the area and the mood hit, I wouldn't object to going back.

review: Point of Interest: This South County and the St. Charles location are not connected in any way.   Visualize the Red Headed love child of IHOP and Denny's and you've created Gingham's. What does that mean? It means you have a good place for breakfast at a reasonable price. The ambiance will be stark and Plane Jane, but you will not care you are there for the greasy diner quality breakfast. Their servers make you feel like a regular, even when it is your first visit.   Anyone who follows my reviews know I am a fan of Biscuits and Gravy and I am happy to say, Gingham's is being added to my list here on Yelp. I enjoyed a flaky biscuit and a milk gravy filled with chucks of sausage. I only needed to add some more pepper to make me truly happy.   I prefer my Hash-browns extra crispy and even when I request them prepared that way so many places just don't get it. However, the grill master here at Gingham's not only got it, but he impressed me. These truly were the crispiest hash-browns I have ever had. He also understands eggs over easy. Not paying attention, when ordering got me two sausage links instead of patties like the SO. I do prefer a patty over a link.   The SO got three pancakes with his breakfast and they were served a light golden color. They were served hot, making it easy for the packaged "whipped spread" to melt before adding the maple syrup. They were good, but I want real butter on my pancakes.   I will not make a special trip from the city to eat here, but when we are going to Costco and want breakfast before shopping we'll be back.

review: Yessss! Why did it take so long for New Orleans to get a fancy milkshake shop?  As soon as I saw the delicious photos from this new spot, I knew I had to check it out. David and I popped in to see what was shakin'. I really love the concept: you pick your ice cream "base" from a lot of different choices, you pick what goes on the outside of your cup (peanuts, sprinkles, candy, etc.), you pick your drizzle for inside the cup, then you pick your toppings.  I chose butter pecan ice cream as my base, with caramel drizzle inside, peanuts on the cup and pretzel sticks and gummy worms as my topping. Yes, I basically made myself a dang sundae in a cup, but I wanted to "ease into" the process. I loved my concoction and it was enough for me and David to share. It was A LOT of sugar and I think if I had one all to myself I'd probably pass out or something.  I went pretty conservative on my milkshake making, but you can add pop tarts and cookies to your dessert, if that's your thing. When I go back, I might try to go a little crazier, but I was pleased with what I came up with. The milkshake is a little pricey at $11, but it's a nice "once in a while" type of treat.

review: The Pickled Heron has been on my list of bookmarked restaurants for a long time, and I finally got to check it out with two girlfriends on Friday. We arrived armed with three bottles of vino. Though the restaurant was featuring some type of restaurant week deal, they still had their full menu available, which was our preference. Unfortunately, the menu didn't exactly match the one online, and my friend was disappointed to see that the scallops were no longer being offered. Luckily, there were still a handful of other seafood options.   I started with the moules frites. The mussels were served in a light, saffron-scented broth and they were fantastic. The fries were piping hot and served in a cone with a mild dipping sauce. Next up was a steak with bone marrow stuffing, mushrooms and onion. The steak was a perfect medium rare as requested.   We passed on dessert but said yes to French pressed coffee. I'm glad I finally got a chance to try The Pickled Heron and I'd be down for a return trip sometime.

It will give you something to talk about the next time you visit grandpa or grandma.   Keith D. was looking for Bing Crosby and Danny Kaye to show up and sing White Christmas. I was watching out for the Andrew Sisters, to sing Bugle Bugle Boy from Company B.

review: Once again, I am thankful I bought my deck of Taste Cards on LivingSocial. I never would have thought of coming to The Shack, but when you give me $10 off my $30 purchase I'm ready to go.   Before arriving, we researched their website and knew we'd start out with their Fried Pickles. Fried Pickles is one of my new addictions and when I see them on a menu, I order them. These were the first that did not impress me. We both thought that they were heavy on the breading, which killed the dill pickle taste. They came with a TK dipping sauce that I found to be flavorless. The fried pickles actually tasted better without the sauce. Next visit I will try the Green Eggs & Ham Loaded Fries, friends have informed me they are the best way to start your Shack visit.  OMG! I enjoyed the Pastrami Sandwich and it is now my favorite Pastrami in Saint Louis. It was served on the best Marble Rye bread, that was so soft and flavorful, that I had to ask where they got it. It came from Fazio's on The Hill. It was packed full of juicy Pastrami and Swiss Cheese. Look at my close-up photo and see how thick this amazing sandwich was. It came with a side of Idaho House Cut French Fries, that were lightly seasoned with salt. I love a fry that still has the potato skin on. They could have been a little crisper, but they still were the perfect side to my Pastrami.   The BF enjoyed the Southern Fried Salad. It had big chunks of chicken tenders tossed with Iceberg lettuce in a Ranch dressing. Ordering a salad at a place that primarily serves pub grub is crazy. It was way to much Iceberg for me and way to much dressing. I highly recommend getting the dressing on the side, to avoid the overdressed salad.   Our waitress was nice, as was the busboy. The busboy was actually friendlier and more attentive. The day manager even stopped by our table to make sure everything was OK and thanked us for coming in.   I'll be back to enjoy a burger and beer and hopefully it will be cooler weather and all the garage doors will be open connecting the patio and bar area.  I loved the sign at the entrance, telling you no one under the age of 21 after 9 PM. What a shame they have to wait till 9 PM to enforce this rule.

review: I had set up and bookmarked Pomodoro when I first read that it was to become the latest restaurant to make a go of it inside the first floor of the Hampton Inn across from the Circle Centre Mall.  Though I had originally planned on stopping by for dinner, I was glad to see that they have recently added lunch hours.  So, I asked my wife to join me for lunch there.  We parked at the mall and walked over to the restaurant (I noticed a sign for valet but assumed it was for evening guests.)  As we stepped inside, we were greeted at the host counter where an overhead menu let us know what they have to offer (small pamphlet menus are also there.)  While we were deciding, a second staff member let us know they also had lunch specials which include half a pizza (cheese or pepperoni only) with a side salad and a beverage.  My wife ordered the pepperoni special while I decided to go with the Meat Lasagna ($18). I was surprised that it didn't include any sides or appetizers for that price, but I decided to stay with it and pay for a side salad as well.  (Note that all salads come with a house dressing.)  After paying, we were given a number to put on our table and we selected our own seat though we were informed a large party was going to take over the back room of the restaurant, so we decided to stay in the front bar area dining room.  Soon, my wife received a large bowl of salad and her beverage while I got my lasagna and small side.  The same individual from the check in brought out our meal and poured the chilled (no ice) water for me.  I knew that the time lapse was too soon for her pizza to be ready, so we began eating.  The portion sizes of my salad and lasagna were suited to lunch time, though I became even more aware that for the price, there needed to be something more than just a modest serving of lasagna.  There was a lot of cheese (three types) and ground beef and Pomodoro sauce.  So there wasn't a lot of flavor from either the meat or the sauce.  Maybe that is more authentic, but I found it rather bland.    After about 15 minutes, my wife had finished her large bowl of salad and I was nearly finished with my meal when we flagged down the server to ask about the pizza.  He went back to the kitchen and then didn't follow up with us.  Instead, he seemed focused on the large party that had arrived in the back.  We then flagged down the second staff member who we met at the desk and let him know.  Again, he disappeared and didn't get back to us.    Finally, we got the attention of the first server and he went back and got my wife's meal.  Surprisingly, the 4 slices of pizza and another salad arrived on the same plate.  He said that the system had not delivered the food order to the kitchen which had caused the delay.  Seems odd that my order and a large salad got to the kitchen, but hers didn't.  Obviously, by this time, my wife was disappointed by the lack of follow up by the two staff members.  To make up for it, the server did comp her meal and gave her some complementary tickets towards future purchases.  But she was not a fan of the pizza which was a bit greasy from the pepperoni and somewhat limp/floppy in the middle (she prefers a crisper crust.)  And the pepperoni slices were not evenly distributed so that numerous bites were just cheese.    I understand that there can be some glitches in service at a new restaurant, but when a customer has to try three times to get someone to check on a meal, that is a basic mistake that needs to be addressed immediately.  I appreciate that the server tried to make amends but the difference of failing to give us feedback on the first request instead of the third makes it impossible for me to give this place a higher rating.  Hopefully, this review can help the management to be more aware of the orders and to instill a follow up mentality in those serving.  Review #3692

review: I've been meaning to stop by this place ever since I first heard about them at a Yelp event (which unfortunately was cancelled).  When I had the opportunity to stop by this business just east of Zionsville Road on 79th Street, I jumped at the chance to check them out.  When you park, there is a shared entrance to a cooperative of three businesses here.  The left doorway is for those 21+ and leads directly into Wabash.  It has a few tables and some other seating between the door and the counter to the left.  A nice taplist of house brews featured a full dozen choices this day.  I decided to go with a flight since this was my first visit.  The flight comes with four 5-oz servings for $7.50.  I grabbed my flight and started drinking while waiting on my flatbread from Between Brews Foodwerks on the other side of the shared wall.  I started with the Whitewater Wit (5.2%, 15 IBU).  Nice and light with very pleasant, almost fruitty taste.  Very pale in color.  I followed that with the Mugga Cherry Blonde (4.8%, 14).  This red colored ale had hint of tartness at the start and ended with a nice cherry flavored finish.  Very pleasant.  I moved on to the Working Girl Belgian Blonde (5.6%, 26).  This was the first I sampled with the flatbread and it went quite well.  I am a fan of Belgian hops, so this was another pleasing choice for me.  My final selection was the BaconFace Brown (6.0%, 27).  This was a very solid brown ale, but I was a bit disappointed that I couldn't taste any notes of bacon.  Maybe it was because I had begun eating, but my taste buds were just not able to taste much other than the basic brown ale.  Okay, but not up to the expectation of a name like BaconFace.   So, overall, I was glad to sample so many pleasant drinks in one flight and look forward to my next visit where I can explore some of the dark and bitter options.  I hope that they can eventually upgrade to glass drinking vessels from the plastic cups used in my flight.  Something about the plastic seems to signal a cheaper product than the fine quality I tasted.    Review #499

review: WHAT A VIEW!  When I heard about the reopening of the Bayou Bar and the Caribbean Room at the Pontchartrain Hotel, a tiny part of me wondered if they were going to open up the penthouse to the public. I was in this penthouse years ago for a private event and the best part of the space is the gorgeous view of the city.  I am happy to report that the penthouse has been converted into a cool bar/club type of space. There are sofas and chairs for lounging inside and there are tables and chairs out on the balcony, so that you can soak in the entire city. Getting up here feels very VIP- you have to get in line and wait for the doorman to let you up. This is for safety reasons, but really makes the experience feel that much more exclusive. The bar feels as if you are in someone's living room at a fancy party.  The balcony area is small, so you have to wait for some space to open up before you can make it out there. On the night I was there it was pretty packed, even though it was late in the evening. I think some people just like to take over the tables and "camp out" for the night.  I definitely want to go back a little earlier in the evening, so that I can watch the sunset from this gorgeous spot. My sad little picture definitely doesn't do this place justice.

review: I stopped by for lunch and ordered a couple slices and an order of breadsticks.  The slices are huge (1/6th of a 20" pizza = 10" long and about 9" across!)  They have the pizza slices sitting out for you to select the type and then they do a quick reheat in the ovens to make sure it is warm when served.    After prepaying, I grabbed a seat in the dining room which looks bigger and cleaner than on my previous visit a few years ago.  It probably isn't any bigger, but it felt like there was plenty of room.  Before long, my order was ready and I went back to the counter to pick it up.  I grabbed some napkins and utensils in case I needed them from a counter to the left of the order window.  They also have a beverage dispenser to the right.  The slices were served individually on their own plates.  I started with a supreme pizza that I believe they call the Southside Special.  It comes with pepperoni, mushrooms, olives, onions and peppers.  After a quick dabbing with my napkin to get the excess grease from the top, I noticed the the green peppers and the onions were in large clumps.  The cook had sliced them, but not all the way across, so I had to manually separate the pieces and spread them across the pizza so that I could have some in each bite.  And when I tried to lift the pizza to eat it, the center was so soft that it drooped and spilled the topping onto the plate.  I understand they may want their pizza slices to be folded, but this was just soggy and disappointing.  Fortunately, the flavor was good.  If they could just crisp the crust a bit before so that centers got done, it would improve the customer satisfaction a star or two!  I moved on to the sausage and pepperoni slice and it was in better shape, but still had a lot of grease on top.  I guess I should have left it since the sausage was so mild that it barely had any flavor.  The pepperoni were okay and the crust had a nice crispness to the bite while still being able to fold it.    It is sad that a local restaurant can't get the consistency down so that customers want to keep coming back.  As it was served, the pizza wasn't any better than a reheated frozen pizza I can get at the store.  Sure, the portions are generous, but I will pay for better quality if I can count on it.  Review #2001

review: For some crazy, still unbeknownst to me reason, I thought hitting the very first Curiosity Doughnuts pop-up at ITV would be a good idea. The pop-up started at 8am, on one of the very first really cold days of the year. My husband and I arrived around 8:15 to a line that snaked down the block. We took our place in line and hoped we wore warm enough clothing (spoiler alert: we didn't).   We waited in line for well over an hour. I am not that girl who waits in line for specialty food products; I still don't know what possessed me to that day... Though I suspect my alcohol-free November had something to do with it. My sweet tooth rages when I'm on dry island and doughnuts are a weakness. Okay, now we know.   As we got close to the door, it was pretty evident through the window that pickings were getting very slim. Once inside, we didn't have much of a choice; we ended up with a box of six doughnuts, most of them flavors that I wouldn't have picked had I had more options. That said, I was thrilled to have any doughnuts at all; they were completely sold out after one or two more customers went in after us. I would have been crushed if I had been in that line still!   At home, the doughnuts were incredible. The insides remind me of a Market Day Canelé (this is a very good thing - Philadelphians, get after it if you haven't had one before!). The exterior had a perfect crunch. Some of the fruity glazes weren't my thing, but the doughnut itself was a work of art.   Now that Curiosity Doughnuts is more of a fixed thing and not a pop-up, I've heard the wait times have improved. Great news for me, as my days of waiting in long lines for food are now officially over. Can't wait to try more flavors!

I probably wouldn't choose this spot over The Sazerac Bar, in the Roosevelt Hotel, but it gets the job done.

review: I had no idea what to expect from Green Goddess when a friend told me that we had to try this place. After a decent walk through the quarter and after being led down an alley, we were here. Oh...we're sitting outside? Great. I'll admit, I'm a complete priss who doesn't like to be hot, so when I saw that all of the seating was outside and it was the middle of July, my heart leaped into my throat. The good news is- there was a nice breeze and after a while I didn't notice the heat. I swear I'm not lying.  There are so many goodies on the menu, we just decided to order a bunch of things and munch. First we got the pate that came with toast rounds. The pate was wonderful! It was nice and rich, of course, but what I liked most about it was that it was whipped and this made it really easy to spread on the rounds.  Next we got the boudin and duck sausage plate. This was served with pickles, bread and mustard. The boudin was so good. It was tender and juicy with a lot of flavor. The duck sausage was quite tasty, especially when it was dipped in the mustard. Then we got the shredded duck which came on a bed of greens with potatoes and bacon wrapped dates. I think this was my favorite of the whole meal. I really could have eaten an entire plate of those dates and the potatoes were cooked perfectly. The duck was really good as well and I liked that it was served on top of a little salad.  Finally, it was time for dessert and we ordered the praline bacon ice cream sundae that came topped with black sea salt. WOW. The flavors on this thing were out of this world. The bacon and salt added the perfect compliment to the sweet of the ice cream. It was a delicious combination, and definitely enough to make me want to go back and get this again.  All in all, I liked my meal here. I'd love to go back, but I will probably wait for autumn to do so.

review: This is a review of a special event in the Penthouse Ballroom.  What can I say? Windsor Court seriously knows what they are doing when they host a special event. I recently attended the Southern Rep Gala here and I was blown away by everything. When I first walked in, there was a main room where everyone could mingle while drinking their drinks and enjoying the yummy appetizers that were being passed around by the professional staff. I think my favorite part of this first area was the patio and the balcony. It was a lovely evening, and you had a great view of the river and the bridge. There was plenty of seating on the patio area so that you could sit and talk and enjoy the sunset. It really felt as if I was at someone's home.  After cocktail hour, we were lead into the main ballroom. At our assigned table we were served an amazing salad that seemed to have a house made dressing. For our entree' we enjoyed a filet that was cooked to perfection, served with asparagus and mashed potatoes. This steak was so perfectly cooked that I was able to cut it with a butter knife. Everyone at our table raved about how fantastic it was. Dessert was a delicious slice of cheesecake that came with a side of strawberries. The entire meal was out of this world and easily one of the best I have had this year.  The entire evening came off without a hitch. We were able to watch the scheduled performances as we ate and everything began and ended exactly when it was supposed to. Everything flowed beautifully.  If it is within your means, I highly suggest the Windsor Court Ballroom for any event. Whatever it costs, it is worth it for the memory you and your guests will enjoy for days after the event has ended.

review: Good music, good weather and the most are good food. I am enjoying this festival with a strong Cuban emphasis. This is more into the Latin cuisine then just Cuban food. I have seen Puerto Rican food there. This year Cuban sandwich winners are Aloha food truck (third place), the Floridian (second place), and the no 1 winner is Trias. Their secrets ingredient is salami.   The Cuban community here is strong and they do hold this festival every year. Latin music playing at the background and people enjoy their afternoon off with family.   We have try Sergio's Cuban sandwich from Miami. The line to get the sandwich is long. It takes me 30 minutes to line up to order. The price is cheap with whole sandwich for $7. I could have just order 10 of them and sell $10 to the people line up at the back. The drinks stand that next to the hot the benefits for the people who are in the line. The sandwich is ok. I have tasted better Cuban sandwich at Miami with better mojo pork.   We also order the grilled steak meat from one of the food stand. It was juicy and nice. My wife gets the Puerto Rican food. It has the blood sausage, pig stomach soup, and bacalao fried dough. I like the fried bacalao and the pig stomach. It cooks with yellow bean base. Those are savory.   Love the festival. The organizer pull a lot of heart include donation to the homeless to assemble the longest Cuban sandwich.

review: Cheeseboro's Kitchen is a stand alone building on Pennington Road that does soul food and other American classics.  It is primarily a take away house, with only a few tables along the front window for those who want to eat right there.  Ordering is done at the cash register, and each meal is prepared individually. The finished dishes come out on the other side of the room in front of the pizza ovens left over by the previous tenant.    The good thing about this approach is that the meals are hot and fresh.  Only the side dishes were premade and chilled as they wait for you.  The down side of this "just in time" production is that when they get busy, the wait can be rather long for your meal to be completed and brought out of the kitchen.  While I was there, people were going outside to wait, or leaving all together to return when the food was ready.  Some customers call ahead, which while a good idea, just prolongs the wait for everyone.   The people working here, including management, are friendly and appear to be working hard to get the food out.  My questions were answered with a smile, even when I was showing my cultural ignorance about how certain things would be presented.  For example, a "sandwich" is not something between two slices of bread, but instead is a load of whatever you want on top of three slices of white bread.  You can make a sandwich of it yourself, but there is way more meat, fish, etc., than can fit within the confines of a manageable sandwich. Easier just to eat the food and as much of the loaf as you desire. Me? I skipped it all together in order to consume as much fish as possible.  Happy to be enlightened.   What about my whiting sandwich and side of macaroni salad (recommended)?  Six large fillets, light breading and flash deep fried, made for a delicious lunch.  I could only eat four of them. The macaroni side came in a plastic tub, mixed with copious mayo and bits of tuna.  Cool and great tasting. Again, more than this man could stuff down.    The only drawback to Cheeseboro's is the wait for the food to be prepared, and secondarily to the unused space in the store that could be put to use with more tables or perhaps, displays.  The meal, with the side and bottle of iced tea, came to around $12.  Quite reasonable for the quantity and quality of the offerings.  Now that I have a better idea what is going on, I will be back to try the rib sandwich, and perhaps, even their burgers, and more of their side dishes.

The french fires were quite good so I was happy with those.  They were nearly out of iced tea so I didn't get to drink my fill of that and then they also seemed to be running out of mustard as the last bottle available had very little left in it.  I think I would probably focus more on drinking than eating here.  It was also very dead in here on the night I visited so it seems to be more of a happy hour spot.  The menu seems to need a revamp as it just doesn't really seem to be a good mix of items for the area and attempts a fusion of things that end up not working out too well other than for maybe Vegans and vegetarians.

review: I've had this place on my radar as a spot to take one of my wine drinking friends, but for whatever reason, I had not made it in.  So, I decided to stop by myself and check it out.  The space is rather small with a wall of wine on the left, a display of bottled beverages (including spirits and beers) centered towards the front, and booth seating on the right.  The order counter is just beyond the centered display with a chalkboard menu overhead.  They have a small food prep area beyond the counter, so I waited as the lone employee prepared a charcuterie board for one of the other patrons.   After the short delay, the employee greeted me and poured a flight of port wines for me:  three 2 oz. samples.  One, a lighter port was from France.  I followed that with one from Portugal and ended with a fruitier California variety.  I enjoyed them all as I sat at one of the tables (one side is a long padded bench while the opposite side is chairs.)  Pleasant pop music played in the background as I relaxed, enjoying my wine.  This is a place you can get a meal including sandwiches and pizzas, but don't expect them in a hurry.  I'll have to come back some time to give their food a try.  Review #3470

There is also a tv outside, if you don't feel like dealing with the smoke or huge crowds that like to gather here on game days.  I have to be honest, this is one of the friendliest places I've ever been to in the city.  I had never been here before and people seemed eager to introduce themselves and make me feel welcome. review: It seems that Café con Leche has been in Newtown forever.  It is a place I used to go to with some frequency, but over the years it fell off my radar as a "go to" place for good Latin/Italian styled cuisine.  When a friend recommended it for lunch I jumped at the chance to revisit an old friend.   Daniel Lucci is the owner/chef in this walkout basement of a restaurant on the Newtown Creek side of State Street.  It is best approached from the parking lot next to Isaac Newtown's, where it must compete for parking.  It is accurate to describe the dining area as small and dark, but for some that adds to the ambiance and charm.  The menu seemed smaller than I remembered it, but it still had Mexican, Italian, and Continental flourishes.    Lunch was from the Sandwiches Menu.  All are prepared on French Bread with a side salad.  The bread is fresh with a moderately crunchy crusty ingratiating bite, and my accompanying salad was potato with celery and a mayo-mustard creamy connector.  The Yellow Fin Tuna Salad was good, layered with lettuce and tomato slices.  It was satisfying and filling.  The Cajun Salmon was nicely blackened with a Pesto Mayo dressing and side garden salad with Daniel's special Balsamic Vinegrette, he calls, "Balsamico." I tasted this and thought it was better than the tuna. review: I expect a place that specializes in TEA to have flavorful options.  What I didn't expect was a delicious soup, sandwich, and dessert as well!  After driving up the alley from 62nd Street to access the free parking behind the store, I entered the rear of the building and proceeded down the hallway to the back entrance of the shop.  I noticed quite a few racks of shop items and assorted "gift ideas" on the south side of the dining area.  There was also a comfy couch section and a couple dining areas.    The menu consists of breakfast and lunch items, numerous tea and beverage options, and a number of desserts (located on the north wall near the order counter).  I placed my order for a lunch meal which includes the sandwich and a small tea (chips are available.)  I decided to go with the BST (Bacon Spinach Tomato) sandwich on an "everything" bagel.  Everything was fresh and the veggies were colorful.  The bagel was thick and chewy, but not so much as to be difficult to eat.  Just a nice texture that complemented the crispy thick bacon.  Excellent!  I also ordered the soup of the day which was a Loaded Baked Potato:  Wow!  It was so dense that I thought it was potato salad, but was loaded with flavor like a great soup has.  Definitely get this if you go on a cold winter day.  Since I was Yelping, I asked for my free macaron as well.  I chose a Hazelnut that was fresh and tasty too.  Are you seeing the pattern that all the food was great?  And I did try a White Chocolate Blueberry tea that was served in a simple cup on a saucer, but even though it didn't have the color and visual impact of the food, the flavor was great.    The staff was friendly and helpful.  I paid for my order at the time I placed it at the counter and since it wasn't busy, they delivered it to a table I picked out.  Otherwise, they have a pick up area on the other end of the counter.  The napkins and silverware are self help at a small table on the south wall.  Patrons are expected to bus their own tables when finished.    Overall, a delicious meal in a quiet and comfy surrounding.  I definitely enjoyed my visit.  Review #479

review: So far this is my least favorite food of all the meat and three joints I have visited in Nashville but they give you a LOT of food for the price (and for being my least favorite in Nashville it is still better than many others around the rest of the country).  The service here is great and good old Southern friendly and pleasant as they kept my tea filled and made sure to check up on me to make sure if I needed anything.  Unfortunately my choice of the "beef steak" was just one of the least pleasing country fried/chicken fried style steaks I have yet sampled and it reminded me too much of some unpleasant school cafeteria meals I had as a kid so I just wouldn't get that again.  The vegetables were all great and I look forward to sampling lots of the other meats and vegetables here as I imagine I will likely enjoy those a lot more.  This is a fantastic dive type of joint as well (in every good way) which adds up to big bonus points to me and as they have kept most of it unchanged for many decades so there is a lot of old Nashville to enjoy inside this place.  Overall this is a decent spot to grab a hearty meal at a good price with pleasant folks working there.

review: Being a new resident of the Godfrey/Alton area, this is my new Lowe's. In the past I was use to the one in Kirkwood, MO a suburb or STL. I was expecting a major difference between an upscale neighborhood and a small town store, but there really wasn't that much difference. In fact, the biggest difference is, you get better customer service here.   I've shopped various departments and have always found what I needed. The staff in the paint department was able to assist me in matching my new houses paint so I could do touch up. Then the clerks in the bathroom department helped me with new towel bars and other accessories.   What surprised me most was, the garden department in January. I had received several small plants as house warming gifts and they have out grown their pots. I was able to find new pots to my liking and special indoor potting soil. In the dead of winter, I thought finding gardening supplies would have been a challenge.   I already have my eye on new lighting fixtures for my entryway and hallways, so I'll be coming back for those.   When checking out, I always use a live person and those that I have experienced, are friendly, fast and efficient. I'm liking this Lowe's.   When: August 28, September 8, October 27 and 29, November 14, December 10, 2020 and January 30, 2021

review: Came down to The Pines Tavern on Radcliffe Street in old Bristol Borough to celebrate mi cumpleanos the other night.  Yelp reviews were very positive, and it had been a while since I had anything more than a cup of great coffee (Calm Waters Coffee Roasters) in this old river city.   The bar/dining room is small, with square bar and perhaps ten to fifteen stools and equal number of tables.  The room is dark with several HDTVs for sport enthusiasts. The crowd was a mix of octogenarians  and middle aged folks, who all seemed to get along smashingly.  Drinks were very reasonably priced, and the custom beer list, while limited, had enough for us to be satisfied. Service was prompt and friendly with black T-shirted smiling servers always available to bring what you needed.    The kitchen feels mostly homegrown talent.  They know what they are doing, especially in the realm of American or ethno-American cuisine.  The plates are full to overflowing, while still being dusted with herb and sauce for that new-American high end look.  I came for the Meatloaf and was lucky enough to discover it was "Meatloaf Night."  Saved a buck or two.  The meal was very good, with Garlic Mashed and fresh Steamed String Beans.  Liked it a lot!   My companions ordered Lobster Mac and Cheese, which came in a low baking dish, topped with Bread Crumbs and melted Cheese.  It was tasty, but to my tongue, the cheese was too strong for the Lobster and hid much of its flavor.  The third entre, a Chicken/Shrimp Thai Curry with Brown Rice, was weaker, as we knew Thai food too well to find this imitation close enough to experience and expectations.  The curry was a little off as if they might not have had all the ingredients needed for authenticity.  Plenty of bird and shellfish.   We also ordered the Buffalo Cheesesteak & Fries app.  It was huge and plenty hot between the Buffalo Red Sauce and semi-melted Blue Cheese.  Our twenty year old inhaled most of this.  It was a big hit.   All in all, we enjoyed our evening at The Pines.  This is far more than your average neighborhood tavern.  A real effort has been made to polish the kitchen and bring in people who want more than just bar food.  In this they have succeeded, even if not perfectly.   We applaud the effort and love the atmosphere.   We will be back.

review: COVID-19 TAKEOUT REVIEW  These are the times that try our souls.  To grab a break from constant at home dining, at least two or three times a week we pick up takeout meals from either a place we haven't tried before, but has been bookmarked for a long time, or an old reliable that for some inexplicable reason had dropped out of the rotation. So it was with Primo Hoagies in the Glen Roc Center near Trenton-Mercer Airport in Ewing, NJ. Nothing like a premium submarine sandwich on a fresh sesame seeded torpedo roll to pleasure and comfort a weary heart. And, Primo, the former Italian deli out of Philly that is now an expansive regional franchise, knows how to bring that iconic satisfying experience home.   We ordered over the phone for curbside pickup and sent the 19 year old who is spending the rest of his college freshman year at home out to secure it. Ordering a Turkey Schwartzie (sliced roast turkey, Swiss, lettuce, tomato, sweet pepper relish and mayo),  Corned Beef Schwartzie, and traditional Roast Beef & Provo Hoagalone, at $10 per, we actually had enough for two meals after cutting them into quarters and mix/match sharing. Our separately purchased bag of uber crisp & spicy Herr's Jalapeno Potato Chips were the perfect counterpoint to the soft semi sweetness of the sandwiches.   And, an outstanding mention is demanded for the wonderful bread encapsulating the quality ingredients. Those babies were so delicious with sesame seeds generously spread atop each creation that I could easily have been happy with just them and a shmear of butter. So good!  As we sat devouring dinner at the kitchen table we were able to forget the seeming war zone coronavirus had turned out peaceful community into for a few minutes and talk of normal things like before this disease ended our innocence. In times such as these, we must fully appreciate such moments together.

review: The more I eat Vietnamese, the more I realize my palette probably leans more towards the "Americanized" version of things, so keep that in mind as you read my review.  I stopped in here for lunch, as this place had been on my list for a long time. I rarely make it into the "deep Westbank", so I was happy to find myself over this way for work in the early afternoon. Walking in, the place is really dark and dimly lit save for a tv playing Judge Judy (loudly) and some lights at the bar. I took a seat and looked over the menu.  Since it's around 90 degrees in the shade these days, I skipped the pho (mistake?) and got a pork vermicelli bowl instead. The bowl was very "no frills" and contained thick chunks of pork, vermicelli, lettuce, some cucumber and peanuts. The vermicelli was great and I liked the sauce they served on the side to add to it. The pork was okay but seemed...off. It wasn't off in a "this pork has turned" sort of way, I just don't think I liked the way they prepared it. It was kind of mushy and didn't have a ton of flavor. I also got an iced coffee, which I enjoyed.  I am glad I checked this place out, but I'm not in a hurry to rush back. I know that they are mostly known for their pho, so I guess I made a mistake when I didn't just get the pho for my lunch, but live and learn.

I had the shrimp boil panini and the next day I ate my winter caprese. Both were delicious. And let me tell you, if you are a beets fan get that caprese. UH-mazing. I got the creole cole slaw and the quinoa salad as sides. The cole slaw was fine; really I'm not that into cabbage anyway. But the quinoa was great.   This yummy spot is definitely going into my rotation.

review: I've only been here for events and never stayed in the hotel.  This is a nice hotel and it has some nice features.  They have a smaller bar area than most New Orleans hotels which still works for them as they seem to have the space they need.  The conference areas are a bit tired and worn looking and could use some new furniture and the rest of the space looks well used.  They have some good but not great food (on the New Orleans scale) they do for the catering at large events so that probably makes it great food anywhere else but in NOLA it is pretty average food.  If you are looking to book an event I would certainly suggest taking a look at the exact space you are booking as there is some range in the conditions of the event rooms here and for the rate being charged you might be able to find a nicer space at a similar price and use that leverage to negotiate a cheaper rate for the more "lived in" looking rooms.

We'll return.

review: My experience at Fishtown Brewpub last weekend was not great. A group of us were out for my birthday and we were hopping from place to place. I had this spot bookmarked because it's new and I thought it would be cool for us all to check it out together for the first time.   We walked in and there were some people seated at the bar, but for the most part the restaurant was fairly empty. Someone else in our party had already locked down a table in the back, so we made our way there. Maybe I misread the body language, but I swear the bartender gave our group some major side-eye as we passed by. It was just a weird reception and vibe that I wouldn't expect from a relatively new business.   Our server was very sweet and brought us all waters and menus. Mostly everyone was stoked on trying some of the house beers, but when we ordered we were informed that none of them were ready yet. So everyone came up with a second choice, but then it took a really long time before everyone at the table had their drinks (a couple cocktails but mostly draughts). We decided at this point to call it and move on to the next place. I'd be interested to get back at some point for a revisit once the house beers are available, and I hope to have a better experience.

review: Sometimes, all it takes is hearing a word before I abandon all other thoughts and lust after said item. For example, bubble baths, shoes, wine, eyelash extensions and, most recently, hoagies.   My mom said the word to me on Saturday morning and for the remainder of the weekend, all I could think about was sinking my teeth into turkey, cheese and fresh veggies on a delicious roll. I've been trying to watch what I eat so I came up with a game plan and allowed myself to indulge - but only if I saved half of whatever sandwich awaited for dinner.   I wanted to try a place that was new-to-me, and with a variety of factors to take into consideration, I eventually landed at Jake's. The menu was filled with mostly hot and very pork-heavy offerings, and there were only two choices for cold sandwiches, but both had turkey. I opted for the schmeer: roasted turkey, sharp provolone, baby spinach, red onion, roasted peppers and garlic spread (i.e. mayo) on a long roll. I say I hate mayo but at this point I think I'm just kidding myself. If a mayo-based sauce is called spread or aioli, I'm all in.  I got that bad boy home and, true to my word, wrapped up half and tossed it in the fridge for later. The next ten or so minutes were spent in heaven, if heaven were a sandwich. It was soclose to my favorite turkey sandwich from Paesano's. More field testing is in order.    A note to the owners: the menu on the website is impossible to read! I thought it was just on the iPhone but looking at the site from my laptop yields the same straining, unless you click on the pdf.   Also, for those with extremely large appetites, Jake's has this crazy challenge where if you eat a dump truck's worth of food in less than 45 minutes, you get your food for free (and the indigestion I can only assume comes with) and your picture on the website. If that's your kind of thing.
