review: Great new restaurant on the near north side!  I found some free street parking next to the building since the parking lot in the back was already full. Be aware that 22nd street is a two-way street while Delaware in only one way north.  As I walked up 22nd, I noticed that they have a separate carry out window for walk up customers.  Once inside the building from the entrance on Delaware, the bar is against the wall in front of you with the kitchen behind it.  The take out window is to the right of the bar.  There was a blend of tables and numerous seats at the bar.  A couple televisions were on the walls, but as of this early review, not much decoration.  I grabbed a seat at the bar and selected one of their local draft brew options.  They also serve wine and cocktails and some additional beer in cans.  To start my dinner, I went with a cup of Bone Broth.  This tasty soup is served in a large bowl that has edamame and bean sprouts on the bottom.  The broth is served in a small tea kettle and is poured over the veggies.  The flavor is deep and savory with a bit of heat on the tale end of the flavor profile.  The sprouts maintained a nice crunch despite the hot broth.  The only negative was that the sprouts, when not herded into a nice bunch, tended to be a little long to eat gracefully, but hopefully, they will give them a nice chop before serving in the future to make it more user friendly.    I also ordered the Egg Rolls.  Unlike any I have had before, these crispy rolls sliced on the bias were filled with large pieces of monkfish and served with ginger scallion dashi for dipping that also adds a bit of saltiness to the flavor combo.  Excellent!  Moist inside, crunchy outside and delicious flavor.  Definitely would order these again!  For my entree, I ordered the Tonkatsu.  This dish consists of Fisher Farms pork tenderloin (about 6 oz) pounded flat and lightly breaded.  The finished piece is then sliced into several strips that are just a bit large to eat gracefully with chopsticks.  (Don't be afraid to ask for silverware if you aren't up for the challenge!)  The tenderloin was thin, but retained its moisture while the breading was crisp!  Some sort of magic must be involved because I have rarely seen meat like this both moist and crispy.  Excellent technique here!  The entree comes in an ornamental dish that has soy sriracha sauce on the bottom with a slice of white bread then the tenderloin and some pickles and onions.  On the side are the condiments:  green chili paste and fish sauce cucumbers.  You can either dip the tenderloin or spread some of the chili paste on top.  Slide your tenderloin around the bottom of the bowl to pick up some of the sriracha, then be sure to add some of the pickles and onions as you take your bite.  Wow!   It's at that moment you realize there are toasted sesame seeds sprinkled across the top of the meat and the flavors are vibrant.  Before you take your next bite, try some of the cucumber to enjoy the acid component of flavor.  It's all good!    Although the menu is fairly limited in quantity, I find myself wanting to come back soon and try some more options.  I didn't ask how often the menu items will change, but I recommend getting here soon so that you can enjoy some great Asian flavors.  p.s.  This is the sister restaurant of Shoefly Public House down the street.  The same husband and wife team are behind both places.  Review #189

review: Good Mood Restaurant sits in the back of the large commercial center on North Olden Avenue, Ewing, New Jersey.  Although there is a very large parking area around it, the proximity of a Planet Fitness and nursing school in session, makes finding a spot somewhat problematic on school days.  Still, after cruising for a few minutes, something opened up fairly nearby.    Good Mood has been open since February.  It has a fairly large footprint, with plenty of tables for a large crowd.  It only serves breakfast, brunch and lunch.  Service is friendly, and they do a brisk takeout trade. The menu is traditional American egg oriented dishes, with a nod to wraps and Mexican options, as well as burgers available at all times. The space is bright and clean, and when you order coffee, they give you a half full thermal pitcher with java, so you don't have to ask for refills.  Nice touch.   My breakfast wrap consisted of a large tortilla filled with scrambled eggs, green chili, chorizo sausage, onion and cheese.  It came with a large side of home fries that were crisp and tasty. The wrap was filling and satisfying, especially after a few drops of Tabasco were added.  Definitely enough to allow me to skip lunch today. Always a good thing.   Everything about Good Mood is solid. For the price, a little more pepper and chorizo would have been a positive. Nonetheless, it is a strong addition to the locale where it can be hard to find a decent meal first thing in the morning.   Wish them luck.

review: OMG! I think I need to add Louie's to my speed dial.  Saturday night both my partner and I were getting home late from work,  I was arriving home first so I was responsible for ordering dinner. He said, he wanted to be surprised, so that was my challenge.   I knew ordering from our regular Chinese or pizza joints would not be a surprise, so what could I do. I flipped through our take out menus/coupons and found Louie's. I knew this place from passing it when I went to my local Tan Co., and thought we'd expand our experience and try something new.  I'm a fan of St Louis style pizza, so when ordering from Louie's I stepped outside my safety zone and ordered their, "Chicago Original Deluxe". We were totally blown away, the combination of chicken, fresh spinach, bacon and tomato was amazing. The Italian seasonings in the sauce and Louie's secret blend of mozzarella cheese made every slice of pizza a masterpiece. I'll still love my St. Louis Style pizza, but I have now become a bi-pizzal.  I also ordered their Original Spicy chicken wings, and House Salad. The salad was "A" typical pizza parlor salad, little larger and more generous with the toppings (love my black olives). Their Original Spicy chicken wings were bone sucking good and hot enough. I could not imagine what the "Extreme Heat" would have been.    The phone customer service was excellent, very friendly and helpful in determining if I lived within delivery area. I was given a delivery time of 45 minuets which was perfect with my plans. Delivery was quicker, made it in 30 and delivery person continued the excellent service.  My partner was surprised, we were surprised by the quality, so my challenge was completed successfully. We will be calling Louie's again and again.

review: You can read it in the owner's statement.  This is a family owned business that primarily caters and makes special order cakes and related baked items for just about any occasion.   But even though the statement refers to the six family members who work here and are owners, the meaning of family runs much deeper than just words.  I had the pleasure of being introduced to Marsha Q and her mother at a recent Yelp event (Yelp's 15th Birthday Bash.)  After a brief introduction about herself and her family business, we all got to ask questions.  I asked about being able to walk in and buy fresh baked items and was told yes, I could stop by, but that there would only be a limited supply of things for sale to the general public.  However, if I wanted to get something specific, to be sure to call in advance to make sure they had the availability to complete an order.  The owners were gracious in their demeanor and the treats they brought to the event were quickly devoured.  One of the things I try to do is make a follow up visit to vendors who provide free goodies at Yelp events as a way to say thank you for their stories and generosity.  So, with my wife and three of my grandchildren in tow, we stopped by on a Wednesday morning and both Marsha and her mother were working that day.  I let them know that I appreciated their participation in the event and they seemed genuinely flattered.  Each of the grandkids picked a Halloween cake pop and though there wasn't much else set out, Marsha let me know she had just taken out a batch of sugar cookies and some cupcakes.  I asked for some of each.  She even asked what type of frosting I wanted on the cakes (butter cream).  She went in the back and prepped them and boxed them for our trip home.  While she worked in the back, her mother shared stories about the display cakes that were in the front of the space.  She also reminded us of how they once made 8000 cupcakes for when Indy hosted the SuperBowl!    Just a note:  The bakery isn't set up as a standard bakery retail place with large counters of items on display.  Rather, it is a little random with items over here, and some over there.  But you just have to ask what's available.  If you are willing to take a chance, then drop in.  Otherwise call in advance.  Before I wrap up, I mentioned how family was mentioned in the owner's business statement.  When I walked in, I was greeted and made to feel like I was part of the family.  They obviously love what they do and wanted to make sure that my family was happy with the items we chose.  That's something you don't see in a lot of places.  Certainly not in the big chain bakeries or the ones who are living on their reputations.  Marsha and her family bake with love and it shines through in every bite.    Review #3249

review: This quirky grouping of bronze sculptures is actually 3 sculptures that were on the site during the 2005 Art Strategies public art promotion with sculptor Tom Otterness.  Back then, 25 bronze sculptures were placed primarily along public ways in downtown Indianapolis.  The Otterness collection was one of the first of several annual public art initiatives sponsored in Indy.  The largest of the three sculptures is titled "Free Money" and was sculpted in 2001.  The dimensions are 107.5 x 69.5 x 84 inches.  I wonder how many tourists observe that the base of the statue is a bag of money?  The smallest of the sculptures is titled "Male Tourist" from 1999.  Its dimensions are 27 x 21 x 10 inches.  The male is left holding the bags for a third sculpture.  The third piece is titled "Female Tourist" and is a slightly taller figure taking a photograph, apparently of the "Free Money" sculpture.  The third figure is 34 x 16 x 14 inches.  If you look closely at one of the attached photos, you can see the spot where the third figure stood before being removed due to an act of theft/vandalism.  However, the statue is restored and completes the three pieces again.  What impressed me the most about the collection when it was in town was that the figures often appeared benign, almost childlike at first glance.  However, several made dramatic social commentary.  My favorite was "Big Big Penny" which was located on the steps of the War Memorial along with "Educating the Rich on Globe" and "Miser".  I recall having several interesting discussions as people stopped by and began noticing the details of the sculpture and how they related to the role of money, power, and the social classes. review: Even on a cold and blustery day, I couldn't help but enjoy my time at this unique gem of a park on the far east side of Greenwood.  Just over a mile east of I-65 at the Greenwood exit, this park is nestled in a neighborhood and has lots to offer.  On the north end, there is a nice lawn area with a paved walking path that I would estimate to be about a quarter mile.  There are very cool looking pergolas on each side with benches near by for resting.  On the west end is Chandler Amphitheater with a stage area on the outside of the path and stone seating terraced into the landscape inside the path.  A few trees have also been planted/dedicated on the southwest end of the lawn for future shade.  To the west of the lawn is new pond for runoff from the neighborhoods that border the park.  South of the pond is fenced dog park with equipment for dogs and owners who want to train them.  And there is a shelter inside the dog park for owners who want to rest while the dogs run to their hearts content!  There is a wooded area with a barely noticeable path along the dog park fence.  It looks like there is every intention of keeping the woods natural.  But hidden within the woods (there is a driveway that leads back to a small parking lot) is a court for basketball and the Big Elm Play Area.  The play area is different from the other parks I've visited.  Sure, it is similar in that it has an elevated area with slides and things to climb on, but it reminds me of a two-angled fort.  There are swings too.  Of course, lots of shade is nearby from the trees surrounding the park just a short distance away.  The park is in great shape (with the exception of the information kiosks which have not weathered well).  This looks like a great addition to the neighborhood and I bet they are keeping it quiet so that they can have free run of the place!  Review #721

review: My wife and I arranged to meet our daughter downtown for lunch at the newly opened restaurant.  Set at the corner of  Market Street and Meridian, the main entrance is found on Market about half a block west of Monument Circle.  For long time Indy residents, you may recognize the former Blocks Department store.  The restaurant only uses a small portion of the once huge department area.  The scale here is much smaller without the opulent decor of the previous tenant.  Upon entering, you see the small dining area and bar.  Additional seating is outside on the expanded sidewalk area.  There was table side service, but the waitress was also the hostess and worked behind the counter too, so there were some times when it was difficult to find any staff in the dining room if we needed assistance.  We noted the the music was cranked way too loud for the small dining area though I will compliment the staff for making an adjustment suitable to make our dining conversation possible.   Despite the small number of staff working, I will say the food was delivered properly and without much delay.  I thought it was seasoned well, but did find that the two dishes ordered with chicken were cooked too long and seemed dry.  I was able to try some of my daughter's shrimp skewer and enjoyed IT.  Not rubbery, just a pleasant bite.  The prices were higher than most of the downtown options) nd the wait  could be improved to be competitive so that diners aren't pressured to leave just to make it back to work on time.  If  you are downtown within walking distance, I recommend  that option on nice days.  Some street parking was available and some parking garages aren't too far away, but on the day I went the doors to the garages  in the building weren't working.  So allow plenty of time for traffic and finding a spot.  I am glad that a landmark building is finding some continued use.  Hopefully this restaurant will fine-tune some of the items I pointed out and will be successful in drawing customers back o this once popular spot. Review #3963.

review: Location, location, location.  We were boating and were able to find a spot along the dock outside of Wolfie's to pull up to and walk up the ramp to the restaurant.  It was a busy day on the water and so the restaurant was pretty full, especially the outdoor seating which we managed to get one of the last tables.  We were seated promptly and our wait staff did a good job of bringing out the beverages right away.  When our appetizers arrived, they came with extra mini plates so that the appetizer could be shared.  The Brussels Sprouts looked appealing, but were definitely undercooked (which gives them a funky smell.)  I like mine crispy with a bit of crunch.  These were chewy.  So, no five from me.  The main courses were pretty good, but my pan crusted chicken was very thin, which made it a bit dry.  Could have used some additional seasoning which the outside tables didn't have.  But the portions were generous and there were lots of options to choose from.  So, nobody left hungry, but just a tad underwhelmed on the flavor. review: Unofficial Yelp Events (UYEs) are always just about as good as a party among social media friends can be, and this was no exception.  The meet up at Tired Hands Fermentaria was my first opportunity to visit this well known brewery in Ardmore, Pa., and to sample its wares.  I've got to say that sitting at a table with about 20 peeps, surrounded by the acoustically challenged corrugated iron-roofed warehouse and close to the stainless steel fermenting tanks where the magic is done, made for a loud amplified afternoon. Yet, sitting with folks that I look forward to seeing, and the new ones that I am about to meet, made it bearable.   Arriving late, I was still in time to find a seat and order a Shamabalac mystical ale and a veggie Banh Mi wrap.  Our server was cool and competent, keeping everyone in suds and sustenance, while allowing us to maintain separate tabs.  Quite a trick that she handled with aplomb.   The drink was blond and had remarkable fruity notes.  Liked it, and ordered a couple more. The Vietnamese interpreted sandwich was hardly banh mi at all, given that it was in a wheat wrap rather than a French baguette.  True, the daikon, carrot, tofu and siriracha were present, but the concept was wrong.  Better to just called it Vietnamese inspired, and leave it at that. It was okay, but the image in my head was abandoned unfilled.   Truth be told, I am not a beer maven, although I enjoy it in small creative doses.  Bourbon is my downfall.  Still, I see what people like about Tired Hands, and brewery clubs in general.  The capacity crowd on this late Saturday afternoon, certainly did, too.

review: Tuesday Morning is not a pretty store. It is not merchandised well and at times it is a little cluttered. However, all that can be over looked when you find the perfect item for your home at an insanely low price.   TM is one of those stores you have to shop frequently. The inventory is constantly changing, so every time you shop it is like an entirely new adventure. There are times I stop by and walk out empty handed, but I know the next time it will be as if I hit the Powerball.   You'll find inexpensive gadgets and small appliances for the kitchen and decorative items for the living room. My last visit I found a Queen size set of sheets that included two extra pillowcases and it was the color and thread count that I prefer. Like I said, sometimes you hit the Powerball. Having four pillows on my bed made this set a winner.  Tuesday Morning even has a great selection for both kinds of children; two and four legged. They have an excellent selection of dog beds and bowls and for the two legged toddlers they had an amazing variety of toys.   I have always found the staff here to be friendly. So many times the staff at discount stores can be on the gruff side of service, but not here. They have always been perky and upbeat when I have shopped.   My advice to you, is shop TM often and search out those bargains. Shopping here will make your gift giving dollars go further, meaning more dollars for you to spend on yourself.

review: I'm taking golf lessons through the community college and the classes meet here. A very convenient location and much more then just golf. Even though they have a large lot, parking here reminds me of Christmas at the mall. As one car backs out of a space, three cars appear out of nowhere wanting that space.   Have three more weeks of class and looking forward to signing up for the next level. review: I popped into Kei for lunch yesterday and it was solid. Everyone working was super nice and I loved that our server was on top of refilling water glasses through the entire meal. I typically like this starter a lot but might not order it again at Kei for that reason. My dining partner had shrimp shumai which looked really tasty.   The lunch special comes with two rolls and soup or salad. I opted for soup which was nice but the salad across from me looked delicious - Kei went above and beyond a simple bowl of iceberg and offered what appeared to be a beautiful starter salad.   The avocado tuna and crunchy spicy tuna rolls I ordered were massive! Two was more than enough after the soup and yellowtail starter. Next time, I'll skip the starter and go straight to the lunch special. I'll definitely return for lunch, hopefully soon!

review: It's amazing how a year and a pandemic can change things. My most recent visit wasn't what it use to be. I truly was disappointed.   A friend and I were out running errands on a Wednesday in December and stopped by for lunch. We were seated on the back patio. I stopped to use the bathroom before joining my friend on the patio. When I entered the patio, I was hit in the face with a strong odor. The bathroom I just used smelled better then the patio. I have a sensitive nose. It didn't seem to bother my friend, so I kept it to myself, but it did effect my experience.   We each had a draft beer to accompany our sandwiches. I had the Cheesy Bacon Burger and my friend had the Buffalo Chicken Sandwich. Both of our sammies came with a side of fries. Both of us enjoy crinkle fries, so we were pleased that is the type Seamus serves and their position is always generous.   My friend was pleased with her Buffalo Chicken, but my burger was not up to the level I am use to getting at Seamus. The grade of beef seemed to be different and my burger was over cooked. I also could not get beyond the odor, I should have spoken up and moved inside.   In closing, I'll say the customer service wasn't what it normally is, but it was obvious they were short staffed, so I will not judge them on that.   I haven't given up on Seamus, I'll still go back and hope for a better outcome.

review: Wow - I honestly can NOT believe that nobody reviewed this venerable (old, ancient, classic, etc.) Media institution.  "The" Townhouse has held countless High School reunions (even weddings), corporate luncheons and functions in their numerous party rooms (and the large "ball room" downstairs).  I attended a small (25 people) dinner last night - but before it began we sat at the (again) classic bar downstairs where Barbara kept those refreshing Arnold Palmers coming!  She is a doll.  (And the $2.00 off each drink at happy hour (4-6 PM) and free munchies were a plus.  They also offer $3.00 bar snacks - but we saved room for our meal upstairs.  Once upstairs I had a ball looking at all those classic photographs from events long past (The 25th class reunion of the Class of '42, and even a picture of Mr. Biddle - when he was about 20 - from Drinker Biddle & Reath).  Nicki - our server has worked at D'Ignazios for 40 years!  We started our "set" meal with a very fresh green salad.  I had the tasty lobster ravioli and others had chicken or a veggie option.  Dessert was an uber-rich flourless chocolate cake.  It was drizzled in a raspberry sauce and tasted like eating fudge.  It was OK, but a bit much for me.  Other folks RAVED about it.  So, yes, I would definitely come here on my own for dinner - or book an event here.  They are "old" pros.    One possible con?  It is an OLD place - so some of the decor is really authentic - so if you want a more polished look (like for a wedding?  I would, personally never do a wedding here) you may be turned off.  For a High School reunion or Corporate event?  PERFECT!!!!!

review: Ahh sweet review #700, it's only fitting that I review the spiritual heart of my city for this auspicious occasion.  St. Louis Cathedral is one of the most photographed buildings in New Orleans (along with the Bourbon Street sign) which is sort of perfect as it shows the dichotomy of our city.  We know how to have a party and yet we know the importance of spirituality (and repentance).  Whenever I'm in the area, I stop in for a moment or two and offer a prayer to my two very Roman Catholic grandmothers and light candles in their honor.  My Granny was convinced that a candle at the cathedral carried more weight than a candle from another church.  The church is a beautiful example of early architecture and it definitely deserves a tour and a donation!  But remember it is still a functioning church, so if you are visiting be respectful of those who are there to pray.  Check out the gift shop while you're there.

review: The menu looks to have prices that are in line with other area Chinese restaurants at first with the exceptions of the drinks which are at $3.00 (and they also didn't have any hot or iced tea available yet which is very un-Chinese).  My Eggdrop soup was good but they had already put the crunchy wontons in it which had gotten soggy and I generally don't like to have those in my soup anyway so it would be better if they left those on the side for my taste.  The Shrimp Wontons had a good taste but were a bit of a small portion for the price on the menu but... they had the wrong price listed so it was a decent deal for $8 instead of $10.  The Dry Chili Chicken seemed to be a really small serving size for dinner and it didn't even come with rice (maybe they forgot to bring it?) so that made this dish not very competitive with other area Chinese options.  Fried rice is much more expensive here than at other area joints so I'm not sure if you have to order the rice separately for the higher price or if should come with an entree?  Overall this place is brand new and just getting up and started so hiccups should be expected.  The menu is still very concise for the moment and they plan to add combos for lunch starting later in the week.  It was quite crowded during my dinner visit like many new places tend to be when first opening so it will be interesting to see how this restaurant develops.  Service was 5 stars but the food I had was certainly more of 3 star experience and the prices certainly made it much less of a value for the quantity along with the lack of rice or other items being included with dinner entrees.  There are a lot of Chinese options in the area so hopefully this place can find their niche and get their secret sauce worked out.

review: If you like your food with a bit of spicy heat, why not try a Flamme Burger!  I was able to find a spot in the busy parking lot outside the restaurant and once I entered, the hostess/manager (?) suggested I sit wherever I liked and she would follow with a menu and place setting.  I chose the dining area over the bar which was surprisingly full at lunch time.  I was greeted by my waitress and after getting my beverage, she took my order for the Flamme Burger and an upgraded fry option, the Truffle Parmesan Fries.  Although they offer a number of dips and aiolis for the fries, I chose not to add any since I wasn't sure what would go with the upgrade I selected.  While waiting, the servers came around to all the tables and passed out fresh baked chocolate chip cookies!  Not sure why since I didn't see them on the menu, but it was a nice surprise while waiting for my meal.    Before long, the burger came out first and then the fries a couple minutes later. Not that big a deal since I was by myself, but not what I would normally expect at a restaurant.  The burger came on my choice of bun (whole grain for me) and was served with a steak knife to facilitate cutting it in half.  I ordered the burger medium per the recommendation of the hostess.  The burger (I'm guessing 6 oz) was a bit pink in the middle, but did have a good char on the outside from the cooking over flam(m)e, so it was moist/juicy but had that nice grilled flavor.  The burger came with a gruyere cheese and applewood bacon, and also was topped with serrano peppers and "flamme sauce" which is like a siracha mayo (I think).  So, with the multi layered flavor, there was a steady build up of spicy heat.  I didn't think it got too hot, but it was definitely noticeable.  Very tasty!  The fries were very plentiful and served in a paper lined metal basket.  I could see the bits of parmesan sprinkled generously over the fries throughout the mix, not just on the top.  However, the fries were a bit on the wilted/soggy side.  Maybe they didn't let the truffle oil get quite hot enough to give a crispness to the fries, but for some reason, the texture was a bit disappointing.  The flavor was very nice and I didn't think I needed any sauce.  Note that if you eat fries with your fingers, you will probably get parmesan bits on your finger tips, so be aware of that so you don't accidentally touch your clothes.  The service was friendly and thorough, with refreshed water and check processing as well.  Overall, a fine meal that was different from most burger places and tasty enough to warrant the premium burger prices.  I would gladly return if I was in the area.  Review #2185

review: Dos Amores (Two Loves) Mexican Cuisine is a strictly take out stall in the Village of Newtown Farmers Market. Along with the rest of the shops it is only open Thursday through Saturday, so there is only a small window for getting in/out with a good sampling of their south of the border offerings. Most are of the self contained variety, like enchiladas, quesadillas, empanadas and chile rellenos, that can be prepared in advance, kept cool and then heated at home in the microwave or oven. You can also eat in the market within the common dining area at the back of the store.   That is what I did. I ordered beef and chicken empanadas, and asked them to be heated for consumption in the market. That took all of 3 minutes. They were handed to me in a paper boat with small containers of salsa and sour cream. Other sides were available, but as it was my first dive into their delectables, I opted to forego any additions.   Both empanadas were very good. The dough was crisp and strong enough to stay together as I bit through them. The chicken and ground beef were both nicely spiced, and I was also able to pour more salsa inside through the bite hole, and keep it contained until next munch. The beef was cooked with more chili powder, and had a warmer profile than the chicken. Still, I enjoyed them both for their freshness and authenticity. Like everything else in this market, prices are high. You pay the same as if you were dining in a full service restaurant.   The atmosphere of the farmers market is entertaining with all the Amish/Mennonite vendors dressed in their traditional garb and speaking colloquially. That is certainly worth the premium paid, as it is the only place in town where there is a real cultural exchange. Admittedly, Dos Amores lacks the Pennsylvania Dutch accent, but their Spanish makes up for that.   I really should come here more often just to step away from modern times for a little while and enjoy all the interesting grub.

review: I make fun of it a lot, but Whole Foods does serve a purpose. They have a lot of organic "high end" kind of food, and if that's your thing, then this place is heaven.  This Whole Foods is like any other grocery store, only a little more pretentious. Hey, they have the right to be. They sell gourmet nuts and have fresh made sushi in store. You walk in and the overwhelming sweet smell of the bakery and the fresh cut flowers combines to form an olfactory pleasing combination that you could probably bottle and sell, if you had the wherewithal. In their parking garage they (naturally) have a place where you can plug in your electric car and charge it while you shop. I didn't visit the butcher shop, but I can only imagine that Whole Foods' steaks are marinated in the (joyful) tears of angels until the meat practically slices itself.  One thing I will say is that this place has a pretty impressive beer and wine selection. If you are looking for rare spirits, start your search here.   I might return to Whole Foods, but don't tell the people that work here that I sometimes drink orange juice straight out of the container or that I have been known to fall asleep without brushing my teeth. I would surely be blacklisted.

review: I really enjoyed my visit for lunch.  The staff was friendly and the menu had a wide variety of options, including lunch specials.  I started with a cup of hot tea (yes, by the cup, not a tea pot).  Since I've been eating a lot of sushi lately, I decided to go with the Hibachi Salmon instead.  It comes with a choice of clear soup or side salad (salad for me), about a cup of fried rice, and a generous serving of delicious sauteed veggies.  The salmon had a nice glaze that was quite tasty too.  The serving of salmon was a little small, but considering how expensive salmon can be, it was reasonably portioned.  The dish also comes with small sides of Yum Yum sauce and Ginger sauce.  The place is a little tricky to get to since you cannot pull in directly from Emerson.  There is a stoplight just north of the restaurant that allows you to pull in an make a few right turns behind the shop to get to the parking out front.  The only negative was that the dish took a bit longer than I expected to come out considering the place wasn't that busy when I placed my order.  I can see waiting a half hour causing some problems for folks who have to get back to work.  Review #1927

review: My sister and I were walking around Haddonfield after Christmas and we came across William Heritage. Things have really changed since I lived in nearby Collingswood ten years ago! Both towns used to be dry and now there are breweries and even wine tasting rooms. I would have loved this when I lived in the area!   We walked inside to check it out and I asked about tastings and was told that they were fully booked that day. I was mostly just curious; my sister is pregnant and I wasn't planning on tasting alone. I didn't receive the warmest welcome from their employee and when I asked about a particular wine I was told it was good. The entire exchange was honestly a bit awkward until I made it clear that I wasn't planning on sticking around for long. I asked if I could taste before purchasing a bottle and the other employee who was helping a customer turned around and said absolutely. I asked about two different reds. One was a blend of CA and NJ grapes. I haven't had much luck with NJ wines in the past and since I didn't want to take up too much time, I sipped just that wine, thought it was solid and purchased a bottle.   The tasting room itself was really cute; up there with some of the prettier ones in Healdsburg and Napa. Will I be returning? TBD.

review: We have a new buffet in town, Color me surprised.  It's near Country side mall so it should do well. Getting in and out may prove difficult, but once you figure it out, it's easy peasy.   We came to eat lunch on a Sunday, there was one cashier, the line was nearly out the door, the process was time consuming and slow.  The eatery wasn't that busy.   Once we were processed, we were told to sit anywhere, so we chose a table in the middle and sat. The hubby let me go up first.  I chose vegie soup which was meh (Very canned tomato flavour) the salad was tasty, and the other veg I chose was good. The fried chicken most certainly tasted of Peanut oil, but there were no peanut allergy warnings anywhere, this could be an issue if anyone has an allergy. review: Okay, this is one of those places where I loved the idea but not quite the execution.  I attended a happy hour here with a few friends. While we were there there was a shift change. The first waitress got some people's orders who were there before myself and then it all turned over to another waitress. As nice as the second waitress was, she was just slow. There weren't a lot of people there and it took forever for her to come and get drink orders and then come and get food orders. We were seated outside, so maybe that had something to do with it, but like I said, the place wasn't packed.  I decided to get an order of the appetizer tuna tartine as well as an order of the queso fundido. Appetizers are half off during happy hour, so I was happy to take advantage of that. The tuna tartine was delicious! It was raw tuna mixed with peppers and spices and I loved it. The queso fundido was okay, but it didn't knock my socks off. It went from melty to "stiff" pretty quickly and didn't have a ton of flavor to it. Some places add spices and peppers to theirs, but this just seemed to be melted cheese.  I had one frozen margarita which was delicious! I was planning on having more than one, but after tasting the strength of my first, I decided one was probably enough. I liked the outside seating area, as the weather was fairly nice and we were in a nice shady spot.  I want to go back for dinner to get a better idea of how the service normally is here.

review: This is a franchised large format Japanese Hibachi house that also offers sushi and a few "fusion" offerings from China and Thailand.  This style restaurant seems to be coming into fashion on the East Coast, although it is more played out on the Left Coast.   This one is apparently under new management, and they are attempting to make the facility more comfortable and attractive.  They have done a good job on the creature comforts, and the service is also attentive, except for the minor language difficulties in understanding each other through the Korean and South Jerzee accents.    I was the guest this night, and my hostess did all the ordering.  I opted for the sushi side of the joint, although the Hibachi room was more active and colorful, especially when they performed their volcano show with the ball of fire shooting into the air.  Luckily, we could see that from the safe distance on the far side of the room.    The Clear Soup was quite good as part of the dinner package.  The Sashimi platter (Deluxe?) was ample with a nice variety of well sliced fresh fish.  They all had good taste, but I would have preferred them slightly cooler.  I tasted all the offerings, but was not feeling compelled to finish them.  The Rolls (Sorry. The names were not disclosed to me) were okay, but not exciting.  Typical sushi rolls, but why the chef put cream cheese in it is beyond me.  Do they even have that in Japan?  This is not something I would consider ordering on my own.  Maybe this is what is popular in this part of South Jersey, or because it is close to Philly, cream cheese is a concession to local culture. Fish and cream cheese? No. Thank you!  I was happy to have dinner with a friend, and content to let her treat in return for something I handled for her.  Still, something more authentically Japanese would tempt me more than this Korean version of an Americanized Japanese Hibachi/Sushi store.  It just didn't hang together for me.

review: There is no doubt that the Tanner Brothers Store that sits at the intersection of Almshouse and Hatboro Roads in Warminster, Pa., could use an extreme makeover to improve the shopping cart traffic patterns, and modernize the check out, but if that were done it would likely sacrifice all that it has been and continues to be.  What's that?  Only a well used, still functional, farm stand for the farm run by the family of that name for generations.  There wasn't a fraction of the population nor vehicular traffic in those days.  It was about the only game in town for fresh produce, dairy and other kitchen necessities before the Acmes, Clemens, and other grocery chains started pushing north into Bucks County.  Seen it this light, it is actually an anthropology museum with daily changing interactive exhibits.   Compared to those modern markers, Tanner Bros does suffer in the amenities department, but makes up for it with generally fresher produce, cheaper eggs, and excellent handmade ice cream.  Sure, as a convenience and secondary marketing attraction, it offers national brands on its shelves, and those things are not as competitively priced.  But, when we plan well, we hit Tanner's first, and then make a run to Giant or its ilk for everything else.  Makes us feel good to shop locally, and spend a little time in the past.    It's great to have large bins full of yams, corn, melons, leeks, etc., to touch and choose.  And, after lugging it all back to the car, to take a few more minutes to appreciate (and slowly consume) a great Butter Pecan Sugar Cone while watching the cows that manufactured the milk for it, lazily chewing their cud in preparation for the next milking.

review: Like Columbus, I've discovered something that others have discovered before me. Yes, like the New World, Three Happiness is pretty awesome.  I am always open to trying new places, especially if they happen to have Vietnamese food on the menu. I had passed this place bunches of times throughout my life on the Westbank and I always wondered about it. I finally decided to stop in.  First of all, don't be intimidated that this place is located in a super sketchy strip mall. Yes, there was a weird guy lurking outside of the place when I went. No, he didn't bother me. Just walk with purpose and you'll be fiiiiiine.  The atmosphere of this place is great. I love that it's wide open and you can even rent it out for parties! I went shortly after normal lunch hours, so it was empty when I got here. I seated myself and looked over the extensive menu.   You should know that this place has a lot of choices- both Chinese and Vietnamese. They have everything from classic Chinese dishes such as lo mein to Vietnamese yums like pho, vermicelli and banh mi. I already knew that I wanted some cold spring rolls and pho with rare beef, so that's what I had.  I love that the spring rolls come 4 to an order. It works out for sharing and guarantees that everyone gets their fill. The pho was great! I got the small bowl, which turned out to be perfect for lunch. The broth had a lot of flavor and there was a nice, generous serving of meat, which made it perfect.  I loved this place and I will definitely be back. They are closed Mondays, so be aware of that. I like that they have a huge menu, so they are sure to have something good that everyone would like.

review: I'm still very much a fan of Garces Trading Company. Armed with a pretty hefty gift card, my husband and I had a fantastic dinner on a recent Saturday night. The place was packed, so reservations are clearly a must for the weekend.   Our server was very knowledgeable about the wine list and made great suggestions. We shared a bunch of starters including some cheese and charcuterie, housemade mozzarella and olives. Olives are on so many menus as a small plate and don't differ much from place to place. Not at GTC: their olives were addictive. There were three types including a green sort that had a rich, almost cheesy flavor. I feel like our server said they were Castelvetranos but I can't be positive. Maybe it was just a super fresh batch, but they were incredible.   For dinner, I had to go with the steak frites. I couldn't decide on the sauce so our server suggested a sampling of all three, which was music to my ears! As always, this dish was a home run. My husband had the trout, which is always delicious as well.   We skipped dessert in favor of more wine and some espresso to finish. Looking forward to our next visit!

review: Yummy Asian (no relation to Yummy Sushi) is a surprisingly decent Chinese restaurant.  Their menu has a large Japanese Roll offering, but little actual sushi, nor Thai cuisine.  If you stick with the Chinese dishes, you should be quite satisfied.    We came in for a Friday dinner.  The house was nicely appointed.  The service was attentive.  We ordered the Walnut Shrimp, Beef & Chicken Hunan and a Dragon Roll.  The shrimp dish consisted of 8 or 9 Jumbos, Tempura breaded, with a sweet mayo sauce covering the entire pile of crustaceans.  It wasn't the best I ever had, but was still quite enjoyable.    The Hunan style beef and chicken was also well done.  This approach uses less straight ahead red chilis, and substitutes a mix of chili and black beans. It retains a lot of heat, but not the fire breathing kind.  The meat was tender and did not seem to have been frozen.    The Dragon Roll was only okay.  The small amount of fish within the construct of rice, avo, seaweed, etc., was not the freshest.  The ginger was colored orange, rather than the natural white, and the wasabi was likewise artificially dyed green.  Clearly, the sushi guy had gone to Sushi College and finished the basic course in slicing and rolling, but was not working with top ingredients.    My friends enjoyed the chance to speak with management in Mandarin, and that seemed reciprocal.  Probably don't get many organically grown Chinese stopping in.

review: Less impressed than I wanted to be - I am dithering between 3 and 4 stars - and here's why...  A colleague and I had a lunch reservation.  Service was good - friendly and courteous.  He had the (last one) "Blue Plate" special - a crabcake (one) and salad.  I chose the heirloom tomato salad with (one lump of) burrata and an EXCELLENT balsamic and EVOO drizzle.  We split an order of WAY OVERCOOKED duck fat fries.  Awful.  Greasy.  Salted.  Burned.  Mess.  My first bite of the salad was of a red tomato and it was rotten. Thankfully the rest of the salad was perfect.  The food is so close to being "as good as it gets" - in theory - but the puny portion size (my male colleague needed the fries as the crabcake plate was app sized.), rotten tomato bite and charred fries soured our experience. The burrata was the "real deal".  The ingredients are all great - they just need better execution.  Meanwhile, our male server was cheerful and terrific. He even took the fries off the check.  ($40 for lunch for 2 - no apps, no dessert, no booze).  Garces - I love ya - but JG needs some tweaking, please.

review: "The Home Of The Tacky Ashtray" is the way this dive bar describes itself.  I'm not a smoker and unfortunately with all the ashtray love this place can get smoky at night so that is a big minus for me.  The barstools are an entertaining sight to see and I won't describe them so you will have to see them yourself.  This place also makes some mighty tasty food and has some pretty great lunch specials that range from Southwestern influenced to NOLA classics like turtle soup.  They have some good burgers and other typical bar grub but the lunch specials typically kick it up a notch or two (or sometimes more).  They also frequently have live music and although the space is a bit tight for dancing they will move the tables out a bit more if there aren't too many people sitting in them.  I've always had a good time at the Rivershack and make it a point to keep it in my occasional rotation as both a good lunch spot and a fun nightlife/music venue.

review: Hong Kong Pearl is a mixed bag.  The facility is dark and dreary at high noon, giving the sensation of being in a 1940's movie.  Yet, the service is prompt and attentive, somewhat anomalous for a Chinese house.  The main courses are well prepared, with some attention to detail, but it takes a few shortcuts that diminish the overall quality of the meal.  The broth for the Wonton Soup is chokingly salty and a brownish tint that suggests use of bouillon with prepackaged salt, dye and possibly MSG to cut costs.  In a similar manner, the Fried Rice arrives artificially colored a dark tawny cast from its mass production earlier in the day. Both soup and rice are vastly inferior to the prime attraction, but as they are served with practically every meal, the overall result is "mixed."    On the other hand, the General Tso's Chicken was quite good in the context of a suburban Americanized Chinese shop.  It used chicken that had not been frozen long, if at all, a pleasant coating, and a sauce that used correct spices to attain the right sweet/hot spot that makes for a happy General. It even had whole chili peppers in the dish.  That was a big positive.   While I would not rush back to Hong Kong Pearl, it was certainly a decent place for lunch.  If they would eliminate the problems with the soup and rice, and attempt to make them the right way - with a long simmering stock and just in time fried rice, it could be an exceptional experience for this part of the world.

review: My 700th review!  You know that I had to come back to an old favorite. There is finally a Felipe's in the booming Mid City area and I couldn't be happier. I don't make it to Mid City often, but I am so happy to see this area developing.  So, what about the restaurant? I came on opening night because I am a huge Felipe's nerd and I wanted to show my support. I was happy that I was seated at the bar pretty quickly. Yes, service took a while, but it's the first night so I didn't expect it to be super speedy. Lord, I was feeling sorry for some of the bartenders because some of the folks coming in where just plain RUDE. Complaining about the wait when they could plainly see that A LOT of people were waiting. Come on. Don't be THAT guy.  I ordered an al pastor taco salad with a side of queso. It took a while, but when I finally got my food, it was so good. All of the ingredients were nice and fresh and I had no complaints.  I will definitely be back to this Felipe's location. One of the things that this location seems to have over the other two is the parking. There is plenty of it in a well lit lot, so that may make the difference between me coming to this location or the S. Miro one (that lot is SO small). The staff was super nice. PJ was my bartender/waiter and he was putting up with A LOT of rude people and handling it all with a smile. They still have a few kinks to work out, but I definitely enjoyed my meal here.

review: Munchie's Café was recommended to me by the phlebotomist who drew my blood for pre-op testing at Penn Med last week. I asked for a place to have a quick breakfast after fasting since midnight. She advised that Munchie's was popular with the staff because of a broad menu and reasonable prices. As she had just been expert in hitting an artery on the first attempt, I figured she'd be accurate on food choices as well.   This long/deep shop sits just off the southeast corner of 7th and Chestnut. Ordering is done at the counter, and delivered to the table. I really felt the need for coffee stronger than for sustenance, so I ordered a breakfast wrap and large java. I got to pour the joe myself at the coffee service table, and sipped while waiting for the food. The drink was decent industrial strength drip that lost its joy of living as it cooled. Became more bitter the longer it sat. The wrap of bacon, egg and cheese in wheat, was just okay.  The bacon was unrecognizable, and had a odd taste. Perhaps, it was beef or turkey bacon without designation.   So, while the grub served to abate my caffeine and hunger gnawings, it was not something I would return for. It was average at best, although the prices were about right for what was provided. There are far superior places in the neighborhood to bring mind, body and soul up to speed.

review: I am not positive, but I am fairly certain that Moonlight was the first restaurant that I experienced as a child.  I remember all the special occasions,  we celebrated here enjoying the Talk-N-Chic, which is their house secret, trademarked recipe for fried chicken. It has been passed down 4 generations and it is so good I'd be tempted to marry into the family just to get the recipe.   Living in Saint Louis now, Moonlight is close, but yet so far away. I agree with George O. and wish they'd open a location on the west side of the river. However, with family still on this side of the river, I will coordinate my visits around lunch or dinner time to satisfy my fried chicken cravings.   Our recent lunch was no disappointment, as with every visit memories floated through my head. We ordered two 2 Piece Platters; one with two thighs and fries  and the other a wing and breast with a baked potato. All the pieces were huge, crispy golden brown and juicy.  The fries were crispy and the baked potato was baked throughout. As a bonus, you can order a small side of chicken livers with your dinner, which we did. I am not a liver fan, but here at Moonlight is another story. When those livers are breaded in the family secret and fried to perfection, I become a fan.   Let me regress for a moment, and talk about our salads.  More importantly the dressing. Their house dressing is Ramon, which is the off spring a Caesar and Mayfair. This is a dressing that should be on your local grocers shelves, not that stuff from PH. Along with the salad they serve up a basket filled with warm, thick sliced Italian bread and whipped butter.   The service here is always stellar. Best way to describe it would be "down home friendly". They are attentive and know how to hustle. When your order of chicken is ready, it is out to your table in no time flat. Lana took care of us on our last visit and when I found out she'd been there 32 years, she and I strolled down memory lane.   In my book, Moonlight has the best fried chicken, period.

review: If you are looking for something COMPLETELY different than your ordinary Halloween Experience, The Vault of Souls is it.   This is -not- your daughter's theme park experience, this is an Upscale experience that you won't find anywhere else. An elegant night of fear.  Don't come with the expectation of lines, of others body to body with you as you're herded though some chintzy maze, because that is not here.   What IS here?  It is a lush party in the arrival, where you will be given your number. While you wait, you can enjoy ghostly music and dancers as they float through the room. Have your aura cleansed and be read by the resident ghost hunter.  Enjoy hand passed appetizers or a drink from the bar as you wait for your time to come.   When your number is called, you will be brought down to the Vault, here you will be given a choice of which path to choose, and that choice is WHOLLY up to you. This is a nonlinear event. There is no ONE way to go. 12,000 sq feet of space for you to look through. You are encouraged to open drawers, read everything and touch.. just not the spirits, though they MAY touch you.   Each vignette is special, there are spirits in each room that will speak with you or not. They will interact with you in a different way. Your goal, to find the way out. They are just happy to see you.   It may take you as little as 20 minutes to get out, if you just briefly look things over, but it can take 90 if you thoroughly investigate and immerse yourself, and this is something you DO want to immerse yourself in. The scenes are beautiful, the Spirits are engaging and it is a world that has been masterfully crafted by a Storyteller who is beyond comparison.   When you do find your way out, you can wind down a bit in the Gin joint, enjoy the music and dancers that perform for you, and of course the delectable libations. Or have your tarot read as well as desserts and gelato up stairs in the reader's clearing.   A couple of things to note: the event starts at $100.00 per ticket, and goes up to $400.00 Each ticket tier has it's benefits, and it is reservation only.   HOWEVER Each ticket comes with valet parking - in downtown Tampa, this benefit alone is amazing.  There is a dress code, Please don't come dressed in sneaks and a Tee, Come dressed to be immersed in the event, as if you were going out to the theater, Just, Please Ladies, no High Heels. The vault contains uneven floors, so spike heels are not suggested. The event is for 18+ and up, no children will be allowed.   -YOU- will be wearing the masks and asked to not speak while in the vault, this is so that the spirits do not follow you home.   Come enjoy a night of paranormal fun, a night of elegant fear with a sinister twist. The spirits are expecting you.

review: Read Catherine L.'s review - and my sentiments are echoed.  A close friend and I came here  for dinner.  When we had trouble finding the place (we were at the "A Full Plate" end of Liberties walk, we called on the phone and a nice man came out to get us and walked us over.  This, alas, was the best part of the meal.  Things got progressively worse and worse.  First we were seated (inside - at our request) and our drink order was taken by a clearly overworked, spread-too-thin male server (who was very nice and tried his best - 3 stars for him).  After taking our meal order we waited, and waited, and waited...  And waited some more...  And finally asked harried server to please bring our chips and salsa (as he had just brought some to another table nearby).  We were starvin'!  The smoky salsa and salsa verde arrive - in hot bowls "fresh from the d/w" and thus we had warm salsa.  Yech.  And the salty chips were "chipettes" (or to be mean - crumbs.)  smashed to smithereens.  OK, things aren't so great - but we await our entrees. Wow - Impressive looking - I order a single beef shortrib and feel like Fred Flintstone.  This thing is HUGE.   Gi-normous!  Like a brontosaurus rib.  Alas - there is no sauce.  My friend orders an "OK" pair of Chicken burritos that are no better than Qdoba.    So here's the kicker...  About 3/4 through the entrees, frantic server appears again with a six-pack of sauce.  He gives me a bottle of HOT and a bottle of SWEET.  I pour out a bit of the sweet onto my plate (disregarding the crust around the rim of the squeez bottle) and dip my meat in.  UGH!!!  Racidity Central.  The HOT sauce is not rancid - and has a nice flavor but it just to hot for me.  My appetite is now officially GONE.  And shortly thereafter, so were we.  I will not return.  Such a disappointment.

review: We popped into the Four Seasons on a whim while in the area on Saturday. I was dying for a hot spiked beverage and I figured the Four Seasons could comply. We were surprised to see dozens of kids in costumes getting ready to perform through the Swann Lounge. The bar was packed, but many of the tables and chairs were actually situated in the hall outside the lounge. A manager assured us that we could still get service there, so we grabbed a table and commenced people-watching.   There wasn't a hot cocktail on the menu but our server said they could probably do a hot toddy. It ended up being delicious and exactly what I wanted. Of course, one drink turned into a few plus a light dinner of mussels with grilled bread and a spinach and goat cheese salad. Everything was great. I'm actually really looking forward to returning some time and trying their cheesesteak, which I thought I spotted on a previous visit and confirmed via the menu this time around. It's definitely on the pricey side but I'm sure it's damn tasty.   If the Swann Lounge added happy hour, I'd probably become a regular.

review: Went here for a desperation dinner - and needed something the 7 year old would like.  (She suggested it).   The good:  The black & white milkshake ($4.05) was freshly made and big enough for the 3 of us to each have a good bit of. - really big enough for 2 to share.  The chicken sandwiches were fried - but freshly fried.  Very pleasant service - an older lady took the orders, a younger gal cooked and served and a teen guy spun milkshakes and got us fountain drinks.  The bad:  Waffle fries are just OK.  Onion rings are tasteless and above a 1/2 step about BK quality.  I wanted the real deal - and this ain't it.  The ugly:  NASTY horrid bathroom.  Used - again - out of a 7 year old's desperation.  We'll be back - in the spring/summer when the weather is nicer.  A junk food paradise.  There is NOTHING remotely healthy on the menu.  Not even an iceberg side salad.

review: This is a good Middle Eastern restaurant but it is the one that I eat at the least of any in the area.  This place is very often quite crowded and parking isn't always the easiest in the area so I usually opt for places that are easier to grab a quick meal like Pyramid's, Mona's, or Courtyard Grill.  The main factor impeding my eating here more often is the problem of its location in proximity to Jamila's, which is so close I will ALWAYS opt for that as my first choice over here, as I enjoy Jamila's so very much.  This place has a a nice ambiance and the energy level of the crowd usually seems to be high.  I think Lebanon and here probably seem to have some of the most jovial crowds having fun while they eat of any of the area Middle Eastern restaurants I've been to.  I've found all of the food to be good and I've always had great service.

review: Disclaimer: I really wanted to give Little Hills a 2, but they offer a 25% discount to Yelpers who check in on their smart phones, so I bumped them up a star for supporting Yelp.   Little Hills has a great patio, unfortunately when I was there the weather was not allowing outdoor dining. I was seated in the little room to the left of the bar that overlooks the patio. I was the only one in there and from the looks of the dust on everything, no one had been in there for some time.  Daily maintenance would help this from happening.   I love chicken wings and burgers with pepper cheese and have list on Yelp for those places that impress me with theirs. LHW will not make either of those list.  My wings came out first as an appetizer. Flavor was good, but they were cold. I mean cold, not even luke warm. I would have sent them back, but I rarely saw my server since I was the only one in the room. I couldn't even get the attention of the hostess and a couple of female servers who were talking "dirt" about a co-worker.  They were ripping her up on side and down the other and everyone could here. Damn, I miss All My Children.   I ate some of the wings cold and pushed the others aside. I also found it odd that the celery was presented diced instead of sticks. My burger followed fairly quick after wards and had huge well seasoned steak fries as a side. I prefer hearty steak fries and these made up for cold wings. My burger was overcooked from what I ordered, but it had my favorite cheese.  Once again, since I was the only one in the room there was no followup on my meal. I ate my well done burger, which still had decent flavor. (Medium Rare would have been better)  My server showed up with my check and I showed him my check-in on Yelp to get the 25% discount. He said, "what is that?". It is a discount for checking into this restaurant on Yelp. "Can I show this to my manager?".  I said, yes thinking he'd go get his manager. Oh no, he grabbed my phone and off he went. Manager claimed she did not know what it was, but she'd honor it. I thanked her for her kindness and suggested she check with owners or other managers, because I was confident she'd see it again.  I was ready to leave, but really didn't want to go. Those girls were still talking dirt, some serious dirt. I think they've missed their calling in life, they need to be writing scripts for the new GCB series.

review: I can't believe I'm saying this but I had my very first experience at Isgro's yesterday. I'm sure I've had their pastries before as they're a Philly institution, but yesterday marked my first visit to the store for my own order.   I placed an order by phone on Friday for a mini desserts tray that would serve 10-15 people for an event on Monday. I said I would stop by in the afternoon to pick it up, but I was out a bit earlier than expected, and got there around 1:30. The tray was nearly finished but the mini cannolis still needed to be stuffed. To me, this was a good sign because cannolis definitely have a shelf life.   The tray was gorgeous and had really nice variety: cannoli, cream puffs, pumpkin cheesecake, coconut brownies, eclairs, and more. The mini sizes were great so you could try a couple at a time. My first pick was a cannoli and it was phenomenal. I'm not typically a big cannoli person but Isgro's may have converted me - their shell was crispy crunchy and the filling had that light ricotta taste with enough sweetness to give it depth. The chocolate chips capping each side were just right.   I will definitely think of Isgro's the next time I'm having a party and need some sweets!

review: Let me start out saying, I enjoy Six Row Brewing Company Beer. I really like their Whale, but my experience here was not acceptable.  It all began with our entrance and how we were greeted. We did not hear, "Hi, welcome to Six Row Brewing Company" or anything similar. Instead the bartender said, "seat yourself, we'll get at you soon".  Okay, I do not mind seating myself, but welcoming me before barking an order to seat myself would been more personable.  Now I know they were extremely busy, they had three people at the bar and two others seated at a table, so we understood why it took 5 minuets to come over to our table. Which gave us time to find two menus laying on another table and begin to decide what we wanted to eat.  Very limited menu and it really isn't a typical pub food.  When the bartender came over to take our order, we asked what she would recommend and what was her favorite. She would only tell us what was popular, which isn't a rousing endorsement when you are not willing to tell what you like.  I love pastrami and when I asked where theirs came from, she replied "I don't know".  I refrained from asking her go check, figuring it might stress her out. We then asked to give us a moment to decide what we wanted.   As she returned to the bar, we made the decision to leave.  We excused ourselves, saying thank-you but we wanted something different. All we heard was, "okay". I must expect to much, I can deal with "okay", but let's add, "hope to see you again". We may have not stayed today, but at least tempt us to come back.   We went to The Scottish Arms and enjoyed a couple Whales on draft a great meal and incredible service.

review: Visiting this McDonald franchise on S. Oxford Valley Road in Fairless Hills, Pa., was the first time that the drive up experience took me by surprise.    First, the voice taking orders was amazingly pleasant.  She seemed to be into her job and sincerely asked how I was doing, and how she could help.  The repartee was longer than expected, and warm throughout.  She didn't seem fazed that I was ordering a small meal off the Cheapo menu, and that the items cost less than $4.    Second, this was the first fast food interaction where I was handed a separate plastic bag with napkins and straw.  Someone realized that cleanliness and ease of transfer were important.  So much better than finding those things stuffed into the bag, or worse, not provided at all.    These made for a positive impression of this Mickey D's, and would have led to a higher star rank had the actual Double Cheese Burger been hot off the grill.  Not even close.  Barely lukewarm. review: This franchise recently expanded into this part of the world, and I finally found a convenient moment to check it out this week.  It is an attractive Chinese house; clean, organized and designed equally for eat in or takeout.  Yet, not an Asian in sight to speak to authenticity.  The options are set behind glass shielded steam tables, where the workers allow you to select from the number of different dishes offered, and spoon them onto a heavy cardboard plate with a side of white or fried rice.  As everything is prepared beforehand,  unless you arrive soon after wokking, the food cools and congeals to some extent, detracting from its overall taste and enjoyment. I went for orange chicken and Beijing beef with the fried rice.  Both had a good look with different shades of orange and red amber goopy sauce.  The taste of each was distinct, and I believe that if hot, they would have been a satisfying meal.  Unfortunately, that was not the case. Both were barely above room temperature when I sat down, and although I appreciated the flavor and textural potential, the heat issue really drove down my enjoyment.  I don't know how they can fix this problem. I don't like micro-reheats, and question whether they could successfully throw it back in a wok.    So, I give them credit for an interesting idea, and a tidy house, but just don't want past prime hanging around food as part of my diet.

Generally I liked this joint and would rate it around a 3.5 except it does lack a bit in value for the meat dishes and they are quite lacking in delighting carnivores here but they make some amazing looking and tasting salads.

review: The food here was by far the best Indian food I have had from a buffet style restaurant.  As mentioned in other reviews, don't let the buffet setting discourage you by thinking it will be dry and overcooked.  On the contrary, the seven items I sampled were all full flavored and moist, with enough spices to let you know this was Indian, but mixed with enough familiar flavors that my palate was able to relate to it.    The staff out front was friendly, but did have a heavy accent which I struggled with understanding.  So even though I repeated my question about my dining options at lunch time, I am sure I looked like a deer in the headlights upon hearing his answer.  I decided to go with sampling the buffet, but I wasn't given much direction about how to proceed.       I wasn't sure if I was supposed to wait at my table or simply grab a tray and start helping myself (I helped myself like the other newbies ahead of me).  I could see staff milling about behind the buffet line, so I wasn't sure if I was supposed to have them serve me or use the spoons myself (I served myself).  I did find it awkward having to bend over to reach beyond the wall to clear the low overhang.  I could see most customers were expressing some concern about reaching over the hot trays to spoon foods from the second row of entrees. Expectations are higher at restaurants when it comes to service and for folks who are new to a restaurant, having someone work the front dining area who can clearly direct customers is a must. review: Color me SHOCKED.  When you think of food at the zoo, what do you think of? I usually think of hot dogs, burgers and nachos. David and I were having a zoo day and we got a bite to eat here because it was right in the middle of things. There was a pretty good crowd for a Saturday, but the line was moving fast. They have a lot of food options here, but still, I wasn't expecting much. I got the chicken strips with fries and David got a shrimp po boy with cheese fries.  Let me tell you- I couldn't have been more pleased with how good the food was here. First of all, you order and they have it ready to go for you right away. Second of all, my chicken strips were HUGE. The batter was nice and the chicken was tender and juicy. David's po boy was PACKED with shrimp, to the point that they were falling off of the bread. Here's the kicker: my chicken strips basket was $7.50 and David's sandwich was $8.50. That's a good deal, any way you want to look at it. As far as drinks go, they have all of the basic soft drinks and water and they have beer and daiquiris, if you've had enough of the kids and want to get liquored up. No judgement. If you want a souvenir cup, it's $6; again, not a bad price at all.  On my next trip to the zoo, I won't even hesitate to eat here. The food is good and the service is fast. You can't ask for more than that.

review: St. Louis Union Station Soda Fountain is the perfect spot to have a quick lunch/bite before or after riding, The St. Louis Wheel.   Our party of three arrived at noon and there already was a wait for tables. Over half the restaurant was filled with convention attendees. It was easy to spot them, they all had lanyards hanging around their necks.  Even with the crowd, our wait was not long.   Normally, I like the coziness of a booth, but today we were seated at a four-top table in front of the actual soda fountain. It was a great show, it was fun watching the, to use a classic term, "soda jerks" make all the sweet treats. Numerous times we were asking our server, "what's that?". They all looked so delicious. For our sweet treat, after our lunch we ended up enjoying, The King.   Now let's talk about the real reason we came here, our lunch before riding The Wheel. I ordered the Single Grilled Cheeseburger and my cousins enjoyed, Fried Chicken Sandwich and a BLT. To accompany our sammies, we all shared two sides; Crinkle Fries and Onion Rings.   I enjoyed my burger, which was loaded up with the typical, LTOP. A single was enough, I could not imagine eating a double along with a side and one of the sweet treats. My cuz who had the Fried Chicken Sandwich said it crisp, moist and flavorful. She normally doesn't like mayo and had them put it on the side. When it arrived, it was a flavored mayo in a little cup and she liked it. Her husband, enjoyed the BLT. He said the applewood smoked bacon was a flavorful twist on the classic sandwich.   We were so glad we all shared the our sides. The portions are plentiful and enough to share. The crinkle fries (my favorite style) were crispy and seasoned with just enough salt. The onion rings I found out are not made it house, but I'll tell you that they were pretty tasty for being a frozen product. It could have fooled me, they were that good.   The dessert, our finale was a delicious sweet treat. As I stated earlier, we went with, The King. It was a delightful mix of sweet and salty. It all centered around a big scoop of peanut butter banana ice cream, surrounded by sliced bananas and covered in peanut butter sauce, topped with bacon and chopped peanuts. A sundae is not complete without the whipped cream topping and maraschino cherries on top.   Eric our server was a delight. He was honest with his recommendations and didn't mind splitting our checks and that we shared our sides and dessert. I was also impressed that one of the managers was hands on assisting all the servers. She even took time out twice to chat with us about our first visit. The floor captain also came over and thanked us for coming in as we were getting ready to leave. Overall, very friendly staff.   When: January 9, 20202 Why: Lunch before riding, The Wheel

review: During 2018, I am trying to get back to at least one restaurant per month that I used to enjoy, but for some reason, hadn't been back to in a long time (a decade or more.)  So when I saw an UYE at Shapiro's, I knew that I had to stop in.    The place is much as I remembered it:  plenty of parking on the outside; lots of tables for groups or families; well lit interior; and a cafeteria line like I used to go through at school, but with food I actually looked forward to eating!  And for as many folks who were dining there, a relatively quiet atmosphere, great for conversations.    Although the line nearly reached the entrance, it moved efficiently well and soon I was standing before cases of desserts, followed by cool sides, then progressing on to entrees and warm sides before reaching the cashier.  Behind the numerous staff working the line is a menu board to help you make your decision while you approach.  If you want a beverage, they are around the corner (self serve) where they also have "to go" boxes available (great idea!!).  Once you have your food, you are free to pick out you own spot.    I was there to meet some fellow Yelpers and we got to meet one of the 4th generation family members (Sally Keck Shapiro) who spent time with us filling us in on the family/deli's evolution through the changing restaurant scene in the 100+ year history of the business.  It's great to see a family owned business succeed and have such devoted followers.    Oh, and lest I forget, the food was delicious!  The Brooklyn Pastrami on rye (baked in house from a recipe a former neighboring business passed along to them) with Swiss and a bit of spicy mustard was loaded!  I couldn't get over how much meat was on the sandwich (served halved).  A tasty pickle spear was included with the sandwich too.  I also ordered the chilled mustard potato salad that had just enough kick and the spice worked really well with the sandwich.     "Cook Good; Serve Generously; Price Modestly; People will come."  That was the founder's motto and it still holds true today.   Sometimes, you just shake your head trying to figure out why it takes so long to get back to a place that is so good.  I'll be sure it won't take nearly so long for my next visit.  Review #826

review: Momma, Mia. I mean Mama Gustos, you make a fine pizza pie. I was impressed with your sauce, crust and generous amount of toppings and cheese.   I had heard so many great things about Mama so when meeting friends at Melt and seeing her next door I knew I was going to get a carry out. When I popped in to order my take out, the staff was friendly as were those sitting at the bar. The chattiness gave it a real neighborhood feel. I felt assured when the men at the bar gave a thumbs up to my order, saying it was their favorite.   First thing that impressed me was the availability of four different styles of crust and not one of them is thin style. I ordered the traditional style which was a little thicker then hand tossed. As my topping I went simple, Italian Sausage and Pepperoni. The cheese was evenly melted over the entire pizza and it had plenty of both meats.  Best of all, the crust around the edge of the pizza was a light golden brown.  I don't need to worry about what I'll do with their crust, I'll eat it.   Mama, I'll be coming back. You are close enough to drop in for a quick dinner and close enough to do a quick pick-up of carry-out. If you did delivery, I am confident your business would soar.

review: This place has friendly staff and a wide variety of tea options, in hot, cold, and latte forms.  They also have some coffees and alcoholic beverages too.  For your munchies, they have bagels, muffins, scones, and several types of cookies.  Catering is also available through this shop.  For those who have been to the shop in Broad Ripple, this is a little different experience.  In BR, it is a tea shop that has merchandise and meals including soups and sandwiches.  It is a place to sit and relax.  The Keystone at the Crossing (KatC) location is a place to get in and go.  It is located in the center of the food court with a circular counter.  One spot you enter the ringed off area and place your order (note that they have paper menus for you to help yourself to so you can decide.)  To the left is a place to pick up your order after paying and giving your name.  In the space between the order and pickup counter is a display of the teas.  I assume you may be able to smell the teas to help you decide, but I didn't.  (I suggest asking the clerk before opening them.)  Because teas require water heated to near boiling and then being allowed to steep for 3 to 5 minutes (dependent upon the type of tea), you will expect a small wait for your order.  Fortunately there are lots of seating spaces near the shop.  I played it safe and simply stood and waited for my Apricot Cream hot tea.  The aroma and taste were really great.  The only problem is that it was served too hot so that I had to wait another five to ten minutes for it to become drinkable.  I make tea at home and watch my temperatures so that by the end of a five minute steep, I can drink it without a scalding risk.  Not so lucky here.  Blowing on an insulated cup which doesn't cool it off much, so I did get a bit of burn on the first sip.  Seriously, if they had managed to keep the tea at more drinkable temp, I would have given five stars.  It's nice to have a hot beverage option inside KatC.  I think I still prefer the BR location because of the wider options and the more relaxing atmosphere.  Review #2188
