review: I hate, hate, HATE to do this to one of my favorite local businesses, but I have not been happy with my recent experiences at Penguin Cleaners. This was my go-to dry cleaning place for 6+ years. Even after my move to the city, I continued to take my clothes to Penguin because I always felt that they were returned to me looking brand spanking new. And for that reason, I didn't mind that the prices are on the high side.   A month or so ago, I brought in a nice dress that I had worn once before getting a grease spot on the front (no more sherry bone marrow shots when I'm dressed all classy-like). I specifically pointed it out to the gentleman who works there and picked up the dress a week or so later without taking a look. Once home, I got the dress out of the bag and the spot was still there. So I brought the dress back during the day, along with two others, and I asked if there was anything that could be done. The lovely woman (whose name is escaping me!) who often helps me out said that she thought they could probably get the stain out and it was possibly just overlooked the first time. She marked the spot with a sticker.   Today I returned to pick up my dresses. Miracle of miracles, the dress is spotless. I'm so relieved. But I also paid to have that dress dry cleaned twice. Once home, I looked at my other dresses. One still has a couple marks on it towards the bottom. I knew they were there when I dropped off my dresses but I didn't think I needed to point out every mark. Now, I have another dress that needs to be dry cleaned yet again.  Like I said, I have always had great service from Penguin and I really like the people who work there, but I'm super frustrated with the quality of services lately. I think it's finally time for me to look for a new dry cleaner closer to where I live.

The staff was helpful and friendly, and although I haven't purchased anything yet, I will be back when I am ready to make my move.  In the adjoining room they have a fantastic selection of swim and workout wear that is sure to make anyone feel fancy on their next trip to the gym. One thing that I especially liked about this shop is the attention to personal details- they had lotions and body sprays along with clothing and I like that for times when you want to pamper yourself all the way.

review: Funny that Brian L compared Fleming's to Capital Grille in his review, because that's sort of what I was doing on my second visit there last night. My first visit was just a couple weeks ago for a charity event, so I didn't really get a good idea about the food or drinks. The private room was nice, though!  Last night, I returned with my mom and a family friend for happy hour before hitting up Rizzieri for spa services (yep, we were spoiling ourselves right before Christmas). They have a "five for $6" special that includes select wines, cocktails and appetizers. Since the house vodka is Smirnoff, we skipped the special in favor of Kettle martinis. But we did order calamari, ahi tuna and a garlicky shrimp dish from the happy hour menu.   The food was pretty great. The shrimp came in a ramekin filled with a spicy garlic butter sauce. There was a small piece of bread so we asked for more and received a warm parmesan baguette with two different whipped butters. The calamari was tossed in a slightly sweet sauce with bell and banana peppers.   For our next couple rounds of drinks we decided to try some of the wines from the special. I had a pinot grigio followed by a shiraz and both were nice. We decided to end on a sweet note, so we shared the caramel walnut turtle cake, which came with fresh whipped cream. It was absolutely awesome.   Our server was nice but I felt like I had to flag her down whenever we needed something. When our friend pulled out a card she had for a discount the server told us it wasn't good for happy hour. Then our friend pulled out another card for a comped dessert, and the server's response was just kind of awkward.  For the amount of money we plunked down on happy hour, I did think the prices were a bit high. But we enjoyed ourselves and I liked the food. I'd go back if we made plans there again but I wouldn't go out of my way.

review: At the intersection of Stoopville Road and Washington Crossing Road in Lower Makefield, Village Market has been dishing out good breakfast and lunch sandwiches for decades.  Their recent upgrade adds to its luster, and the newly engineered intersection makes it easier to get in and out with risk of bodily harm.  It is easy to miss the deli section in the white building next to the Exxon station, but try to stop in.  VM has a deserved reputation among locals for hearty breakfast sandys and over-stuffed burritos, way above average lunch options (especially Cheesesteaks and Chicken Salad subs and wraps, and even decent fresh coffee. It is primarily a take out joint, and the parking is adequate.  The staff moves efficiently and knows what the regulars want.    There is a bit of confusion as to who has jurisdiction over Village Market.  Although much closer to the center of Newtown, it is actually in Lower Make.  Don't let that squabble deter you from sampling their homemade menu.  But, if you have the misfortune of being pulled over for speeding on Rt. 513, the police who will be stopping you and issuing the summons are from Lower Makefield, so don't blame Newtown.

review: This is a great old school neighborhood eatery with classic New Orleans Creole and Italian dishes.  They offer classics like turtle soup, gumbo, red beans, fried chicken, pasta and po boys along with more ambitious entrees (and for the Texans that crave it yes they have a chicken fried steak for a lunch special).  They have a fantastic roast beef poboy with delicious chunks of garlic and a nice thick gravy.  The ambiance is more 70's style than classic New Orleans architecture and the crowd certainly trends more towards the geriatric but this place is more hip than any hipster could ever dream of.  The menu selection is excellent while portions are generous and prices make this place a good value.  This is an authentic locals joint with most of the folks working here being locals that give it that extra bit of local soul that many places have lost over the years.

review: The Olde Worlde Bakerye & Café has 30 foot ceilings and suggests an old villa in Tuscany, with faux stone and large bread racks showing their attractive wares.  It does seem a little out of place sitting on Smithville Road in Eastampton, NJ, but that does not detract from its pleasant scale.  Outdoor patio seating for nice days is a definite upgrade from the ordinary java joint.    I stopped in around 10 am for a light breakfast and coffee.  The large menu is suspended from the ceiling behind the cashiers.  Only brekkie sandwiches are available during the week, although a full brunch operation happens on weekends.  No sweat.  I wasn't looking or a big and hearty meal.  The unmistakable aroma of baked bread permeated the room, although they were not baking anything when I was there. The racks behind the counter were loaded to make a bread lover swoon.  All shapes and sizes demonstrated the artistry of the baker. Impressive.  My Sausage, Egg & Cheese on a Roll was okay, but not more. Their bread was fresh, but lacked the texture and yeastiness I expected from a homemade offering. The sausage patty was about the thinnest I have encountered, but still tasty.  The fried eggs and cheese were ample, and clearly cooked/melted on the grill.  At under $6 for the whole shebang I was ultimately satisfied with the value, if not the exuberance of the sandwich.   Maybe their brunches have more of a "Wow!" factor.

review: FD Subs has been at this location in Ewing Plaza Shopping Strip for a few decades with different owners and levels of satisfaction. When I stopped in this week for late lunch of a turkey/swiss sub, the wall menu looked like it had been hung in the last century. Still, it was extensive and provided succor for the famished. It wasn't open for in house dining yet, but the husband wife team were well versed in their menu and demonstrated prodigious production skills.   Their strong suit was that everything for the sandwich contents was cut on demand, and thus as fresh as possible; and decent torpedo rolls (really the most important element of the creation) were pulled from a bag only as needed. My Honey Turkey and Swiss hoagie with shredded lettuce, mayo and hot/sweet peppers wasn't zoftig, but ample enough to warm and fill the belly of the beast. I enjoyed it.   I have been on a deli kick of late, and FD was about as rewarding as the other local family run shops in the region. Good to help keep all of them in business by chosing mom & pop businesses open and thriving, rather than those factory like places that offer gasoline as a side dish.

review: I'll be the first to admit that I usually don't go for donuts. If I'm going to go for something sweet, I just go for cake, but Joe's might change all that. For some reason, I've become kind of obsessed with their donuts. More specifically, their chocolate sprinkle donuts and their glazed chocolate donuts that actually have a really rich chocolate flavor. Either one will make for a perfect dessert when a craving hits. They also have a variety of other sweet and pastries that I have to resist when my sweet tooth kicks in. Did someone say McKenzie's turtles?! Oh yeah.  I've been here for lunch once and the experience was great. Even though the restaurant was packed, service was attentive and friendly. I got a club sandwich with a side of grits and some donut holes, because when you're eating in a diner, and all of that is available, you go for it. The sandwich was really good, but curiously only had ham and bacon on it as the meats. I guess that's their version of a club and that's fine with me, I enjoyed it. The grits were yummy and, of course, the sweets always hit the spot because they're known for their donuts.  I have yet to try breakfast here, but I'll be doing so soon. I'm glad there's a Joe's in Terrytown.

review: I really don't know if I can accurately put into words how extremely grateful I am to the team at Sbraga for hosting my wedding. They went so above and beyond expectations and completely blew us away.   When we got engaged, Art and I knew we wanted to host our wedding in a non-traditional venue with an emphasis on great food and drinks, dancing, and just having the most fun possible with our friends and family. We reached out to our friends at Sbraga to pitch them our idea of hosting the ceremony in one of their restaurants and the reception in another. To our extreme delight, they were into it!    Three months before the wedding, we were called in for a meeting with our main contacts, Tyrone and Ben. I knew it was a bad sign when I saw Kevin Sbraga sitting at the table. He delivered the news personally that our reception venue was not going to work out. He quickly followed that up by telling us that they had a plan. And that plan was to apply for a permit to shut down Pine Street and put up a giant outdoor tent next to Sbraga, so that we could have our ceremony and reception all in one place. And that is exactly what they did.   I don't think anyone could fully comprehend what our wedding was going to look like until the day it happened. Our ceremony took place inside Sbraga - it was a tight squeeze with 185 guests but somehow it worked. Even with so many people, the vibe was romantic and intimate. I was filled with love and surrounded by it. Our ceremony was quick, and guests made their way over to the tent for a cocktail reception. The walkway between Sbraga's side door and the entrance to the tent was covered entirely by an awning so the cold and slightly rainy weather was not a factor.   Tent is probably the wrong word to use for the beautiful venue that was constructed for our reception. Inside was a fabulous room with twinkling lights overhead, a gigantic dance floor, several bars and all of the other arrangements we discussed with regards to seating and food stations. The team at Sbraga even hired security to make sure we didn't have any uninvited guests.   Every single person who worked the wedding was genuinely excited for us and happy to be there. And the food. I'm not just saying this because it was my wedding but the food was the best I've ever had at a wedding, hands down. Stations were set up in the tent and also in the restaurant, and the plethora of pastas, proteins and sides was astonishing. We also had a bread table that was overflowing with homemade breads and crackers by Sbraga's amazing pastry chef, Marqessa. She also made our gorgeous and incredibly delicious cake, a chocolate chip cake with buttercream icing on the outside and salted caramel icing on the inside. To finish the night, we had a savory sendoff of The Fat Ham's hot chicken sliders.   In addition to the full bar, head bartender Nate crafted three custom cocktails that everyone was talking about the next day. I regret not trying the punch because I was too busy downing Flying Caucasians and prosecco (special thanks to Tom for always, and I mean always, keeping my glass full throughout the night).   After the special dances and speeches, dinner stations were opened and guests could enjoy at their own pace. Because of this format, the dance floor was poppin' all night long - exactly what I wanted.   Thinking back on our wedding day, there is honestly not one single thing that I would have changed. Choosing Sbraga and placing our trust in their team was the best decision. Thanks so much to everyone at the Sbraga family who made this dream come true. Your commitment to service and quality is unmatched!

review: The Mack is truly a hidden jewel in South Hampton neighborhood. I would have never discovered the diamond in the ruff if it were not for Mark S. telling me about it in a Hamburger talk thread here on Yelp. Thanks Mark, for expanding my burger world.   We went for lunch yesterday and had a totally enjoyable meal. When having a burger for some silly reason, I always need to start out with an order of chicken wings. I always get a giggle when a menu says, "Our Famous Chicken Wings". The Mack, lives up to that boast. Their wings are crispy on the outside and moist on the inside. They have just the perfect amount of spice and kick.  After the wings,  I had a Half Pound Burger with Pepper Jack Cheese and the SO enjoyed The Southside Burger. Both were charbroiled to perfection and I love it when a burger is hand pressed. There is something, about a burger that isn't perfectly shaped that seems to add flavor.   My burger was topped with rings of white onion, lettuce and a slice of tomato that made it perfect. It was as if I were enjoying a juicy burger at a backyard cook out.  The Southside Burger was topped with Cheddar Cheese, Crispy Onion Rings and BBQ Sauce. Both burgers were huge in size, so huge that we had to take some of ours home. When they brought us our box to take our leftovers, I was pleased to see that their container was Eco-Frinendly.   They offer two kinds of fries to compliment your burger; "traditional" and "waffle".  The traditional were slender, crispy and had a seasoning similar to Lawry's. which is A+ to me. The waffle fries were huge and I loved how they held the ketchup when dipping.   Their server did a great job of waiting on the tables and serving the bar, she is trained well. By that, I mean she is trained like Pavlov's dog. When food is ready, the kitchen pushes a buzzer that you can hear behind the bar and off she goes to retrieve it. I found it funny and when I shared my laugh with her, she laughed too. She commented that she never thought of that, but it was so true.   I am a new fan of The Mack and it is being added to 3 of my lists; Burgers, Wings and Eco-Friendly.

review: I would have never discovered The Post if were not for a talk thread on Yelp. Everyone was sharing their favorite places in Maplewood and several mentioned The Post. I became curious, so one day I checked it out and now know what all the excitement is about. In fact, I already established myself as a regular with check-ins on my iPhone.   The Post offers some very good bar grub. I will say, they are #1 in my book for wings. Their wings are good size, meaty and very juicy. What I love is they offer for an additional 50¢ to bake your wings. After your wings are done like normal wings they give them a ride through the pizza oven. This bakes their fantastic and flavorful sauce into the wings and it also makes them less messy while eating.   On our first visit I was surprised to do my iPhone check-in and get a 20% off coupon on my entire bill. Now that is one hell of a Yelp deal.  We chowed down on wings, cheeseburgers and fries. I love bars that offer my favorite cheese on their burgers. No, I am not talking provel. I am talking about pepper cheese for that extra bang of flavor.  Our drinks of choice  were soda which gave us another surprise, they are served in plastic tumblers that you get to take home. When I got home, I washed mine and placed it next to my other souvenir glasses from the 2006 World Series and 1983 Miss Universe Pageant. I have a very varied collection.   The next visit was a dinner to experience their pizza. I have a hard enough time choosing my topping, now at The Post you need to select you crust. The Post offers 8 different types of crust. We choose Parmesan Peppercorn to complement the "Kitchen Sink"  toppings. We ordered a small size and it was enough for two, with enough leftovers for a next day lunch for one.   My only complaint about The Post is that there are not enough TVs to watch a sporting event. Ha Ha - just kidding. TVs are plentiful, and you have a great view from any chair or bar-stool in the restaurant.  Young ladies if you are looking for a hot man, go to  The Post on game night you will plenty to choose from. However, to get their attention from the TVs or their lap tops and fantasy teams may be a challenge.

Also service upstairs was not and getting a refill on a drink was never going to happen so I deeply regret leaving a tip as I sure didn't get anything approaching service.  Overall this is a cool place to hang out at in the beer garden but save your tips for the bartenders.  Pro-tip:  You can skip the tourist line and go order upstairs for a shorter line.

review: Don't know about the salon in New York (although born and raised there), nor reputations well earned or not. But, I know what a good cut looks like, and how staff treats people. Most importantly, I know what makes my wife happy and what doesn't.   After parking the car, I arrived at Room 209 about 20 minutes after she went in for her appointment. There were a row of barber chairs on the right, and a statue of a black horse rearing on its hind legs on the left in front of the high cashier counter. Lao po was in the rear having her hair washed, so I took a seat in the front waiting area.   Eventually, she moved to her chair, where several assistants had their hands on her head combing and asking questions about her desired results. Sam came over to assess the situation, ran his hands through her hair for a minute or so, seemingly to contemplate the proper approach. He walked away a few times to supervise the other customers, but ultimately returned, shears in hand to put the finishing touches on the cut.   A bit of blow drying and final shaping and trimming, and they were done. She was clearly happy with her look in the mirror, and I have to admit with her face framed with straight black hair and falling easily on her shoulders, she was a sight to behold. Her classic facial structure, deep eyes and high cheekbones gave her the image of an empress.   Took my breath away.

review: Just for the record: I'm not very adventurous when it comes to Chinese food. I usually get the cheap take out stuff and that's good enough for me.  Dustin suggested China Doll, mainly because of their Tiki bar, Yes, China Doll is  the only Tiki bar in New Orleans, at the moment (Tiki Tolteca is currently closed for renovations). So, we decided to check this place out. We sat in the bar area and looked over the drink menu. They have pretty much any classic Tiki drink for $5.75 each. I decided to start with a Fog Cutter and Dustin got a Mai Tai. My drink was really good, and of course it's sweet, which I liked. The next drink I got was a Piña colada, which was a nice blended drink and was a nice follow up to the strong Fog Cutter.  For actual food, we decided to split the Empress chow mein. This dish is a dice blend of chicken, shrimp and vegetables over crunchy noodles with a nice sauce. It was really good and it was A LOT of food and there was plenty left over to take home.  Everyone was so nice at China Doll and I will definitely be back. The Tiki Bar is definitely an experience and the food is good, too. Go early, if you are planning on eating in the dining room. While we were there a long line formed of people waiting to be seated.

review: Wow! This is my final review for 2014, and this brings my tally to 765, I can hardly believe that, and I'm ending the year on a high note!  I decided that lunch today was going to be at a place that I've heard people talk about, so after finding out that it was only minutes away from Tj Maxx, I headed to the local and walked right in. There was no line, only one lovely young lady writing "Happy New Year" on the To-Go sacks as she welcomed me to the store.   She asked if I knew what I wanted, or if I needed a few minutes. It was my first visit, so I said it would be a moment as familiarized myself with the menu.  First thing I notice is that their menu is similar to Five Guys, but their quality is STEPS above. I Ordered what I would normally get, a burger, with provolone, bacon, grilled onion & grilled mushroom, lettuce & A1 sauce on the side, an order of fries (Which is 1/2 pound of real potato) and a fountain drink.   I was given a number, shown where the fountain was and made my way to a seat.  They use real silverware, plastic glasses and real plates. Their teas were good, a choice actual brewed Jasmine tea as well as green and another. that I don't recall, but the Jasmine was Delicious!  When the burger was delivered, it looked fantasitc, it was cooked perfectly and so were the fries.  A few minutes into my meal, the Manager came over to see how I was, he asked how I found out about the place, I told him Yelp, and he called the Owner over, who happened to be visiting!  The owner was happy that it was working in his favour. He said that he found that most Yelpers were more discriminating than usual food critics. ;) As an elite, I think that's true, that and we give our true opinion, it's not bought and paid for.   I'll certainly come back to this place!

review: Cafe Nino would really be more of 2 star joint to me except it has a unique New Orleans Dive personality so it gets extra points for the sheer uniqueness and the fact the owner is usually around giving it some character. This is a good basic place for some quick Italian.  It's more of a cafeteria style joint where you pick out one (or more) of the entrees that is available that day (and on display in hotplates) and you then take your tray (with your paper plate and plastic utensils) to your table.  It is all self-service and the environment is a very basic dive type aesthetic.  The portions are usually good but the price is a bit high for the environment (especially when they only take cash).    Usually (but not always) the owner will offer you an after dinner drink (typically white or red wine) as you're leaving.  This certainly isn't a place to just hang out or bring a date to impress them (over a classy paper plate meal) but it has always been consistently decent food.  I've been here many times but I've never been here when it is crowded so it seems to always be a safe bet for some decent quick food if you're in a hurry.

review: I recently attended the first St. Louis Food Media Forum, a two day conference that was held in the Chouteau Room at Moulin. The room was the perfect venue for 80 -100 foodies to congregate and discuss; food blogging, recipe writing, food photography, food writing ethics and marketing/branding.   Having attended my fair share of business meetings and conferences, the two things that are always topic of complaints are acoustics and room temperature.  Here at Moulin neither of those were an issue. The sound system made it easy for the speakers to heard through out their entire presentations and PowerPoint displays could be seen easily from all tables. Even with three digit temperatures scorching the city of Saint Louis, the Chouteau room held a very comfortable coolness.   Our first day lunch was provided by Moulin, which was a variety of cold sandwiches  & wraps served family style at each conference table. Jimmy John's and Subway could learn a thing or two from Moulin on how to make a good sandwich. The second day PW Pizza treated everyone to a pizza buffet that had me gaining weight just cruising the line. If you're going to cheat your diet with Pizza, it might as well be a PW. review: You know that a Honduran restaurant is good when you sit down and the first thing that the waitress says is, "I don't speak English." Indeed, no one here spoke English except for me and my dining companion and that was just fine with me.   We were given a menu, and although it is completely in Spanish, there are pictures of the food on the menu and some of the stuff is pretty easy to figure out, as it is basic Latin food.   Everything in the menu sounded really good. I decided on the Honduran tacos. They were delicious hard tacos that were rolled and fried with chicken inside. They were topped with lettuce, tomato and huge slices of avocado. I posted a picture, if you want to check it out. It was so good! The tacos were huge and I finished two and took the rest home. They cost $8 and it was definitely a good meal for that amount of money.   I will definitely be back. On my way out I noticed that someone had ordered something that looked like a quesadilla, so I will probably try that. Don't be put off that no one here speaks English or that it's in a shady looking strip mall. It's worth it.

review: I went to see my first movie at a cinema in a long time as the pandemic is stabilizing.  Our group of 3 got our tickets ahead of time which is good because our ideal time was already sold out (just after lunch on a Friday).  The theater was limited to 50% capacity to allow adequate spacing and so we felt comfortable going.  We didn't order any food having just finished lunch and not feeling certain about how much we wanted to risk contact.  We were able to tell our seating and though my wife thought she had ordered something farther back, we ended up sitting in the 2nd row in those super stuffed lounge chairs.  Two of the three seats we were seated in didn't adjust posture and foot rests like they were supposed to, but one of the attendants immediately helped us and got the chairs to work.  Good service!' This visit, we weren't able to go to the IMAX theater, but got the Dolby which definitely added to the experience.  Though I am prone to afternoon naps, especially in a dark environment, the incredible audio which literally shakes the chairs during the action sequences was clear to understand (my wife didn't need her aides to understand!)  We were able to comfortably spend the time in the theater.  It wasn't too hot or cold, but I did keep my sweatshirt on.     The signs for the exits could use better identification as some led directly outside, while some led back to the lobby.  Since it was my first visit, if they could let you know which ones could get you to the lobby without wandering in the near total darkness.  I didn't miss much of the movie while wandering around, but with steps and people having their legs extended, it is not a place you want to turn around and watch the screen while walking.  I made it okay, but it definitely crossed my mind that an improvement could be made.     My wife bought tickets and thought our seats would be higher up than the 2nd row even though the tickets said row B.  As I searched for the exit, I think I did see a second row B above the midway point.  (Probably where we should have grabbed our seats) but it seems odd that they use the same row name for two different rows.  Maybe could have used a double letter designation if they have too many rows for our alphabet.   Oh, well, we still had an enjoyable afternoon and were glad to be able to enjoy it at the movies. review: While in the area to photograph a mural sponsored by Chuck's, I decided to stop in and support this fairly new (2018) business.  The traditional Coney Island hot dog is available here, but I suggest trying the "Detroit Dog" for something tasty and new in the area.  It easily bested the traditional in my opinion.  Finding Chuck's is easy, but getting into the parking lot is a bit challenging.  I literally circled the block to figure it out.  There is an alley next to the fire station and if you pull into the alley from 10th St, you can get access into the spacious paved lot next to the building that is home of the restaurant and the barber shop.  The restaurant is long and narrow and is decorated with all things Detroit.  Lots of Lions and Tigers stuff on the walls.  At the back of the dining area is an order counter with a bench for waiting on the right and bar stool seating on the left.  I was greeted and when I asked about the Detroit Dog, I was pleased that the young man working the desk had lots of information that made it clear.  (I just wish I could remember all the details.)  Anyway, it turns out the Detroit Dog is really popular there and offers a different spin than the Coney Island or the Chicago style dogs.  The Detroit Dogs come on a super light and fluffy bun with the dog covered with a Detroit style chili sauce, cheese, and crispy bacon pieces.  Really good!  The Coney Island comes with the same bun and dog, chili, onions, mustard, and if you want it, shredded American Cheese.  It was good, but pretty standard.  The fries I ordered were plentiful and were spiced/seasoned which included a lot of black pepper.  Nice flavor but the fries were just a bit too soggy to be 5 star.  Good flavor, but the seasoning was a bit inconsistently applied.  Some a little bland, others rather spicy.    The meal only took about ten minutes from the time I ordered, so the wait was very reasonable.  If you are looking for something different and want to support another local business while doing it, give Chuck's a try.  And get the Detroit Dog!  Review #2930

review: The Bulldog is one of my favorite places in the city and I have been going here for years.  As a girl who likes good beer, The Bulldog has a fantastic selection of both bottle and draft.  If you can think it up, it is pretty much a guarantee that this place has it.  I prefer this location over the one on Canal because it's smaller and has a more intimate feel.  I know that this might put some people off, but I love it.  It makes mingling a lot easier, and you meet new friends when you share a table with someone.  The bartenders are always attentive and go out of their way to accommodate me, even if they are busy.  Don't hesitate to ask for a sample of a new draft before you pay $5 for a pint.  They are also quick to give a good recommendation on something you might like, if you tell them what your "regular" is, and you are in the mood to experiment.  Big screens above the bar make it great for game days.  Get here early for Saints games or major sports events, because the place gets packed!  The food is good and cooked to order.  My fave is the Abita burger.   What I think I love most is that the patio is heated during cold months, so if you are one of those people who is more comfortable sitting outside, you can still have a good time.  Oh, and dogs are welcome on the patio!

review: I've been several times since my last update. What amazes me, is how this is well above average pub grub. I still kick myself in the a** for not eating here sooner.   Since my last review, I've done carryout twice and have been pleased with both. The first one was a pizza. I don't know about you all, but I love eating a pizza while watching the finale of The Biggest Loser. It just seems like the right thing to do.   I ordered a medium sausage and peperoni plus a dinner salad with that infamous white french dressing. Experiencing the "white french" a second time left me with a more favorable impression then my first dining experience. Their pizza is St Louis Style with the thin crust, cut into tiny squares. Toppings were plentiful and an even mix of both choices.  Their cheese fooled me. While eating I didn't think it was provel, I think with the combination of flavorful sauce and my topping it confused me.   My next carryout was a full rack of ribs on a Saturday night and a large Caesar Salad. Both were top notch. Their ribs are the meatiest ribs I have ever seen. Pappy's and Bogarts ribs do not come close to this much meat. The Cesar was huge and a typical "Hill" Caesar. We did Baked Potatoes at home and had a fantastic dinner.   When I picked up the ribs is when I discovered they use provel on the pizza. I asked one of the servers and she very proudly answered provel.  Oh well, it still tasted good and I'll eat it again.   Earlier this week Brad and I stopped in for lunch. The weather was great so we opted to take advantage of their outside seating. It's not a patio, it just out on the sidewalk, but you're outside.   We ordered burgers. I choose pepper cheese and traditional fries and Brad had Soft Cheddar and Waffle Fries. Both burgers were grilled well, not well in temperature. My pepper cheese melted better then his soft cheddar. They'd be off offering true cheddar instead of that scoop-able cheese. Loved my traditional fries, but the extra seasoning on the Waffle Fries was a surprise bonus.   The wait staff here is always friendly, giving it that neighborhood & family feeling. When I'm lazy, or can't think where to go, Biggies will be the first to come to mind.

review: It's Sunday night and the Cards are in the playoffs, we're not cooking or going out for dinner. We didn't want pizza, Chinese or any type of fast food. We were at a a loss for ideas. I was searching Yelp for ideas and checked to see if Joey B's did carry- out and to my surprise they did.  We checked the menu and made the call.   We ordered two of their Blue Plate Specials; Country Fried Chicken and Homemade Meatloaf. Both came with mashed potatoes and gravy and corn on the cob. The meatloaf also came with a side salad that was humongous, it was big enough for both of us to share. My Homemade Meatloaf  with a brown gravy truly had to down home taste. It is way better then other "Blue Plate Specials" near and on "The Hill". My SO enjoyed his Country Fried Chicken and its white gravy topping. Their great taste surprised us coming from a sports bar which is known for burgers and pizza.   I think Joey B's will be getting some more carryout orders from us.  They're close, the prices are right and the food is good.

review: A little slice of peace and tranquility right in Philadelphia! I'm so glad I got to -finally- check out Shofuso Japanese House & Garden. Shofuso is located in Fairmount Park, and there is a small parking lot onsite. You must leave your shoes on a rack before entering the house (don't forget to bring socks!).   The gardens are small but lovely, and I especially enjoyed the koi fish in the pond, which were enormous! The house is very interesting; some rooms you can walk through while others you can only look into from outside, but each room has a sheet with information so you can learn more about the function of the room. The docents were all tied up with leading other people around the house but I overheard some of the information which was quite interesting. If you can snag a docent to lead you around, do it!   The wraparound porch overlooking the pond was a great place to sit and relax after the tour. I could see myself going back on a nice day simply to enjoy a refreshing mental break. Philadelphians: add this to your summer to-do list!

review: I am so glad I stopped by this shop on Small Business Saturday.  It is filled with so many cool toys and collectibles that it was hard to keep from smiling as I explored.    The shop is located in a shopping plaza on the southeast corner of the intersection.  The entrance faces Madison and is set back from the road quite a bit.  But there is plenty of free parking in the lot which lets you browse as long as you like.  The main entrance is filled with action figures, pops, and so many toys/collectibles that I remembered buying for our kids when they were little.  There were even some that went far back enough that they were something I had too.    The north section of the shop (a separate room) is filled with Lego pieces and kits.  I wasn't into those as a kid, but the place is packed, so if you are a fan, you need to check this place out.  Now that I am old(er), it is a little easier to resist making large purchases, but if you want to see your kids smile, bring your wallet when you bring them in.  It's like Christmas!  Review #3373

Not gourmet - but good.  It's a solid 3 star joint.

review: I've always had excellent food and fun times at Clancy's.  The only downside is that Clancy's is very much a neighborhood restaurant so parking is a bit challenging in the area and when it gets crowded it can get very tight on the street.  I'm also sad to have noticed that the dress code has pretty much disappeared and all sorts of people run around in blue jeans and all types of other uncivilized ruffian outfits.    It can get rather loud and boisterous in the restaurant at times and especially downstairs.  Some of my friends go to just hang out at the bar as they enjoy the social atmosphere so much.  The lunches I've had at Clancy's have always been a relatively calm affair compared to the night time fun with very few people in attendance.  Certainly a great spot to enjoy a great night of fun and excellent food.  The good news and the bad news is that it can be very difficult to find if you don't know where you're going so that is good news for locals that like to keep some of our secret spots to ourselves and bad news for tourists that will have a challenge finding it.  Please dress up a bit for traditions sake and come prepared for some great times and great food!

review: I stopped in here for a late lunch and the place was understandably dead. It was fine with me- I don't care if I'm the only person in a restaurant at any given time.  I was seated, and as I looked over the menu free chips and salsa were dropped off. Have you noticed that fewer and fewer places bring you free chips and salsa? I can understand charging for queso, but I like having the chips to munch on while I'm deciding what to eat. I decided to keep it simple and go for the burrito dinner which comes with a ground beef burrito, beans and rice.   The food came out within 5 minutes, which immediately made me go "hmmm". I like fast service, but when food comes out that fast I wonder how fresh it is. The burrito was okay, but nothing special at all. It was literally ground meat in a tortilla. I'm not even sure you can call that a burrito. The beans and rice were decent, but forgettable.  I might have to go back and try something a little more complex. The food hit the spot, mainly because I was starving, but if I had been expecting really good Mexican food, I would have been left disappointed. Also, service was okay, but my waiter was handling a beer delivery at the same time that he was waiting on me, so I had to flag him down a few times and remind him I was there.

review: In what seems like months ago, Blake F., Caroline P. and I made plans to dine at Sycamore.  Our wait was finally over on a blustery Wednesday night, when we descended upon Lansdowne.  The restaurant was full but for one table when we arrived around 8:30.  The décor was warm and inviting, with rich fall colors and holiday accents.  Our lovely server, Elle, seated us and promptly brought water, bread and the amuse bouche du jour, a creamy potato soup, to our table.      Although Chef Sam Jacobson is a friend (full disclosure), he assured us on our arrival that everything we ordered would be served exactly as it would to a stranger.  In other words, he wanted us to have the most honest experience possible.  And since we're all being honest here, I can't think of a single thing Sam could have done differently that would have made the meal better than it already was.  We started with a cheese plate, which featured four very different cheeses that were well complimented by other items on the board, my favorite being the drunken raisins.  I want to eat cheese and drunken raisins every day!    Next up was a fantastic baby arugula salad and a delightfully crunchy carmelized onion, goat cheese and pancetta phyllo tart, which was served alongside a frisee salad.    For my main, I opted for the boeuf bourguignon (although the fontina stuffed meatloaf could be heard calling my name from the kitchen).  The beef was fork tender and served in a hearty broth over mashed potatoes.  The broth itself had strips of tender carrots and - brace yourself - bacon.  It was fantastic but I had to stop short of finishing in order to save room for dessert.  We shared an orange scented flan, a pumpkin cheesecake that had the most wonderful crust and a delicious banoffee tart that Sam claimed the Brits were first responsible for creating.  Many props to our friends across the pond for that one!  The check arrived and with it came three house-made cocoa dusted truffles.  It was a beautiful ending to a fabulous meal.  As Caroline mentioned, we were fortunate enough to catch a glimpse of the New Year's Eve prix fixe menu, and it sounded wonderful.  Do not hesitate to give Sycamore a try; it's a suburban gem and it won't be long before resies are hard to come by!

I stayed consistent with my main and got the Seoul hot chicken sandwich, with fries. It was delicious and definitely spicy. My husband had the pork ssam - I didn't try it but it looked great. Can't wait until we can enjoy a meal at the restaurant again but, in the meantime, I'm happy to know we can enjoy the same delicious food at home.

review: I've been going to this grocery location for years way before it was a Rouse's.  I really miss the 24 hour operations that used to exist before Katrina when this was a Save-A-Center as I like to do my shopping late after all the crowds are asleep.  The quality of the food and the design of the store has drastically improved since Rouse's took over and they have consistently upgraded things at this location.  There is a really good selection of local Louisiana products and some local produce featured.  They have a decent to good prepared food selection here along with the excellent Progress Grocery muffalettas and Rouse's house brand olive salad is among the best there is.    My biggest issue with this location is that there is almost always a line at the deli counter and I often get frustrated with how long it takes to order and check out at this location.  Another bone of contention with the deli is they will often advertise deli meats on sale but when you place an order for such a special they often forget to give you the sale price and this has happened frequently enough that I complained on their website but I NEVER heard back from anybody.  They still have the self-checkout machines left over from when this was a Save-A-Center but they don't use them for whatever reason and I wish they would re-activate them to speed the frequently slow checkout process at peak hours.    Rouse's constantly works to improve this location but it still has some weak points that chronically disappoint and there is still a lot of room for improvement.  Overall this is still a good spot to make your groceries at typically good prices.  The nice selection of local brands, products, and produce is certainly appreciated.

review: I understand why people love Casnova's Kitchen for breakfast. It sure doesn't look like much driving up, but once inside things start to come into focus. The dining room is a tight squeeze with only a handful of booths. But, if you go to the left and look around the back wall, you will find the infamous kitchen and a short luncheonette counter with a half dozen stools. If you enjoy watching the chef do his thing on the grill, and the entertaining talk between him, customers and his staff, then this is the joint for you.   Grab a spinner, check out the large menu and go for something good. Anything with eggs and coffee is the right idea. I went with a sausage, egg and cheese on kaiser roll, but those omelets being prepared on the hot steel looked real appealing, too. All the while, the second gen Casanova (Tim?) exchanged information with me and had funny dialogues with the guys coming to this backroom man cave grill. They all knew each other well, and the comradery was patent. Even as a stranger I felt I was almost part of their clique.   And, the sandwich was very good, too. Sausage logs (not links) a little crisp, with folded fried eggs and a couple slices of cheese, all on a  superior fresh roll brought in from a bakery in Jersey. Java refills as needed.   This was a three ring, holy roller circus. It didn't look like a winner, but much like the other special places around Bucks, the ones that are hardest to find or hidden in plain site, are usually the best.  One of the best breakfasts of the year!

review: This is a review of the beer/bar area and not the food.  We stopped in here on Mardi Gras, just to check it out and try out the beer. The downstairs area was pretty crowded, so we headed upstairs and snagged a seat at the bar. I would say that Crescent City Brewhouse is more of a restaurant than a brewhouse- they only offer four beers, but nonetheless, i was eager to try what they had. review: Let me start by saying the food was delicious. I had absolutely no problem at all with that. I've been several times to the Lagerhaus in the past and I've always enjoyed my dining experience, however tonight was ... different?  I came in alone, the husbeast was busy with preparation for our Vegas trip, so I got to catch dinner on the fly. I spun Yelp and came up with this as a destination, and since I hadn't done a review, I was especially happy!  When I entered, I was greeted by the hostess and let her know there would be just me "We can do that." and she drew me back to a table with a singular seat - it happened to be at a corner of the wall, just in front of a LARGE party table. She told the waitress serving that table that she had me as well. The waitress looked... -thrilled- (sarcasm).  I was greeted with no eye contact, no smile. Asked what I wanted to drink, and when it contained no alcohol, the contempt was clearly there. Unsweet Iced tea was ordered and brought to my table, and I was asked if I wanted to place my order. Weinerschnitzel, with a Caeser Salad & Grilled Vegetables.  With a nod she went and took it to the chef.  My menu was never taken away. It stayed on my table until the very end of my meal.   At some point before my food came to the table, I managed to get her attention, I asked for some Sweet & Low. Rather than tell me they didn't carry that and offer me splenda (I'm allergic to it) she reached behind me, to another table - one that had a full set up - something mine lacked (No salt/pepper, etc) and plopped it down in front of me, no words, nothing. Color me unimpressed.   The food was run out by other waitstaff. And mind you, I got my salad with the Entree and side. Something that hasn't happened with my service in the past. I'm used to getting the salad before I get the main course.  When the food was delivered, I needed salt. Rather than flag her down -again- I turned around, and I saw it. She was kabitzing with the table behind me, Has been the entire time. They are a large party of 8. I see that she is enjoying their food with them, sharing in their conversation and everything. And that's FINE, if you don't have other people to attend.   I made eye contact when I got the salt briefly before sitting down.  She came back over about 10 minutes later, and with a lifeless voice -told me- "Evertyings good." And before I could answer, she walked away. It was about then that I was mostly done. Half of my dinner remained, I was sitting with my back against the wall, my phone in my hands, avidly NOT paying attention to my food, and trying to catch her eye as she passed by me 3 or 4 times. She had to pass me, because the Computer to input orders was right around the corner.   Finally another waitress saw the posture and asked if I needed a box, and I said yes, "And my check." The box was given as was my check, handed to me by "my" waitress. When I received it, I did something I don't ever do, You see, I work in the service industry, Tips are important, but they have to be earned. I tipped, but ultra low. Clearly she didn't care about her service level to me, so I didn't care about my tip level to her, and noted it on the bill as well.   I hate that I had to drop the review by a star because of this kind of service, because the food was Delicious! Their schnitzel was great, the vegi's were tasty and the salad... well it was salad! But poor service is poor service and attitude is everytihing. I'm sorry if she was having a bad day, and if a singular person who isn't going to be a burden to you is the final straw... but it pays to pay attention.

review: 3.5 stars is about right rating for this restaurant. They are popular among the local neighborhoods. We saw many African Americans customers when we visited this place. Fried seafood is one of their favorite food. Parking is kind of limited. The seat down table also limited if you want to eat there. Many people ordered to go.    We got the fried conch as appetizer. This is my first time to have fried conch. The coating is good. We also got the oyster and fish combo box. The oyster is in good pieces. We like the fried shrimp. It was delicious. The fish can have a choice like Basa, tilapia, salmon or mullet. For fried food I like to eat it there.   There is a wait after ordering. I don't mind with fresh fried seafood. It is good to eat there instead of take home.

review: Out of town friends chose to stay at the Radisson Hotel Philadelphia Northeast for a few nights while visiting the area.  I tried to tell them in advance that the hotel was not really in Philadelphia at all, but just beyond the city limits in Bucks County.  I also described the neighborhood as groaty old Route 1, auto dealers, by the hour motels, and garish liquor stores. They didn't care. The price was right, and they wanted to shop in the surrounding malls.    I went to see them there a couple of times. Parking was easy with a big lot.  The building looked a bit dated, but still highly functional.  Nice atrium in the lobby.  Cool black and whites of historic buildings in Philly.  A decent bar and free breakfast.  Clean, comfortable rooms.  Small bathrooms.   They managed to eat at several interesting places within a short distance (Steve's Prince of Steaks, Andy's Diner, Mission BBQ, Starbucks, to name a few).  They had nothing but good things to say about the place, other than they wished they had stayed in Center City, and could just put their horses in the stable and walk around town.    Maybe next time.

review: Grand Opening of Chinese take out joint on South Broad Street, Trenton.    It has a postage stamp size dining area with only 2 tables for eating in, and 3 chairs for waiting on take away.  The space is still clean and the kitchen shiny, as it has been open little more than a week.    The menu is extensive and basically a traditional Chinese/American emporium.  Nothing authentic, but if you wanted really good Chinois you would not be parking your wheels on S. Broad in the first place.  My Orange Flavored Chicken was a load in the styro container they give to even those who eat in.  The chicken was fresh enough, and had not been deeply frozen.  The sauce was gloopy orange colored, although the taste of the citrus was weak, despite the orange peel in the mix.  The Fried Rice was a bright yellow from the dye used in the bullion stock that morning.  It had plenty of roast pork and veggies in it, but I did not see much (if any) egg scrambled into it.    The people here are Fuzhounese, the province just north of old Canton, and across the straits from Taiwan.  Their cuisine is similar to Cantonese, but has some other influences.  It tends toward less sweetness, but close enough to allow for success in the Chinese take out wars.    If you are interested, go soon while everything is new and clean.  The owners are there and take an interest in getting things right.  Just remember what you are dealing with, and you will not be disappointed.  PRO TIP - They don't serve hot tea!

review: One of my favorite memories of the Peristyle was dancing across it, just spinning and spinning...of course I was just a tot when I did that, although yes I would do that again...as soon as it gets a little cooler. Yesterday when I passed by the entire pavilion was full of tables and chairs as caterers were setting up for some sort of to do.   When it was built, in 1907 it was designed for open air dances with a band on one side and a dance floor on the other. I love the neo-classical colonnade and I miss the melty faced lions. Who knew our weather would be so brutal on their faces but those were "renovated" in 2012 and look more lion-y now.   You can rent the space for your event from City Park, hence the catered event yesterday, but if it's not booked you can have your own dance party/photo session/impromptu soiree in it's environs and backed by beautiful Bayou Metairie.

review: After a day at the beach, one of our family members asked us to join him for dinner, but left the destination up to us, figuring since we lived in Pinellas Co, we'd have the scoop.  I played Yelp roulette and landed on one place, but it was closed, so Roosterfish Grill was our 2nd location.   First impressions are everything and this parking lot was busy. Busy parking lot means popular destination.  It was early on Sunday evening, just 5:30 pm so Early bird as well, as seen by nearly every head inside was a shade of gray and I think we were one of three tables under 55.   Id never heard of the location, so I had no idea what to expect, the name said chicken/fish and that is more or less what the menu said too.  Our waitress, Carmen was very prompt, very friendly, absolutely wonderful.  My brother in law placed an order for the ahi appetizer and seemed to enjoy every bite.   When our mains came to the table: Popcorn shrimp platter, Fried Grouper and a NY Strip, we were surprised at the sizes of the portions. The grouper came with 3 fillets, the popcorn shrimp was huge. The NY Strip was large as well, 12 oz.   The sides were generous and well seasoned, I really liked the green beans and their garlic mashed potatoes.   I was disappointed in the steak and this takes one star away from what would have been a 4 star review, because the meat tasted more of propane than it did of meat. It lacked seasoning, not even salt & pepper. Other wise our dining experience was fine, the paper towel rolls above your head is kitsch and a bit off putting, but that's my issue.

review: Bravo Pho has replaced the earlier Vietnamese restaurant at this location, and all I can say is, "Hallelujah!"   There is no comparison between the two enterprises. Bravo is the real deal, not just a reasonable facsimile for folks who don't know from authentic Viet cuisine. The menu is extensive, and the noodle soup (pho) and rice dishes (com) are excellent. The owners and chef are legit from Hanoi, and know their way around a Vietnamese kitchen. No excuses necessary!  I was in the mood for their version of wonton soup, which was basically pho broth with a large number of dumplings rather than noodles in the hot bath.  Same accoutrements (Thai basil, sprouts, jalapeno slices, lime wedge), and same great taste, but with beef/pork stuffed wontons. I thought it was a very good version of the classic.   Why not five star? Well, because I am spoiled by visiting Vietnam and eating incredible food in both the north and south of the country. The small houses in Philly and Ocean Grove, California are often excellent, and this one may yet transport me to the Mekong River as those do. When that happens there will be five stars shining above its door.   Bravo to Bravo for being as slurpin' good as it is!

review: Jack's Cold Cuts & Catering (aka Jack's Deli) on Street Road in Bensalem, Pa., has been around for a while making fat sandwiches and catering local parties.  When we walked in around 8:30 one morning last week, they were busy stocking up on the provisions that had just been delivered by the bakery.  We were looking for breakfast, and Jack waved us to a booth with a smile as he carried a large tray of breads to their bin.    The coffee wasn't made yet, so we knew it would be fresh.  We ordered a couple of sandwiches (Sausage, Egg & Cheese on Kaiser, Pepper, Egg & Cheese on Croissant), and settled in to the sound of the staff getting ready for the day.  The place is old enough to need a little TLC, but it is bright and airy.    Our meals arrived in plastic baskets a few minutes later.  They were hot and melty, but not best of breed.  Run of the mill roll and croissant, and average innards.  Adequate, but not calculated to win any awards.  The coffee was on the same level.  Okay.    Jack's advertises that it is a "Jewish Style Deli."  Maybe.  It does have the smoked meats and East European breads and soups that identify that cuisine.  But, it has ample pork products for the rest of the customers.    Jack's seems like a place that is loved by people who have grown up on their dishes, but more objectively is happy to be quite average.

review: If you read my recent review for Tria Rittenhouse, this one is essentially going to be pretty similar. We once again ordered the Cheesy Package for 2 from Tria's current takeout menu. This time, we went with pickup instead of delivery because we also wanted some wine.   Again, everything was packaged so nicely though I will say Rittenhouse had a slight edge because they packaged their side salads separately (not a big deal). This time, we went with two sandwiches, one turkey and one tuna. I asked for aioli on the side for the turkey sandwich but didn't think to ask for no mayo on the tuna since our sandwich the week before didn't have any. Turns out, the tuna sandwich does come with mayo and it was on there pretty thick, so it's something I'll keep in mind for next time.   We also switched up our dessert from the flourless chocolate torte the week before to the ricotta cheesecake. I didn't think the chocolate could be topped but the cheesecake was incredible! Next time, we might have to add on the extra dessert because it will be tough to decide between the two.   Can't wait to enjoy Tria in person again but I'm loving their current to-go offerings!

VERY expensive for what it is - picnic food - but we love to get take out meals from Gross'.  Years ago you could get the most amazing frozen meat (and cheese - but I liked the meat better) ravioli here, too - but alas, no longer.  Want a neat idea for a quick picnic?  Don't feel like cooking?  Like tasty chicken?  Try Gross'.  It's NOT at all gross.

review: Wow! What a cool experience right here in downtown Indy.  As a local, I've heard the Vonnegut name for most of my life, but wasn't that familiar with the author's work until recently.  Having just read "Slaughterhouse Five" and a collection of short stories "Welcome to the Monkey House", I got an appreciation for how imaginative and engaging the author was.  The museum is open for visitors to view with three floors of items and artwork, a book store, and soon, a coffee shop.  But if you want to get your money's worth, contact the museum to find out when the guided tours are...they make the experience so much better.  My tour guide was very knowledgeable and had a sense of wit that complemented the author's.  The museum has several sections which are interesting for different reasons.  One section has a collection of banned books and I just can't get over that some narrow minded communities think that ideas can be shut down.  Hint:  There's a thing called the internet and people will get whatever they want, so don't be an * about it.  There are also books that are by authors that inspired Vonnegut or fit into the styles of writing that the author liked.  Note that members of the museum can take advantage of the lending library here.  Up on the second floor is a gift/book shop where you can find items to purchase related to the author.  On the third floor, there was a Slaughterhouse Five exhibit that features a lot of text and imagery from the author's time as a prisoner of war after the Battle of the Bulge during WWII when he was forced to march to Dresden and kept in an underground slaughterhouse.  Also of note is that if you go online at the station on the second floor, you will find a wide variety of information and images about Vonnegut for you to explore.  For those who have trouble negotiating stairs, there is an elevator available.  I highly recommend this museum for adults who consider themselves free thinkers.  I don't think this is a place that children would appreciate simply because they probably won't have had enough life experience to understand the ideas and concepts the author wrote about.    Parking is free in the mini lot that surrounds the building with access off Indiana Avenue as well as West St/MLK Blvd.  Metered Street parking is also available on Indiana Ave.  The tour lasted about 40 minutes (mine started at 11 a.m.)  Definitely worth checking out to get a fuller experience from the museum. review: Yesterday I had what was one of the best customer service experiences in recent memory. While putting on my coat to go forage for a late lunch somewhere in the GradHo 'hood, The Quick Fixx popped into my mind. I took off my coat (who really wants to go out in the rainy cold, anyway?), perused the menu and gave them a ring.   The owner, Matt, answered the phone and, once I gave him my digits, told me that he had planned to call me this week so we could discuss my recent experience. It was pretty obvious that he had read my Yelp review, so we talked about the restaurant, their products, etc. It was clear that he valued the feedback and wanted to make sure his customers were happy. This pretty much cemented me as a repeat customer.   I ended up ordering a salad off the menu, the Di Carlo, which is a Caesar with grilled haloumi cheese. I added chicken and also ordered some of the tomato bruschetta, just in case. With a can of Diet Coke, the order came to around $15, but Matt gave me a five dollar discount for the fact that I was willing to chat for a few minutes. Totally unnecessary but definitely a nice gesture.   My order arrived in the quoted twenty minutes and I was happy with everything. Their Caesar dressing is seriously tasty (and by the way, the toasted bread is how they do their croutons - Matt and I discussed that also). I do think the salad and a side of bruschetta was just the right amount of food for lunch. Until next time!

The menu is short and sweet but very well-rounded. I loved that there were several options for breakfast meats. I ordered the eggs, meat, bread, potato plate and asked to sub a side salad for bread, which was not a problem. I selected the turkey bacon as my meat and it had great flavor. I loved the seasoned potatoes as well. My dining companion had the banana pancakes which looked heavenly.   Our servers kept our coffee and water glasses full and were very sweet. Great experience and I'm looking forward to my next visit.

review: I enjoyed my brunch at Front Street Cafe a few weeks ago. I love when restaurants feature a brunch menu during the week; it's the best time to check out spots that might otherwise be too crowded on weekends.   The eggs benedict with bacon was very tasty. I love when there's a side salad and the one that came with was fresh and flavorful. I was so curious about the oven roasted potato so I ordered one on the side. It was super crispy on the outsides and fluffy in the middle. Delish.   The restaurant is quite large and features a beautiful bar as the centerpiece of two dining rooms (there is also an upstairs area and a courtyard for warmer months). It's a nice place to get some work done or meet up with a friend, especially during the week. Looking forward to my next visit.

review: Now that I am spending more time at the USCIS building on 41st Street, and the immigration interviews and other proceedings start as early at 8:00 am, I need a place to cool my jets over coffee or breakfast while I wait to be heard. I learned long ago that it is better to arrive early and wait for court or other meetings, than to deal with heavier traffic later in the morning, and risk arriving late. Today, I asked one of the guards in the security area where to go for coffee until the public was allowed into the building at 7:30.  He was thoughtful and thorough, giving me a list of places within a few blocks.  When he mentioned the restaurant on Market Street that had a full breakfast menu, he showed more enthusiasm then for the others mentioned, so I took my clients there for morning repast.    Turned out that Hamilton Restaurant is an old school luncheonette, with long counter with spinners on one side, and tables on the other.  Kitchen in back. The offerings were plentiful, with both breakfast and lunch available during open hours.  We opted for a couple of omelets (w/ home fries), turkey sage sausage, egg & cheese on Kaiser roll, and a grilled blueberry muffin.  Ten minutes later we were served by a very friendly and considerate woman, who seemed to anticipate our needs.  That was unexpected and exceptional.   Our food was very good.  The omelets were stuffed to the gills with the cheesesteak and sausage fillings two of them wanted, while my sandwich was not overly large, but very tasty with the turkey sage sausage a surprise star of the show.  Very happy with that recommendation.  The muffin had a strong resemblance to Costco muffins, but there were no complaints. Coffee was strong and the request that one be half milk, well received and delivered.   This location is beyond the spreading influence of UPenn and Drexel.  That means that it is still an original joint that has not been gentrified yet.  The cozy neighborhood atmosphere was palpable, and the prices reflective of that.    Very happy to find a place where I can eat and be comfortable while waiting to go to work.

review: I'll be honest, I really don't want to like HL because of some of their political views that are known to everyone. However, shopping with my cuz this holiday season, HL has grown on me. I wont become a true regular, but you'll find me here when I have special needs.   This past holiday season, HL made my life so much easier. I bought multiples of their gifts boxes, bags and tissue. It made my gift wrapping this year, a breeze. All I had to do was tie a Tiffany style bow around each of the boxes and I was done. It was so easy-peasy and when I bought it all, it was 50% off.   Since I had so much luck with the gift wrapping, when it was my turn to host the holiday luncheon at work I came back. What did I get this time? I got coordinating plates, napkins, glasses and paper table cloth. I even got plastic utensils in red & green. Again, the prices were 50% off and lower then Party City. My table looked stunning. review: I was in the mood to grab a bite to eat before catching a movie at noon at one of the local theaters, so I decided I wanted something quick.  I hadn't been to Primanti Bros before, but my wife had and liked what she ordered.  I pulled into their private lot and asked the hostess about getting a "to go" order.  She directed me to the bar and said that the staff there would help me.  I was greeted and saw menus by the counter.  I helped myself to one and ordered a Corned Beef and Cheese with Classic tater tots.  I also asked about how long the order would take and was told about 10 minutes.  Sure enough, my order was ready then and I was on my way.  What I will tell you is that even though the sandwiches are pricey and don't include sides other than chips, the total size of the sandwich is huge.  Thick bread, lots of meat, and a tart cabbage/slaw instead of sauerkraut made for a nice meal.  Of course, the meal was enough for two meals, so I saved the second half for later.  The only negative, which was minor, was that I got French Fries (a generous portion) instead of tots in my order.  I am not sure if fries are what they mean by "classic cut", but it wasn't what I was expecting.  I will say that the staff also packed a comprehensive "to go" bag full of condiments for me which also was generous enough to keep.  I can't tell you how many times I've had to go orders that skimped or completely forgot to include condiments.  Overall, a quick and tasty meal with enough leftovers for another one.    Review #3134

review: Sorry everyone, but I just don't get the warm and fuzzies for this place.  Don't get me wrong, the store itself is nicely laid out and very cute, but the items are priced at highway robbery levels.  The free yoga classes do nothing to add to the appeal for me, because I don't live in the city and I'm not a big fan of yoga.  Lastly, and many will find this statement upsetting, I found the sales staff to be downright annoying.  One girl sang along to the background music at full volume (am I the only person who finds this awkward?) and another asked a customer "what was wrong with them?" when the woman decided against whatever it was she tried on.  As if there couldn't possibly be a reason for not loving every piece.    You may be wondering why I didn't simply leave the store to save myself this aggravation.  Well friends, my New York brother must have decided back in December that this trendy athletic wear store would be the perfect place to get my mother and I gift cards.  That, or there was a location in very close proximity to his workplace, or Penn Station, or both.  (Steve, if you are reading this, I kid.  You know I love your thoughtful gifts! Now, get thinking because you have exactly one month until my birthday!)  Therefore, since making a purchase was a necessity and not an option, my mom picked up a very cute gym bag, and I nabbed a workout tank (on sale for $29).  At the counter, I noticed some individually packaged thongs, which I can only assume have some sort of special power as they were priced at thirteen dollars a pair.  The girl at checkout snapped me out of my daydream when she asked if we needed a bag.  "No toots, we're just going to cut the tags off of this bad boy and throw everything in there!"  My actual response was a terse "Yes.  We would like a bag."  Sheesh!

review: You've heard of a dive bar. This is a dive deli and you'll love it just as you love your local dive bar. If it were not for a Meet-Up group, I would have never found this little mom & pop sandwich shop in The Patch neighborhood.   28 members of, Dudes, Dining and Dives descended on this small neighborly deli (They knew we were coming) for an amazing lunch.  Typically you'd order at the counter, but with our special group, we had our own waitress in a separate dining room. 28 diners vs 1 server and she won. I'll admit, there were a few bumps, but she and the sandwich building crew got them resolved quickly.  For my lunch I did a small side salad and 1/2 of Navy Chief. The salad was a good mix of iceberg and romaine lettuce, tossed with diced tomatoes, shredded provel cheese and  topped with parmesan cheese. When ever enjoying a salad out, I always go with the "house" dressing. Here, it was a flavorful vinaigrette.   Having a salad, I only ordered a half of a sandwich. I went with, The Navy Chief. Many of the deli sandwiches have a nautical theme name, which is apropo for the delis name. My Navy Chief had, salami, pepperoncini, pepper jack cheese and garnished with; tomato, onion, lettuce, pickle and provel cheese on toasted garlic bread. They are not stingy with the toppings, so I glad I went with a half - I was stuffed.   Only downside to RDPYC is that there is no view of the yachts coming and going from the docks. If they had the view, they'd definitely be a 5 Star deli.   I'll be back? - It's off the beaten path, but yes I'll return for a sammie.   When: January 23, 2018 Why: Lunch with large group

review: This Denny's on Old Lincoln Highway (Business Rt. 1), Langhorne, PA, is an older, bigger version of "America's Diner." It has large windows facing its southern exposure, making for a warm seating area even on cold days. It was so bright at my booth that I had to close the shades to keep from sweating.   There were only four other tables occupied when I arrived. I was greeted promptly and escorted to my booth. Coffee and menu arrived moments later. I hadn't been inside a Denny's in years, and my memory of Country Fried Steak was dominant in my head. I ordered that. It included two eggs (scrambled wet), and rye toast, in addition to the unlimited java. Service was friendly and timely. I was approached every few minutes as to my satisfaction and needs. Never felt neglected.   My tastes have changed since the last time I had this breakfast in my early twenties. I remembered the crunch and meatiness of the steak, but had forgotten how heavily cloying the gravy was. I was able to remove a lot of it, but it was still a strong element of the meal, making for a salty and overly caloric feast. Still, the eggs were done perfectly, and their home fries were nicely crisp. With the three mugs of coffee I drank, it was a filling meal.   Not sure there will be a next time, as, obviously, I seldom have the urge for Denny's. Yet, it was a decent, if salty, breakfast. It briefly connected me to my earlier life, and alerted me to how my tastes have changed. If there were to be a next time, I would lean to the french toast or pancakes, which they offer in abundant varieties. Prices are still quite reasonable.

review: I chose Villa Barone as the location for some of my college crew to get together for dinner on Saturday night.  The decision was based partly on the affordable prices but mostly on the ability for us to get a little rowdy without being asked to leave.  We were seated promptly upon arrival, which was great considering the restaurant was crowded.  We had a bottle or two of wine to each person, plus a flask of vodka (one of the girls is allergic to wine--bummer, right?!).  Our server kept our bottles rotating through the meal.  Wine glasses were never empty for more than a few seconds, which was fab.  For the first few minutes, we all sat staring at the plates of olive oil and spices--it wasn't until our drinks were delivered and orders placed, that someone requested bread for dipping.  (Okay, it was me.  You know I love some bread.)  After that, our bread baskets flowed for the rest of the meal.  And that meal was de-lish!  We started off with a tower of mozzarella, which was wrapped in prosciutto, fried calamari that came with two types of dipping sauces, fried mozzarella with capers and a fantastic tomato-based sauce and bruschetta.  All four starters were fantastic, and provided more than enough food for our party of seven to share.    Everyone seemed happy with their dinner selections as well.  By the time my rigatoni and vodka sauce arrived, I was already pretty full, so I didn't get too far into the plate o' carbs before me.  What I did have, however, was rich and delicious.  After a couple shared desserts and a few cups of coffee, we called it a night.    Should we end up having another get together in my neck of the woods again, chances are high that we will return to Villa Barone, for the group-friendly aspect.  One observation: the restaurant is also family-friendly, and there were a couple kids running around which was bothersome to my friends on the other side of the table.  Luckily, I was far enough away and a few glasses deep so I didn't really notice.

review: This is a cool little place to see live music.  Some friends and I saw a band here a few weeks ago.  The stage area is small, but the sound quality is good, which can be tough in a smaller place.  I really like the atmosphere of the place and the way it's decorated with a "kitschy" New Orleans feel.  My only complaint is the bar.  It's a really long bar, the place gets packed, and there was only one bartender working on a Friday night.  It took forever to get served and the poor bartender looked super frazzled (and I couldn't blame him, at all.  He was just swamped with customers.).  My suggestion would be to add another bartender on Friday nights.  Maybe this was a rare night with only one server.  Anyway, I would definitely go back, especially since they have Taceaux Loceaux being served in the kitchen.

review: Grapeseed is in my rotation of my local hood restaurants that I can get a quick and satisfying dinner. It's another one that I am not surprised that it made the STL 100 List. It did surprise me that the "must order" recommendation was the Turkey Nachos.  I'm typically a breast man, especially when comes to turkey. I love the turkey breast at thanksgiving and enjoy a smoked turkey breast at BBQ joints. So when I saw, that these Turkey Nachos were made from the leg, I never thought to order them. Now that Ian, said they are a must order, I've given them a try and they are a winner.   They make for a light and simple dinner with a craft beer. The turkey is from Buttonwood Farms, which always a plus. The foundation of the nachos is crispy sweet potato chips, topped with the meat of a turkey leg, braised in house "firecracker" sauce, grape tomatoes, red onion, roasted red pepper and topped with a buttermilk dressing. Best thing- it's gluten free for those who need to be concerned about that type of diet.  The Burger and the House Cut Fries will always be my favorite and would have been my "must order". If you are having trouble finding a place to park on the street, don't fret, you can park in the lot over at Tom Bess Automotive.   When: April 16, 2016 Why: Nachos and STL 100
