review: Several weeks before Thanksgiving, I took to Twitter to find out which local businesses were taking orders for pecan pies. I received several recommendations, but Wedge & Fig stuck out since I had been wanting to get back in the wake of an awesome YEE in October.   When I called to order my pie, I quickly discovered that W&F was not taking orders for pecan, but they were doing two other varieties. After explaining the mix-up of info I had received on Twitter, they generously agreed to bake a pecan pie especially for me. Floored and touched, I promised I would not reveal this information to the masses. Now that Thanksgiving is over, I think it's safe to let the cat out of the bag.   For the record, the pie was absolutely delicious. Everyone in my family had a slice and all agreed that the rich, buttery flavor and crunchy, sticky texture was spot on. Out of the three pies we had, the pecan yielded the least amount of leftovers. I enjoyed a coveted second slice this morning, and it was every bit as good as last night.   My mom told me I am now officially on pie duty for Thanksgiving. I know where I'll be ordering my pie from next year, and I can only hope that the pecan will be offered as one of the selections.

review: Well, at long last, I can scratch Le Bec Fin off my to-do list.  Finally, I was able to justify the expense...  My husband & I celebrated his birthday by attending Chef Georges Perrier's Chef's table last night.  The main dining room is amazingly gorgeous.  What a place for a wedding or party!  We were seated in a slightly less glam area at the front of the house at a long table for 20.  (17 in all)  Perrier is running a special all summer Mon. - Thurs.  (20 seats per night) a "pay what you wish" 5 course set menu.  If you can, ACT FAST and get in on it before August is over.  The first course was the chilled pea soup from the regular menu.  Very good - but no way I would have ordered this in real life.  It was pluched with a dollop of almond ice cream which was heavenly.  (Made up for the fact that it's pea soup.)  2nd course was a single seared scallop.  DH & I are not scallop lovers - in fact, DH won't touch 'em so he had a salade ennui (boring salad) in its place.  I forced myself to eat the scalop and it was, indeed, perfectly cooked and surprisingly good (for a scallop fan I bet they'd LOVE it.).  3rd course was a slightly overcooked white fish called Limon (like a fluke or flounder).  I was looking so forward to this course and it was sauced with a lemon foam and plated over a few fava beans (yummy), chanterelles (a bit salty to my taste) and a tasteless hazlenut puree - the consistency and color of putty.  4th course was the best (save for dessert which was REALLY the best.) - a rare hanger steak.  3 -4 morsels in a decadent bordelaise (or was it a red wine/demi glace reduction?).  The sauce was lick-the-plate worthy.  And for dessert one of the BEST classic creme brulee.  Lightly laced with Gran Marnier and a crispy top.  Service was very attentive UNTIL the end when we needed our check.  At about 9:45 PM nearly everyone (there were several waitstaff) disappeared.  The Chef came out to our table prior to and during service and was collegial and utterly charming.  (Really.)  It helped that I speak un peu de francais and was seating next to a lovely, fluent, Belgian woman.  (Merci, Madame!)  Will I return?  Oh yes - but not in a hurry.  I would simply like to sit in the bar downstairs and have desserts off that AMAZING dessert cart (not part of our meal, alas).  That opera cake has my name on it!  Bien Fait!  Oh - and don't laugh but I actually drank (again don't laugh) a Mojito with my meal (I know, I know - in a French restaurant) and it was GREAT.  And it was $10.  My husbands manhattan was $12.  They do not serve Veuve Cliquot - which was what I was jonesin' for.

review: Long story short: it's a mall. Since Yelp requires me to expound a little more on that sentiment, here we go.  I agree with other reviewers who say that this is a good place for tourists, but not worth going out of your way. I would, however, go out of my way if I was in the market for something specific. One thing they have here is a fudge shop. I love fudge, so that was worth the trip for me. They had quite a few stores that were having "season change" sales, so it was nice to browse around and check out the deals. There is a store that sells Michael Kors purses, another that sells kitchen ware and other various clothing outlets. The food court is okay- there are some pretty basic chains like Cane's and Izzo's. The one burger place they had had the longest line of any of the food options. There's a daiquiri shop as well as a nice little bar in the middle of the food court, if you are making a day of it and feel like drinking.  The main selling point of the Riverwalk is the view of the river. I really love any spot in the city where you can hang out on a nice day and watch the water. I just have different memories of the Riverwalk from when I was a kid. I remember more local places and less chains, but I could be imagining things.  It's good for what it is, but nothing overly special.

review: WOW! I cannot tell you how excited I was waiting for the Copper Pig to open. Now that it has opened, I am sad to say, it is the winner of a Stevie B Yelp Award. It is the winner of; The Absolute Worst Meal at a Restaurant in 2015. They disappointed me with; food, cocktails and service.  Let me start off with the positive points that saved them from getting a 1 Star Review:  1) Linen Napkins - They're always give a nice upscale feeling to any restaurant.  2) Eco-Friendly To-Go Vessels - Thinking of our planet.  3) French Fries - European style fries & a little cup of ketchup.  4) It's in my hood - Brings variety and vitality to the neighborhood. 5) Girl with water pitcher always made sure your glass was full. (Also see negative point)*  Now the reasons why it was The Absolute Worst Meal at a Restaurant in 2015:  1) Service - Very rushed. We ordered cocktails and three appetizers. When our drinks were served, waitress asked for the rest of our order. We stated we wanted to wait until our small plates arrived. Later when the small plates arrived, she again asked for order. When we ordered a second round of drinks, she responded, "I meant your entrees". The time we were there, it was obvious they wanted us to eat, drink and go as quickly as possible.  2) Deviled Eggs with Bacon Chips - Had the taste of refrigerator. 3) Crispy Brussel Sprouts with Miso and Bacon - Bacon dominated the dish with Brussels Sprouts that were undercooked and hard. Dish was overly salty. Good thing for the water girl.  4) Beet Fries - Tasteless. I love beets and these were flavorless mush. I think they were prepped to far in advance.  5) Bulgogi Cheesesteak - Tough and hard to chew. Disassembled sandwich to see if that would help, but it was the actual beef that was making it tough and chewy.  6) Board Burger - Mealy burger, with a grey tint. My friend said, it resembled a burger patty from McDonald's. Her dog wouldn't even eat it when served the leftovers which were the majority of the burger. (Take note of photo) 7) Cocktails - Weak and unprofessionally prepared. Obvious their bartenders are more comfortable opening beer bottles and pour a draft beer. No skills in a well crafted cocktail.   After leaving CP we went down the street to another establishment and ran into several other diners who where at the CP as well. We all compared notes and were in agreement that they have a lot of improving to do.   I hate for a business in my hood to be on my Terrible Two's List. review: The new distillery/brewery from Sun King is open!  The building is spacious and has a lot of cool features to make the visitors happy.   First, despite the construction, you can get here from the east or west and park for free inside the new Midtown Parking Garage (located on Veterans Way).  Be careful of construction workers if you cross the Monon Trail, but you can get through!  Second, there is a new plaza being built right in front of the building, so Sun King has provided a nice sidewalk to skirt around the construction on the east side of where the plaza is going in.  That should add to the view of the location even more.  Next, the building is very cool.  Two stories of contemporary design with lots of wood (patterns on the walls, stairs, and a flag on the second floor) and lots of gray tones for a somewhat industrial look.  Note that this building doesn't look like a warehouse.  Also, a second floor patio is located on the west end of the building just outside of one of the bars.  Behind the second floor bar is a private room that can be reserved for parties.  Speaking of bars, there is one on each floor, both on the west end.  You can place your beverage orders directly at the bars and grab a seat there, or in one of the many seating areas.  However, you can also flag down one of the roving servers and they will take your beverage order and deliver it to you.  Each table top has a full menu of the liquors, the cocktails, the beers, and even a list of all the food items from each of the food vendors on site.  As far as food goes, three of the four food vendors were operating on day 1.  On the main floor, Oca has a shop in the center of the building, beyond the staircase.  They sell food to eat and packaged items to take home.  Also on the first floor is La Margarita (from Fountain Sq) serving Mexican dishes.  There is room for another restaurant to the right of La Margarita.  On the second floor, you can get pizza from Pi (which also has a food truck in Indy).    For all of the food vendors, you simply go to the counter, place your order and pay and then wait for your food.  I tried the personal sized pizza and only had to wait ten minutes on opening day.  Note that you pay for food at the counters and the beverages on a separate bill unless you are getting a soda from the vendor.  I took advantage of the wait to select one of the cocktails on the menu:  the Matcha Bird which is made from a collaboration of Sun King and Cardinal with a Bird Royale Spirit, Matcha (tea), honey, passion fruit, Topo Chico (bottled water) and Sumac Sugar.  It was delicious!  The server brought my drink to the second floor dining area I selected and the drink went well with the pizza.    The only negative beyond the construction is that the distillery is about a month away from producing their own line of liquors.  In the meantime, they have invited a number of local, state, and regional distilleries to collaborate on some liquors.  As the Sun King brands become available, they will eventually phase out the other items and go solo.  Some of the collaborations are in short supply and may not last long.    I really enjoyed my experience and was welcomed by the staff which encouraged me to browse around so that I could make up my mind.  I look forward to my next visit.  Review #1039

review: I can't think of one thing I didn't like about my stay at the Omni Hotel, aside from the raucous guests who were partying loudly on night one in the room across the hall from mine (they were kicked out of the hotel, from what I later heard).   Okay I lied. There was one slight snafu at check-in, though it was quickly rectified. The woman I checked-in with said my reservation had been cancelled. I assured her that I had not cancelled my reservation as I was there for a work trip. She was able to get me into a room and no further problems were experienced. (I have a feeling the cancellation probably happened when I called a few weeks before the trip to inquire about something to do with my room, though at no point did I say that I wanted to cancel my reservation.)   The guest room was large and had everything I needed. I love when the nightstands have outlets built right in - so convenient! The room and bathroom were spacious and very clean. I felt very comfortable staying there for the three nights I was in town.  My colleague and I took advantage of the UPS business center and transactions were seamless. I also hit the coffee shop on several occasions which was solid. Finally, the gift shop had a really vast selection of necessities, which was great because it didn't seem like there were any pharmacies nearby.    The location of this hotel really can't be beat. I wouldn't hesitate to stay there again!

review: A smokey neighborhood bar where everyone knows your name, except those of us who do not live in the neighborhood. I didn't mind that the bartender didn't know my name, but at least acknowledge me when I sit down at your bar. He was to involved in the football game on TV.  Once the game went to a commercial, all was good. Some of us like football and some of us like myself like baseball, so I forgave him.   I asked to see a menu so I could do a carryout order. Brad was craving a French Dip and we had heard their "Stallion" was one of the best. They slow simmer the Italian Beef with peperoncini, crushed red pepper and their special blend of Italian Seasoning. It is then served on garlic French bread with provel cheese. Brad loved it, said it was good comfort food. I was not impressed, I thought the bread was dried out, they were skimpy on the meat and provel cheese. To me the sandwich was mostly bread.   To go with the Stallion we had Felix's Wings. A 1 lb. serving that has been trashed and thrashed with Jalapeno Ranch.  These wings were great, so great that I will be adding Felix's to my list for Wings. They were large, crispy and seasoned perfectly. What I liked most is that they did not a heavy sauce on them, it was like a dry rub. You could eat and enjoy with no mess.   After placing my order to go, I asked how long it would take and I was told about 20 minutes. I had a motive in my asking, I saw they had a special for $6.45 that included a slice of pizza and a pint. What a deal. I had a Schafley's Pale Ale and Italian Sausage. The slice was a large slice of the pie and very good. I enjoyed the spicy tomato sauce and there was plenty of sausage and cheese. Who knows, I may be returning to have a couple of pints and a whole pizza pie with a friend.   Only negative, lot of smokers and I was the only one not smoking at the bar.

review: After watching Alton Brown create pizza on a HUGE mini bake oven, Anna M and I needed Pizza. It wasn't a want, it was a NEED, so with our handy dandy spinner, we found the 8th avenue pub!   This is located just off Main Street in Safety Harbor, Parking can be tricky if you're not good at paralel parking, but Main street has a lot of open spots. The place is nice, the music is ecclectic and fun. When we arrived, it seemed as though the tender might give us a bit of attitude, but once we were seated, she warmed up and took care of us well.   We ordered a pizza to share and I got a salad, the salad was delicious, crisp lettuce with cherry tomatoes, craisns and cucumbers and cheese. The dressing was on the side and quite tasty.   The pizza was equally tasty. The toppings were generous on this Pub Pie: Pepperoni, Mushrooms, Onions, sausage and garlic. While I didn't find it under done, Anna seemed to think it was.  The location is set up to have live music and it appears they have a lovely outside area as well. Neither was active this night.   Lots of local beers are available on tap! So if you're a beer drinker, this might be the pub for you!

review: If you don't mind paying $23 for a four pack of local suds, Newtown Brewery is a worthwhile destination for the yeast heads in the crowd. The facility is very attractive with plenty of wood and stone, and the beer is excellent for the most part.   We stopped in last weekend and the room was hopping. Tables full of folks escaping Covid captivity. But, we weren't ready for a space packed with over a hundred people without masks, nor social separation, so we bought our "I lost My Marbles" Belgian Tripel four can and headed home. Just didn't feel safe (and thus the one star deduction for lack of public awareness by management).  Under better circumstances, Newtown Brewing would be a big hit in these parts, and in fact, it appears it already is.   The beer was quite strong at 11% alcohol content, but the taste was great, and the color a robust rusty slurry. Liked it a lot. I'm no expert, but these guys seem to have the right recipes.   They do have a food truck in the parking lot most weekends, and we were fortunate to approach the window of Stuff'd Bunns and grab two sliders to partake with the ale at home. They were great and a perfect partner to the cold fermentation. More on them in a separate review coming soon to these Yelp pages.   I hate to have to take out a loan to support my occasional beer addiction, but aside from that, and the insensitivity to the CDC guidelines, Newtown Brewery really enhances the neighborhood. Just hope no one gets exposed to the virus. That is a price far to high to pay for a momentary pleasure.

Although they have other main dish menu, I would recommend just the taco. I have the fish, steak, pork and beef tongue taco. Beef tongue??? There is no such word. Just use Cow Tongue. I actually like that taco.  We have the food to go but it is still good at home after three hours. Be careful about the hot sauce. If you not use to it, it will burn your mouth. They close at Sunday. So save the trip on that day, you already have enough days for the week to enjoy it. For the price you paid, and the quality of the food, they deserve 4 stars.

review: I've had Steve's bookmarked for quit awhile, so when the BF said he wanted to go here for lunch I agreed. I'll disclose up front, I am not a Hot Dog eater. Normally, the only time I eat a dog is at a Cardinals game and occasionally in someones backyard.   I will start off by saying it is a cute little shop specializing in Hot Dogs. Can you say, Urge.  I got a giggle out of the occupancy sign above the front door stating the maximum was 18 people and when I counted the chairs at the tables, there were 22. Which was okay with me, I would have given them 24 or 26 occupancy.   The staff was extremely friendly and was really excited to be selling Hot Dogs. She smooth talked us both into ordering the Two Dog Combo for $11.99. We saved a dollar each by showing our check-in on Yelp.  When I made a comment and selected the A&W because it was diet. She quickly guided me to the Craft Soda, Empire. Telling me that it was a much more flavorful soda. The bf tried the Sarsaparilla by Empire as well. Both were damn good, now I need to find out where I can buy them by the six pack.   From what we were told, Steve hooked up with Vitales Bakery across the street and created his own special Hot Dog Bun. It basically is pizza dough made into a bun for Hot Dogs. Neither of us were impressed with the bun, it was way to chewy. It was also had to cut in to bite size pieces. Many of our dogs were covered in plentiful toppings making it hard to pick up and bite. We wanted so bad to slice them in to eatable bites.  I wish they offered an old fashioned bun as an alternative for us old fuddy dud-dies.   Doing the Two Dog Combos did give us the opportunity to experience four different dogs. Selecting from the large (16) variety was hard, but we quickly narrowed it down.  Steve's Famous Chili - Cheese, St. Louis - Chicago Dog, Crazy Cajun Creole and Bacon - Bacon Jamaican. All four had good presentation in their little red baskets and Steve is very generous with the toppings.   The Chili - Cheese was very messy and hard to hand handle. This one for sure, needs to be cut and eaten with a fork. The Chili had a good flavor and can easily stand on its own in a bow.   I like the fact that they smoke their own dogs and brats on site, we saw them at work as we approached the entrance. The STL - CHI Dog was a true ballpark frank. I could enjoy this one at a Cardinals and Cubs game. The only change I'd make is removal of the tomato,  I'm not a fan of tomatoes. I'd also reduce the amount of onions, to reduce the heartburn.   Bacon - Bacon Jamaican Dog, was a disappointment and it had two of my favorite things; bacon and pepper jack. The description said, two slices of bacon and I expected two slices, one of each side of my dog. Instead, it was chopped and on top.  However, the jerk seasoning and sweet chipotle sauce was a nice touch.   The winner of the four was the Crazy Cajun Creole. A locally smoked Andouille sausage with grilled onions, spicy brown mustard and Sweet Baby Ray's BBQ Sauce.  This one I could hand handle and enjoy, but still found the bun to be chewy.   If either of us return, I know we will go with simpler toppings. The ones we selected on this visit gave both us heartburn, indigestion and upset stomach. We must have delicate digestive systems.

They remade it a second time and it was good - but not the smooth, limey-sweetness that it usually is.  So I drank it.  I got fish tacos ($9 for 3 tacos) and they are the exact same tiny tacos you get for $1 during happy hour - no rice or beans or anything with them.  So I got a side order of corn on the cob (good stuff!).  I am sticking to happy hour here from how on. My husband will stick with Qdoba.

review: What a fantastic little spot! Fellow Yelper Jeff C. suggested that we try this place and since I had heard a lot of good things about it, I was down.  This cozy little restaurant on Tchoupitoulas is the perfect spot for a date night or a celebration. We made reservations for 8, and although we were a few minutes late, we were seated immediately upon arrival. We were given our menus and we ordered some wine. Looking over the menu, I immediately knew what I wanted. I have been on quite the grits kick lately, so when I saw that they offered catfish and grits, I knew that was the dish for me.  As a starter we decided to get the scallops, which were pan seared with butter, lemon, croutons and capers. I'm normally not a HUGE fan of scallops (it's a texture thing), but I am always willing to try food that I haven't liked before prepared in a different way. My experiment paid off because these scallops were delicious. They were flavorful and I really liked them a lot. The capers and butter created a nice sauce for them and I didn't think about the texture once!  Next came the catfish and grits. Check out my picture- this dish was just beautiful. The catfish was crispy and fried to perfection and the grits were nice and firm and not watery at all. The smoothness of the grits was a perfect compliment to the fish and I was sure to get a little bit of both in every bite. I really can't say enough about this part of the meal and I was beside myself happy.  Finally, we really decided to indulge and we treated ourselves to the chocolate mousse. This delicious concoction of whipped light chocolate came in a small chocolate shell bowl. The mousse was delectable and light and was the perfect conclusion to the meal. I also liked the presentation. I posted a picture- it really is a work of art.  The staff was very attentive the entire time and was quick to refill the wine glasses and clear the plates when necessary. I was really very pleased with the entire experience and I think that Tomas Bistro might be one of my new favorite dinner spots in the city.  I would absolutely go back and I am now hungry for more catfish and grits.

review: Friends, some things are better left in the past:  Ex-boyfriends. ck one. College pizza.  The one that rings truest to me is the pizza. Things have changed drastically since I've left my old stomping grounds. Or maybe I was just used to accepting mediocrity on my budget at the time. Regardless, I revisited my college pizza fave while passing through town yesterday, and I'd like my six bucks back.   The pizza still looked decent (see pic - deceiving, no?). They had all my old varieties: chicken romano, cheesesteak, bruschetta, etc. I selected a slice of white with spinach and tomatoes and a piece of the bruschetta Sicilian. After five minutes in the oven, the pizza was ready to go and I got to it.   Disappointing. Both pies were beyond dry and nearly flavorless. I ate out of hunger, but not with gusto. Life beyond college is so much better.

review: This new Sake House is about 3.5 stars. Since we are here for their Happy Hour Special, I round up to 4 stars. The food is good with fresh fish. For price we paid during happy hour, I would said try their happy hour menu. Actually dinner special menu is no bad either. For same two rolls, with extra $2 from Happy Hour, you get salad and soup.   We have the happy hour 3 rolls. We have the Mango Roll. It is spicy tuna top with mango. The spicy tuna have a bit sesame oil to enhance the flavor. It can be more. The second roll is the snapper special. The inside is cucumber and top with slice snapper. The snapper is firm and bouncy. This is a sign of freshness. Our last roll is the Dynamite roll. This is yellowtail and tuna then deep fried.   All three roll is good. Can tell the service is good since we are at their early happy hour and only customer that time.

review: Nomad Roman is my preferred Nomad location. Although I do think the Nomad just off of South Street is nicer, decor-wise, Nomad Roman on Locust Street has two things going for it that the other doesn't: less children and better pizza. Of course, pizza style is definitely a matter of preference. For me, the super thin and slightly charred crust at Nomad Roman is worlds better than the slightly thicker and much more chewy crust at Nomad.   The salad with mixed greens, pears, dried cranberries, blue cheese and pecans is a perfect start to a meal. Meatballs with broccoli rabe and a dusting of parmesan are also really great. You can't go wrong in the pizza department but the Trenton pie is pretty close to perfect. It's also just five bucks at their amazing happy hour, which also features five dollar glasses of house red and white.

review: I am going to make this one short and sweet.   I love the salsas, jellies and spreads form Harry & David. The Jalapeno jelly is one of my favorites.   On my last visit they had Chicken Pot Pies on sale for half price. What a deal, how could I pass on this opportunity to try something new.  It made for an easy dinner that night and we were impressed. The pie had lots of vegetables and white breast meat. It was large enough to feed 5 adults, or in our case lunch the next day.   The customer service was friendly and extremely helpful. When I asked about one of the spreads, they went to the back and brought out an opened jar for sampling. What a nice touch.   Be sure to sign up for their email list so you will be informed of sales and on occasion they send you coupons and we all like coupons.

review: Of all the movie theaters in a 30 minute Jersey-radius, this is by far my favorite.  Although... after going from the Ritz 16 to "Showcase at the Ritz," things aren't as good as they once were.  My main complaint is the bathroom sitch.  During two recent visits, the cleanliness of said b-room was questionable and paper towels were a thing of the past. Despite the bathroom issue, this theater is still my preferred place for movie-watching.  There are always a few indie flicks that you definitely won't catch at other suburban theaters.  And thankfully, whatever rule they have about excluding young children still exists, because I continue to enjoy my cinema in peace, without anything too obnoxious going on around me.    It should definitely be noted that the popcorn here is waaaaaay better than at other theaters.  I suspect it's because it's popped fresh and/or laced with cocaine because my good intentions of "just a diet soda" seem to fly out the window once I get my first whiff of buttery goodness. On the one in five visit when I do maintain my self-control, the coffee bar rocks my world.    Showcase might not be The Ritz of yore, but it still blows other theaters out of the water.

review: I was doing some work at the mall and I was pretty much forced to eat here, because it's the only relatively healthy restaurant in the food court at Lakeside Mall.  I'm going to start by saying the food was good. The system is simple: you let them know if you want a wrap or a bowl and then you pick your meat, veggies, and all the other stuff and it comes with a side. It's basically the "Subway" business model. I got a wrap with chicken and veggies and my side was a Greek salad. The wrap was great- the chicken and veggies were fresh and it had a lot of flavor. The salad left something to be desired. It was basically just lettuce with some vinaigrette dressing on it. That's their version of a Greek salad, I guess.   As good as the food was, I found it a little pricey. The meal itself was $9.50 and my water was another $3 (even though it said water is $2 on their menu board). I just wish that the healthy option at the mall wasn't the most expensive, but I guess that's just the way things go. I wouldn't have a problem paying $9.50 for a wrap and a side salad at an actual restaurant, but I did find that a little steep for mall food and $3 for water is just insane.  I'm giving four stars because the food was fresh and service was fast, especially considering there was a line. I liked my wrap, but I probably wouldn't get it again because paying over $12 for a wrap, a pile of lettuce and some water makes me feel pretty dumb.

review: Note:  I only ate at the restaurant without shopping at the grocery.  I didn't realize until I started working on my review that there are Tiendo Morelos restaurants/markets all around town.  I don't usually shop at a Mexican grocery unless I am looking for cotija cheese for making elote.  However, I entered the grocery because the sign in front of the restaurant entrance said it was closed.  I clearly saw people working at the food counter and a customer standing there, so I went through the grocery to see what was going on.  Apparently, nobody had removed the sign and left a "caution" cone blocking the door.  Anyway, after the weird start, I enjoyed my experience.  The colorful dining room has lots of festival streamers hanging from the ceiling and loud Mexican music playing.  (Note that the grocery has an equally loud sound system playing something completely different so you get a weird stereo effect that is hard to tune out.)  The dining booths go about half way back into the restaurant on both sides.  Beyond the left side is a cooking area with a large menu posted over the top.  Even though there is a counter at the cooking area, you don't order there.  Behind you on the right near the back of the restaurant is a smaller counter with a cash register and a menu booklet that you order from.  Once you place your order and pay, you wait and they will bring it out to you.  Note that any beverages are sold in bottle form and are self-serve from the cooler next to the order counter.  The wait was fairly short considering they prepare the entrees to order.  I went with a couple tacos (with the cilantro and white onion) and ordered rice and beans.  Apparently the cashier had a little trouble understanding me when I ordered the Asada and Pollo tacos.  I was brought out the Asada and Lomo instead. (I was the only customer at the time.)  But, instead of sending it back, I like pork loin as well as chicken, so I simply added some green sauce (mild) and a few drops of red (supposed to be hot, but I didn't think it was that hot.)  The tacos were excellent.  They were served on double layered corn tortillas.  I usually prefer flour, but wasn't given an option here.   These were the best tasting corn tortilla shells I've had.  And the ingredients inside were delicious with the added items being colorfully fresh.    The side of beans and rice were forgettable.  Not bad, just lacking much texture and flavor.  Very bland and not much other than filler when compared to the robust flavor of the tacos.  The staff was friendly and the restaurant was pretty clean looking, so given the high quality of flavor, I would recommend stopping by to quench your Mexican food cravings.  Review #2698

review: Oh, Dat Dog.  I had only heard rumors of your awesomeness.  Then I got to experience it for myself.  Dat Dog isn't your daddy's hot dog.  Leave those franks at the ball park.  With such options as bratwaurst and crawfish sausage, you can't miss.  You can get your hot dog topped with your choice of toppings from onions to cheese and much much more.  They also serve fries that you can get topped with chilli and cheese.    I had a fantastic alligator sausage hot dog with cheese and mustard on it (I'm a purist).  It was WONDERFUL (see my pic)!  Also, there is something about the buns that just makes the whole experience great.  Warm, soft and a little bit...sweet?  I will definitely be going back and I'm eager to try all of the sausages that they offer.  Yum!

review: I came here Wednesday night with a group of 9 for Clayton Restaurant Week. Bocci was kind enough to put our group of Yelpers in a little private dining room.  The ambiance of the entire place is nice and relaxing, but having our own private room was a nice touch.   Overall I have to only give Bocci 3 Stars for this visit. With it being Clayton Restaurant Week I would have thought they'd have their A-Game on. Instead, they were at best a B- or C+. I have friends who enjoy Bocci immensely so I will give them another try.   I will break down my first impression in to Pros and Cons.   PROS:  Private Dining Room for large group Waiter with foreign accent Bocci Salad is made with Bibb lettuce and the Avocado was super fresh Vanilla Gelato with Caramel Sauce and Biscotti made my knees go weak Fantastic Bread and Olive Oil for dipping No trouble splitting checks  CONS:  Discombobulated bartender, she seemed very disorganized  Draft beer not served in chilled glass Grouper Milanese was sub par - I've had better prepared for me at a grocer Portion sizes of Grouper varied greatly from each serving. I understand it most likely was done by ounces, but the size varied so much in appearance that we were giggling like kids saying mine is bigger then yours  Risotto was too mushy for my personal taste and had minimal zucchini  Chocolate Mousse Cannoli was a total miss - Cannoli over baked and coco in the chocolate was to heavy handed and I am a chocoholic.   I will revisit soon, to see if I can fall in love with Bocci like my friends have.

review: Sunday morning marked my fourth completion of the Broad Street Run. That's ten long miles down Broad, starting in Olney and ending in the Navy Yard.   I love this race.   For me, the Broad Street Run is all about stepping outside of my comfort zone, challenging myself, and doing so with over twenty five thousand other people.   The sense of community that pumps through the air on the first Sunday of every May is incredible. In the beginning miles, priests and parishioners cheer from the steps of churches, while families wave from their doorsteps. As I passed a group of gentlemen near a fast food restaurant last Sunday, one yelled out something to the effect of "keep running; you've got junk in the trunk!" I did a quick survey of my neighboring runners, and hoped he was referring to the woman on my right. Regardless, I was inspired.   In the middle miles, throngs of supporters crowd the sidewalks from Arch to Ellsworth, and musicians keep the vibe upbeat.   At mile 8, the Rocky theme is played from... somewhere, and the knowledge that the end of the race is near starts to set in. review: How is it that a place that is known for it's burgers, puts out a better salad? We went yesterday for lunch and were surprised that Brad's salad was better then my burger.   We started out with their Towering Onion Rings, which were awesome. They're huge, crispy on the outside and a fresh ring of onion on the inside. I dipped mine in the Tangy Campfire Sauce and Brad preferred good ole ketchup. The TCS had a good soft kick to it and if it were available in a bottle you'd find it in my ice box.   Our lunches were the Red Robin Gourmet Cheeseburger and the Crispy Chicken Tender Salad. I love that the burgers come with bottomless steak fries, but can not imagine anyone ordering more. When I declined more fries, I asked the server if anyone ever orders more and she said it was rare. Still it is a nice marketing tool and gesture.   Brad's salad was huge. It was a nice mix of greens with hard boiled eggs, tomatoes, cheddar cheese and applewood smoked bacon. What made it stand out above other Crispy Chicken Salads was the fact that the bacon is fresh and not Baco Bit's. He choose a Honey Mustard Poppyseed dressing. I'm not a Honey Mustard guy, but his being mixed with Poppyseed gave HM a new twist that I liked.   Loved my Steak Fries, but the burger was a disappointment. Great bun, plenty of toppings, but it had me using the classic line, "where's the beef". A place that is suppose to be known for it's burgers, I'd expect a big beefy patty hand pressed instead of a thinly machine shaped burger. My burger was totally hidden in all the toppings. I could hardly taste the meat.  Our lunch beverage of choice was ice tea and after a couple ice teas I need to use the restroom. I'll be honest, I really wanted to see if they had Dyson Airblades. They didn't have Dyson, but they had televisions hanging from the ceiling and positioned towards the stalls.  I'm surprised sports bars have not thought of this. A man can sit on the porcelain throne and not miss a play in the game.   Our server was cute, sweet and friendly.

review: Wow, this TJ's is a lot bigger than the one I'm used to in Jersey. But being in the city means there are far more people to contend with. Even though I wanted to check out all the merch, I couldn't because I felt weird taking up time and space for more than five seconds in any one spot. But I'm guessing Friday evening around 5pm isn't the best time to swing by.   Backtracking a bit, I knew there was parking but I wasn't sure where. I circled the block twice before I decided that yes, the parking lot with the line into the street was the free lot for Trader Joe's and not a paid parking lot. There was even an attendant at the front to let the next driver know when a spot opened up. We chatted for a bit and he said they mostly do this on weekends and before holidays. Nice.   The selection of produce was far superior to the location I'm familiar with in Marlton. Actually, across the board, options were plentiful in mostly every area. I couldn't find croutons for the life of me, but I did find about three different styles of pistachios.   Check-out was painless even with so many people in the store. It seemed like all the registers were open. A hand basket full of groceries came to something like twenty-five bucks. I was also able to get up to $50 cash back from using my debit card. That's more than any other store I've been to. Next time, I'll try to sneak in during the day to escape the masses.

review: Great south city dive bar. You do not come here for the service or the ambiance. You come here for the good BBQ and the neighborhood camaraderie . My most recent visit was for a UYE, which ended up being just me and Norma. Thank goodness we had smart phones and were able to check  the Yelp App and see that everyone else had bailed for some reason or another.  Oh well, they just missed out on some good south city BBQ.   I enjoyed a couple of Schafly IPA's on draft and Ms Norma was drinking vodka and tonic tall. Filling a beer glass is easy, but some how they had trouble with  making a simple vodka and tonic. They were very stingy with the pour of vodka, her drinks were extremely weak.   We started our UYE with a Smoked Chicken Wing and we each had an Atomic Turd. The turds were hollowed out Jalapeño peppers stuffed with G & W Sausage. They were very tasty, and packed some serious burn power. When we commented to our waitress how hot they were, they informed us most people do not eat the tip of the pepper. She explained that they can not clean all the seeds out at the tip and that is where the burn came from. As a server, I would have shared that tid-bit of information when I served the dish.    The Chicken Wings are their claim to fame and they were smokey and tender. I found them to be on the small size, but flavorful. They are priced individually at 90¢, for either piece little drummie or wing section. Raise the price to maybe $1.75  and give me both sections in an order.   I had a Jacked Up Sammy with brisket which was topped with melted Pepper Jack Cheese on a bun. The portion of meat was huge and it was cut with a fork tender making it easy to bite and chew. I had Mac-n-Cheese as my side and it was good enough to earn a spot on my Yelp List for Mac-n-Cheese. Elbow macaroni covered in a rich creamy cheese and baked just enough to give a crunchy top. YUM.   I forget the name of Norma's sandwich, but it began with Alabama. It had chicken , cheese and bacon, so it had to have been good. Her side was Potato Salad and we both commented how huge the chunks of  red potato were . She gave it a thumbs up approval.   The service was hit and miss. Our server was kind of  a space cadet. We had to wave her down more then once during our time there and she only had three other tables.  Then again, as I stated in my opening, you do not come here for the service, you come for the BBQ.   Great place to meet friends, chill, have a cold beer and some BBQ.

review: I ate at their pop up inside of Milkfish and my table had the pickled tea leaf salad, papaya salad, ginger garlic chicken and amok fish.  It took quite a while for our order to be taken but once that happened the food came out very fast.  The salads really didn't impress very much as the main flavor was salt from the nuts that overwhelmed everything else and I didn't really seem to have all that many pickled tea leaves in my tea leaf salad while the papaya salad was the much better of the two and had a bit of spice heat to it.  The chicken didn't have very much garlic or ginger flavor and I actually found it to be pretty bland but juicy and the side of okra it came with was nice.  The amok fish was probably the best tasting item of the night and was done with catfish and I would've preferred another fish but it was the highlight of flavor for the night.    The service was really disorganized and slow and only got worse as the place got slammed and they had people lined up to get in.  They were giving 10% of the proceeds at this nights pop up to help Burmese children so it was a very well attended night so they should've been able to raise some funds to help with that.  Overall it was a pretty mediocre experience and nothing really impressed me much to inspire me to want to return other than possibly the amok fish if it were done with another type of fish.

review: Not a fan of the Chipotle approach to Mexican food, I was disappointed that the new Mariachi Grill in Campus Town on the edge of The College of New Jersey adopted that process. Their shops on Parkway in Ewing and Quakerbridge in Hamilton are the traditional full kitchen variety, and are pretty good representations of Mexican American cuisine. Although the "pick your ingredients" can be considered  the way to customize a taco or burrito, to me it seems more the way to limit the menu to only a few possibilities, while preparation of the elements in advance means you often secure overcooked and dried out parts. A look at all the choices on the steam table behind the counter, offered proof of theory. The steak, chicken and ground beef all seemed desiccated and lacking energy.   They were out of the al pastor (roast pork & pineapple), and the only remaining juicy-looking choice was the carnitas (BBQ pork). I went with that in their duo taco plate (rice, black beans, lettuce, tomato, lime, radish & pico). The double tortilla soft shell kept its poise throughout the meal, with minimal leakage. They were tasty and well spiced. The rice and beans were forgettable. At just under $9 with drink, the price was fair. I left belly full.   Still, I prefer other Mexican dishes like chili rellenos and flautas, not to mention fresh fish and fruit drinks,  much more than tacos, burritos and quesadillas, which all have the same contents with different packaging. Such variety was not on the menu there, although they are in their other tiendas.   If all you desire is basic Mexifast food, you can be satisfied at Mariachi. But, Mexican cuisine is far more diverse and delicious than portrayed here, and deserving of exploration and ravishing. There are plenty of those places across Trenton, Hamilton and Hightstown. Once seduced by those amazing spicy senoritas, it is difficult to really enjoy the Chipotle approach to South of the Border cooking.

review: I've been going to the City Market for nearly 40 years now.  In that time, there has been a major shift in focus on making the place vibrant and an asset to downtown.  For years after Market Square Arena was demolished, that side of the Mile Square was tied up in development plans that showed promise, but failed.  Finally, there is new life in the neighborhood and with it, the City Market has undergone some renovation and transformation to make it a great place for workers and visitors downtown to grab a bite to eat from lots of small businesses that occupy the central food hall.  Some have been there a long time.  But thankfully, there are some new places too!  Lots of ethnic foods, some vegan/vegetarian options, and some tasty snacks/pastry shops as well.  The building itself has a rich history that is too lengthy to include here.  If you have time on a Saturday morning, schedule a tour of the catacombs underneath (see a separate business review).  Outside, there is a plaza which frequently holds concerts and festivals on the west side of the food hall. review: What a delightful surprise and too think we almost didn't come to Schneithorst because come of the reviews on Yelp. After reading them more carefully, we decided it was one of those places that you either love it or hate. We loved it.   After dropping off our foster dog at the doggie spa, we needed breakfast and headed over to Schneithorst. We were promptly greeted as we entered and taken to a table for two. As we were seated, they promptly asked what we'd like to drink. We opted for ice tea, since we already had plenty of coffee at home. When our server returned, we asked for more time to glance over the menu since it was our first time.   The selection of breakfast items was much larger then your typical IHOP or Denny's. Or at least it seemed so to me, there was so much to choose from. Would you believe it, with such a variety of choices, we both wanted the same thing. We ordered their "Southern Pride",  which is two farm fresh eggs, golden hash browns and authentic Southern style biscuits and gravy. We differed on our side dishes, bacon for me and sausage patty's for him.   I love the salesmanship that goes into the writing of menus. I giggled when I read the word, "authentic" in the description of their biscuit. Come on, how authentic can a German restaurant make a Southern biscuit. Well, the laugh was on me. This was the best damn biscuit I have "ever" had. It truly was a "authentic" southern style biscuit and the gravy would put a farmers wife to shame. The biscuit was the moist and flaky, not dried out like I have found at so many other locations in the Lou. The milk gravy covering the two biscuits, had chunks of sausage and the right amount of pepper to give the flavor an extra kick.  Their kitchen did a great job on our eggs too. I like'm over medium and Brad ordered his over easy. You could see the difference, in our yolks and that is no joke.  Sorry, I just couldn't resist saying that. The hash browns were good, next time I will request them extra crispy.  As simple as our sides were, they were very good. As usual, our eyes were bigger then our stomachs and we took half of our sides home as a treat for the dogs.  I found the service to be very friendly. You can tell they have a lot of regulars, because everybody kinda knew every-ones name. There was also a lot of glad handing between tables.  If this were in my hood, I'd make it a regular breakfast stop for sure.   *The above review was my 400th review on Yelp.

review: Parx Beer Garden is a recent addition to the Parx Casino complex in Bensalem, PA. It is an indoor/outdoor facility with folding doors separating the large warehouse space from the attractive green garden area. This, it is much nicer in warm weather when the high walls are open and the fresh breeze is free to flow throughout.   There are many tables and a long bar capable of holding a couple of hundred guests. The draft beer list runs about two dozen, with an equal amount of bottled options. The bartenders are well trained in the art of cocktailcraft and chatter. Because the casino operates 24/7, it is possible to catch a late happy hour after 9:00 P. M. for a fair price on their decent bar food, brews and daily special drinks. Most folks seem to come and go between the gambling floor and the alcohol break in order to extend the evening and catch their breath from the honky tonk pace of money and chips changing hands. Problem is, the acoustics are poor, so between the sound drifting in from other parts of the expansive rooms, the sound system, large HDTVs, and general hubbub, it can be difficult to hear your friends.   Still, if your not expecting too much real entertainment, and are really there for poker and roulette, the Beer Garden is a nice place to clear your head, grab a bite and brew for a reasonable price, before heading back into the maelstrom.

review: I have experienced HWK as a single diner. I went to Brunch on April 15th and was to sit at one of the hightop tables in the front window. When I called to make my reservation, Tori the dining room manager answered the phone and was very perky and pleasant. She asked me if the hightop would be acceptable and I responded, yes. When she asked for my name, I admit I did use an alias. I figured they'd be on the alert for a Steven and I did not  want special treatment. Once I gave my name, she commented that she thought I had been there before, but I said "no this will be my first". (I think they knew it was me)  When I arrived that Sunday morning, I was seated at the hightop close to the hostess stand. It was comfortable and I had great light for reading, since I was dining alone.  I love a Bloody Mary at Brunch, HWK calls them a Bloody Wilbur. Their twist has; Bacon Vodka with tomato juice and garnished with pickled asparagus.  I was famished, so I ordered two entrees; Biscuits and Gravy and Eggs Benedict.   After I place my order, John the husband of Cassy approached my table and asked me if I were the Steven from Yelp. Yes, I was busted and I wasn't surprised.  Part of being a good Yelper is taking ownership of your reviews, so with a smile I acknowledged who I was. Our conversation was very pleasant and as Cassy (his wife and executive chef) said to me in private messaging they are thankful I brought the single seating to their attention and apologetic my previous experience.   Now let's talk food, after all that is what restaurant reviews are all about.  I'll break it down item for item.   Bloody Wilbur: Love the bacon vodka, proving everything is better with bacon. I also enjoyed the the garnish of pickled asparagus. Asparagus is my all-time favorite vegetable so adding it to a brunch cocktail, is A-Okay in my book. Their choice of tomato juice, held this drink back from being spectacular. The juice was weak, a rich and thicker type tomato juice have made this classic brunch cocktail truly pop.   Biscuits and Gravy: They made this old farm boy proud. These truly were some kick ass, B&G. A picture is suppose to be worth a 1000 words, but B&G do not photograph well. So let me tell you the best I can. When you have buttermilk biscuits with chives and cheddar topped with gravy containing huge chunks of sausage - it does not get any better. These Biscuits and Gravy will be added to my Yelp list of Best B&G.   Mimosa: Meyer Lemon is a staple in my kitchen/bar at home. So when I saw that they use it for their mimosa, I was already sold. I found the the sparkling wine served with the Meyer Lemon and honey to be a refreshing twist to traditional Mimosa. Two thumbs up and remember I am dining alone.   Eggs Benedict: No English Muffin, they use a Grits Cake instead which gives an original twist. I'm not a fan of grits and I enjoyed the difference in texture and flavor. The eggs were poached perfectly and the use of Tasso gives it a Cajun kick. They then top it off with a Spicy Hollandaise and Flash Fried Spinach.   I'm glad I finally got to experience HWK and I'll be back for a lunch soon. My rating is more of a 3 1/2 Star (wish Yelp would let us do 1/2's soon). If Wilbur would have been bloody better, it would of been a 4.

I did score a $10 off online card with my purchase so perhaps I'll take a gander to see what's on sale.

review: Unfortunately, the first observation from my dealing with Pho & More in Montgomery Commons is that while it may be a Vietnamese house, it certainly is not a Thai kitchen. As I ordered from both ends of the menu, I found myself happy with the Roast Pork Banh Mi sandwich, but damned dissatisfied with the Lemongrass Coconut Soup (Tom Kha) and the Drunken Noodles (Pad Kee Mao).   Why? Because although both those dishes have lemongrass spice as the key ingredient, there was absolutely no lemongrass to be found in either the soup, nor the wide flat rice noodles. The soup tasted of watered down coconut milk, with ample chicken and mushrooms, but without the strong bite that lemongrass provides. Very poor effort.   And the Drunken Noodles were not hot and chewy at all, but really just Chinese Vegetable Chow Fun with a few leaves of Thai basil mixed in. I ordered it "very spicy," and the cashier dude repeated that request to me upon pickup. Yet, despite the reasonable quantity of noodles and veggies, it totally lacked the heat punch desired. Boring, semi-sweet fat noods without redeeming fire signature. Major disappointment.   If I had to guess, I would venture that there was not a Thai person in the kitchen, nor even a real authentic recipe for Bangkok cuisine in the house. If they don't have lemongrass in stock, they just aren't Thai, and shouldn't misrepresent their abilities. Yet, the Banh Mi was decent and I grant that someone may have trained in Ho Chi Minh City or Hanoi to perfect their pho stock.   Had I known the truth about this joint, I would have happily stayed in Vietnam, and travelled to Thailand another day. As it is, with dishonesty at their core, I will never return to find out what they are really good at.   Fooled me once, shame on you! Fool me twice; never happen!

review: Alton Restaurant Week  WOW! I am so glad I came here during, ARW. I was totally impressed. So impressed, that I am confident Bossanova will be become a regular in my restaurant rotation, here in my new neighborhood.   Upon my arrival, I choose my favorite spot at any bar, a stool at the end. I like this space for its privacy, especially now during a pandemic. I started out with a Dirty Martini, made with Tito's. The bartender commented that was her favorite drink and I believe her. She made my cocktail so superbly, you'd think she was making it for herself.   For my dinner, I choose to go with the 10 oz Filet. They prepared it to a delectable medium-rare. Before my filet, I enjoyed a Caesar salad topped with Parmesan cheese and crunchy croutons. I would have liked some fresh cracked pepper, but the freshly ground in the shaker did the trick. As my side, I went with the Green Beans instead of the creamy garlic mashed potatoes that the bartender recommended. The green beans were top notch, they were prepared with bacon and we all know bacon adds that extra flavor. On my next visit, I'll try those garlic rich potatoes.   For my dessert, I choose the Gooey Butter Cake and had packaged to-go. I was stuffed and had no room to eat it that night. Being a recycler, I was pleased to see their carry-out vessels are Eco-friendly. Being from STL, I am spoiled with Gooey Butter Cakes, so I found this one to be just, okay. It was good, but not as flavorful as those in the city where it originated.   The bartender was delightful in conversation and attentive in service. I'm looking forward to sitting at the bar again on my next visit.   When: January 15, 2021 Why: Alton Restaurant Week

review: I'm going to have to return soon.  I was in a bit of a hurry and when I walked in, the menu board listed Root Beer Float and I honestly didn't look any farther.  The gal behind the counter immediately asked if I wanted to go with the traditional vanilla ice cream and then began scooping the frozen treat into the cup.  A&W Root Beer was then opened and poured over the ice cream for that not so pretty foam that tastes delicious.  She even gave me the rest of the can of soda to go with the dessert.  The space is easy to spot from the highway, but requires turning into the shopping center (the one with the movie theater) and then driving behind the frontage buildings to about midway down the row.  An alley area leads passed the outdoor seating (located underneath a former drive through area for a bank) to the parking and entrance.  Inside, there is a party room on the right and a play room on the left of the entrance.  Beyond those, there is dining on the left and the order counter on the right where they have lots of barrels of ice cream and a variety of other sweets.  Service was fast and friendly and before long, I was out the door.  I'll have to go after lunch the next time so that I take more time to see what else they have available.  Review #2722

review: My wife and I recently scheduled lunch at "The Loft" (6-9-16).  We went on a day that the weather cooperated, allowing us to sit out on the balcony and enjoy a great spring day while dining.   Although we didn't have reservations, we were seated promptly and without much delay, were brought water and asked about our beverage selections.  We informed our waitress that we had about an hour before we needed to leave for another appointment, so we went ahead and placed our order for our meals at the same time.   I selected the Lake Trout on a bed of millet and mustard aioli, along with asparagus, shallots, and almonds.  The skin of the filet was crispy.  The flesh of the filet was moist and tender.  So, excellent marks for preparation.  I also thought the flavors worked well together, although I am not a big fan of millet.  Still, the food was served timely, and tasted delicious as well.  I also ordered a bottle of Ginger Beer which was quite tasty.   My wife ordered the house burger after ordering a root beer float.  She liked both, but needed a "to go" box for the remaining half of her burger.  She ordered the Kettle Chips as a side, but she wasn't a fan of the salt and pepper flavor combination on the chips.  (I tried them and found them quite good, but couldn't get passed the notion of some other herbal taste there as well.) review: What can be said that hasn't been said already? The Philadelphia Museum of Art is a landmark in Philadelphia and a beautiful place to spend an afternoon while taking in some culture.   I attended the Van Gogh exhibit recently with a friend and though the lines were long and the museum was crowded, I thought the staff did a nice job keeping things moving. The audio tour was just great. You could view pieces and listen to the narration at your own pace. While the narrators were a bit stuffy, it was nice to learn something about the art and the artist, and it definitely beat listening to certain self-important guests who were loudly voicing their own opinions.   Last summer I enjoyed taking some bootcamp classes right on the famous steps of the museum. As I squated, sprinted and lunged my way around the courtyard, the experience was made somewhat bearable with the distraction of beauty and the occasional mist of the fountain.   I'm dying to check out Art After 5, a live music and art reception held on Friday evenings. Snacks and cocktails are available for purchase, which is really fun.  We're lucky to have such a great home for art in Philadelphia!

review: I cannot believe that I have not written a review for Corner Bistro - I've eaten here so many times that I have almost experienced the entire menu. I guess I thought all the pictures that I have posted, were my review. After all, they do say that a picture is worth a thousand words.  Since I've eaten here multiple times, I am just going to list some of my favorites:  Bistro Burger - A hand pressed burger, topped with Applewood crisp bacon, cheese, lettuce, tomato, onion and what I can only assume is a secret Bosnian spice. The flavor is unique and makes the burger stand out from a typical American hamburger. It was served with crispy fries and a little cup of ketchup.   Spicy Chicken Wings - Ooey Gooey Spicy sauce covered the entire wings. Finger licking good and good thing they have paper napkins over linen, because you need to use serval to keep fingers clean.   Ham & Cheese Panini - Puts Panera Bread to shame. Thinly sliced ham, smoked cheese, roasted red peppers, lettuce, tomato and mayo on a Ciabatta bread. The sandwich is crisply toasted on the outside and the ingredients on the inside are piping hot. A side of crispy fries makes this a winning combination.   Their pizzas are some of the best in STL. You'll be surprised how tasty they are and they do not use provel.   Chicken & Mushroom - Freshly sliced mushrooms and diced white meat chicken.   Meat Lovers - Hamburger, pepperoni and bacon. The perfect combo of meat.   Buffalo Chicken - (My favorite) A zesty cheese pizza topped with chicken tossed in buffalo sauce and drizzled with ranch dressing and more buffalo sauce. Totally different and worth the experience.   I also give a thumbs up to the house salad and Bruschetta.  I've dined in and I've called ahead for carry-out and every time I have been pleased with my meals. The service at times can be slow, but that has never bothered me, because the food is that damn good. The dining room inside is small, but when the weather is good the patio almost doubles the amount of tables available.   I want this place to continue to succeed, so I recommend it to all pizza lovers. I just hope it doesn't get so popular that I cannot get in to enjoy one myself.

review: I seriously love this place.  The menu looks like a newspaper and there are 3 pages full of items for adults and one page for kids.  There are about thirty different varieties of grilled cheese, and breakfast is served all day, every day.  The best thing about their breakfast is that the menu deviates so far from the traditional fare on diner menus.  Last Saturday I had a "Farmer's Market" egg white omelet with Swiss cheese, herbs and tons of fresh veggies.  There were about 12 other original omelets featured, as well as a "create your own" option.  The wheat toast that came with my order was thick-cut and grainy.  In other words, bangin'.     There are also loads of salads, sandwiches, soups and platters to satisfy any craving.  My sister loves the Foghorn Country Chicken salad, and it's so big that I have never seen her finish it.   Last but definitely not least, there is a HUGE ice cream menu that puts the Friendly's version from my childhood to shame.

review: Well it took me a while to get back to Iron Hill in Maple Shade but last night I made it happen, along with my sister and our dad. The service was great and so was the food. We shared the nachos (creature of habit, here) and there was more than enough for all of us - we brought about a third of the serving home.   All three of us had Caesar salads - my dad's had seared tuna, my sister's had grilled chicken and mine had grilled shrimp. No complaints there, either, though my dad would have liked the fish sliced instead of served in two big pieces, which I would agree with had it been my plate.   To drink, my dad and sister each had one of the house brews while I sipped on water. And now here is my gripe: nachos, three dinner salads (with upgraded proteins on two of them) and two beers cost us $93, including tip. That. Is. Bananas.   Iron Hill's rewards card actually seems like a good idea if you go there with any sort of regularity. I'd imagine you'd easily rack up the rewards with those pricey dinners. Of course, to join the program, it will cost you $25 up front (and that's an annual fee).

review: After meeting our son to look at his latest construction project, he suggested coming to Boathouse Grill for lunch.  He had eaten here about ten times during the project and said he really liked everything he tried.    So although I wasn't thrilled on my previous visit, I decided to give it a try.  And I am glad I did!  Although not much has changed in the three years since my last visit, this time I ordered the Italian Beef (served on a hoagie) and it was delicious!  The giardiniera veggies, Provolone cheese, and the au jus made a wonderful combination with the tender sliced beef.  The bread held up well even after dipping it in the sauce.  It was soft and thin enough bread to not make this difficult to get a full bite.  My wife said her taco salad had a crispy shell and the seasoned chicken had a pleasant taste.  Thought the sauce was just a little hot, but other than that, she really enjoyed her meal too.  The place does get full around lunch time and quite noisy.  The waitress got busier as the crowd rolled in, so other than it taking a little longer to get our check and processed out, the service was good.  Seems like a popular spot on 56th just between I-65 and I-465.  Rev. #42

review: This is causal restaurant with some fine dining options which has been displaying a vigorous lunch crowd and more relaxed dinner scene.  Generally Porter & Luke's averages a bit over a 3.5 star mainly due to consistency issues as they absolutely can put out some four and five star food when they are firing on all cylinders but they seem to often have misfires.  They have a decent LARGE private back room and smaller private side room for meetings, events or other private dining groups.  The location is in a strip mall on Metairie Road which leaves a lot to be desired aesthetically but provides ample parking.  This is definitely a vast improvement from the last restaurant in this space, Zeke's Restaurant, that even Gordon Ramsay couldn't save. It is a smallish space with a row of tables along the wall, with kitchen on the opposite side behind another wall that gives the appearance of being a very narrow dining room.   I ordered a slice of Brooklyn pie and another tradition regular triangle. The Brooklyn slice was pretty good - thin crust, Marzano sauce and dollops of mozza in a square pan. It was firm, crisp and pleasantly chewy.  The regular slice was not as good.  The crust was limp despite requesting it be reheated well done, and there was ample oil drip onto the paper plate. Just not a strong presentation.  The price was good at around $5 for the slices and bottle of water. Service was pleasant from start to finish.   There is much better pizza and tomato pie right nearby.

review: The Groveland Grill on RT. 611 in Pipersville ,PA, is a small roadside kitchen specializing in breakfast and lunch. It sits in a small commercial strip and is easy to miss if driving at normal speeds. I actually had to turn around and go back to it as I went north and didn't spy it until I was passed the driveway into their parking lot.   The house is clean, with about ten tables and a counter with seven stools. The folks working there are very friendly, and welcomed this first timer with warm greetings. I took a seat at the counter across from the Bunn O Matic where Ellis coffee was being brewed. There was a dark blue ceramic mug with side stainless of milk in front of me in seconds, and a two page breakfast menu placed before me before I reached the counter. These people were on their game.   There was a list of omelettes, benedicts, pancakes/French toast, and combo platters, but I decided on a standard breakfast sandwich of sausage, egg and cheese on kaiser. The side of home fries with grilled pepper and onion bits was also too tempting to pass up.   The sammy was doubled up, making for a fat and filling meal in its own right. The taters were alright, but despite the flavor from the sauteed onion/pepper, the tubers themselves were a bit dry like they had been sitting on the corner of the grill too long. Maybe my arrival at 10:00 had some to do with that, but a word to the wise...  Loved the Ellis java, which was refilled as often as I desired.   Groveland Grill is definitely worth your breakfast attention.

review: This Chicken Holiday has a few things going for it.    First, it turns out top of the line Fried Chicken, BBQ Ribs and Buffalo Wings.  Each order is individually prepared when it comes in, so nothing is sitting around waiting for an unfortunate to consume a less than prime meal.  I found the chicken to be moist with nicely spiced breaded and fried coating.  The Ribs were large, dark brown from the basting sauces, and nearly "fall of the bone" tender.  The BBQ taste was both sweet and tangy, just as it should be.  The Wings are larger than found in most outlets, but the hotness covers every nook and cranny.    I can't say that these items were the best I ever had, nor that they were as good as it gets.  Yet, given what is available in the area, they are all on the high end of taste and enjoyment, and for me, there is no need to look further afield to satisfy my Fried Chicken Addiction.   And, if you come on a Sunday afternoon you can enjoy an impromptu car show in the parking lot.  Folks are there from all over opening their hoods and hooking up their stereos to external speakers so everyone can check out their wheels to Deep Purple.

review: When you first enter here you may say to yourself, "Where's the beef? Where's the pork?" What you need to do is stop and think. What is the name of this BBQ joint? It's Gobble Stop Smokehouse and it is, "Where Bird is the Word".  Which means their specialty is chicken and turkey. It's a specialty that they truly have mastered. So you'll soon forget that they do not offer beef brisket or pulled pork.    I would have never discovered GSS if it were not for Brian M. organizing a UYE lunch. To my surprise it is just down the street from my dogs vet, so I know I will be visiting again and again. Now I will be requesting appointments near lunchtime, instead of the early morning.   My lunch was the Smoked Chicken Wings and they were Gobble-icious.  They were served drummette style and seasoned with their signature herbs and spices. They may have been slowly smoked, but I gobbled them up fast. I had the sauce served on the side, but was totally satisfied with the signature rub. As my side, I choose Green Beans which had pieces of ham. They were the perfect accompaniment to BBQ as they would be a Sunday fried chicken.   I couldn't enjoy a new BBQ place without taking some home for the other half who was working in the yard. A Half Smoked Chicken with two sides would be the perfect reward. As his sides, I choose Cole Slaw and Potato Salad. He was so impressed with their Smoked Chicken, that he wants to check out their fried chicken in the near future.   If you are in a hurry, I suggest calling ahead and ordering. The service is friendly, but is on the slow side of Southern Hospitality.

review: Another solid addition to the Greenwood dining choices arrived last December at the former location of Louie's.  The new place has covered outdoor dining, plenty of parking, bar area seating and a separate dining room area that is kid friendly.  They have a full service bar with a nice selection of drafts as well as a large number of bottled/canned craft beers.    I stopped in for lunch and started with the Crispy Brussels Sprouts.  These were halved and deep fried with a bit of salt seasoning and a house mustard sauce for dipping.  Excellent!  The serve them in a brown paper lined dish that really soaks up the excess oil to keep the sprouts from becoming too messy.  The portion could be shared, but I had no problem devouring it myself.  I also had the Indiana Tenderloin with fries.  The tenderloin can be breaded or grilled.  The fries can be substituted out for cole slaw, or several other sides.  My tenderloin was a reasonable size, not some ridiculous slab.  The bread and toppings were good, but the breading of the tenderloin itself was under seasoned.  So, the bites beyond the sandwich portion were bland.  Still, the meat was served hot and moist inside, while the breading was cooked properly to add a little crunch.  The fries were a bit on the salty side, so eating the combination of tenderloin and fries together worked out well.  The service was friendly and brought any thing I asked for promptly.  I think on my next visit I will go for one of the house burgers that seem to be their specialty.  Review #260

review: Most of us in NOLA are not big into chains and especially this close to the French Quarter but for a chain this place fills a niche that they do well at.  This is definitely one of the main spots to eat mass quantities of meat in the NOLA region and is the best example we currently have of the Brazilian style steakhouse genre.  Service can be over the top with being so attentive and frequent that it becomes nearly intrusive with going overboard with changing your plate out far too many times.  If they pull back on the aggressive plate changing the service experience would be at a great level.  I find the meat to be acceptable but on average trends towards too overly well done for my liking and they do attempt to accommodate your level of preference.  The meat is brought at regular intervals but the servings were on the small sides at times.  The food bar contains a decent selection of items if you want to expand your feasting beyond the carnivore realm and they have even more meat on that in the guise of salmon and ham.  It is fairly priced during lunch while a bit on the pricey side at dinner and overall I think I would generally just prefer a nice steak but this establishment does have its moments when you are just in the mood for some debauched gluttony of meat.  Tip:  The best meat I've had here are the lamb chops.

Having a car while living in the city is definitely a luxury, but it's an expensive one. Regardless, I need my wheels to work like a well-oiled machine whenever I want to get out of town. After 7+ years, my car is still treating me well, and I probably have CH Nissan to thank for part of that.

review: I stopped by on a chilly Tuesday for a late lunch after running errands in Greenwood.  This place shares the building with a Family Video store on the south east corner of the Greenwood Mall property (north west corner of Frye and Madison).    The signs out front and on the side mention sushi, but guess what.  They no longer have sushi on the menu and the waiter confirmed that they don't have it any longer.  So, scratch that from my selections.  I decided to go with a cup of Rangoon Tea/Coffee based on other Yelper suggestions and followed that with a bowl of Steak Noodle Pho.  The tea was served at a drinkable temperature and was surprisingly sweet!  I know I've tasted the underlying flavor before, but I'm unable to determine what it reminded me of.  Whatever it was, it was great.  (Note that a single cup was plenty for me.  I don't believe you get free refills.)  Before long, by large bowl of Pho arrived with a fork and Asian soup spoon (ceramic).  It also had a small plate with sliced pepper (looked like jalapeno), mint sprigs, and raw bean sprouts.  I also received bottles of Hoisin and Sriracha sauces.    I must admit I have had Pho three times previously and was clueless on what was proper.  So I You Tubed it and solved the problem.  I added the individual leaves off the mint, the sprouts, and the pepper slices and stirred them in, letting the hot broth semi-cook the new ingredients and let their flavor spread into the pho.    The broth was tasty even before I added the new ingredients, so I really enjoyed the perked up flavor.  At the bottom of the bowl, the long rice noodles (think white thin spaghetti) and the thin sliced beef nestled.  I think the owners realize that most Hoosiers would struggle using chopsticks to fish out noodles, so the fork was a welcome tool.  And whenever I speared a bit of the steak, I dipped it in the Hoisin sauce I had put on my small serving bowl that the soup spoon had been delivered in.  The steak (and probably all the meat options) don't have a lot of seasoning since they soak in the broth, so dipping the pieces directly in the Hoisin makes for a much tastier bite.  Yes, the meat gets a bit chewy, but because it is sliced thin, it wasn't difficult to get used to.  (I am not sure how the shrimp would hold up since I am not a fan of it when it gets rubbery.)  The dining room was pretty sparse, so the noise level was low even with some classic rock playing softly in the background.  Not much atmosphere inside, but the bright tangerine walls and a few decorative plates kept it from looking too sterile.  Overall, a good meal (huge quantity) and nice service all at an affordable price.   Now, if they would just take down those Sushi signs...  Review #2219

review: The best place to stop before a long drive north or south coming from Newtown, this DD is hidden in the office/hotel complex next to the Hampton Inn, right of Rt. 95.    The coffee is decent (far better than the coffee @ the other DD in Newtown), and the staff organized and efficient.  While I am not a fan of their baked goods, push come to shove, I can be found with breakfast sandy or toasted bagel in my possession.  My 13 year old goes for milk and a couple of glazed rounders.    All in all, a reasonably tasty coffee at a good price, with a smiling face.  I don't need more than that at a caffeine oasis.

At the check out, I had to wait behind an elderly woman who was, quite literally counting out her coppers. I entered my loyalty number to get points (For what, I'm not sure) and was told to "Be Well" (something else I hate.. it's both annoying and stirs bad memories or makes me want to respond  "BE F*cked" as a quote from a movie)
