review: Love me some Sauce On The Side. It is so gooey, goody, good, you need to eat with caution. Otherwise, you may end up with sauce on your front.   I'll be honest when SOTS won so many of the RFT awards recently, I was skeptical. So when the International Supper Club was to hold its May meeting at here, I was eager to experience Sauce magic. Now that I have experienced that magic, I can tell you they deserved every award.   The night immediately got off to a good start when I got Prince parking right in front of the restaurant. I was the first arrive and waited patiently on a bar stool. As I started to read the menu, to narrow down my selection, I was greeted by Dan one of the owners. He immediately knew I was one of the large group coming to dine and asked if I wanted a beer while I waited. What great customer service, they even allowed me to run a tab to which I added my meal and a carryout for the BF when I was ready to go.  Let me begin by saying, their beer list is huge for a small specialty restaurant. I stayed local with my selection and enjoyed a Schlafly Pale Ale in a chilled beer glass. Once all our Yelper's arrived we begun chatting and catching up on our lives outside Yelp. As another large group arrived, Dan who was chatting with us suggested we quickly get in line and place our orders. It was a nice gesture, but seriously his team knows how to hustle. They had those calzones and salads out for both groups pronto.   I recently have become obsessed with jalapeños, so I enjoyed a Pancho Villa.  In addition to jalapeños, my calzone was stuffed with Chorizo, yellow peppers and smoked cheddar. Then it is basted with Smoked Chili Oil and served with a side of Queso for dipping. It was so good, I was texting pictures to my cousin while eating, telling her it would be a great spot to eat before or after a Cardinals game. I even snapped a pic of Anita K.'s Smokehouse Salad to send her. Anita, shared a sampling and it was amazing. Don't be fooled by the name, there's no meat on the salad. A vegetarian would love it. To go I got the Costanza, for the BF. It was stuffed with pepperoni, eggplant, mozzarella and Ricotta.   My cousin and her family went Saturday after the Cardinals won a shut out at home. As they ordered they chatted with guess who? Dan. They told him they came on the recommendation of "me" and Yelp. He treated them like royalty and they loved their food. They enjoyed an Italian salad and Meat Me In St. Louis.   SOTS and Dan have me being a fan, which will bring me back time and time again.

review: A big thank you to Livingsocial for introducing me to Spiro's in the Lindenwood neighborhood. I am embarrassed to admit it, but I will. I live in the Lindenwood neighborhood, I am The Baron here on Yelp and I have never enjoyed the Greek cuisine at Spiro's.   When I saw the Livingsocial coupon, I jumped on the opportunity to have a lunch at Spiro's.  The day we lunched was late, we got there about 1:30 PM and there was only one other table. However, in the back party room they were serving a large funeral lunch. Even with the large banquet going on, our service was attentive.   What would a lunch or dinner at a Greek restaurant be without an order of Saganaki? Enjoying Flaming Cheese is part of the experience. OPA!! They flash fried the Kassen Cheese right at the table and it was the perfect accompaniment to the fresh bread.  We also shared another popular Greek appetizer, Dolma. A large grape vine leaf stuffed with rice, ground beef and lamb then top with egg lemon sauce. Both were very flavorful and will be enjoyed again.   The SO enjoyed a large Athenian Greek Salad, with slices of rotisserie lamb on top. These salad is defiantly large and could be shared by two who can also share an appetizer or two. Momma always told me a good boy shares.   I enjoyed a Gyro Sandwich, which was very very good. Yes, I meant to do a double very very, it was that good. It was the most tender and flavorful rotisseries lamb I have had in a Gyro. As with all Gyro's, it was served in a pita bread and garnished with fresh tomatoes, onion and tzatsiki sauce. As a side dish they served up thinly sliced potatoes that were fried with a crispy shell and a hot moist meaty inside.   We were so stuffed, we could not try their Baklava, but we are looking forward to that experience on our next visit.

review: I'm torn between three and four stars for my first experience with Real Food Eatery. I've been wanting to try it for a while and finally decided to place a delivery order on one of a small handful of days last week when I opted for healthy foods over carbs, cheese, more carbs and alcohol. The holidays, am I right?   I love the variety of choices for mains and sides. Don't like beets? No problem, there's about six other sides to select from. I went with salmon over brown rice, with sides of kale and mushrooms and parmesan broccoli. I also ordered a side of roasted apples.   The food arrived and I was very happy with the size of the platter. I wanted to eat healthy but I didn't want to go to bed hungry. I will say that the piece of salmon was minuscule, but perfectly cooked. The kale and mushroom side was extremely salty but was a bit more balanced when I ate it together with the rice. The apples were a perfect sweet treat with zero guilt.   I'll definitely give Real Food another try when I need something healthy but don't feel like cooking.

review: Of all the places in Philly why, oh why, would I ever come here? Three words.  Fifty Dollar Gift-card.  Or is that 4 words (2 words and a compound word?)?  Yes, folks, I won a $50 gift card good at ANY Hard Rock location from a charity auction so a good-sport friend (I love her - and she put up with Hard Rock well) and I decided to play cheap-meal roulette.  I read the menu online before we went and luckily, they sat us is the back room (the Philadelphia room) which is much less loud and crowded.  Our self-effacing server, Stewart, was attentive and kind - especially since I can be such a pain in the a$$.  I ordered a pomegranate martini and ask for it NOT to contain Sierra Mist.  (I mean, really, Sierra Mist?)  The $8.50 martini was basically vodka, Monin Pomegranate Syrup and seltzer.  It was fine and I was able to cultivate a buzz in about 12 minutes.  My friend wisely chose the shrimp fajitas which were served on a sizzling platter and tasted pretty good.  I poorly chose a great steak which was so gristly I had to send it back.  Poor, Stewart took it back and the next one they brought was at least edible.  But flavorless.  I literally had to put salt and pepper on it and was eyeing the A-1 (I HATE A-1!). A good steak should have flavor on its own.  Maybe that's why they put "Cabernet butter" aka Country Crock on all the grilled items?  Anyhow - dessert was a BOMB. Over sweet cheesecake on a cardboard and wood-shaving crust.  Do not even think about getting the syrup-ed-out creme brulee here. At least it was cheap ($2.99 for the dessert "bites")  Believe it or not - I am giving them 3 stars (they really deserve 2) because they were very accomodating to all of our requests and we had a fun time.  Would I come here again? Not unless I had another gift card - and even then - I think I would re-gift!

review: East Lincoln Highway, Langhorne, PA, is primarily noted as the location of the Reedman-Toll automobile dealership, the largest car outlet in the country. In its shadow are many smaller businesses, including this Friendly's restaurant. Obviously, it is well known, as when I arrived around 7 pm on a Sunday night, it was more than half full of customers chowing down on the traditional American cuisine and ice cream desserts for which this chain is known.   I was guided to a booth along the front wall by the hostess, and handed the laminated multi-paged menu. Their Sriracha Burger sounded interesting, and I went with it, medium. I was assured by my server that I would receive a pink finish from their never frozen ground beef.  She was right. Unlike many burger joints that promise the desired degree of grilling, but inevitably deliver only a well done puck, this kitchen did keep its word. I was given a medium burger that was lightly pink throughout. Gratitude.   The rest of the accompaniment - pepper jack cheese, bacon, onion straws, lettuce, tomato, sriracha mayo, on brioche bun - were all present and accounted for, although the "crispy" onion was soggy. The overall taste satisfied my burger craving for the week. At ten bucks it was priced beyond its actual value, but it was good to know that Friendly's was keeping up with the burger wars, where every food emporium had to offer a decent six ouncer to stay competitive.   It is safe to say that Friendly's keeps up with the other franchise Joneses in this universe. You can come here for a burger or other of their beef and chicken offerings, and leave sated. And, if in the mood, their ice cream makes for a very convenient and creamy end of meal.   Looks like Friendly's will be around for a while longer.   3.5 STARS

review: Wow - am I ever glad I finally got a chance to eat here.  It is MUCh better than Miran.  (Sorry, Miran.)  I got a Galbi for dinner and upgraded (for $1.00) to the multigrain rice - which I am so glad I did.  The rice and grains were so healthy-tasty.  The Galbi was "textbook perfect" with a delicious BBQ flavor and just the right amount of fat. (Not greasy - but tasty and beefy.)  The side dishes of Kimchi and Sweet Yellow Soy beans were also "textbook perfect".  The Gabli and rice came with a mixed green salad dressed lightly in a soy dressing - fresh and good.  Also steamed carrots - naturally sweet and a few YUMMY edamame.  What a great meal.  Can't wait to come back again.  (Wanna get a Dolsot Bibimbop next time.)  Oh, and the man behind the counter (who I am guessing is the manager and possibly the owner) was very nice.  It's counter service, but he was so friendly to me. (It was not busy when I came.)  Also the clean bathrooms have really cool tiles.  BONUS!

review: I used to come to Pit Boss ages ago. It was my Dad's favorite place in the world. Since I was craving MEAT, I took my mom out for food. When we got there, the scent of roasting meat over whelmed us  (in a good way) and we made our way inside to the almost empty dining room.  We were told by the waitress (Who was eating her own lunch ) to sit where ever we liked, so we did.   Mom ordered the Pitboss special - a pulled pork sandwich, 2 sides and a drink ($8.99) and I ordered a full pound of ribs dinner (+2 sides and bread) with an iced tea.  We didn't need any appetizers and we reminisced while we waited for the food.   When it came, the serving sizes were pretty large. Mom and I both ended up taking things home. I adore their potato salad, but their green beans were pretty weak.  Their ribs were amazing.

review: It took me two tries to find the front door of Mauceri Pizza.  It has combined two storefronts.  The one to the right lets you in, while the door on the left is permanently closed on the dining room side of the establishment.  It is not immediately apparent that this is now one operation, so take this tip to find your way.  It is worth your while to come inside.   First glance, it still looks like an Italian pizza shop with a couple of pies on display, and large ovens toward the back.  It is rather hot in there on a humid Judy day, but the now-glass wall between the two rooms also insulates the strong air conditioning in the dining room.  As there was no one else eating when I arrived, I sought permission to enter and have lunch.  No problem.  Although a Salvadoran house, most there spoke English well enough to understand each other.  The room is rather large with ample tables for a nice dinner crowd.    The menu is a cross between Italian and Salvadoran cuisine.  All the usual suspects on the Roman side, and substantial offerings in Spanish, as well.  One of their specialties was Chili Rellenos, one of my favorite Central American dishes, and I went for it.  What followed was a parade of plates from Chips and Salsa, to Pickled Peppers, Tortillas, and a huge platter with the Rellenos, Rice and Salad.  The stuffed chili pepper covered in egg and drowned in spicy red sauce, was about the best I had ever eaten.  The stuffing seemed to be a combination of ground meat, cheese, onion and more pepper.  It was filling and delicious. I will never know how they expected one man to eat that much.  I barely touched the tortillas and the rice.  My cold Jicaima Juice was a rich dark cranberry color, sweet and refreshing.   The only question that arose was the actual price for my meal.  The hand out flyer listed the dish at $7., while the hard menu said it was $8.  I was charged $9. They should work on getting some consistency in pricing to avoid any chance someone might think they were trying to take advantage of a gringo.  Yet, even at the highest price, it was still a deal. I said nothing and let the confusion slide.   This piece of Liberty Street is attempting to come back to life after a rough couple of decades.  There are now a few restaurants and shops on the street and a new CVS down the block.  With a little luck, they will all do well.

review: I read the reviews of this bakery opening not too far away from me, so on a Saturday morning, I stopped by.  There was a convenient parking lot across the street and as I approached, I could see the place was already filled with people dining in both sides of the business.  As I entered, there was a menu over the counter and two display cases:  the one on the left featured the cookies, macarons, brownies, etc.; the center one had tower displays of croissants.  Before I had a chance to look through everything, it was my turn to order.  After making the decision to eat in or carry out, I started making my selections.  As it was later in the morning, I went for the savory Ham & Cheese croissant.  So delicious!  nice and flaky outside with a deep buttery taste inside.  The ham was placed all on one end which made my first few bites just croissant with a bit of cheese.  Still, it was good.  And when I got to the ham, it went to another level.  It tasted like the ham was seasoned (maybe a bit of rosemary?)  Very good.  I also picked up a Honey Almond Croissant.  I only got a little of that but my wife assures me that it was really good too!  She thought the almonds were perfectly toasted.  I wanted to pick up some macarons as well, so I went with one Hazelnut and one Lavender.  They were much larger than I've found elsewhere.  They measured nearly 2.5" across and were stuffed with a creamy filling to be about 1.25" deep.  Fresh and packed with flavor, the macaron dissolves as you eat it.  I noted that the Lavender particularly had a floral flavor punch.  I didn't try any of the coffee available.  They do carry Tinker Co brand, so I am sure it is good.  Overall, the service was friendly and efficient.  Note that this is a bakery, not a donut shop.  The pricing reflects the artistry that goes into making each item, so expect to pay more.  If you are okay with that, then you will have a great time tasting the items you purchase.  The hard part is trying to figure out which ones to select.  Review #1149

review: My wife and I enjoyed our lunch.  The parking lot was nearly full, but once we entered the restaurant, we realized there was a lot of room inside and we were quickly seated.  No problems at all with service.  We had our food before much of a wait, including our free chips and salsa, and our beverages.  (A slight delay on getting our bill, but even that wasn't too long.)  The chips were crisp and the salsa had a decent flavor, but was a bit on the watery side, so it was necessary to keep a napkin handy.    I ordered from the Mexican (adjusted to American palates) menu and got a Texas Fajita which was large for a lunch offering.  It came with beef, chicken, and shrimp with a couple flour tortillas and a boat of shredded lettuce, pico, guac, and some sour cream.  There were also some tasty refried beans with cheese on the side.  Back to the fajita, there were loads of onions, bell peppers, and tomato slices in the spiced sauce.  Good flavor, maybe even delicious.  Just that the meats were pretty overcooked, so they got either chewy or rubbery.  Not so bad that it stopped me from enjoying the taste, but enough to mention if that is a big deal to you.  My wife ordered a burrito deluxe which thought pretty good, but the more she ate, the more the red sauce reminded her of spaghetti sauce than anything Mexican.    Overall, a pleasant experience with good service and good flavor.  Not my favorite Mexican spot in town, but a solid showing.  Review #1896

I wanted unique and thoughtful gifts, and that's exactly what I found. Yay for shopping local!

review: El Libre has been on my "must try" list ever since they opened and man oh man, this place did not disappoint.  The restaurant is completely no frills: order at the counter and sit upstairs or downstairs to eat. I decided to get the Cubano (obviously) with a side of avocado salad. The Cubano is out of this world. I really think I have finally found the best Cuban sandwich in NOLA and I am not exaggerating. I know I'm not an expert, but I just loved that the sandwich was nicely pressed and the bread was tasty and flaky. It was really a "melt in your mouth" experience for me.  The avocado salad is BEYOND good. Fresh avocado, cilantro and corn mixed up into a bowl of yum! It was the perfect side and I am stealing this simple idea for a salad and I'm going to start making it at home. It was basically guacamole before it's "mole'd" and I couldn't get enough of it.  I also got a Cuban coffee, which was a small shot of tasty coffee that was strong without leaving me jittery. It had a lot of flavor and I didn't need to add anything to it to make it enjoyable.  The staff here was super friendly and chatty, even though they were having a busy day. I will absolutely return!   Note to El Libre owners: PLEASE open one on the Westbank or Uptown!

I just wish the food had been as good as the views.

review: I've had it with Capital. They used to be so reliable about a year ago but lately, not so much. It seems like every time I call for a cab, I end up waiting outside as the minutes tick by, growing more and more anxious as I realize I may be late to whatever meeting, appointment, etc. I may have.   This morning was no different. I called at 8:37 for a cab to 30th Street Station. Twenty minutes later, still no cab, we started walking towards busier streets so that we could simply hail one. While in transit, I received a call from Capital that my cab had arrived. It was 9:04. Thanks. In the past I would have called to cancel, but this has happened so many times that I have come to expect that a cab may not show up in a timely manner, or at all. Bottom line, if there's a delay, people need to be notified. I will not call Capital again.

review: Today I had the pleasure of dining at the Island Way Grill. The location was chosen partially because it was a place I'd never been to, and to celebrate my mother's 72nd birthday.  Upon arriving, the scent of the place was amazing, the food could be smelled from the outside and it set my mouth to watering. Inside, my eyes were dazzled by the glass artworks everywhere.  As we sat, we were taken to a table that sat four and our waiter was incredibly efficient and personable.   Drink orders were taken, I tried one of the top shelf martinis, and lawdy! it was delicious, very smooth and tasty. Our starter of the wok grilled scallops was delicious, and our salads were fresh and lively to the palate. Our entrees came, and they too, were cooked to perfection. Or uncooked as the case may be in the evidence of Sushi Joe.    In the end, the bill was as we expected, for 4 of us it ran just under $150 +tip. review: If you are in the mood for a simple meal and want to support local, you may really like this place.  If you want a burger and don't want to pay over $12 for it, you may like this place too.  If you want to get away from the corporate restaurants and like the idea of going to a place that is celebrating its 100 year anniversary doing the type of food they've always done, then this may be one of your favorites.  So, since I hadn't been here in a long time, I thought I would see how the food and experience held up in my absence.  I remembered that they were packed before, so I decided to target around 1:30 to avoid the lunch rush.  The parking lot was still full!  When I entered, I was a little surprised that there were plenty of seats at the bar or at one of the many tables inside.  There wasn't anyone greeting me at the door, so instead of standing there waiting, I headed over to the chairs at the bar.  (Note that the restaurant is for 21+, so they don't have to segregate the bar from the dining area with some faux railing/wall.)  Before long, I was greeted by the server behind the bar and after asking if I had been there before, she made sure to remind me that it was a "cash only" operation.  With that out of the way, I went with a simple single burger with cheese, ketchup, mustard, tomato, and lettuce and an order of fries on the side.  Before long, my plate was ready.  The burgers are small compared to most restaurants.  They are served very thin so they can get a crisp char on the edges (I like my burgers with a tasty browning to bring out the flavor.)  The toppings are also served inverted.  The tomato was on the bottom with shredded lettuce next, then the burger and melted cheese were next.  The problem here is that the cheese sticks to the bun, so the self serve condiments require lifting the cheese and burger off to apply the sauces.  Without lifting the burger, I wasn't sure if there were any condiments on the sandwich until I took a bite since the server hadn't mentioned they were self serve.  Overall, the burger was cooked nicely, but was under seasoned.  Yes, they do have salt and pepper shakers on the bar, but I'm simply stating that I have expectations that my food will be seasoned when delivered.    The fries were crisp on the outside and tender inside.  Very good!  But again, they were unseasoned.  I did add salt to them and used the ketchup bottle to add flavor.  No problems there.  Overall, it was a decent burger, maybe a bit unique in its presentation and preparation.  But honestly, I can make this meal at home without having to drive to the near west side.  And I don't have to worry about having enough cash.  Review #775

review: We were leaving Roulaison Distillery when Andrew mentioned something about a chocolatier right next door, and before I knew it I was at Piety and Desire Chocolate. It's next to a distillery and brewery, which is perfect!  The shop is really small, but their case is packed with the most beautiful little handmade bon bons you ever did see in your life. They come in interesting shapes like tombs and dragon's eggs and they even have shiny little king cake chocolates, that are just adorable. I decided to get a couple of the cute little king cakes and I couldn't wait- I snarfed one down in the car. This particular chocolate had a gooey filling and I felt quite fancy eating a gourmet chocolate on this rainy afternoon.  You can buy the chocolate individually or by the box and you can mix and match whichever ones you please. They also have real king cake, but the owner told us to call ahead and make sure that they have it because it's only on certain days. If you're looking for a fancy gift, especially something with a New Orleans flair and a touch of uniqueness, this is an excellent place to start.

review: I can't believe I don't have a review for Chatham Tap on Mass Ave until now.  I remember going here for lunch and enjoying the English Pub atmosphere even when there wasn't a soccer game on television and I wasn't having a beer.  I remember good service and some tasty food.  When some recent developments in my life necessitated my being downtown near lunch time five days a week, I remembered that Chatham Tap had some really tasty "Prince Dean's Angel Wings" that seemed to be calling my name.  Despite the pandemic and the blocking of Mass Avenue to through traffic, my wife found a spot to park and wait nearby while I walked over to pick up my carry out order (twice in the last couple weeks.)  Sure, you may find less expensive wings, but I'm telling you that you can order the wings in different quantities and they do offer different flavors for the wings including teriyaki, BBQ, Indian Curry, or chipotle-apricot, but I went with the house flavoring once and a split between the signature sauce and some teriyaki.  The wings were excellent and the staff, despite the social distancing on my recent trips were efficient and friendly when transacting our exchange.  Sadly, I forgot to get photos of these tasty treats, but I encourage you to stop by and see/taste for yourself.  Treat yourself to something remarkable and try some wings for yourself.  Review #3765

The root beer was delicious, and free refills are always nice.  My only complaint is the price. For my burger, fries and drink, the total was $9.30. That's not a lot of money at all, but that just seems like a little more than I would like to pay for a quick lunch, especially considering I ordered at a counter and picked it up myself. review: Although I used to live in Greenwood, I never took time to explore this park.  From Main Street, which is the entrance you can drive through, it appears to be just a baseball diamond.  But when you slow down and enter the park, you see all kinds of things to do.  Beyond the initial parking lot, a lane winds its way back toward a creek that runs through the middle of the park.  Additional parking near the creek is convenient to reach the tennis and basketball courts, the multiple site playgrounds, the shelter and restrooms, and even the dog park!  If hiking is more your source of fun, you can walk over the bridge spanning the creek by the parking lot and get a good work out.  To the right, you wind between the creek and a clean dirt landfill that has elevated the ground about ten feet (the area is fenced in for safety reasons).  If you go straight after crossing the bridge, it leads you up a hill.  If you stay to the left, the trail leads you towards the entrance of the park.  I don't think the park has a loop to bring you back without retracing your steps.  I look forward to checking the park out once the weather is warmer and the foliage is in full greenery.  Review #544

review: No small market seems to define its neighborhood more than Hank's Supermarket in the Bywater. While you might not find it listed in any tourism brochures, Hank's is a place of legend; from the locals who darken the door, to the fried chicken and daily food specials. It's served as a place of comfort for many New Orleanians for about 50 years.  Walking into Hank's, you can immediately tell it's a bit different from other corner stores. Not only is there a 24/7/365 hidden treasure of an extensive craft beer and wine selection, but you can get a hot meal whenever you want it.  New Orleans is known as a food town and the corner stores are no different. Everyone seems to have that one thing they are known for- for Hank's, it's fried chicken. My original intention was to enjoy this delicacy at home, but the smell of the 4-piece dark meat was so enticing, that I had to throw caution to the wind and sneak a few test bites in the car. The flaky crust and tender meat made for a delicious surprise, and for about $3.50 for four pieces, this might be one of the best fried chicken deals in town.  Even if it's your first time visiting Hank's, there's something about the place that feels familiar and welcoming, kind of like New Orleans itself. More than a market, it's a home away from home that has a little bit of everything you need -- whether you realize it or not.  *Portions of this review was originally written, by me, for Very Local New Orleans. review: All reviews are in the end subjective.  Sometimes all the variables are evaluated, but in other instances one aspect so dominates that the other pieces are minimized by comparison.  For me, when the atmosphere of a restaurant so overcomes me with a sense of comfort and well being that the food or service tends to fade quickly, I react emotionally and start to fall in love with the entire experience.  I can't help it. I'm a hopeless romantic.   So it was with Coffee Cup Café on Bellevue Avenue, just off one of the ugly parts of business Route 1. I had seen the place for years, but was never tempted to stop and frisk the joint until reading the Yelp reviews.  It seemed like a decent place for breakfast, so I set aside a morning when not too busy to stop in.    Stepping inside after parking on the street in front, I immediately felt the effect of time warping taking me to circa 1980.  An old counter with about 6 or 7 spinners, and large kitchen service window in the wall behind, and more classic coffee mugs hanging on the walls than I could count. There was a nice size dining room to the side, and another tiny one right in front of the building.  Everything white with blue trim.    Then Beth approached from behind the counter and asked if I wanted coffee.  "Yes, Mam," as I took in her vivacious eyes and well-tatted skin.  Well, all right!  This woman had a story to tell, and I hoped she would share it.  After mentioning this was my first visit, she gave me the history of Coffee Cup Café back through the early 1970's.  She was second generation ownership, and her son, Jesse, working the kitchen grill would be the third.  She was proud and loud, and she was a groove. She welcomed me to look around, and even step into the galley for a photo.   The food?  It was just fine.  Coffee hot and fresh.  Breakfast sandwich loaded on a Kaiser roll and able to fill my happy stomach.  I could have hung out there all morning. I felt like a friend and guest of the house.  Some places are just that way.  How many coffee mugs are found in Coffee Cup Café?    I'll never tell.

review: Maybe it's because I have visited China Café often enough over the past few years to be its Duke, or maybe it's the way the owner of this twenty plus year establishment smiles at me when she sees me walk in, but the food here seems to be getting better.    The joint still looks every day of its longevity in Lalor Plaza, and sorely needs a makeover that brightens it up and takes the storage out of the dining room, and it wouldn't be the worse thing in the world if Mr. Café trimmed his Confucian beard.  Nonetheless, some kind of magic is happening in the kitchen that is creating more distinct and enjoyable dishes from the lunch menu.    Today, the Hot & Sour Soup took me by surprise.  I told the Mrs. that I did not want MSG in it, and she assured me there would be none.  Sure enough, the small bowl arrived without the telltale sheen on the surface that denotes the presence of the food enhancer to which I am allergic. It was loaded with tofu, sprouts and other veggies, and had a great taste.  Next up was the Roast Pork Egg Foo Young.  It came out as two pancake omelets full of sliced pork, veggies, and covered in the ubiquitous brown sauce.  The eggs were not particularly oily and the sauce was hot without the aftertaste of sitting around too long.  Liked it a lot.   No one will mistake China Café for fine dining, but it seems to have found its equilibrium at a higher point than most other local wok shops.  The ingredients seemed fresher, and the attention to detail and timing of the elements more rigorous.  Given that I rarely give such houses more than an Okay grade, the upmark for this place is significant.    Whatever the reason, China Café has my appreciation, with sincere hope that it continues on this path.

This pier was demolished 1967 due to deterioration. It was a major attraction.   1973 the city rebuilt with inverted pyramid. This design is definitely the icon of St. Pete for long time. It has restaurants, shop and aquarium. It attracts a lot of visit. 2013 the pier is close and make way to current pier.   The new pier was constructed and finished 2020. The improvements did create a square for people to gather. Fishing area with fish cutting board. Dual path way pier. I like some of the new features with a lot of green and open space. Tram service is free if you don't want to walk. A good day will attract a lot of people. Museum also can be found along the pier. Shops are located at the beginning of the pier.

review: I stopped in for lunch and Wow! What a great meal! Twenty Tap recently reopened and they must have been fine tuning their service and food prep the whole time they were going through the remodeling.  I had never been here before, but lured by the Yelp Top 50 designation (2017), I thought it worth the trip from the southwest of Indy to drive here.  First, know that there is no parking lot, so you need to find a spot on the street.  Mine was a couple blocks away.  There is a small front patio area (covered) for outdoor dining, but I wanted to see the inside and waited for the staff to find a table for me.  Service was prompt throughout my meal.  Water brought out, extra napkins and a bottle of ketchup delivered without asking, and quick turnaround on getting my bill at the end.  The wait on the food and drink were short too.  Like I said, good all around!  I started with a draft local (Bloomington) and got the full pint for $5.  That is less than I am used to for craft beer, so I counted that a win.  (The beer was cold and tasty too!)  I ordered the Short Rib Grilled Cheese sandwich with a side of seasoned fries.  YUM!  The sandwich, served on Texas toast, was one of the best I've had all year! The short rib meat was juicy and when paired with the smoked gouda and Havarti cheese, made a winning combo.  The cheese was completely melted and gooey, so it held most of the ingredients together (although a bit of meat did drop a couple times.)  There was also a cherry bourbon glaze on the meat and a jalapeno marmalade along with the carmelized onion and arugula.  What surprised me was how sweet tasting the sandwich was.  The marmalade had just a hint of pepper flavor, not any detectable spiciness.   And the fries were so good!  I couldn't really tell what seasoning they used, but they reminded me of fries I've had that were cooked in Duck fat.  Almost buttery tasting while being crunchy crisp on the outside.  Nearly perfect fries!  Overall, a really positive first visit to this place.  Can't wait to return to try one of their house burgers!  Review #381

review: It's official: I love this spot.   My very first experience with soup dumplings actually took place at Bing Bing on the tail end of a girls night out a couple months ago. I thought they were delicious, along with a few other things I was able to try (that bubble tea cocktail - love!), and I couldn't wait to go back.   Saturday, my fiancé and I decided to swing by for Bing Bing's first lunch service. Apparently the masses had not yet been informed so we were seated right away. The servers were all so friendly and knowledgeable about the menu. They recommend ordering 2-3 plates per person. We ordered: kimchi pork soup dumplings, turnip cake, rice noodle rolls, pan fried bao (mushroom and cheddar), xo chicken wings. We were also treated to the green beans, which are really delicious.   The soup dumplings were so awesome. I may need my own order next time. Though I certainly wouldn't have room for anything else - the food is very filling and we took enough home for a hefty snack. The bao are pretty large; I loved the taste of the mushroom and cheddar. The turnip cake is super unique and fun to eat. I'd probably pass on the rice noodle rolls in the future only because I enjoyed everything else so much more. Looking forward to my next visit!

review: WARNING: This pub is a smoking bar. If that keeps you away, you are missing out on a great pub.  To be honest, I didn't even realize it until I was leaving, I was having that much fun and enjoying some outstanding bar grub.   We started out with a pitcher of beer. I don't think I've ordered beer by the pitcher, since I was in college. I've enjoyed, buckets of bottled beer, but not a pitcher. I thank our waitress for stirring us in the right direction on that one.   I love how you can or order your chicken wings here. It's simple and I wish other bars would follow their lead. You can order in increments of 6. 6,12, 18 and 24. Then of course for catering, they offer 50. After selecting your quantity, you choose your cooking style; Traditional Fried, Hand-Breaded and From The Pit. My mind was blown when I got to select from 21 sauces. We ordered a 6 Hot and a 6 Lemon & Pepper. L&P has become my favorite when it's available and Nick's did not disappoint.   For our entrees we both went Fish-n-Chips. Four large pieces of fish, crinkle fries and two pieces of toasted garlic bread. The fish was crispy on the outside, with a hot and flakey inside. I'm okay with fries at a bar being from a bag of frozen fries, especially if they are crinkle. I like how the crinkles hold on to the ketchup. I enjoyed the garlic toast, I was able to create little open faced fish sandwiches.   I've also been here for two private parties and I can say the mixed drinks and pizza are top notch, too.   If you're looking for a fun bar with cheap beer, good mixed drinks and some of the best bar grub in the city - check out Nick's. You just might see me there.

review: I really hate to give St. Lawrence 3 stars, because the staff was super nice, but I was still left disappointed.  First of all, we ended up here because this is one of the few places that has a pretty decent menu and serves food after 10. We were STARVING (at least I was starving), so I was expecting to be blown away by whatever I ended up getting here.  The first thing we ordered was the Irish stout cheese dip. Whoa! This is super good and it comes with kettle chips for dipping! Everything else on the menu sounded so amazing. Shrimp and grits, a Cuban sandwich and the bacon cheddar burger had me torn. I decided to go for the burger.  So, we ordered, and although they didn't seem super busy, the food took a while. Then the waitress comes out to tell me that they accidentally made my burger "well done" (I wanted medium), so they had to redo it. The other food order was ready, so they brought that out, so my dining companion could eat. I'm still waiting and I'm still starving and the burger is taking forever. I wasn't about to send it back, so I just dealt with it. The fries were cold, as I'm sure they were made when my first burger was on the grill. review: Pure class. It was a class act all the way, from the service, to the ambiance and the presentation of food and cocktails. Definitely one of my favorite bars during my recent visit to New Orleans.   I stopped by The Bombay Club, shortly after Happy Hour had started. Their HH goes from 4-7 PM and the menu they offer would make anyone happy. As a light snack to hold me over till my dinner later that evening, I enjoy an order of Boudin Rangoons with Steen's Sweet n' Sour Sauce. $4 made it a great value. After enjoying them, I wanted a little more nosh, so I ordered the Pork Belly Tacos with Smoked Black Beans and Kimchi Slaw. Both were very good, but I favored the PBT's. Gotta love my pork belly.   The weather wasn't a typical hot and humid NOLA day, but my Pimm's Cup ($11) was cool and refreshing. Strong, too.  I have a favorite place for Pimm's back home in STL, but this one put it to shame. I wanted to stay and have a second, but when in NOLA for only three nights, I wanted to experience as much as I could, so it was off to the next adventure.    Great time. I'll be back on my return visit and most likely will be one of my first stops.   When: August 27, 2016 Why: Happy Hour

review: Could there be a better place to celebrate, National Double Cheeseburger Day? Perhaps, but I choose here for the nostalgia of the drive-in and the fact that I haven't been here since moving back to IL.   When I arrived, the car-hop was busy bringing out to-go orders. She did acknowledge me with a wave and ran back inside. I was kinda looking forward to having the tray with my burger and fries attached to my window, like the good ole days. However, it dawned on me my car will be a year old in November and I still have not eaten food in it.  About that same time, I noticed a sign on the dining room door saying it was open. When the carhop/server returned, I told her to make things easier for her, I'd go inside and eat.   Once inside, I am glad I made that call. Picking up a paper menu, I was able to see other offerings that were not on the board outside. Being a jalapeño junkie, I was immediately sold when I saw the Lion Tamer. It's a smashed burger topped with fresh jalapeños, two onion rings, spicy mayo, pepper jack cheese, lettuce and tomato. Actually, I had them hold the tomato for me.   This burger was perfect for my celebration. It had my jalapeños, my favorite cheese and a spicy mayo. The two big onion rings were a bonus. To accompany this delicious burger I added a side of fries. To my surprise, they were cut with skins on and fried crisp. Gotta love a fry that has slight crunch to the bite.   Oh, before I forget, they make their own Root Beer. It is so refreshing. It's way better then any mass produced you get out of a typical soda fountain.   They had a limited staff, but it is a small business and they were hustling as fast as they could. Even while they were hustling, the service was friendly and professional.   King Louie is a short drive for me, but for a quality smash burger, it is well worth the drive.   When: September 15, 2021 Why: National Double Cheeseburger Day

review: I've only eaten here at lunch but I've eaten here MANY times at lunch and it has always been very good.  They always have at least 2 different fish specials for lunch along with several other very tasty options.  You get a very large fish portion compared to almost all the other area restaurants.  I especially love when they have Amberjack and Acropolis easily gives you three times as much fish as a comparable special at Drago's.  You get a choice of soup or salad along with your lunch special and the soups are usually the way to go (they have this amazing 6 onion soup with a pastry top that you need to sample ASAP).  They have chicken, meat, and kabob specials that are also delicious.  I've also ordered from the menu and found everything to be very well done.   They also have several Italian dishes which is a bit strange in a Greek place but they are very tasty and I really like the lasagna.  They usually have at least one pasta special during lunch and it is a LARGE portion and usually very good.  They also have many excellent Greek versions of dishes you also find in Middle Eastern food such as kabobs, stuffed grape leaves, and hummus.  If you don't arrive before noon (sometimes before 11:30) then there can be a long wait to be seated as this is a very popular place.  Parking can fill up rapidly in the front and there is additional parking in the back with a back entrance that is easy to miss if you don't know it is there.  Definitely worth a visit and some really nice people working there.

review: I just came onto this page to write a review update and realized: I have never written a review at all! How could I have forgotten to write about one of the city's best places for brunch, beer and great service?   Every time I go to Hawthornes I remind myself that I need to go more often. Their brunch is seriously awesome, and offered every day. The cream chipped beef is the best I have ever had, including my dad's.   Last night, we made a last-minute decision to swing by for dinner since we were in the neighborhood. Unbeknownst to us, they were hosting a Philly Beer Week event with an Oscar Blues lineup and an awesome blues band. The large windows in front were wide open, and with all the pretty plants and flowers around, we could still enjoy the beautiful spring evening, despite being inside.   Our server was great, very attentive. I wanted something light but still flavorful and she guided me towards the tilapia soft tacos. They were awesome, especially with a few shakes of Frank's. Homemade tortilla chips with pico and sour cream were served alongside and provided just the right amount of crunch.   The best part about Hawthornes is the bottle shop, and the option to grab a beverage from the case to enjoy with your meal. The prices are still bottle shop prices, which puts most beers around the three dollar mark, which cannot be beat when dining out.   In the winter months, the fireplace and seating nearby makes for a cozy place to hang with friends. In fact, I always thought of Hawthornes as more of a winter hang, but now that I've seen how lovely it is on a breezy spring night, I'm thinking this is just a great place to go year-round. Looking forward to my next visit, hopefully soon!

review: I stopped by here, not because I had read other Yelp reviews, but because it caught my eye when I was heading from Circle Centre Mall towards the Circle.  Because I had already eaten lunch and was unaware that they had paninis and crepes inside, I went in for a smoothie.  I was surprised that there were only a couple patrons seated and only one person waiting to the right of the cashier for her order.  So, I was able to place my order and have it prepared in just a couple minutes.    I decided to enjoy the smoothie called Tarzan and Jane (Banana/Pineapple) while sitting in a lounge area by the cashier counter.  They do have two dining rooms with conventional seating as well.  As I looked around, I saw that to the west (left) of the counter was a hallway that was lined with frozen yogurt dispensers and across the aisle, a bank of crunchy topping dispensers. review: Location Alert - MLE is located inside Tamm Ave Bar.   Once you've made it inside, Mac's ordering window is in the center room. You'll order and pay for your food at the same time. If you want a beverage, you'll then have to see the bartender at TAB. Both are separate businesses and operate individually. Yes, it is a pain in the ass. However, it is worth dealing with to enjoy this bodacious burger joint.   I love flat grilled, diner style burgers and MLE takes them to another level. I altered the Dirty Sancho, instead of two pork patties, I went for beef and they had no problem accommodating my changes. Their toppings are my go to for a burger, so I was ready to go - Pepper Jack Cheese, Onion and Pickled Jalapeños. It was delicious. I also had to try the, Riplet Fries. Crisp, fries seasoned with the same seasoning as STL famous Red Hot Riplet Potato Chips. It's better on fries, then it is on a potato chips.   There's no ambiance. It's rustic, beat-up and a minimalist would even want to add to the decor. However, you're not there for atmosphere, you're dining for a bodacious burger.   The service from MLE, is very hospitable and friendly. The service from TAB could be better, but it is what it is and I still got a cold craft beer.   I'll be back? - Yep. I may even host a UYE here.   When: January 31, 2018 Why: Wanted to experience the burger

review: Although I am not an expert when it comes to craft brewing, I do like a high percentage of the brews I have sampled at Sun King.  I really appreciate that they have a continually changing line of specialty and small batch beers.  However, they are smart enough to have three house brews that are available all year round for people like my wife who orders the Sunlight Cream Ale whenever it is available.   I like to be a bit more adventurous, so when I stop by the brewery, I like to order the specialty flight which allows me to sample six drafts of my choosing (the standard flight gives you the three house beers and your choice of only 3 of the other drafts available.)     There is usually a "Small Batch" option available.  The Small Batch is truly that, but means it was brewed at the Fishers location where the brew masters apparently have a lot of fun trying all kinds of combinations.   The lineup of draft options may also have a Nitro option, a Kings Reserve / barrel aged brew, and a variety of ales like IPA's, stouts, and even malt liquor.   If you are there late in the week or on a weekend, you can ask about tours.  I went on one on my last visit and learned about the history of Sun King and of beer sales in Indiana. They also showed me the production process equipment and answered any questions I had.  You don't have to go without a beer on the tour which lasts a little over a half hour.  They only take people around on days that production is halted for safety reasons.   So, if you are looking for something fun to do and want to try some good beer, check on Sun King.  Review #213

review: Way back in 2009 when I attended my friend Jessica M's wedding, I was so blown away by the DJ she hired that I sang their praises to anyone who would listen. A year or so later, at my girl Karen B's wedding, we tore up the dance floor all night. Once again, No Macarena was responsible. I knew - KNEW - that they would one day DJ my wedding, and they were one of the first vendors I booked once my man and I set a date.   Kim, the owner, hooked us up with Jonas, who was amazing to work with. We had some venue changes a couple months out and he worked with our venue contact on logistics. I sent over the music request sheet a couple weeks out and we spoke on the phone to go over everything, including how to pronounce the names of everyone in our wedding party. I thought this was great and so thoughtful.   We were stuck on a final song and I told Jonas the song we wanted, but thought would be awkward because of a talking interlude. He sent me a version without the talking part, which is what we ended up going with - it was the perfect choice (Home, by Edward Sharpe and the Magnetic Zeros, in case anyone is curious)! Also, I asked Jonas to play my grandparents' song, and he checked with me first to make sure they were ready and available for their dance. He really thought of everything.     My only advice would be to provide all of your song requests up front. Including songs that aren't part of the reception but that you still want to hear on the dance floor. review: I hadn't been to Frank & Helen's for years and I do mean years. Then the other day, I saw one of my good Yelp friends checked in on their smart phone and it brought back memories of the broasted chicken and the fabulous creamy garlic house salad dressing. So when I got off work Sunday, I knew I wanted to a traditional Sunday night chicken dinner.   We arrived about 6:00 PM and the dining was half full or half empty which ever view to take. Either way, it didn't stay that way long. In a New York minute, it was packed.  As we waited for our waitress, we glanced over the menu and watched other tables be served their pizzas and the famous broasted chicken. I giggled as I looked around, the place hadn't changed since my last visit. Oh, did I mention my last visit was in the late 1980's? Yes, it had been that long and trust me it still looked the same. The same tacky plain Jane ambiance, but you don't come here for ambiance you come for comfort food.   The Creamy Garlic house dressing was as good and amazing as I remembered. As I've aged, I do not like my salads made with only Iceberg lettuce, but when Frank & Helen's house dressing is drizzled on top all Iceberg is okay.   What is so cool about ordering chicken here, is they let select various combinations in your half chicken. I went with the traditional mix, but the BF loves thighs and went with the three thighs. My side was Steak Fries and the BF with with Mashed Potatoes with Chicken gravy. The mashed taters were awesome, you could tell they were truly made from scratch. The steak fries could of been a little crispier, but I always enjoy a big meaty fry over a crinkle cut.   As an appetizer we stayed with the chicken theme and choose chicken wings in their Original Spicy. They were tangy, but I found them to be a little too greasy or too much sauce. I'd skip their wings and try something else.   The service was a team effort. Since they got slammed with a full restaurant very quickly, everyone was helping and making sure things continued to run smooth in the dinning room.   I'll be going back to try the pizza.

review: I was in the neighborhood, so I stopped in for a brunch lunch on Memorial Day. This is a cute little cafe and I was happy to be seated immediately.  I believe the owners were the servers on the day I was here and there was a decent crowd in the place. I already knew exactly what I wanted as soon as I looked over the menu: give the shrimp and grits with a side of bacon! The server suggested a poached egg on top, so I went with it.  The dish was great! I think I read that the sauce on it is made in a Bloody Mary type style and it was great. Just a warning: if you aren't a fan of tomatoes, it might not be the dish for you. The shrimp were tail-off and perfect and the poached egg was a perfect, gooey addition. Yes, I crumbled some of the bacon into the mix, because I was in a party mood. review: Gibby's is another of the 1950's style ice cream houses that dot lower Bucks County.  It is all glass, stainless and jutting ascending red roofline, staffed by high school cuties that bring the innocence necessary for a complete summer childhood reverie.  It sits at the bottom of Veterans Highway, just south of New Falls Road in Levittown, PA., across from a long row of old strip commercial drive ups that help complete the sense that you are more than just an ice cream licker, but also a time traveler.    The Store carries mostly hard 'scream, with a nod to vanilla and chocolate soft serve. Given the lack of choice compared to its siblings in the area that offer at least a few more soft flavors, I went with Black Raspberry and Butter Pecan in a medium paper cup.  At $3.50, it was a steal, or more accurately, confirmation that I had entered 1976.    The only real issue here is that the creme glace was not as good as the other joints in the area.  Not sure who makes their brand, but it had a flat taste; nor was it as creamy and sweet as expected.  The Butter Pecan had fewer nutty implants, and lacked the mild saltiness of the pecan that so well offsets the usual sugar rush on the tongue.  The Black Raspberry had a mildly tart afterbite. Not bad, but had me wondering why it was there.    After the individual scoops melted and merged into each other, it was more enjoyable.  Still, not the heavy smooth happy zazz found in Jo-Jo's, nor the amazing cool creaminess of Dairy Delight.

review: Chinatown Café is an refugee from Race Street, Philadelphia.  Owner Cary is a Bucks County pioneer, coming to this frontier lacking in quality Chinese cuisine, and opening his shop several years ago because he saw an opportunity to be one of the first quality chefs to start a business. He knew there was a great need, and the socio/economic means to support it.    He has succeeded.  Chinatown Café stand above most of the rest of the Chinese restos in Central Bucks, if not the entire domain.  The quality, taste, and overall gestalt of his shop are exceptional.  From soup through fortune cookie, the dining experience feels wholesome and well suited to the Chinese/American palate.  Cary knows what people like, and provides it at a high level.  When inside his world, you feel you will be exiting onto 11th Street.    This week I went in for lunch.  Although there is a lunch special menu, after my recent experience with an awful lunch at another place, I did not want to go that way.  So, I ordered off the main menu - Duck Fried Rice.  I knew that Cary was a duck wizard.  Out came a huge steaming platter loaded with well seasoned rice and big pieces of roast duck.  It was enough for 6 people.  It was moist, flavorful, and exactly what I wanted.  Just Ducky!   Cary and I chatted a bit about our businesses, and when he realized I spent time in China, he brought out a bowl of Wonton Soup for me to sample.  Very nice of him to do so.  The broth was rich, golden and as good as my Jewish grandmother made. Swimming easily in the bowl were several fancy goldfish wontons, with nearly translucent skin, and silky tails.  Stirring the mix gave the impression that the wontons were alive and enjoying themselves peacefully in a koi pond.  I think this style wonton is actually called, "Butterfly Wonton," but they look like goldfish to me.   The last remains of the Duck Fried Rice sits in my refrigerator awaiting consumption.  I have enjoyed it daily since the visit.  I have to finish it before I can go back for more.   Four Stars with a Bullet.  I have to see what Chinatown Café does not the spicy end of the spectrum to be completely in love.

review: I took my wife to this new restaurant on Main Street and thought they had done a lot of things right.  I was a bit disappointed in the flavor, but I think there was a reason.  I'll get to that soon.  The restaurant is just east of the Arts District and kudos to them for having a small lot on their east side and a public lot directly north of the building without having to cross a street.  That is very helpful!  The place looks really cool too.  There is a large pergola covered patio and the tables have large umbrellas that with their ability to be tilted by the staff, did a pretty good job of keeping us comfortable dining outside even when it was nearing 90!  The staff was also very helpful.  Kind of a team concept and doors where held open for us and water was kept filled.  We were able to get our beverages and place our order promptly.  And when the food arrived, the orders were very generous is size.  My wife ordered Mae Mae's Meatloaf and it had probably two cups worth of meat!  There were also real mashed potatoes (with some chunks left) and a combo of collard and turnip greens that had a bit of seasoning (probably 1.5 cups worth!)  So, a lot of food.  My wife had to be coaxed to come her so I could try it, so it wasn't a big surprise to me she wasn't a fan of the greens.  I tried them and thought they were pretty good.  I ordered the salmon and it also was a large portion with a tasty coconut rice, citrus black beans, some buttery asparagus, and pickled red onion.  I was eating it and just thought it seemed lacking in flavor.  The salmon was cooked through, but not dry.  It just tasted like plain salmon.  I finished eating it with bites of my sides and it wasn't until I got home that I remembered it was supposed to have a chili lime butter.  So one of two things happened:  either they only add just a minimal amount, or they forgot it completely.  I couldn't taste it.  If I would have made the connection (they take away the menus when you order), I would have said something to give them the opportunity to fix it.  So, I will give them a 4 instead of what I was initially thinking was a 3 star meal.  Maybe the owner will read this and be able to tell if the chili lime flavor was there.  I just couldn't taste it.  We ended up getting a to go box for my wife's meal and got a round of Key Lime cake that was quite good (to go too!)    So, generous portions at the $15-25 range for entrees.  Hopefully they will dial in the flavors of the food as it goes out to customers.  Review #3050

review: Going to The Cup today, I discovered a new fashion boutique that gives me a reason to shop local. The shop offers women's and men's fashions. The sweaters ranged in price from $169 - $89 which I found to be very reasonable. One of their hoodies was by a San Francisco artist who is originally from STL and sold for a mere $60. Many of the shirts were also unique in design. It is so much fun wearing something that is so different then the "mall" fashions that people ask, "where did you get that" and that is what you'll hear when you shop 10denza.   Next time you are in the CWE drinking or eating on Maryland, I suggest you stop by 10denza and discover for yourself what I discovered today.

review: We had lunch on Fat Tuesday at Baileys' Range and were totally surprised. I have drug my feet coming here due to the mixed reviews and now regret that I didn't come sooner.  Not only did BR amaze us with burgers, but their wings, chili and fries were equally as good.   Our feast at Bailey's begun with Smoked Pablano Chicken Wings and a Cup of Chili. We enjoyed the wings, they provided a different twist to the traditional "hot" wings and the chili was kick ass. The chili had a spice that provided a good kick that we could not name, but loved it just the same. It was topped with melted cheese and croutons. Croutons are a nice upgrade from oyster crackers and add an additional flavor.   To test a new burger restaurant, we figured it was best to try the "basic" burger. If they can not do a basic burger, how will they be able to do the "specialty" burgers. They nailed it! Our burgers were juicy, cooked to our specifications and served with all the toppings. Bailey's doesn't stop at a good burger, they put it on a house made bun, that can rival some bakery buns.   We shared a small order of fries and I can tell you a small is enough to satisfy two. Their fries are house cut, no frozen pre-cut fries at BR. As our sauce we choose "crazy catsup", which I wish could be bought to take home. I love the way they serve their catsup, in the small mason jars. I recently have become a big fan of places that provide catsup in small cups instead of nasty bottles.   A visit to Bailey's Range would not be complete without having a shake. Again, we went with the a traditional shake instead of one their now famous "boozy shakes".  I had my favorite flavor, strawberry and Brad got creative and mixed vanilla ice cream with blueberry sorbet. They said, they have not had anyone mix ice cream and sorbet before. His creation was fantastic, he joked that he is glad we do not live in a loft downtown, because he would have one everyday. The shakes were better then a specialty parlor down on Locust.   Our waitress was friendly and provided great service. I will be honest, the reason they did not get a five is fault of the kitchen. All the food was excellent, but we had just received our wings and chili when another server approached with our burgers. Next time, we will hold back and not order burgers until we are finished enjoying our appetizers. However, they took ownership of the error and without complaining they made it right by treating us to our shakes and removing them from our bill.   Bailey's Range, I'll be back. You gave me good service, good food and I like that your carryout vessels are eco-friendly.

review: Color me surprised that this is a new review for me. I know I've eaten at this restaurant previously. And at multiple iterations of other restaurants in this space over the years...  Last night I enjoyed their delicious Coolinary menu and it did not disappoint. We had early reservations because it was packed on a Tuesday! So I was able to enjoy a HH old fashioned to start. Yum! LOVED the rolls that they dole out like gold during your meal. They are smart to not put a basket on the table; I would gobble them up like a piglet.   My first course was the tomato gazpacho with crab, watermelon and pequilo peppers; it was light and delicious. I was also able to snag a bit of the cobia ceviche and the shrimp risotto... both delicious but I made the right call for me. For my 2nd course, I had the salmon and they were kind enough to sub out the bacon vinaigrette for a saffron sauce. The corn bread pudding was delicious and the salmon was perfectly prepared. The sauce was light and airy. Delicious. If you're starving, get that pork shank... it's comically large and very tasty according to my dining companion. For dessert, I got the chocolate fudge pie, mostly because I was already too full and I knew that I was taking it home. Rich and decadent!  We also tasted their seasonal cellos which included dill, fennel, orange and lemon. I think I was the biggest fan of the fennel, but the orange was really the highlight for me.  Service was on point, like watching a well-choreographed dance, especially with the small space and so many people. The atmosphere is light and airy. And if you're dining alone, there is plenty of the room at the bar.   Excellent first Coolinary meal of the season.

review: When it comes to pizza, loyalty to a geographic region's tomato pie comes close to fanaticism. It is completely understandable that raging debates about whether Brooklyn or Pittsburgh or Trenton or Philly or some little shop on the wild streets of South Boston make the best pie.  But, the wise peacemakers among us know the secret - they are all the best if you love them. So much better to put aside parochial claims of superiority and just eat them all! Even the worst is so much better than what those poor souls have to accept as pizza in Colorado or some other state with altitude.   Just mange and enjoy. Let your oralgasms carry you away...  Newtown Pizza makes a decent pizza, but it will never be mistaken for an escapee from Napoli nor Roma, let alone Brooklyn Heights nor Chambersburg. Yet, walking by the display counter with all the attractive pies can set your glands a-squeezing, and the Trenton Pie is very aesthetically pleasing to the eye and tongue.  The crust holds the weight of the toppings firmly, perhaps because it is a bit thicker than Romana, and the ingredients are top shelf.  Still, the overall taste sensation is not the transcendent experience of  my favorite pizza shrines. Nonetheless, it is a standup slice worthy of consumption.   The Eggplant Parm is not always prime, as I have found it to be tough chewing at times.  The same goes for the steak sandwiches.  Mostly a good fill, but occasionally a little under or over grilled.  Just enough to keep you guessing.   Friendly ownership, staff and crew, and a good citizen in the community.    As offered at the top, to each his/her own when it comes to pizza. For those of us who love Ntown Pizza, the world is your oyster. Chow down close to home.  For the others of us who have different pizza needs, we know where to go to satisfy them, both near and far.  8.27.13 I just had a couple of great slices of Newtown Pizza's Margarita Pie. Really excellent. I like a slightly charred crust because it tends to be crunchy and supportive of the weight above it.  This one was, with a mildly sweet sauce and fresh mozza, doctored with a light dusting of hot chili pepper flakes. Take a look at the photo.  It was as good as it looks.   Keep it up fellas and cinco estrellas could be close at hand.

review: Hawkeye's Country Tavern is a modern roadhouse on Route 113, Perkasie, PA. It has a decent, but limited beer list, and talented hands in the kitchen. The menu is primarily American classics, with a large sandwich page and multi component entrees for those desiring a bigger meal.   I sat in the step down barroom that felt like a basement with low ceiling and large rectangular bar. I didn't see the dining room. My server was prompt and friendly, bringing the draft Stella Artois to me in seconds. My plan was to have an early solo dinner while the family worked into the evening, and to bring home food for them so they had something interesting to eat when they arrived.  The chips & salsa table nosh was a nice touch.   I liked the homemade meatloaf dinner that came with mashed potatoes and fresh steamed zucchini. It was def a step up from a burger, with texture and flavor coming in part from the dark brown gravy on top. Washed it all down with the cold Stella.   I ordered the Brisket and Cuban Sandwiches and their Original Burger (grass fed locally w cheese, grilled onions and avocado) as takeout for the fam. Later that night I tasted the brisket on brioche and it was quite tender with a nice almost sweet BBQ bite. The Cuban disappeared without an offer from the stepson, while the burger was devoured by son after the rest of us went to bed. Told me he liked it, with special mention of the creamy avo adding interest when I saw him in the morning.   Overall, although labeled as a roadhouse tavern, Hawkeye's felt like a family restaurant (although I didn't see any kids). It did a very good job with the cuisine standards, and with a better curated brewery component and deeper whiskey shelf, it could attract a more rousing crowd and rock out.

review: While I feel really bad about removing a couple stars from 11th Street, it has to be done. The guys who work there are the sweetest, and I don't doubt that they know their way around cars, but on my recent visit, I was told that my check engine light was on for something really minor and it was turned off and I went on my merry way.   When the light came back on a few weeks later, I took the car to my dealership and found out that my catalytic converter needed replacing. This is no cheap affair, but had it not been replaced, the engine could have blown, which would have been a catalytic catastrophe on my savings.  The guys at 11th Street were spot on about the heater's issues, so I'll give them that, although the temporary fix they finagled still left me on the receiving end of cold air after a day or so.   As much as I hate shelling my hard-earned money over to the dealership, at least I know my car is safe and the issues were addressed appropriately.

review: I had not been back in over 2 years - so 2 ladies from my office and I had lunch here.  Good but not great.  It also took a long time (15 -20 minutes) for the lunch to come out (nobody ordered apps nor drinks and we were on a strich time frame).  My fried-green-tomato blt was great!  But the side of green beans with tomatoes was nearly inedible.  I chose green beans as a healthy alternative to fries, but they came swimming in oil and loaded with a salty spice blend.  NOT what I was expected.  Next time I'll order them steamed or plain.  Also they gave each of us a $2.50 up charge for subbing a different side for fries.  Not the end of the world, but it would have been nice to know that before we ordered - and not as an added "bonus" when the bill came.  Meanwhile, I'll be back but I won't rush back. Years ago I loved it here - but over the years it seems less thrilling.

review: I was excited to try Sacred Floats. I've heard about it in passing, so when a friend of mine got a couple's float through Groupon and invited me to come with, I jumped at the chance.   I'm acquainted with things in the Woo range, and this is most certainly there. The comfortable space of the reception area/sales floor is made more so by the warm energy of the varied crystals and jewelry up for sale. The small oxygen bar sits off to the side of the baroque red plush sofa.  Once we signed in, we were shown the bathroom/shower and instructed that when it was time, we'd come in and shower without soap. make sure to remove all oils on our skin. Then we'd go back to the individual pods, insert ear plugs and get in, closing the doors behind us.  Seemed easy.   We were shown the pods, these were rectangular, about 4.5' high, the same width, and 6'long, draped with a mandala. A little table to hold your personal items and a little box that holds the individually packaged earplug sets.  In one corner of the room was an infrared sauna that had jaunty lights - this is their sauna and light therapy offering.  Our host left and we proceeded to follow his directions, each of us careful to take a towel with us - One thing to note, the floors just outside of the shower, though there is an anti-slip pad, just beyond that, is very slippery, watch your step.   We each chose our pods and began our journeys. Here's what you need to know: The pods are filled with a water/Epsom salt /hydrogen peroxide solution. Some people may have issues with it, so keep this in mind please.  The water is comfortable upon getting in, it feels just above skin temperature, and as you settle in, you lose the difference between air and water. The air around you is close and warm as you slow your breathing and settle, letting yourself relax.  It is dark.. completely dark.  If you are claustrophobic, this might not work.  And with ear plugs in, all you have to focus on is your thoughts, your breath and your heartbeat.  It is very womb like.   My friend M, she said she fell asleep. I did not, but I did relax greatly. My body seemed to lengthen, to stretch. My shoulder which has been aching for a dog's age is feeling much better than it has. I did not have a spiritual experience, but I did have very clear thoughts.   When our time was up, our host came in and knocked on our pods and we got out slowly.  Keep in mind, you're covered with salt infused water, you will see this as soon as you hit the air.. since my friend was taking her shower first, the salt began to dry on me, which meant it began to itch.  Be thorough in rinsing your skin, don't forget your ears, you'll find salt in the oddest places.  If you want to, bring conditioner, soap and shampoo is provided (and they smell really nice!)   All in all a really nice experience, I would do this again in a heartbeat.

review: This is an interesting pan Asian cuisine. I have try many, and many are about the same for pan Asian cuisine. This restaurant make a bit different than the most. Not just the food has variety in spice, creativity and presentation of the dish are very nice.  When the food look good, it achieve the eye candy effect.   Don't forget about the happy hour. It is real deal for good food. Please check my picture for when the happy hours. We started with spicy garlic edamame. I have not seen a chef use high BTU wok the edamame. It very nice and rich in flavor. The second dish is the gyaw-zah. I like the dumplings they make it nice and top with Asian straw mushrooms. The food taste has good balance. The next two dish is special Roll of the day and spicy tuna roll. This roll is big. The next dish is the velvety shrimp. It have lovely cream sauce and the shrimp is good size.   Our main dish are turmeric rice and the stuff cuttlefish. The rice is turmeric and serving in the clay bowl that heat up and make the rice crispy where they touch the edge. It top with grilled beef. I believe the beef has some lemon grass ingredients that make this grilled meat separated from other. The cuttlefish is stuff with ground pork and shrimp. It sauce up with tomato and scallions.   Overall our experience is great. I will be back for other items in the menu.

review: Meet some fellow Yelpers here for a UYE Breakfast. While our food was good as usual, the service this morning was not what it normally is. I should of been prepared when the BF and I were the first to arrive and one of the servers told us they are short staffed. Why didn't I hear those warning bells?   When the other attendees arrived and we were seated, I commented to the young lady that it looked like she got some help and wasn't going solo. She gleefully responded, "yes, we got someone to come in early." Let me tell you, it didn't help. To get attention to order or to ask for anything additional and our checks, we had to wave them down.   Our food however, was exceptionally good. The UYE theme was Oktoberfest, so I ordered the German Utopia and recommend it to anyone who loves a bratwurst. It was two huge brats, cut in half lengthwise and grilled. They were so big, I'd been happy with one, but I did manage to eat them both. They came with a spicy mustard for dipping, two fried eggs and potatoes. I would of liked my potatoes to be crispier, but they did do my eggs perfectly over easy.   The BF had the Corned Beef Hash and said it was spot on for him.  I've never understood CBF, so I'll take him at his word. It was breakfast, so he also wanted a side of bacon and sausage. We asked if we could have a side of two bacon and two sausage and they were accommodating with our request. We should have asked the price? $4.29 for two pieces of bacon and two swiveled up sausages. That one is on us and we'll not do it again.   Good food, but service was lacking and they did not seem to be that busy.  The servers did seem to know everyone else dining. Perhaps our service lacked because  we were not regulars?

review: My wife and I stopped in for lunch on Sunday afternoon and took our seats at the outdoor patio tables on the east end of the business.  Our waitress (India) was excellent with her attentiveness to our needs even though she had a large group near by.  Even though there was a bit of a delay getting our food delivered from the kitchen, it was a nice enough day to relax and enjoy our beverages.  My wife order a Basic Brewpub Burger with a 1/2# of angus beef.  She upgraded to include cheddar to go along with the garlic aioli, lettuce, tomato, and house made pickles.  Excellent flavor, but too much for her to consume in one sitting. She went with the fries as a side.  Although fries can be ordered with a number of seasonings, she opted to ask for the basic salt on hers and said they were great.  I tried the Korean Fried Chicken sandwich. The breaded boneless chicken was topped with a slaw made with a sesame teriyaki sauce that was delicious on a brioche bun.  The only negative was that the chicken were thick "nugget" sized pieces that made it difficult for the slaw to stay inside the sandwich due to the bulky shape.  The chicken itself appeared to be chunks of breast meat, not some cheap composite like fast food places.  The brioche bun also added to the height of the bite, so I ended up mashing my sandwich when trying to fit it in my mouth.  The bun crumbled a bit and I ended up getting some sauce on my fingers, but it was delicious!    The side for me was the grilled Brussels Sprouts.  Excellent with just a bit of char to round out the flavor.  Highly recommended!  All the food was great.   I also ordered a flight of 5 samples (about 2 oz each) for $4.  I really enjoyed the Tripel (9% 35 IBU), the Cherry Oat Ale (5.8% 10 IBU), and the Salted Caramel Wheat (6.4% 10 IBU).  The Mai Bock and the Mandarina Farmhouse Ale were okay, but weren't as distinctively memorable as the others.  Most of the beers I have tried, particularly on the less bitter end, have been enjoyable and I would consider ordering as full sized pints.  If you aren't in a rush, drop by and enjoy some of the food and beverages.  It's just north of I-70 on the west side of SR 267.  Good stuff!  Rev #25

Ask, ask, ask your server to bring you the cuts you most want.  Once they do get 2 slices of those you love the most (for me the Lamb (chops not leg) and Angus Beef (Classic) were the best picks. 4.  Allow adequate time - at least 2 hours.  This is not a place to go if you are in a time crunch. review: This is overall a pretty decent military surplus and outdoor store with a good selection of several items.  It is a decent sized store for military surplus and they have most of the basic items.  Sadly you just don't find large quantities of cool WWII stuff very often in stores like this anymore and I miss the days of my childhood when that stuff was everywhere in places like this.
