review: I have taken the guided tour of the stadium and been to events held at the stadium, both on the field and in the conference rooms below.  So, my overall impression is quite favorable.  There seems to be generally comfortable accommodations in the seating for the big events without feeling packed.  Sure, a little more room between rows would make it easier for attendees to get passed each other, but we seemed to manage okay.  Although an effort has been made to make signs to help attendees navigate this huge space, I did find it somewhat confusing when fortune made using the ramps necessary.  There seems to be signs for the ramp system that lead to dead ends or closed doors without electronic opening buttons to push.  That required coordination between the guest in the wheel chair and myself on navigating through the openings.  Seems like it was awkward in general and could be dangerous in an emergency.    I like that the stadium hosts events of many kinds including overflow for the convention system conveniently located next door.  There are some dining options available, but considering the large number of attendees for the events, you need to either eat before arriving or plan on allowing enough time to get through the lines.    Most of all, having the stadium opens the possibility for attending events that would not be possible if the facility were not here.  Accessible from each side of town, the location is perfect for those staying downtown during a convention. For those in the suburbs, traffic quickly disperses from the area, unlike many of the waterfront stadiums which force all the traffic in a single exit route.  As someone who used to be stuck in traffic on Lake Shore Drive in Chicago, this is infinitely better!  The tour that is provided at a low cost during the week is informative and is generally held in groups small enough that allows for attendees to ask lots of questions.  The scale of the stadium is immense, especially when you stand on the field and look at the seating/roof area during the tour.  The engineering necessary for such a facility is mind boggling.  Overall, it is a stadium/facility that serves the community well.  Review #441

review: Nonno's Italian Coffee Parlor is what a true café should be.    It is attractive to visit with its old wooden fixtures and furniture; it is truly artisanal in how it produces its signature drinks, both hot and cold; and offers creamy, colorful Gelato and bakery sweets to complete a wonderful experience.  It is no wonder that the place is packed from morning to night.  People know a great thing when they sit and taste it.   It really is that good!  But, there is a downside to success.  If you just want to stop in/take out a latte or capp, or even a small lemon gelato slurp, you may end up waiting as long as those people choosing to sip/dine in.  The service is often slow, making a quick business stop on the way to the office or a meeting, problematic.  They really need to figure out how to handle the crowds that love their stuff. The snaking line doesn't work when feeling rushed.  The other issue is the no credit card policy.  What's up with that?! Normally, that suggests a few financial problems that obstruct the acceptance practices of the offering banks.  The success of this venture suggests otherwise.  Cash flow does not appear to be the problem.  Offering an ATM in the back hall by the bathrooms is not really the image a Eurostyle café should be demonstrating.  This situation detracts from the customer service expected in quality establishments, and should be rectified.    But, man, the drinks are good. Makes the annoying sloth-like pace and cash only deal tolerable as long as I am not in a hurry.   To make 5 Star rank these things need to be fixed.

review: Solid experience at the Deptford Five Guys last weekend! My husband and I were on our way to a wedding in deep South Jersey, and we needed something quick and easy for lunch. I hadn't been to Five Guys in ages so we decided to grab some burgers.   We walked in right before a crush of local athletes so our timing was great. I didn't really get a chance to take in the menu before the cashier asked us what we wanted to order. I felt a little rushed so just went with a bacon cheeseburger and order of fries to share. It was only after we placed our order that we carefully read the sign and realized that our burgers wouldn't come with any toppings. My husband ran over to the counter to see if we could add lettuce and tomato. The staff took care of that for us which was greatly appreciated! review: This is a location of the Bear's family of eateries that are also in Covington, Slidell, and Mandeville that is located behind Genaro's Bar on Metairie Road.  They are noted all over the Greater New Orleans area for their roast beef po boys. I do like the flavor and texture of the meat and it certainly is a good roast beef sandwich but it is a zero to 1 napkin sloppy level and I like my roast beef po boys dripping with thick gravy and want to have to use multiple napkins to clean myself up after diving into my food.  They offer several more po boy options with my other favorites being the oyster, shrimp, and BBQ beef.  They also have some very good burgers here with my favorites being the blue cheese and the "New Orleans Burger" that is topped with their roast beef debris.  The service here is friendly, quick, and efficient and the atmosphere is definitely a dive type environment.  They have a lot of nearby parking here which is a big bonus for making this place very convenient.  This is certainly a good spot for a quick and filling lunch or dinner.

review: I personally found this Maggiano's to be on the dank side compared to how I remembered the Philadelphia location. Granted, I haven't been to that Maggiano's in years but I always enjoyed the food, service and even the atmosphere. Cherry Hill Maggiano's was not feeling very lively on a Sunday afternoon, but I guess that shouldn't be too surprising considering the summer months and mass exodus to the shore each weekend.   My friend and I kicked things off with a glass of wine and some warm bread with olive oil. We shared the mussels in white sauce, the Maggiano's salad and a special salad with avocado, shrimp and crab. The mussels were pretty good, but I felt both salads were overdressed. Ask for dressing on the side if you're sensitive to that sort of thing. Despite this, both salads were crisp, fresh, and with just the right amount of toppings (although the shrimp and crab salad probably could have used more lettuce).   This isn't a bad option while at the Cherry Hill Mall, but I wouldn't go out of my way, either.

review: While on the east side of Indy, I decided to stop by for ice cream and ended up getting that AND dinner.  This colorful shop sits on the corner of Sherman and English and has free parking around the building.  Inside, there is an assortment of "to go" chips and ice cream treats, the payment counter, and a bank of ice creams that conveniently have the names written on stickers on the glass above the frozen tubs.  There is also a spot by the ice cream with a full menu available to peruse.    I went ahead and ordered a Coffee (flavored) ice cream and while they made it, the menu caught my eye.  It was primarily in Spanish but fortunately, there were lots of photos.  I am the first to admit my knowledge of foreign languages is poor, but fortunately, the woman behind the counter was able to understand me and communicate pretty well.  I selected from the lunch menu (lonches) and ordered what looked like a sandwich.  The Planchados o Dorado is apparently a sandwich type meal that deep fries the bread to a golden (dorado) color and then pressed or ironed (planchados).  I went with the Cochinita filling which is a shredded pork with a spiced (some heat) seasoning.  I also added tomato and onions to my order.   I ate my ice cream while they made my sandwich to go.  The ice cream was creamy and the waffle cone tasted fresh.  A nice combo, though not really a "Wow" flavor.  The sandwich arrived and I paid at the counter before heading out.  The pressed bread takes on a chewy texture, but in a pleasant way.  The flavor was really good, though the juiciness made it something to watch out for since the juice had an orange color that looked like it could cause one heck of a stain.  Fortunately, they wrapped it in foil and then put it in a small plastic sleeve to catch the drippings.  I simply peeled back the foil and slid the sleeve down as I ate and managed to not spill a drop!  I still needed some napkins, but was relieved that I didn't have to do laundry when I got home!   The folks behind the counter were friendly and made the wait time seem minimal.  I appreciated their willingness to explain some of the terms that I was unfamiliar with.  Seems like it is authentic Mexican food and worth checking out.  Review #2578

review: If anyone wants to know what Baseball Heaven is like, all they need to do is visit Busch Stadium. It truly is, where a Field of Dreams come true.   As a stadium it is only 5 years old and already is home to 2 World Series Championships, 1 Allister's Game and 3 incredible concerts; Dave Matthews in '08, The Eagles in '10 and an unforgettable U2 in '11.   Busch Stadium is also the only place I will go and will happily pay $35 for 4 beers, $22 for 2 Hot Dogs and Fries and still walk away with a smile and not feel like I've been overcharged (even though I know deep down inside I have been). After all watching the Cardinals win is "priceless".   The stadium work staff is friendly and it is obvious they all have that "Cardinal Fever". Some of the concession stand employees move to slow for me, but that's because I want to get back to my seat and cheer on my true "boys of summer" to victory.   Thanks for a very memorable first five years and I look forward to many, many more. Let's see how many Championship Pennants we can place on your brick and mortar.

review: Impastato's is owned by the brother of Sal of Sal & Judy's fame.  Some of the dishes are very similar to what you can get at Sal & Judy's but some are very different and still very tasty.  I've enjoyed all of the food I've had and there are still many dishes here I still want to sample.  The service has always been very excellent and the servers have made some very good food and wine recommendations.  Impastato's has a very unique atmosphere with an impressive collection of sports memorabilia, worthy of any sports bar, decorating the entire restaurant (and the owner seems to always be in the restaurant and happy to talk about his passion for collecting every time I've been there; and there might even be a few well known coaches or athletes dining along with you).  There usually is live music and you might have to chase a violin player away but that can add to the fun.  Certainly worthy of a visit and an interesting and great place to take a date.

review: I've been saving my Saenger review for a special occasion...and here it is. Review #1700.  The newly (reopened 2014) theater is a joy. Yes it's almost 100 years old and the Rococo ornamentation reflects it's 1927 opening date. However, the sound system, the HVAC and the other mechanicals are definitely 21st century. Of course, they had 9 years to get it right.   The theater has wonderful acoustics and even the nosebleed seats offer a decent view (bring your opera glasses). The ushers are helpful and the theater does offer handicapped seating on the 1st floor.   There are bars on each floor so while one might be crowded the next one won't be...especially if you head down to the Grotto at the lowest level of the theater (which is always cool). Bonus this layer has the largest number of restrooms too.  My only kvetch is that while the starry sky is back, the cloud machine isn't. Even before theater was flooded in the aftermath of Katrina, the cloud machine had broken down. I miss the illusion of random clouds moving across the ceiling.

review: I had not been back here in years once I discovered Vic's and other places. A good friend really wanted to come here for lunch and we both split an order of 8 steamed frozen) gyoza (They offer chicken, pork, veggie, shrimp or beef - wow!) and we each got the $8.95 lunch special.  It includes miso soup (good - but tastes like a kikkoman restaurant-mix) and your choice of 4 half-makis (4 pieces).  I got spicy yellowtail (OK), yellowtail scallion (very good), albacore cucumber (real Albacore - not Escolar - yay extra star for that), and Tempura Salmon.  Very inexpensive for lunch and quite filling due to all the rice.  The owner/manager from years ago seemed to remember me, too - which was nice but also made me feel bad that I had not been coming for a long time.  So my faith has been restored in Mizu - and although Vic is still better quality sushi, it is much more pleasant to dine here - at a table and not elbow to elbow with the other 7 seats at Vic.  I'll be back - and sooner than I had planned.

review: The husbeast and I wanted to try someplace new for dinner, so we went to what used to be "Pauls" and now it's Gusto D' Amore, a pizza joint with a bar and other food. Stepping in, we thought maybe it was karaoke night, because we heard someone singing pretty flatly. But no, this was the evening's entertainment.  There was an Honest to God Lounge singer, complete with smarmy leisure suit and keyboard. He was singing all our "favorites" from the 60's and 70's but not doing them justice. he wasn't on key , pathetically flat and lacked enthusiasm. I can't blame him for the latter, as no one seemed to care he was there.   The interior of the place was inviting, the food smelled good, so we looked over the menu and placed an order for a starter of Garlic Cheese bread and marinara sauce.  Our main would be a large "Special" Pie ( Peperoni, Sausage, Onions, Mushrooms and green peppers - anchovies by request)    The bread was tasty, but odd, because it appeared there was Mozz & American cheese? There was some garlic, but not a lot of it to flavor the bread, but it was crispy where it counted and the Marinara sauce was tasty.   The pizza was a different story though. The toppings were tasty and fresh. The peperoni was sparse as was the sausage and mushroom but the onions and green peppers were plentiful. And the crust was.. well it was not the worst I've ever had, but it was like cardboard. It was thick and had a flavor almost like a saltine without the light/flakiness.    The service was OK. Our waiter, Hunter was brand new and though he felt like he was stumbling over everything, he really wasn't. He was polite and helpful and very sweet.  We'll come back, to try something OTHER than the pizza, and pray the entertainment ISN'T the same lounge singer.

review: I'm tempted to give four stars, because I've never had a bad experience (besides the standard wait time for a table, of course), but something is holding me back... most likely, the extra weight I put on after my meal on Saturday evening.  Picture this: three relatively health-conscious girls out to dinner.  Nobody was trying to get all South Beach or anything, but it was clear that we wanted healthy meals so we could splurge a little on dessert.  Two orders of wasabi tuna and an order of miso salmon seemed like a safe enough bet.  Not so much.  My friends' wasabi tuna entrees were really delish, but the wasabi crust had a fried consistency to it-- good for sure, but totally not necessary.  My salmon dish had an absolute river of thick creamy sauce going around the plate.  Luckily, the salmon itself was on dry land, located on top of an island of rice.    I just don't understand why the people behind the menu at Cheesecake Factory think that healthy food has to be bombarded with fat before people will order it.  The salmon was fantastic with just the miso glaze-- and the tuna didn't need such a thick, greasy crust.      Oh, the CF does have healthier selections on the menu.  You'll know what they are because they are listed with the words "Weight Management" before each item.  What genius came up with this idea?!  Can I take his or her place on the marketing team when he or she gets fired?

review: I stopped by on Friday for lunch and although there was a nice sized crowd, I could get in the door (unlike the opening week!).  There is a small parking lot in front of the restaurant that is shared with the grocery and coffee shop.  It is a bit of a tight fit, so you may want to choose some street parking on the south side of the lot as a better option.  The restaurant is one that you may place your order at the counter (plastic menus are available to read or you may read from the overhead menu behind the counter.)  Once you pay, you are given a number to take to your table and they bring out your food when it is ready.  They ask you to be patient since it is not "fast food" despite looking like it.  No heat lamps here keeping things kinda hot until you order.  I ordered the Original burger (1/4# of pasture raised beef) with Mug sauce, American Cheese, LTOP, on a plain, soft bun.  I also went with the "Fresh-cut Fries".    The burger was thin and had a nice char without being dry.  I am not sure I can describe the Mug sauce flavor, but it was unique to my burger experience and a pleasant surprise.  I definitely recommend it.  The fries were generously portioned and had a crispy crunch.  The lard used in cooking adds a little flavor, but because the crunch layer is thick compared to the overall thickness of the fries, the potato flavor is muted.  The server asked if I wanted catsup and salt for the fries, but instead of a bottle and shaker, I was given a packet of each.  Sure, I could have grabbed more from a central display inside, but I would definitely prefer have bottles and shakers so that I didn't have to tear open a bunch of packets.  (Am I the only one who finds it odd that the place is promoting natural foods, but using lots of plastic and paper packets?)  Anyway, since I didn't grab any additional salt and catsup, the fries didn't have the flavor that I expected.  Note:  you can add toppings to your fries for more flavor for an upcharge  I noted garlic and pulled pork options while there.  The menu has desserts, beer, and wine available to go with their assorted sandwiches and sides.  The staff seemed positive and efficient.  The only negative is that a number of folks who were getting their food to go or waiting on others to join them tended to congregate in front of the counter.  (Maybe they should make some sort of line to help newcomers.)    So, if you want to grab a decent burger and fries while in Irvington, give this place a try.   Review #159

review: This International House of Pancakes on Mt. Holly Road, Burlington, NJ, sits in a renovated former fast food structure, and is small compared to the more recent versions of this franchise around the country. All the cues are there to prepare you for a hearty breakfast.   I walked in before court last week for a light bite and coffee, and to kill some time before my workday began. I took a seat at the 5 stool counter and was served by Tim, a young dude who seemed diligent and engaging. After a short look at the long menu, I opted for their traditional french toast and strong java. All the other choices seemed like they would be way too sweet with berries and whipped cream. Didn't want those calories.   My plate arrived ten minutes later looking attractive and tempting. I spread the cup of butter across the egg pocked surface, and poured on the old fashioned syrup (maple not on the counter).  First bite was very good, but a realized that their signature approach to this dish was to add pancake mix to the beaten eggs.  This was visible in the unusual shine on the surface of the toast, as well as the distinct mild taste of buttermilk with each forkful. I had not tasted this before, but I enjoyed this take on a historic platter.  Nice for a change of pace, but not something I would specifically request, as I prefer the traditional approach to french toast.   The carafe of hot coffee in front of me is another thing they do well. They realize that coffee is an inexpensive way to appear generous.   I have never been a IHOP regular, as I normally prefer a mom and pop shop to a chain or franchise for breakfast, or any meal. Still, I appreciate what they do, and their effort to find a new approach to their business. They even are doing burgers now. Haven't tried them, but they do look good on the menu.

review: I am glad we have another option for dining while shopping at the Galleria besides the food court and The Factory. However we've got to be honest, it is a chain restaurant that is an upscale version of Houlihan's and Applebee's.   I was anxious to try BlackFinn again after attending a special VIP Dinner Party. I wanted to see how the "real service" was going to be. We were seated for lunch at approximately 12:45PM and there were a few booths filled around us. Different servers were attending to their needs, but no one acknowledged us. We finally spoke up as one was serving tea to another table and asked if we could get some tea too.  He quickly responded and sent our server over with our tea. Once we got our tea, our server was very attentive explaining the lunch specials and various other points on the menu. So, I will attribute the slowness at first to new opening jitters.   Our lunch begun with an order of Crispy Calamari, which also has cherry pepper  mixed in with the Calamari. A big bonus for us being fans of Jalapenos, was the fact that there were also slices of Jalapeno fried with the Calamari and peppers. For me, this just made this better then any other Calamari I have experienced recently in Saint Louis.   Our lunch entrees were Stir Fry with Chicken and Fish - n - Chips.  The Stir Fry was by far the best of the two. Like I said in my review of the VIP Dinner, the vegetables were done to perfection. Vegetarians are going to love this place. For our SF we added chicken, you can also add shrimp. Our chicken was tender and moist, but when I order this again and I will it will be just the veggies.   The Fish - n - Chips was your typical FnC, nothing to write home about, so do not expect a post card. It fulfilled my craving for fried fish, which you would have thought should end after Lent. The Haddock had a beer batter that was extremely crisp and the fish was flaky and the french fries crispy the way a fry should be.   I will return, in fact next week I will be back to check out their Happy Hour.

review: Ariana's Pizzeria & Italian Restaurant on Levittown Parkway is a basic pizza parlor with booths and tables that seems primarily to toss and bake tomato pies and related sandwiches, calzones, wraps, etc., that can be found in most red sauce establishments. They also have a short list of dinners and entrees that looked appealing on the menu.   We were all hungry and took the chance on the bigger (more expensive) meals, rather than the safer sandwich route. To some extent we regretted that decision. Each came with small side salad, heated torpedo rolls and butter, and a bed of pasta under the chicken offerings. Salad was fine. Bread hot and crusty, and spaghetti copious.   Problem was that while the marsala was decent with a nice load of fresh mushrooms in a sauce closely resembling what it should be, the Ricci and Abbruzzio chicken dishes were not quite right.  The Ricci lacked much flavor despite the load of sauce and melted mozza, and a corner of the pasta was much cooler than the rest of the platter, like it had been sitting too long far from the stove. A little red and black pepper in the mix while cooking would have made a big difference. The Abbruzzio with the large bore pasta looked great, but the chicken was overcooked and tough, and the sauce flavor, AWOL.  I was overall content with my dinner, but the fact that my family ate so little of their's reflected the reviews they would write if asked. We took the leftovers home to see with we could improve them with a little doctoring. Yet, at more than $15 per dish, we were unhappy with our choices and the abilities in the kitchen.   Teaches us to go out to eat hungry. Definitely clouded our judgment on how to attack the menu.   2.5 STARS

review: Toppers has been around for-eh-ver.  They were the first to popularize the day spa to Philadelphia back in the early '80's.  Back then Toppers was in the Bourse and was pure luxury.  They'd even pick you up in a limo for your "queen for a day" of beauty.  Nowadays - a lot of the shine has been diminished.  The rude (and disorganized) reservation system and lines at check in and check out really take away from the over-priced just OK massages and pedicures that I have gotten.  I can't speak to the salon (hair/make-up) services - but for spa treatments - there are better places to go.  That said I got a gift certificate for $100 here and I gave it away to the receptionist in my building who was absolutely thrilled and delighted with her first-time ever massage.  But for a jaded, ex-NYC day spa owner, toppers needs to re-tool it's customer service and therapies in order to continue its legacy.  Try Terme di Aroma, Spa Elysium in Chestnut Hill - or even the pricey Phoenix, instead.

review: This is the laboratory collection location preferred by Parx Casino for prospective employees. After the initial interview at the casino, they hand over a large manila envelop with the proper Quest Diagnostics form for completion, signing, and to turn in to the Quest personnel for processing along with a urine sample.   It is not the most efficient operation, but they get you in and out as quickly as possible. There is a sign-in tablet for registering your presence, which seemed to work when we were there. The employees didn't have bubbling personalities, but they weren't rude, either. Just another day of handling blood and piss for them.   At the end, they keep the forms and samples, and send the results back to Parx within 24 hours in most cases.   If you've had illegal drugs in your system in the recent past, these tests will show them, and the job will be forfeit.

review: The sister property to Conroy Catering's Glen Foerd Mansion, Knowlton Mansion is a gorgeous venue for any special event. The place retains much of its character from when it truly was a house. Living areas are furnished accordingly and seem to flow into the ballroom area. A cellar that is primarily used for cigar smoking feels like something out of an old castle; gray stone surrounds and old barrels and bottles and books are all over the place. Probably for effect, but I totally bought into it.   As always, Conroy Catering put out a fantastic spread at a recent holiday party. Hors d' oeuvres included spicy quesadilla slivers, curried shrimp salad, mini crabcakes and a fabulous sushi presentation. Dinner consisted of three stations; Creole, Italian and American. I didn't even hit up all three, going straight for the filet, green beans and scalloped potatoes at the American station and supplementing with some Caesar salad, gourmet cheeses and assorted charcuterie from the Italian station. While the desserts looked fantastic, I instead opted for a cup of coffee topped with fresh whipped cream... and Jameson.   I highly recommend Knowlton Mansion and Conroy Catering for any large scale event for a lovely experience that will leave a lasting impression.

review: So thrilled that I got to see their last show of the season!  I was able to attend an earlier walk through of a portion of their show with the lights up thanks to the Legendary Haunt Tour. The fact that I was able to go back later and actually see the whole thing LIVE? That made my entire trip.  Six haunts rolled into this one magnificent location that just becomes all that more omnious when the lights go out and the fog comes up. Since this was a dark show, the only light we had was that from an orange glow stick.  All my friends and myself did the whole experience, the tracking device (glow necklace) and the bloody X on our face. We only had an issue with the people behind us who were so freaked out they wanted to blunder through the event. We eventually let them pass ahead.   The intake is probably my favorite, that Cell block 12 that opens up into the rotunda was just amazing, it really did turn out well and creeptacular with the fog and roach characters that inhabit the place.  And getting to do the detour up to the 2nd floor to see where they've seen the banshee was pretty cool and really spectacular.  One house that doesn't work when the lights are off is the 4D house. the effects that rely on 3D glasses don't work when you can't see them.   All in all a solid haunt that's been running for 27! Years.  Keep doing what you're doing and the crowds will come back and see the show.

review: I'm afraid the only thing this place has going for it is late night hours and cheap prices.  I pulled into Nashville around 10:40PM and was badly in need of some food so this seemed to be about the only nearby option.  On walking in I quickly wished I would have skipped the nearby option and went to the late night Greek option instead but I thought I would risk going ahead with eating here despite my instincts telling me otherwise.  It was pouring down rain and when I walked in there was a leak dripping water down from the ceiling.  I at first wanted to order the country fried steak but they could only do it with white gravy and were not able to make it with brown gravy which I've never been anywhere that couldn't do that.  So instead I just ordered a cheeseburger.  Next I observed that the iced tea was that lazy processed fountain kind that comes out of a concentrate instead of freshly made tea.  Then they had no lemons for my iced tea which seemed to be a constant Nashville theme for some reason.  When I got my burger it was a pretty pathetic looking creature and it tasted even worse.  I considered trying a biscuit to maybe add some redemption to the place but again only gross white gravy could be done.  This joint is cash only but it still took forever to pay.  This was by a large margin the worst food and experience I had in Nashville during my visit.  Maybe the cheap prices and late hours make the food acceptable when you are drunk outta your gourd but other than that I just see no reason anybody would ever eat here as the food was just awful.

review: If someone did not tell you where Blue Sky Tower Grill was located, you'd never find it. It is so off the beaten path of Brentwood, that you'd drive by and not even notice that it excised.  It sets across from the Galleria in the main level of that tall dark skyscraper known as the University Club Tower.  I had just gotten my haircut at Mitchell James and my stylist was telling us about BSTG's good Happy Hour and salads. So we thought we'd give them a try since they're right next door to The Boulevard.   It was the final night of the playoffs so we were wanting something quick and light.  The menu seemed to have a large variety, but we focused on the salads and choose; Fried Chicken and Cobb. As an appetizer we went with Truffle Fries, to balance out the healthiness of salads.   The Truffle Fries were good, but a little limp. I would have enjoyed them more if they were crispier. Both salads were served in huge bowls and had a nice presentation.  The amount of toppings in both were plentiful. My Cobb had a huge amount of Blue Cheese that almost overpowered the other ingredients.  The SO's  Fried Chicken Salad was huge and he said the chicken was flavorful. The salads are so BIG, that if you get an appetizer, two people could share one salad.   Their ambiance was overpowering for me. The colors were to bright as were the lights. Our waiter was friendly, but neglected to tell us the nightly specials. Once we had eaten and he was taking the order from the table next to us, he told them about a Meatloaf Special. I admit we went in wanting salads, but both us would have been tempted away with meatloaf. I think that will be my next new Yelp list, "Meatloaf".  Looking at their Martini selection, I think I'll revisit for a Happy Hour and see how happy they can make me.

review: Royal Street is to the Quarter what Magazine Street is to the Garden District- you can find it all on Royal Street.  Royal Street is my favorite street in the Quarter for a few reasons: it's not packed with bars like other streets, there are a lot of gorgeous galleries to pop into and take in the lovely art, antique stores don't get any better than on Royal and the street performers and buskers add a certain charm that you would be hard pressed to find anywhere else. There is nothing better than walking down Royal Street on a nice afternoon and taking in the vibe of the city and maybe stopping into some shops along the way to do some browsing.  Royal seems to be in the center of it all, and when you find yourself here you can guarantee that you aren't too far from a good time. If you spend enough time on this street, you will absolutely be able to catch a second line or two.

review: I've been holding off on writing this review, because I don't exactly know how to put this place into words.  I guess we'll start with the word "exquisite" and go from there.  A friend of mine decided bring me here one night.  Actually, this was all my friend's idea, as I had honestly never heard of the place.  I know I know.  I should be ashamed.  The atmosphere has a very relaxed feel.  Although it is an "upscale" restaurant, it's not as formal as Commander's or Antoine's.  You could definitely go to this place for after work drinks or appetizers and not feel out of place.  They have an extensive cocktail menu and the wait staff is extremely helpful in choosing one that is right for you.  They have everything from whiskey mixers to cucumber martinis.  For a starter I decided to get the white truffle parmigiano toast with wild mushrooms.  It was amazing.  The toast was very lightly toasted and the mushrooms were in a veal glaze that was delicious.  For my entree I had the black drum which was served with cous cous.  It was cooked to perfection and it melted in my mouth.  It was light enough so that I didn't feel bad about enjoying every bite.   My dessert, which was amazing, consisted of a fresh baked brownie topped with a delicious vanilla ice cream.  It was more than just some run of the mill "brownie bottom pie", it was decadent and delicious.  I would love to go back to Lilette and I hope I have the opportunity to do so  sooner rather than later.

review: Welcome to Feelings Cafe, home of the tiniest servings in the world. Okay, not quite, but the servings were pretty small.  We got here on a Friday night and didn't have a reservation. The place was pretty packed, but we were lead upstairs and told the wait would be 30 minutes. We were seated before the bartender even had a chance to give us our drinks, so that was great.  The upstairs area is pretty dark. I would call it "cozy" if I wasn't trying to read a menu by a tiny candle, like this is the olden days. We decided to start with the chicken liver mousse, because that sounded just divine. A really generous portion came with some bread rounds. It wasn't long before the rounds were gone and I was going after the remaining mousses with my fork. Hey, all's fair in love and liver.  For my entree I decided to get the drum, which came on a bed of spinach. The food came pretty quickly, and I'm not gonna lie y'all: this was a little baby portion of drum and spinach. I KNOW that it was probably what most people would call a "fair" amount of food, but I'm HUNGRY! I like to eat! And for $17 you better give me more than just 4 or 5 (yes, I counted) bites of delicious drum! That's another thing: the food was really good! So good that I wanted more of it!  "But Marielle, the picture you posted looks like a reasonable portion." "Lay off me, I'm starving!"  I should have read the reviews; more than one person mentioned the small portions. Oh well, I guess you live and learn. I would probably go back, but I would go in knowing what to expect and I would probably stop at apps and drinks.

review: Corner joint on Brownsville Road, Trevose, Pa., Peppe's Mexican Grill is a family run kitchen turning out good South of the Border plates. Owners appear bilingual, adding a splash of interest and authenticity to a shop that is full of local schoolgirls behind the counter.   The menu is small compared to the casas Latinas in the Hispanic community in Trenton where I normally indulge my love for this cuisine, but what they do, they do well. Our burritos (chicken & shrimp) were stuffed to the max, and the two young guys devouring them barely came up for air. My flautas de carnitas were nicely rolled, stuffed and grilled tortillas full of roast pork, chilies, cheese, with bright red salsa, avocado, shredded lettuce and drizzled crema on top. Looked and tasted good.   Although we ate in, the food was brought to us as if it was to go. Plastic plates and utensils, wrapped in foil, etc. I prefer to be treated like a dine in customer when electing to eat while the food is hot, and would pay a little more for the pleasure. Too, the environment would benefit from less throw away stuff.   I liked Peppe's, understood it's neighborhood, but it could make a few moves to be a lot better. They do make their own horchata, which is a great sign of the possibilities.

review: It had been a bad week and by Friday I deserved a massage. LOVE that they have online booking here AND that they have appointments after 5.   Checkin was very easy and I was escorted to the ladies locker room and shown how the lockers work (really I do need that sort of help). I was offered my choice of beverages; yes bubbles, please. And after changing into a robe AND some slippers (they had baby feet sizes!), I waited in a staging area, sipping my bubbles that were left for me next to my name.   I opted for a Swedish massage instead of deep tissue and it was LOVELY. I was offered the stress relief oil at an upcharge but it was so very worth it. And the massage was great. I am kicking myself that I am so terrible at names and do not remember my therapist. She was amazing and really released a lot of my stress knots out.   She escorted me back to the lounging area to continue relaxing and to have some of their spa water. Then across the hall to the dressing room.  There are a few dedicated parking spots behind the spa; parking lot is accessible from Carrollton Avenue not Canal. But otherwise there is street parking.

review: Water ice is a tasty dessert that's big in the east, especially in Philadelphia. The finely granulated concoction is blended with flavor throughout and scoops and eats like ice cream. It melts slowly and makes for the perfect treat on a hot day.   There are 20 flavors to try including blueberry, lemon, strawberry lemonade, cotton candy and cherry.  I tried the cherry flavor and, as someone who had never had anything like this before, I was immediately hooked. It's so much different than a New Orleans snowball. The flavor is evenly blended throughout the dessert and the taste is refreshing- I was a fan after my first bite. I like that it doesn't melt quickly and get all soupy, like some other ice desserts.  If you want something other than dessert, Tapeh's provides lunch items such as chicken and waffles, sandwiches, nachos, fries and Philly cheesesteak. review: Last night, I dreamt I went to a crazy, no-holds-barred, Jersey shore-themed party... only it took place in one of Philly's classiest, most heralded restaurants, Zahav. The large, bright space was cleared of its tables, and all of the staff members were transported from a late 80s Def Leppard concert, with big hair and stonewashed denim as far as the eye could see. When I glanced into the open kitchen area, I almost pinched myself (but didn't because then I would have had to wake up). There stood some of Philadelphia's most notorious chefs, elbow to elbow, preparing delicious renditions of Jersey shore staples such as juicy hamburgers, spicy pizza turnovers, garlicky fried clams and savory crab boils. To wash it all down? Miller Lite and Miller High Life pounders, sold straight out of a wheeled ice bucket, natch. The pièce de résistance? A Journey cover band that also dedicated plenty of play time to Jersey boys Jon Bon Jovi and Bruuuuuuce.   This morning, after turning off the alarm and sleepily sitting up in bed, I noticed the blue stamp on my hand. The epic party from my dreams was real!!!

review: I wanted to re-review, because since my last review I have been here many more times and ownership has changed. The most complicated thing I had to get altered was a vintage dress. I was nervous about doing anything to it, because it's made from a satin material and I'm not sure how easy or difficult that is to alter.  I brought it in and I needed a few things done: I needed it pulled in a few inches, I needed it brought up a few inches and I needed the sleeves brought up a bit. I went in and tried the dress on and told the man working what I needed done. He pinned it and marked it and told me it would be ready in a week. Well, he did a fantastic job! The dress fits perfectly and you would never guess that it needed any work.  As I mentioned, since my last review the shop has changed owners. The owner is now a man who does all of the alterations himself. Even though ownership has changed, the prices haven't and you can still get a really good deal on all of your altering needs. I have been to this man quite a few times and he always does a fantastic job.

review: This huge park (82 acres) has so many amenities that I am already looking forward to my next return.  The appeal of the park is more as a nature and activity site than as a standard park.  Sure, there is a dog park and a playground, but the park is divided by a creek and has lots of trails that you can hike if you bring the right footwear or wait until the trails are a little more dry.    There are a two shelters on site and a paved parking lot well into the park so that you aren't stuck at the south end.  There is a lot of lawn space on the higher ground so visitors can engage in activities they may not have room for at home.  And one of the coolest features is the steep (!) hill that is next to the parking lot.  After a heavy snow, this becomes a great hill for sledding.  It has a nice level are at the top so that everyone can line up where they want to launch from.  I guarantee your can get a great workout from climbing the hill a half dozen times!  I like that you don't have to worry about hitting anything at the bottom or worry about traffic like when I was a kid and we used the streets to sled.    Review #632

I can find anything here, from casual to dressy and for a really great price.  There are dresses here from the same brand as dresses I have seen at Dillard's (for a lot more money).  I love to come here and look for a nice sundress, when I need one for a summer party and the ones I have have become boring.  Now, the bad.  Oh, Ross.  Why do you have only one register open out of seven?  Don't you see the super long line this creates?  Don't you realize that most times I don't visit you, because the length of time I stand in line isn't worth the money I will be saving by patronizing you?  I mean, there are TWO greeters at the door.  Couldn't one of those ladies be working another register?  Certainly they have more skill than just saying, "Welcome to Ross!" when I walk in.   Also, your aisles are super narrow and your shopping carts are super wide.  I understand that you are pressed for space, but a few inches would make a world of difference.  Also, wouldn't it make sense for customers to NOT push their wide carts down the aisles, thus blocking anyone else who would like to shop in said aisle, but can't, because it would be a squeeze?  I thought this was common sense, but here we are.   Last but not least, all of the sizes are mixed up.  You have 2's mingling with 12's and 6's cavorting with 10's.  There's no rhyme or reason to this.  That's one thing if I'm at a thrift store, but Ross, you aren't a thrift store.  Don't sell yourself short.  Get organized!  Let's be honest, Ross, I am being very generous with my two stars.  You know it.  I know it.  So many simple changes could be made in order to make this store great.  PLEASE start with opening more registers.  There are people who would LOVE a job right now.  Hire more people.    In conclusion, Ross, you have an assignment: 1) Hire more people and open more registers. 2) Expand the aisles.  More space means more shoppers! 3) Organize your selections by size!  2,4,6,8,10,12...etc.  In that order, Ross!  Don't get creative!

Priced at a mere $2.50 each, I'll be sure to return when my sweet tooth starts calling.  The space itself is cute, with long wooden tables for sharing and a counter along one wall with stool seating. A refrigerated case houses juices, orangina and sparkling water.   What a nice little nook of serenity in the center of the concrete jungle!

review: A nightcap (or two) at the garden bar on a perfect summer night is about as magical as it gets in Philadelphia. After dinner in Queen Village, we decided to take a stroll and grab a drink, when we realized how close were were to Talula's. There were only a few people left at the bar when we arrived, and soon it was just the two of us.   The cocktail list is full of refreshing options for summer. I tried their take on a Moscow Mule - it was tasty, but I do wish it was served in a copper mug. Drinks are pricey, with most in the $11-$15 range. That adds up quickly! Our bartender was great, and happy to answer questions. I'm really jonesing to return for a romantic dinner on the patio. Talula's is definitely in the running for my birthday dinner later this summer!

review: I generally enjoyed my visit to Deviate Brewing.  The interior is a bit crowded and dark compared to a number of breweries I have visited, but the bartender was friendly enough and mentioned a couple brews that were available even though they weren't listed on the chalkboard behind the counter.    I decided to go with a flight (4 five ounce selections) which have varying prices dependent upon the brews selected (anywhere between $8-14 for the four choices).  Lots of Stouts and IPA's are featured.  The four I chose were full flavored and I enjoyed 3 out of 4.  The PB&C, a peanut butter imperial stout was full of peanut flavor and was quite good as a special choice.  The Color Blind (blonde stout 7.8%) was another smooth and full flavored choice.  I also enjoyed the Kuppa Kopi (coffee porter 5.7%) for its smooth coffee taste without the bitterness.  I would drink each of these again!  My only choice that didn't taste quite so appealing was the Victimless Crime, an oatmeal stout orange zest.  Something about it seemed like an odd pairing the more I drank.  Even though it was only 5.3%, it seemed more boozy than the others to me, and the orange flavor when paired with the other flavors in the profile, just didn't appeal to me.  Still, 3 out of 4 ain't bad.    It can be a little tricky getting in and out of the parking lot since it is located at such a busy intersection (96th and Michigan Rd).  I managed to time traffic okay to head west on 96th to leave, but trying to get back on the interstate or to head east on 96th during rush hour would seem difficult due to excess traffic.  Enjoy the beer, but keep your wits about you when you head out!  Review #426

review: I've wanted to try Restaurant August for quite some time and kept hoping to find someone else to pay for the pleasure...  Unfortunately that never happened, but E decided it's where he wanted to celebrate his birthday earlier this week.    Reservations were easy to get on a Tuesday night and we were seated promptly.  First up was hot sourdough rolls and cocktails.  I love bread and the room temperature butter was welcome.  Then came an amuse bouche that looked like a soft-boiled egg.  Presentation was excellent but the flavor was a little flat to me.  E is not a big egg fan so he had a couple of bites & was done.  For our 1st course we each had a salad, his came from the VEGETARIAN TASTING MENU.  (As an aside I was stunned that this was published alongside the meatier tasting menu.  Yay John Besh for being diverse compared to most NOLA fancy restaurants!)  Mine was more standard the blue cheese & greens.  E's grilled melon & heirloom tomatoes was the much more exciting choice.  For our 2nd choice we each got a fish dish off the standard menu.  E got the redfish "courtbouillion" and I got the trout. E's dish was definitely not my Daddy's courtbouillion (pronounced COO-bee-yon in Louisiana).  It was a piece of redfish pan seared with an herb persillade crust plus crabmeat and shrimp.  The sauce was a bourride and poured over the seafood like a stew.  The sauce was so rich that it was not something either of us could eat with a spoon although one was provided.  Guess we're wimps.  My dish was a beautifully cooked piece of trout with lump crabmeat and chanterelle mushrooms with the best hollandaise sauce I've ever eaten.  Dessert was the nougatine napoleon which was a wee bit too salty for me, but E loved it.  PLUS we were given some peanut butter brittle & fancy chocolates as a parting shot.  Final tally:  Amazing food, -1 star initially because there was a large LOUD table in the same room with us who were very disruptive, +1 star for having a vegetarian tasting menu (although it was definitely not vegan) = 5 stars.  Now I just need someone else to pick up the tab next time...

review: Sometimes when you find a good thing and become a regular at that establishment, you totally forget to update your review on Yelp. Or at least that is what happened to me and Three Flags Tavern. My first review was written after they had only been open a few days, I've been back numerous times, in fact I've been back so many times that a percentage of the staff know my name.   To get caught up I'm just going to highlight things that I order on the regular:  Brisket Burger - It easily is one of the best in the city/bi-state area. It was even highlighted in St. Louis Magazine as one of the Top Six Burgers.   Brussels Sprouts - One of my favorite veggies and they do them well.   Fried Chicken - Crispy, Juicy and just the right amount of spice. I always clean my plate, so no leftovers for the next days lunch.   Steak Frites - Best way to handle a hungry man.   Lobster Beignets - A simple dinner with a glass of Pinot Grigio.  Chicken Wings - Perfect for when sitting at the bar.  Ian Froeb ranked them #25 on his STL 100 List for 2016. So you can see I am not the only one who thinks they are pretty damn good. Added little bonuses for me; they serve their ketchup in little cups and have linen napkins. Those two details are my hot buttons.   Why: One of my go to restaurants in STL When: Too many times to keep track.......

review: There is a lot to enjoy at Lion's Park.  First, it has a great location that is easy to get to from either the south or east side of town, located near the old Zionsville downtown.  Although the park is quite a bit lower than street level (it is near Eagle Creek), the city has built a really impressive stair/ramp system to allow folks to be connected to the shops in old downtown.  The ramps have a manageable slope as they zigzag first to the south then back again to the middle halfway up, continue to the north and return to the middle at the top.  Great planning!  Between the baseball parks, there is a central gathering point which features a gazebo, lots of playground equipment, and what appears to be a concession stand (I went in March, so it wasn't open).    Beyond the central area, there are other amenities (I didn't go through the entire park but could see basketball courts.  What I didn't see were any shelters where you could rent for a family picnic/gathering.  Not sure if I missed them, but they weren't apparent from the center of the park.  There is a large parking lot on the south end of the park.  As with any low lying property at creekside, I can imagine you need to watch the weather if you are planning on hiking around here after heavy rains (the last major flooding was in 2013).  The trails are paved for conservation purposes, hoping that hikers will stay on them.  The park is not part of the city's park system, but ran independently by the Lion's Club.  Still, it is a welcome addition to the areas green spaces.  Review #710

The water of the gulf was chilly at first but my feet readily got used to it. This time of year it's not overly crowded, it's got restrooms and a few snack bars. The parking is plentiful and the sand is sugary white. Honestly it is a small sliver of paradise right outside of Dunedin.

AMC Fashion District has definitely earned a spot in my movie theater rotation!

review: If mid 20th Century Archie & Veronica malt shops and Back to the Future big fin American road steel move your imagination, then Jem's Restaurant in East Norristown, PA, may be for you.   What from the outside looks like another shopping center fast food luncheonette constrained by its surroundings to be a boring food dealer, is in fact a real trip down memory lane. The joint is a museum of cultural artifacts from the early days of television, with large posters of Rebel Without a Cause, James Dean, and Seven Year Itch, Marilyn Monroe. Perhaps that's why the room was full with retirees and people over the age of 70 (except for those of us needing to eat and run). This place is the original greasy spoon, for all the right reasons.   The double "U" counter separated the kitchen from the dining room. My spinner faced the grill operated by two short order cooks who worked smoothly in tandem. I ordered coffee and Jem's Scramble with feta and rye toast. The full insulated carafe of java set in front of me was a nice touch. I listened to the repartee between customers and servers. It was familiar and entertaining. Most everyone seemed to be a regular.   I noted the pile of chunk cut red bliss potatoes and metal tray of bacon on the grill. I watched eggs, pancakes, french toast and breakfast sandwiches being cooked and constructed as spatulas flew. I also saw that the grill was not scaped clean between orders, allowing residue from everything grilled there to build up and become part of the next dish. No judgement. Then, my small Scramble arrived, steaming in my face and fogging my glasses. Smelled awesome and looked like a gently beckoning glistening syren.   It was delicious. The eggs held the sausage, onions, peppers and feta in a wet/warm embrace, allowing each forkful to hang together with all elements dancing on my tongue. There was also a hint of everything else that came before, making for a mysterious, yet very pleasant flavor.   Maybe that is the house secret to success, or just how it accidentally became an amazing greasy spoon. Intentional or not, Jem's has a full house every morning, and is definitely doing something right.

review: My wife and I decided to head to the near north side for lunch one Friday in February.  We appreciated the free parking in the lot north of the restaurant.    The atmosphere was clean and a colorful with a long row of tables by the windows and a huge amount of seats next to the bar counter.  We were seated promptly at a table.  After looking over the menu, I decided to go with the Hoosier sandwich (pork patty, apple, arugula, smoked gouda, and hickory dijon) and Yucca fries.  The sandwich flavor was excellent! review: A few years ago I noticed that Mill Street, Bristol, PA, was experiencing a rebirth of vital commerce with many new stores, restaurants, cafes and even a classy bakery with a beautiful dining room and sugar coma inducing display of cookies, cakes, danish and donuts. That shop, Angelina's, was the subject of my breakfast explorations last week.   First impressions were tremendous. Everything was whitewashed and had a Victoriana vibe. There were a dozen or so tables, and counter/highchairs in the two window bays on either side of the front door. Further back, the baked goods sat shelved and lit like colorful jewels and crystals waiting to be bagged and consumed. So seductive.   I sat close by the front and checked the front of the two sided breakfast/lunch menu. I went with the "Thin French Toast," over the "Thick" alternative. I figured I was in a bakery, and it had to know about the proper approach to this traditional dish. Well, perhaps I was overconfident about that.   The first clue of what was to come was the delivery of the FT accessories - butter and Smuckers syrup. The spread was fine, but that amber colloidal suspension was all high fructose corn syrup, about the worst thing for a human body. Luckily when the plate arrived, the four pieces of bread were sprinkled with powdered sugar, so I could skip the drip. Regular sugar is a better choice than artificial or high fructose sweetener.  When the finished platter arrived it looked good. I spread the butter to melt on the surface and cut a small wedge. It was obvious that it had spent little time in the egg/sugar/cinnamon/vanilla extract mix. The outside was nicely grilled, but the inside was dry. It had not been dredged in the mixing bowl long enough to permit absorption, but put too quickly on the grill. The chef needs find a better recipe.   Oh, well. This wasn't going to be my best morning. *%It happens.   I'll be back to check out those georgeous pastries. I suspect that is where I should have begun this adventure.

review: Spencer's Grill is a rock solid diner. It is classic is all sense of the word. I stopped by this morning to join in the 70th Anniversary celebration. To celebrate 70 years as diner, shows you how good it is. The food is consistently top notch, breakfast or lunch.   They are known for their Crispy Pancakes and I normally order them when ordering breakfast. However, today I went with a #8; Biscuits & Gravy with two eggs and a side of meat. I had my eggs scrambled and choose bacon as my meat. The farm boy inside of me, made me order it.   The gravy was thick, full of sausage and draped over the fluffy biscuit with extra gravy to spare. Surprisingly I needed to add to salt, which is a good thing for those who do not like over salty foods. My scrambled eggs were blended well, making for a soft yellow presentation. The bacon, was crisp, no limp wimpy bacon here. The coffee was black and the cup was kept full. My breakfast was very filling, but I wish I would have ordered a side of Hash Browns. I would have been over-stuffed, but they serve the best HB's.   As always, the staff is friendly and they keep the diner running smooth and fast.  Breakfast or lunch, give Spencer's a try.   Will I return? I always do.   When: October 24, 2017 Why: 70th Anniversary Celebration

review: Not my shot glass of vodka and I love vodka. How this place was selected as one of the best 100 restaurants in STL is beyond me. The only thing that saved it from getting a two star rating and being placed on my Terrible Two's list was the $1 off my cocktail for checking in on Yelp and the fact that the Pork Pelmeni which Ian Froeb recommended was actually good.   What I did not like was the odor that hit me in the face as I entered. It was not a just freshly cleaned smell, it was an unpleasant scent. I just ignored it and took a seat at the bar. Which was a big mistake. I think I would have been better off at a table. Not only did I have to brush away fruit flies, but the bartender was busy servicing the tables more then she was the bar. At first I thought it was strange that she kept rushing me and pushing me to order everything at once. She also seemed put out when I asked questions about the items on the menu.  Then I realized, she was hustling and working the bar and both sides of the restaurant as a server.   Here's the run down on my order:  New Old Fashioned - I've had better, but can I really complain about a $5 cocktail.   Brussels Sprouts Salad - The bacon was rubbery and the burnt honey vinaigrette was bitter  Pelmini - Good pork flavored Russian style dumpling. Saved them from only getting 2 Stars  The fruit flies were a big distraction, having to wave them away constantly. The bartender even waved them away from my area. I gave up on eating my salad when I saw two resting in my salad bowl.   I also felt sorry for the bartender/server. They were way to busy, to so understaffed. If she wasn't so rushed to do everything, I'm sure she'd been more attentive.   When: August 9, 2016 Why: Lunch - STL 100

review: The Bowl inspired Grill (sic) is a relatively new entry in the luncheon wars in beautiful downtown Trenton, NJ. It is located on South Warren Street, the cobblestoned lane that manages to look good despite all the degradation around it. It is an Americanized Mexi house that does it's best to imitate Chipotle, with bowls, burritos or wraps made to order as you select the rice, beans, meat, salsa and drink of choice being constructed behind the counter. All this for around ten bucks.  We walked down last week. The room was empty, but for one table when we arrived at 1:00. The two women working the assembly line were friendly and knew their craft. I ordered a bowl with brown rice, red beans, shredded beef, corn salsa and cilantro. It felt hefty on the plastic tray.   The result was tasty and filling, but far from special. Then again, I don't frequent Chipotle for the same reason. I prefer the authentic version of Central American cuisine so prevalent and delicious around this capital city. Yet, for a downtown foodery it certainly carries it's weight and contributes some variety to the lunch scene in these parts.

I've also stopped in for Lunch on their $5 burger Monday's.  They're not kidding, those burgers are HUGE. One caveat, tell them if you want the burger more done than medium. I was fine but my mom likes things a touch more well done.  The onion rings are to die for!     The service is always friendly & they're pet kind too, so bring your pups and let them enjoy the atmosphere too. OH! and they have a poker club that meets on Thursday nights, if that's something you're into, by all means, check them out!

review: I really like the fun vibe and the ambiance of this place but I'm just not a fan of the whole Latin and Caribbean fusion style food into tapas concept.  I generally hate small plates and that is about the only type of plate you will get here.  I've eaten a few decent things here over the years since they first opened but really after several visits nothing has ever really knocked my socks off to motivate me to return.  They used to not have a corkage fee but the last time I ate there it was around $8 per bottle.  I can go to lots of other better places that serve much bigger portions of food at lower prices that don't charge any corkage fee.  I don't mind paying a corkage fee in a nice restaurant that already sells wine but this place is a far cry from fine dining and has no alcohol permit. review: There is a good reason that Iaria's has been in business for a long time: they serve a good meal!  I stopped in for lunch after parking in their private lot on the north side of the building.  (The doors are somewhat tough to open due to vacuum pressure, so pull hard!)  At the doorway, there is a hostess station sign asking you to wait to be seated.  To the right is a hallway that leads to the bar area.  I opted for the dining room since the bar looked somewhat cramped and packed.  The dining room has a wall of mirrors on the far end to make the space seem more open.  There are 4-top tables with chairs and some booth style seats.  The booths look padded, but be careful to not sit too hard.  The "padding" doesn't do much to protect you from the hard, uneven seating underneath.  (I tried scooting in to a corner and caught a raised joint where the benches were together.)  The waitress was pleasant and though handling a large group at the tables next to me, minimized the wait between interactions.  My water was refilled and my check was processed in a timely manner.  I went with one of the lunch specials, the beef lasagna.  It came with a side salad as part of the deal.  First, I received a complementary basket of sliced bread and crackers.  The bread came with room temperature margarine and there was already a bottle of olive oil on the table.  The salad was next and the Italian dressing I ordered was in a cup on the side with a spoon to allow me to put as much as I wanted over the salad. The dressing was really good and may have been made in house.   The salad plate was 8" and was made using iceberg lettuce that was mostly cold and crisp.  However, some of the ingredients didn't look quite in top shape due to possibly too cold temperatures.   The lasagna was served unadorned in a bowl that allowed extra sauce to be held in reserve for when needed.  The noodles were very tender and the beef was lightly seasoned.  The flavor was good but not layered like I've had other places.  The sauce worked quite well with the beef and noodles.  The portion was appropriate for a lunch portion too.  I was satisfied without feeling stuffed.  Overall, I enjoyed my return visit to Iaria's.  Lunch was quick, service friendly, and reasonably priced for the meal.  Review #1033

The prices here seem a little bit steep for what seems to be just a casual dining place.  I will say that one of my friends ordered the seafood platter, which came with fried crab, catfish, oysters and fries.  It was huge, looked really good, and can definitely be split between two people.  The service was good and we were seated quickly, with only about a ten minute wait. review: Some reviews can't wait until the morning. Y'all, Sidecar is back!!!  I have to admit, my last few visits to Sidecar had gone from so-so to bad. After our last visit, it sort of became this unspoken rule in our house that we weren't going back. Yet, I didn't have the heart to downgrade my review. Sidecar has been a neighborhood staple - the first neighborhood staple, actually - for more than a decade. I definitely wasn't cheering for its demise.   Then, news came of how the crew behind Mike's BBQ and Stockyard Sandwich had taken over Sidecar. The photos of new menu items looked extremely promising. Finally, after late nights at work, my husband and I met up in our neighborhood and hit Sidecar for a late bite. The place was packed, like it used to be.   We sat upstairs and perused the menu. I was thrilled to see Heineken 0.0 on the beer list! This is my go-to NA beer and I am so so happy to see it in my hood!   We tried to order a pizza after seeing so many photos of it on the 'gram, but our late arrival meant they were already out. So I ordered a hot chicken sandwich with a side of fries, instead. You guyyyys. They did Nashville proud! Easily one of the best takes on Nashville hot chicken I've had outside of Nashville. And the fries were bomb, too!   We didn't have room for dessert but I've got my eye on the carrot cake. So stoked we have our neighborhood bar back and wishing the new owners all the best!
